0022d5d2ee0fa87f.text: The remains of the nuraghe Corongiu are located in the territory of Ollastra, in the area of Serra Laccus. Unfortunately, the monument has been almost completely dismantled. It was presumably a tholos nuraghe, although its planimetric layout is not clear.

00255c319c8644c3.text: Natural cave used as a storehouse for large containers for foodstuffs dating to the Middle Bronze Age, with items found on site completely intact.

0025e6faa271a4a4.text: Almost on the top of a small hill is located the nuraghe of Monte Pedrosu. During the first or second world war it was used as a madhouse, as evidenced by the concrete wall added to the summit portion of the archaeological site.

002fe3f0054ac9c6.text: Remains of a Nuragic village composed of about fifty huts. Communication took place through underground tunnels, many of which remain unexplored to this day. The presence of the "meeting hut" — conspicuously restored — was noted.

0044e4789e967362.text: Single-tower nuraghe with probably a settlement.

005407399da1246a.text: Nuraghe Loschiri, located in the territory of Semestene, a small village in the Meilogu (visible in the background to the right of the image). Partially collapsed, it preserves intact its entrance portal and large internal sections.

0066d8f888a686a0.text: Nuragic gate that leads to the rock above the cliff.

0090c9430f1eba3d.text: The settlement is characterized by the presence of a settlement, documented by sacks and foundations of huts, attributable to the Nuragic period, particularly the Middle, Recent, and final Bronze Ages, and the early Iron Age. The Recent Bronze Age phases are mainly attested by numerous finds of grey-ardesia pottery made in the 1980s, coinciding with the initial discovery of the site.

0093f57fadd2b56a.text: In the countryside around Samatzai there are several scattered menhirs. Many of them, once standing, now lie overturned at the edges of paths and farmland; some have become and are used as boundary stones between one village and another, like the one still visible on top of the hill Bruncu sa Furca, where a prehistoric village may have stood. This standing stone is 1.30 m high, with a quadrangular section, rounded at the top, and without any particular signs of working.

009e2b84bf042855.text: The grave is the state of abandonment and decay we currently face. Unfortunately, the lack of institutional interest—despite numerous requests for intervention—leaves us indignant. The structure is interesting and some parts are accessible despite the collapses. The corridor emerges with a dolmenic door onto the cliff face a short distance away. mu

00bf0e2255befc06.text: The actual location of the site needs to be verified.

00c10e5347143ec5.text: It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the Tratalias area and is located in one of the numerous medaus, known as is Cuccus. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a remaining height of about 5 m, built from megalithic blocks of andesite. The internal circular chamber is about 5.50 m wide, features a topless tholos, and is completely free of collapse.

00d8ee3c51378cf2.text:
The monument, of tholos type, is not accessible internally due to collapses, but features a circular plan with a diameter of about 9 m and retains, externally, a section of wall up to 2.20 m high, composed of 5 courses of large trachyte stones.

A short distance from the nuraghe, the remains of a wall are found, likely a surviving fragment of an outer wall.

00e29de96df8ff60.text: The Ruiu in question is an abandoned single-tower nuraghe completely enveloped by vegetation, yet we were able to penetrate through the thick undergrowth to enter it. The tholos is not intact, and unfortunately vegetation dominates the structure.

00f7a4e93e7076ae.text: As far as can be seen through the vegetation, it is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall; I believe it is well preserved despite the collapsed tholos, though it still requires excavation and cleaning.

00f7d61f05100a58.text:
It was built in the Nuragic period for the water cult. Situated in the locality of Is Pirois, this Nuragic sacred well has the peculiarity of a single-tower nuraghe erected on its summit, built on the false dome that closes the well chamber.

The vestibule is defined by two wall faces composed of granite blocks. From the lintelled entrance one enters the stairway leading down into the well chamber, which is closed at the top by a false dome.

0112c126875b0b52.text: Visible from the road, they are domus with modified entrances set slightly above the countryside level and located within the sheepfold.

01429a0e0110d865.text: The Atzara nuraghe is a complex, three-lobed type featuring a slender main tower characterized by a wide base. The walls connecting the three external towers are still in good condition, while the reinforcement structures were built during Punic and Roman times. Recently it has been cleaned, but it awaits a more detailed excavation to better understand its structure.

0176ec711785071e.text:
The funerary site, datable to the 3rd millennium BC and used until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC, consists of thirteen domus de janas. The finds recovered are attributable to the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures and are now largely preserved in the Villa Sulcis Museum in Carbonia.

A single-tower nuraghe stands on the summit of the hill on which the necropolis is situated.

019265a5a00a2afe.text: A small isolated hill in the middle of ploughed fields. Many believe that within it there is a nuraghe completely covered in earth. This view is supported by the stone ashlar cap at the top.

01f195b88098662c.text: The monument stands in a commanding position; the extensive collapse of the outer wall face prevents an accurate reading, but it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and two storeys, with a spaced outer wall.

01f591470bd3e1ef.text: On a plateau used for crops and pasture, only the basal course has been identified, made of large, roughly dressed blocks, of what is thought to have been a nuraghe. Its sub-circular ground plan, which incorporates a large natural granite boulder, is still legible. Because of stone-clearing work and the reuse of the ashlars for dry-stone walls, not even traces of the collapse survive.

01fad16c4d292bf3.text: It includes three hypogea, of which the first (with 7 cells) should also be called "Sa Spelunca de Nonna".

0229d8b7ecbb1e15.text: The lower register of the stele, slightly trapezoidal (1.02 m – 1.05 m – height 0.98 m), has a frame running along the profile of three sides (0.16/0.18 m wide on the upper line; from 0.18 m to 0.13 m on the vertical sides), raised by 0.35/0.15 m. The thickness of the slab differs on the two sides: on the left, at the lower edge it measures 0.34 m; 0.40 m at the top and 0.56 m in the middle zone; on the right it decreases from the base (59 cm) to the top (32 cm).

02446a93da58467f.text:
We approach the south-east wall from the inner face of the nuraghe, past the "guardian niche" on the right and the start of the helical staircase on the left.

These two chambers are inaccessible as the interior has completely collapsed and is filled with ashlars. However, the outline of their layout remains clearly visible, with the upper part of the staircase emerging above the access chamber and completing a full circuit around the tower.

024b681ec33f1d06.text: Single-tower partially collapsed and covered by vegetation

025dbdae9b1668d7.text:
It is of mixed type, built of large granite blocks, with a central tower reaching 12 metres in height, with corridors and surrounded by three secondary towers. The lintelled entrance gives access to a corridor with a side chamber containing a well just under 2 metres deep. In the central chamber there is another corridor where the helical staircase leading to the upper floor is located.

The other three towers are partially collapsed and difficult to access;

0262bfc32dcd94ce.text: Nuraghe built of calcare ashlar. On top of it a shelter was constructed with the erection of new walls made of small calcare ashlar. To the north, at the entrance, there is a concio with a carved recess.

027859001ccc6685.text:
Administratively it belongs to the municipality of Thiesi, province of Sassari, from which it is about 10 kilometres away.

The necropolis consists of four domus de janas cut into a trachyte outcrop on the slopes of Monte Ittiresu. Among them, Tomb III stands out for its importance; also known as the "Painted Tomb", it is considered one of the most interesting testimonies of the Sardinian Neolithic. Because the site has been left abandoned, the frescoes are undergoing continuous and rapid deterioration.

02acf19a9755561e.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower with a subelliptical plan, built from roughly shaped trachyte blocks, in a state of collapse to the south and partially buried, and it is completely surrounded by vegetation.

Only faint traces of the staircase and a niche remain from the central chamber.

On the side facing the valley, a feature that was presumably an opening in the outer wall is visible.

02b1e8100436d410.text: Damaged nuraghe, with three courses remaining. Likely nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted" nuraghes.

02e265fdcd43bb61.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a ruined and buried village

02e5ed197683aaf2.text: Man-made structure submerged by the artificial lake

02eaad7d2b6d2982.text: Nuraghe of the tancato type with a main tower and an additional structural body (second tower and courtyard). The monument is located adjacent to the parish church.

02f94fb45e5d48ec.text: Single-tower nuraghe located in the plain, enclosed with a metal mesh. Currently visible are four courses of the external wall face on the north-east side, composed of medium-sized stones. The presence of other archaeological remains in the surrounding area cannot be ruled out.

02fb93c6a37331ca.text:
The tomb belongs to the cemetery of Campu Majore, composed of 24 domus de janas, which are located within private properties and are not accessible without permission.

The entrance to this domus faced the village of Busachi, which during the Second World War was modified with a reinforced concrete wall, adapted by the owners to serve as a shelter against bombings.

Today it is used as a water reservoir.

03095083a1d01ccd.text: Originally the menhir complex consisted of 12 menhirs arranged in a circle. Today only one remains, about two metres high. The others have disappeared, possibly removed for construction work.

03107a242d36fc82.text: Various domus de janas of which no description has been found

0310c9ab029607ea.text:
The split rock, a narrow and low, dark, dusty space that forces you to kneel, as a reminder that you are in a sacred place.

But when you turn on the light, everything becomes visible—the rock takes form, and the ancient symbols seize you, transporting you through time.

031362500d6378cd.text: Well located a short distance from the nuraghe Unia, along the catchment of a stream, of probable Nuragic origin

034b24ead383619f.text: "Nuraghe Ianna Bassa, under the Monte Sedda Sos Campos, near good springs, are the remains of the nuraghe, part of the foundation and above, a heap of stones. In Antioco Sanna soil." The Taramelli's description, seventy years later, is still substantially consistent with the current state of the ruins.

034fe8ed0a35ac54.text: The nuragic complex consists of nine towers, three belonging to the central structures and six to the robust outer wall. Its absolute peculiarity is the direct superimposition on its structures of the ruins of a small country church, dedicated to the eponymous saint and dating to the early 17th century; eleven burials found in the area around the sacred building belong to its period of use. On the hill of San Sebastiano, traces of a Punic occupation are legible.

038ff9c22e11617d.text: Complex nuraghe, completely buried and destroyed; only three courses of about 1.20 m in height remain of the main structure, with a diameter of about 9/10 metres.

039dbb95e4d64bf4.text: The monument comprises a main tower, against whose front side, from east to south-south-west, a bastion (8) has been built enclosing an open courtyard (11), and two corner towers (13-14). All around are visible the ruins of several structures, probably belonging to the associated settlement.

03a20587dc28c360.text: Now fully incorporated into a mass of rubble, it is in very poor condition with stones scattered throughout.

03a40af86b6e7b1c.text: It could refer to the construction of a giants' tomb or to a nuragic hut associated with the nearby homonymous nuraghe.

03a494f8116c2021.text: Elliptical building, slightly raised on an artificial platform. Function to be verified.

03b3d8bce6a92bd5.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. It is almost entirely covered by climbing vegetation, especially on the N–NE exposed face. The west face is the most visible, with structural remains exceeding 4 m in height, while the tower as a whole reaches a total height of about 7 m.

03dc4f0b5a90f147.text: A single-tower nuraghe that has collapsed inwards, of which the doorway and about five courses of the tower survive.

03f2eed4bebea07a.text: Two giants' tombs, probably associated with the nearby Prizzada nuraghe.

03fb528bb302c5f6.text:
Isolated domus with reuse.

Excerpt from the publication "Archaeological research in Marghine-Planargia" by Moravetti

0405a09fbe71e3e5.text:
It can be counted among the most extensive of those known and is rich in particular architectural symbolism. Hewn from a rocky plateau of red trachyte, it consists of at least twenty hypogea.

The domus de janas very often reproduce the ground plans and certain details of the dwellings of the living.

In some of them anthropomorphic petroglyphs are carved, known as “capovolti” because they are thought to represent the souls of the dead returning to mother earth.

043a873fbccde45d.text: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.

044c7f731283edf2.text: It is a tomb with a rectangular burial chamber clearly in a state of degradation, almost entirely covered by moss and difficult to identify; the chamber is about 15 metres long.

04628ea2ecf62ce7.text: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

0469dc0966e4ee91.text: Nuraghe in very poor condition, only a few external points are visible, many stones are scattered in the adjacent ground, and almost the entire structure is enveloped by vegetation.

047d72b1943b2e07.text: It is reduced to ruins but very interesting for its star-shaped layout. A Megaron-type temple is present. For clarity I will use the number I to indicate the first of the three found in a very small area with the place-name Giaganu Dominigu. I do not have the systematic survey carried out by the Sassari Superintendency; on my part I propose an ideal reconstruction that comes as close as possible to the real one, considering that we are "on home ground".

0489a33d2629f084.text: Complex-type nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and four additional towers. The structure, datable to 1400–1000 BC, is located at the border between the municipalities of Oristano and Villaurbana. Surrounded by scrubland and vegetation, it is not easily accessible or visitable.

048e09a1eb1c9626.text: Destroyed nuraghe and today no longer visible

04cdfb8b48db9796.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition, with entrance and tholos partly buried but relatively intact.

04de16dd429b4a4e.text: Interesting from a structural and typological point of view for the domus. It is a true necropolis: the domus are simple in form but also complex. Ranging from those with an antechamber and a single chamber to the most elaborate ones with many well-crafted chambers. The vaults of some have collapsed, but careful visits are still possible. mu

0519b885f0326450.text: Complex nuraghe with village. It is located at the border with the municipality of Sinnai in the Campidano State Forest. It is situated on a mountain side completely covered in stones and it is very difficult to see the structures. In some areas walls can be observed.

05275dc39021e8b5.text: The nuraghe, of which no trace remains, was located at the cape now known as Torre Canai – Turri. The map of Sant'Antioco, drawn by the geographer Maggiore Besson in 1744, suggests that the tower, built at the order of the King of Sardinia, Carlo Emanuele III, in 1757, on the cape “su moru”, was constructed using nuragic structures.

05285af62c002dfe.text: Natural with modifications, it dates to the Bonnanaro culture period (2200–1800 BC). Used as a burial site.

05299977d78d81d2.text: Discovered in 1881, it was buried and then rediscovered in 1982 by the Superintendent.

056c8fec6e61bca2.text:
Dimensions: h. 1.50 m; length 10.50 m; width 1.40 m.

The tomb stands on a small rise whose gentle slopes are currently used for vine cultivation. The left wing of the exedra survives, formed by large blocks that decrease in size from the entrance towards the lateral ends. The entrance, lacking the stele, shows an interesting arrangement for its setting: a shaped granite block on which a stele presumably rested.

056d341b94307511.text:
The burial – of the coursed type with an arched stele – partly preserves the apsidal tomb body, oriented to the east and built of medium-sized polyhedral blocks of granite and porphyry. The short rectangular inner corridor has walls formed by basal orthostats supporting three courses of roughly dressed blocks; the floor consists of the outcropping rock.

The burial dates to around 1500 BC.

05714d6e265cfd66.text: Giants' tomb in a state of complete abandonment, located just a few dozen metres from the nuraghe.

057ca08ba01ab740.text: "Tancato" nuraghe Funtana Mela, Macomer. The plan is taken from Moravetti, Archaeological research in the Marghine-Planargia.

058ff5a3d50d8de5.text: The structure, likely Nuragic, features straight wall traces defining a rectangular plan aligned along a north-south axis. It is plausible that stones removed from the ancient building were reused in subsequent enclosure and hut constructions; the original building, by shape and visible features, resembles a megaron temple.

059a3724fb272071.text: At Scivu, by the beach of the same name, stands the nuraghe known as Nuraghe Narocci or Cancedda. The nuraghe sits on the hill of Punta su Nuraxi, 226 metres above sea level, overlooking the valley that slopes down to the coast. The structure consisted of at least four towers and covered a large area. Some of the scattered material has been found even at the foot of the hill.

05dd806986afd12c.text: Ruined single-tower nuraghe. Part of the tholos survives on the west side. In the past it was altered to house a sheepfold shelter.

05e4978406f67e83.text: Described by Lamarmora and Mackenzie, who had seen it almost intact, at least in plan, and defined by Pinza as “the façade of the most beautiful giants' tomb known in Sardinia”, the giants' tomb at Imbertighe is now reduced to only the arched stele and the arms of the exedra composed of three rows of stones.

05e720eb7ce2d0e5.text: Lapidary circle. It could be a nuraghe left incomplete.

05e83484ab0d6271.text: The nuraghe is located at the end of a valley on a small rocky spur.

05f1d89f910dcd91.text: What remains of a dolmenic giants' tomb completely collapsed, mainly consisting of the vertical elements and the surrounding foundations.

05f3934f8432297a.text: Complex nuraghe composed of two simple towers added laterally and joined tangentially, oriented SSE and NNW. The SSE tower has its interior choked with collapse; on the south side there is a break in the wall outline. The second tower, oriented NNW, does not preserve its full perimeter, which is interrupted in several stretches by collapse probably caused by the dense vegetation there. Other building masses are present but not clearly definable because of collapse and vegetation.

05feab4866339001.text: It is one of many nuraghes in the Tertenia area and preserves the tholos intact.

060d73ed56cd7276.text: A few metres from the two tombs of Sa Perda and s'Altare lie the foundations of a circular hut (diam. 10.70 – thick. 0.50) whose size and structural type suggest a nuragic origin; unfortunately, only the base course remains.

060e1dce1b912005.text: Present on topographic maps but evidently destroyed in the past. The sheepfold visible in the photo is not a nuraghe.

062a90eefcb03308.text:
It is a burial with a rectangular corridor cut into the rock and equipped with a calcareous slab flooring.

The chamber walls are built with marl ashlar, originally bonded with mud mortar, arranged in horizontal courses, which on the upper part of the wall face show an oblique exposed surface. No trace of the semi-circular exedra remains.

062bfd198bf1fb0c.text: It dates to about 1500 BC; the collapse is dated to the 9th century BC, and it remained uninhabited until 100 BC when the Romans arrived. It consists of a central tower surrounded by five other towers and an outer wall (outer enclosure), with a further seven towers forming another defensive curtain wall enclosing several courtyards. A second outer curtain wall and a third with three more towers are also present. The total number of towers is twenty-one. The area exceeds 5000 m².

065b0bbd285842fe.text: It is in complete state of abandonment, enveloped by vegetation, with some parts buried but mostly collapsed, partly due to the actions of tomb-bearers. Nuraghe with at least two rooms or smaller towers attached to the main tower and an entrance certainly oriented to the South/East. It is mentioned as a nuraghe with a furnace. Visually connected to the nuraghes S'Omu 'e S'Orku, Monte Eghedda, and Brandanu.

06614473dc3ab248.text:
The necropolis consists of 18 domus de janas, cut into three superimposed horizontal levels starting from the base line of the ridge, for a maximum height of 3 m above the ground.

The finds recovered during the excavations have allowed the burials to be dated to a period ranging from the Late Neolithic (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro culture, 1800–1600 BC).

06a324c12a48b20f.text: During the Nuragic period the area was densely inhabited due to its highly strategic location: near the lake stand numerous nuraghes, including one known as Sa Pigalva.

06cc102901d056ac.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, diameter 11.20 m, with residual walling of 3.20 m in height, four courses. The masonry consists of polyhedral blocks, roughly shaped. Already at the time of the Taramelli the nuraghe had been destroyed, leaving only the base.

06d79757f5109603.text: The olive trees growing in the burial corridor are destroying what remains. Debris, leaf litter, and eolian sediments have covered the cavities. On the anterior side of this TdG, someone had built a sort of hut using part of the ashlar blocks from the exedra. Today, however, due to thorny bushes, the tomb is hardly accessible.

06de47d91947acec.text: Nuraghe in good condition. The interior is almost complete. The tholos is open because the closure ashlar is missing.

06e09c4c563c1afc.text: Large cave composed of a single chamber used from the early Middle Bronze Age, where materials belonging to the Bonannaro culture have been found.

06e9365b7ae94767.text: A short distance from the settlement of Gonnesa, in a channel within the shale walls, we find the Domus De Janas. The tomb is very simple, round in plan, consisting of a single burial chamber. Vegetation thrives around the site, suggesting that the channel may conceal other burials.

06f1c6adef737819.text: Domus de janas inside the settlement of Buddusò, excavated in a granite outcrop with a cross-shaped plan.

0711a552a181ceae.text: The nuraghe remains for about 3 metres on the north side and has a diameter of about 10 metres. Constructed from medium-sized trachyte blocks, it is partly enveloped by vegetation. Dispersal of medium-sized Roman materials on the northeast side of the site.

071618fcf9ed6c07.text: The Nuraghe Piscu, located within the municipal archaeological park since 1982, lies along the SS 128 towards Mandas. Piscu is the most representative monument of the Nuragic civilization of the Trexenta region.

07466f961edf2433.text: At the base of the nuraghe, beneath a rocky outcrop, there is a cave used as a water reservoir. The entrance to the cave has been narrowed by the construction of masonry structures made by stacking trachyte stones of various shapes and sizes, thus increasing the water-holding capacity of the reservoir. The interior is full of stones and mud.

07475599e06b992e.text: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried, for which it is not possible to define the structure.

075b5f9436d8c5c4.text: Collapsed single-tower nuraghe. Some people mistakenly call the nearby Molafà nuraghe "Piandanna".

075bb741efa64013.text: The near-total absence of building stones has left just enough to understand the nuraghe's ground plan. There is practically an X-ray of the layout: it is as if someone had razed it to the ground, for a massive entrance with its lintel still in situ is detectable, and another, megalithic lintel lying on the ground. The basal circle is composed of ordered stones with a corridor and orthogonal cells. Formidable for specialist study.

0760512fd139a736.text: The megalithic wall is of pre-Nuragic date. It has a covered entrance with a flat lintel on the southern side. It ends at the bend of the stream towards the west and, following an arcuate path, reaches the proto-nuraghe of the same name on the northern side.

0760f97bb47fdc52.text: Nuraghe partially collapsed with intact tholos

076275318240b8c8.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, adjacent to a nearby road that may have caused its damage, is covered by vegetation, but the corridor and the stone wall structure—composed of sub-squared granite ashlar in courses—can still be observed.

07b19a36cc3335ce.text: Submerged Nuragic village noted by Pierluigi Montalbano in public conferences

07c1d8569543696a.text: Domus de janas with a sacred well placed at the entrance to the park on the south side

07e5f7bb74e92144.text:
The underground chamber is located about 750 metres to the south-east of the Nuraghe s'Infurcadu, while about fifty metres to the north-east two menhirs and traces of ancient habitation are found—though these have been erased by uncontrolled land-clearing works.

The domus, excavated in a basaltic rock outcrop, consists of a short pavilion leading into a cell with a niche.

07ff3fc77d206c78.text:
Il Corvos, apparently a single-tower nuraghe, is in fact a complex nuraghe whose central two-coloured tower still survives in excellent condition, with the first level in limestone and the second in trachyte.

Once through the entrance threshold, the unusual anticlockwise staircase is immediately noticeable, starting on the left side of the corridor; the chamber, which has three niches and is largely buried, preserves its intact tholos, about 5 metres high. The upper floor, however, has collapsed.

0807994981b2dd9f.text: The cemetery consists of three domus de janas, among which the tomb I stands out for its size and decorations.

08115f711fb6013e.text: Megalithic circle located on Monte Ladu. It is situated near a small allée couverte.

08305cf0388399da.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, built with large calcareous blocks shaped and preserved for 6 or 7 courses (height 3.50 m). It has an entrance on the east and a long passage, with two chambers opening to the left and right within the wall.

08347f327fdd64c5.text: The site is difficult to identify due to the Mediterranean scrub. Along the roadside there is a significant scatter of betili, probably dating to the Roman period. Around the nuraghe there are traces of collapses.

086d37a1474bc614.text:
It is a proto-nuraghe in a dominant position on the edge of Pranu e Muru, the basalt lava flow in the territory of Nurri, east of the Flumendosa river. From the red crown one commands the Santa Vittoria mountains as far as the Gennargentu and, below, the canyon in which the roughly 17 kilometres of the Medio Flumendosa lake have been formed.

The corridor nuraghe joins its austere bareness to the majesty of the landscape that can be admired from there in a full 360 degrees.

0892030b83bffc81.text:
It is a corridor nuraghe with a roughly quadrangular plan (18 m x 15 m) featuring a singular projecting wall section (length 7 m – width 3 m) at the south-west corner.

The wall face is composed of polygonal masonry with large, roughly shaped blocks.

The monument is reduced to a heap of stones, making it impossible to clearly define the internal spaces.

08ad114f8392c67a.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which is without a vault, has on its left a wide staircase about 1 metre in width.

08cf87675554882b.text: A natural cavity adapted into a domus de jana that has hosted games for generations of children from the village of Uri, currently abandoned due to changes in time. Access is from above via a "manoeuvre" that is quite dangerous, and it is situated at a height of about 6 to 7 metres above the ground.

08da93a8deb20899.text: The name derives from the toponym of Atarzu mountain. In the Chiaramontese dialect we call it de sa pedra atarzina, a name that aptly describes the mountain's abundance of such stones. Never has the name been more fitting, as several sites of flint working have been identified, where tools for daily use or for hunting—such as blades and arrowheads—were produced. Only a few large megaliths exist, hidden beneath a massive mass of mastic.

08e6f9420cec0bfa.text: On the slopes of Monte Santo three separate boulders hold ancient Neolithic tombs along an uphill path. Three erratic boulders in which the tombs were cut. In the first boulder encountered on the way to the summit, Su Crastu de Santu Eliseu, which gives the site its name, the domus de janas has been reused as a Christian place of worship. Next comes Su Crastu de Santu Elia and finally Su Crastu de Santu Enoch, which has a domus de janas with two fine bull's-head protomes.

0927a2fdfe6f1aca.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition, partly covered by vegetation. In the field, a scatter of Roman pottery.

094df33a93748ff2.text:

The nuraghe has yielded an extraordinary Nuragic altar. Three construction phases can be identified.

The first, perhaps of Middle Bronze Age I (16th–15th century BC), saw the laying out of a bastion and an outer wall with corridors and cells.

In the second, of Middle Bronze Age II (14th century BC), a sinusoidal trilobed bastion was superimposed, together with a new outer wall of four towers linked by irregularly straight curtain walls.

In the third phase the outer wall was provided with another tower and curtain walls.

Only a few features remain, as the site is covered by a soil fill and an unstructured heap of stones resulting from land reclamation, but due to historical and cultural degradation, its essence has been destroyed. mu

128d68f21c7d270e.text: The Nuraghe Codas is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, situated about 7 km south of Paulilatino. Together with the Nuraghi Forreddos, De Mesu and Su Guzzu it forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. Despite several collapses it has kept its majesty intact.

12a667dfd59cc79e.text: Domus de janas enriched with various bull's-head protomes carved in limestone

1301ff876f81b113.text: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain

130817fa9e3cf015.text: Single-tower with its top missing and a tholos partially collapsed, accessible from the inside

131193dc597df707.text: Nuragic village with remains of Roman-period dwellings, most of which were destroyed by the commune during the eucalyptus reforestation.

131dcbc721a74dc3.text:
Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. Several courses are visible and the entrance, facing south, can be observed with the monolithic lintel still in situ.

The interior of the chamber is filled with debris from the collapse of the structure. Blocks from the collapse are found around the raised remains, especially in the north, east and south directions.

13308d41469ec027.text: It is the only one in the entire territory inaccessible due to environmental incompatibility: the monument is presumed to have disappeared entirely. mu

1373d0b90cb65231.text:
The nuraghe is known by several names: Nido dei Passeri – l'Egua – Spiaggia Grande. It is a single-tower nuraghe in a mediocre state of preservation.

The nuraghe that stands on the cliff at the locality Nido dei Passeri is a single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte stone.

1387de6a3fbeb585.text:
This nuraghe has a trilobate plan, that is, it consists of three towers, a central one and two lateral ones that are half destroyed.

In the central tower we find the main chamber, a circular room in which the wall, narrowing as it rises, forms a true vault ending in an opening that was probably closed in the past by two smaller stones. Near the entrance, on the left-hand side, a spiral staircase with rough steps begins.

138bc494fb3d3809.text: Four-lobed nuraghe with a very complex structure. Central tower with at least four connected towers linked by a curtain wall that encloses a large courtyard.

13cf16c9142449c1.text: It consists of at least three tombs.

13d54441cb7ea593.text: Located at the top of the hill known as Montes. It commands a wide view of the landscape.

13da45e2688a857d.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber bordered by at least one niche, built in trachyte.

13fbc668bd7a31e6.text:
It preserves an intact tholos.

Single-tower basalt nuraghe about 10.80 m high; from the entrance, 1.60 m high, you enter the corridor and immediately on the left the stair with 13 steps.

13fee44c222c3688.text: Pre-Nuragic and Nuragic village, of which only very few traces remain, already disappeared by the end of the Bronze Age.

140884f3c8322e20.text: Archaeological site of Mont'e Prama, where statues, baetyls, and the linear necropolis of pozzetto tombs have been found.

141b02027bc3ee70.text: Single-tower nuraghe. Destroyed by a bulldozer to build a restaurant in the 1980s–85. A pot and a bronze dagger were found during the excavation. Built in the Recent Bronze Age (1300–1150 BC).

1424e5e0cd1bda6f.text: It includes remains of a nuraghe and a village, the entire structure "correctly" transformed into dry stone walls.

1438ab1cbf8ece0f.text:
The nuraghe is in very poor conservation conditions (only a maximum of two courses remain) and is completely covered by vegetation.

Around it there is a vast scatter of baetyls, laterites, and coppi.

144653848b72b120.text:
It is located within the municipal territory of Donori.

Prehistoric and historical emergencies, the archaeological area is partially damaged with overlapping cultural phases presumably attributable to the Nuragic, Punic, and Roman periods. A large number of cyclopean stones entirely made of grey granite indicate the presence of the village and the cemetery.

1449d252751882a2.text:
Proto-nuraghe, corridor type. The structure is built on a solid rocky foundation, controlling the southern bank of the Rio Cispiri. The nuraghe is constructed from polygonal basalt blocks locally sourced, with the base courses being notably large in size.

Visually connected to various nuraghes such as Zenna Uda, Muschiu, and Serra Crastula.

147654e5cbabbf9b.text: Complex nuraghe of the type with lateral addition. Built of local basalt. It has a partially collapsed and recently restored vault, in relation to the last use as a sheepfold.

14aa4ff88c34e7ee.text:
Traces of a nuraghe and a Nuragic village, with finds from the Roman period as well.

The monument stands on a granite crag overlooking a large wooded area, about 1220 metres north-east of the village of Lei. Around the Nuragic building, especially to the east, the remains of a village can be made out and the ground is scattered with pottery of various periods. A short distance away, traces of Roman buildings were found in 1867.

14c7ee5e56513192.text: A single-tower nuraghe with its top missing, built of limestone blocks, whose perimeter is broken on the south side by the collapse of the outer wall face. The interior of the chamber is not visible because it is hidden by vegetation and filled with earth and debris.

14ce2eef3059f187.text: Structures related to proto-nuraghe of the corridor type. The building is constructed from large polygonal basalt blocks of local origin. The plan is roughly quadrangular, though an accurate interpretation of the monument is not possible due to the complete vegetation cover.

14ebae0bd791f06f.text: A Nuragic temple in the territory of Nulvi, almost completely collapsed. At the apex a worked lintel remains that surmounted a doorway, reached by a spiral staircase inaccessible from the inside; the last steps and the covering slabs in a single block survive. From the remains the pediment appears to have been similar to that of giants' tombs. Around it are various remains of nuraghi, a village, and the enclosure wall that ran around the apex of the promontory.

14ec08367915c178.text: Linked to the Grotta di sa Ucca de su Tintirriolu. It opens into a tiny niche between stones, then into earth (difficult to identify), followed by a deep and dangerous well of 28 m. Exploration is NOT RECOMMENDED! even for expert speleologists, as the well does not open onto rock.

152e98f59bdd1bc6.text: A "antenna" bronze sword found at Ploaghe near the nuraghe "Attentu" (in 1874 the nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Giovanni Spano, native of Ploaghe, who carried out the first stratigraphic excavation in Sardinia there).

155c28e6bdb1ba9e.text: Nuraghe almost completely disappeared, named by Prof. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica”. At the base of the hill there is a large rock with artificial cavities.

155fec9a146e403b.text:
The archaeological complex of Piscina Caboni belongs to the Culture of the Circles of the Arzachena area, which, in earlier years, appeared to affect only the Gallurese region.

Site occupation, in the absence of excavation data, begins to be dated to the third millennium BCE.

15638b94ad0fd8fe.text: The monolith, finely worked basalt, stands on a flat terrain less than 100 m from a domus de janas known as "Su forru'e su Taleri".

1567acaee8476bb6.text: It is the second corridor nuraghe named Peppe Gallu in the Uri area, following Peppe Gallu of Cuga. The attached village, very extensive, has been destroyed by agricultural mechanization. It is a proto-nuraghe of corridor type. It features two elevated entrances, above the farm level, which could be accessed via wooden or rope ladders.

15796582236069c9.text:
Located 500 m from the village along the road to Sarule, the circular-plan nuraghe was probably of single-tower type.

Today only the base course, composed of squared trachyte blocks, is visible, and to the north, a portion of the second course.

1582054cbe6e5f37.text: The tower remains as a mound of earth on which the filars of the nuraghe emerge, probably part of a complex.

158d8620d8be85d7.text: A central tower rises up to four courses, over two metres in height, surrounded by a wall. The entire structure is connected to circular and straight walls that emerge from the ground but only at the upper edge of the last course of stones. Most of the complex nuraghe lies buried beneath the soil. To the north-east of the tower, at a distance of about 7–8 metres, there may be a "sacred" well.

15925617c6acf71d.text: Domus de janas with the particularity of a double door on two opposite sides, with the roof collapsed on the vault.

15963b1acd066da4.text: Less than 100 metres south of the nuraghe lies a small giants' tomb, of which only the funerary chamber remains, composed of large granite orthostats, together with traces of the external wall face and the peristalith.

159b50c8e110c642.text: "Nuraghe Su Nuragheddu, or de Sa Taula, or de Su Coddu 'e Su Nuraghe. It is located near the Rio di Posada, within a narrow gorge between cliffs, guarding a passage; it is ruined, but clear traces of the nuraghe remain. In terrain of Deiana Serafino".

15b2193e3b8ee4ee.text: Located near the municipal pine forest, four km north of the village, the nuraghe Jana is in poor state of conservation. The nuraghe, in addition to having collapsed internally, was previously used as a shelter for shepherds, so that most of its stones were arranged in a radial pattern as a boundary wall.

15d7eb3a586e447e.text: Domus de janas with superimpositions on the stele

15dd7172bdd0222a.text: The main nucleus of the archaeological complex of Pidighi is located within the municipal park of the same name; it consists of two nuraghes (Pidighi and Muru Accas) together with their respective settlements and their respective water supply sources...

15e0ace0e6025880.text: A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of small size, is identifiable only by the funerary corridor, while the other parts (still buried or destroyed) that composed it are not visible.

1656c492a5a6f0a9.text:
Complex nuraghe built of the local volcanic rock. Largely covered by vegetation and hidden by collapse, stretches of walling from the towers that made up the building can be made out. One part has been disturbed by illicit excavations.

At the foot of the hill, to the north, a hypogeum, perhaps an air-raid shelter.

It is likely that on the summit of the hill, in the private land enclosed by fences and inaccessible, traces of the protohistoric cluster of huts may survive.

165ffcb67754b2f7.text: Giants' tomb, dolmenic, completely exposed, with only a trapezoidal stele and part of the original exedra remaining

166d4d3777dddd7b.text: Nuraghe of the final phase of the Nuragic period, built on the cliff that dominates the valley of the San Pietro Paradiso waterfall, also known locally as "Cascata de s'ascedu".

168cb2285c1212d3.text: Giants' tomb, of which the base ashlar stones remain, one slab of the stele, and one from the abside.

16a831d9b0dadcb7.text: The tomb is almost buried under a substantial mound of earth and stones. The basal orthostats follow almost the entire perimeter: a semi-circular exedra (arc 10.40 m – chord 3.80 m) flattened on the south-east side with arms surviving for 6.66 m on the right and 4.45 m on the left; a rectangular body 10.60 m long and 4.20 m wide where it meets the exedra wings; a burial corridor (length 7.20 m – width 1.10 m) bounded by upright slabs.

16ac0b0107236255.text: The tomb, still buried, clearly shows the violations it suffered at the hands of looters. The chamber is rectangular, built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, laid dry with packing wedges. The entrance, facing ESE, has its doorway completely buried, topped by a lintel shaped like a rectangular block whose sides appear perfectly smoothed. The tomb was preceded by an exedra, of which some boulders remain in situ to the north of the tomb body.

16db2a0af53a8dc3.text: Giants' tomb of Deruta. Located just 50 m from another Giants' tomb in better condition, on which the municipality has carried out minor interventions for cleaning and improved accessibility.

16eea19268438a6c.text: Nuraghe with buried entrance. Access to the interior is possible through a passage leading to a staircase chamber. The chamber features three niches, with the tholos intact. In the area, several baetyls and cremation urns are also present.

16fb7e2399a28261.text: Only faint traces of two towers added tangentially remain.

170717e38444da92.text: Composed of 10 megaliths in the form of parallelepipedons, placed one next to the other (one eleventh is found at the centre), forming, thus arranged, a semicircle of about 10 metres. Some ceramic fragments found at the site are attributable to the Monte Claro culture, therefore the Neolithic period.

1727440595a86384.text:
The Sas Arzolas de Goi necropolis dates to the Ozieri Culture period (3200–2800 BC).

Five domus de janas have been identified so far; they lie on the slope of a trachyte hill that has been extensively affected by quarrying.

Tomb 1 is particularly interesting because it displays two complete bull's-head protomes, with ears and head, carved above the entrance hatch and on the pillar inside the burial chamber. The horns at the entrance are carved in convex relief.

173cd08f5426e4de.text:
The underground chambers at the site are two: the first tomb is the more interesting one, as it features a series of incisions above the access door; the second is located a little further on, near the edge of the road, and has its internal space almost completely flooded.

Both burials are of the pothole type and date back to about 3000 BC.

1744f42a69491cea.text: The archaeological site stands a few dozen metres from the Christian-medieval one, set among centuries-old olive trees. It is divided into two areas: in the first you will find a sacred well temple, dating to the Final Bronze Age (12th century BC), embraced by a sacred enclosure (themenos) shaped like a keyhole. Built of finely worked basalt ashlars with precise techniques, the temple is a jewel of perfect geometric forms.

178d45ac31aaa436.text: Group of domus de janas immediately beneath the road embankment. It is suspected that other domus de janas may lie beneath or have been destroyed by the works for road construction.

179685665d4843c5.text: During construction a spring was found beneath the site, which keeps the domus full of water even in times of drought. For this reason it became a temple dedicated to fertility, so much so that the female reproductive organ was carved into the rock around the entrance of the domus and, above it, the male reproductive organ. These are joined by a small channel cut in the rock, signifying fertilisation.

17b4c09023bd3817.text: From the aerial photograph it appears to be a complex nuraghe with a village.

181db1e077030ae0.text:
Also known as Su Lotto. In ruins, a few boulders of the primary circle remain that define the base.

Nuraghe della Sorgente della Pietra. The name probably derives from the fact that the site, used for centuries as a quarry, so that the nuraghe has now almost completely disappeared, is characterised by the presence of surface springs.

182050e17514ed77.text: The imposing single-tower nuraghe Sa Fraigada stands a few dozen metres from the summit of Monte Cresia and is the largest in the area. The ancient Nuragic building has suffered major collapses, making its ground plan hard to understand; the lintelled entrance, presumably on the east side, is not visible. The circular tower is about 8 metres in diameter and can still be seen to a surviving height of 3.70 metres on its south-western side.

18280f73747d52cf.text: The nuraghe is located within the territory of Villaputzu; it appears as a subcircular structure, with only a few elements visible due to demolitions carried out to extract ashlar stones for use in the construction of the adjacent church. On the northern side is attached a semicircular structure.

1859d46b049d82fe.text: Likely location. Today only the megalithic basal structures of the nuraghe remain, although it is possible that much of the stones above have been broken up and incorporated into the walls of Villa La Favorita.

185db7d77cd3c013.text: Remains on a rocky outcrop from which the valley below is visible.

186e88c9cd794522.text: It is located within the municipality of Nuoro. It is not the only Nuragic site in the city, but it is the only one that has been systematically excavated. Around the nuraghe, remains of a village dating to about 1600 BC (early phase of the Nuragic period) are visible, originally composed of more than 200 huts. Historical records nevertheless indicate the presence, along the hillside, of some domus de janas.

187f8e3d6991adaf.text: Megalithic astronomical clock, built in the early Nuragic period, before the 15th–18th century BC. It is circular and built of large boulders with open spaces to let sunlight pass onto a central boulder covered with white pebbles that favoured the reflection of the sun's rays at different times — equinoxes, solstices — and in the lunar phases it reflected moonlight in specific directions.

188b3c68aebe7d2b.text: Locally also known by the place name of the land "serra porcheddos". It would appear to be a single-tower nuraghe, even though the whole surrounding area shows a high probability of survey evidence. — Tripod Nuraghe. For other nuraghi whose names refer to objects of use or connected with worship, compare Nuraghe Trìbides, Cogàlzos, Manos d'òro.mu

1896c13293c257e9.text: Nuraghe Maistu Peldu (commonly called De Su Par e Pelda) still has two small towers standing, each 2 metres high. The collapsed vault reveals the interior of the tholos, about 1 m deep. The ashlars, which are fairly large, suggest that the site may be a watchtower nuraghe controlling the entrance to the Chia valley. In front of it stands a menhir, the "praying menhir", De Su Par 'e Pelda, visible from provincial road 72.

189877885177222d.text: A single-tower nuraghe built on a spur of granite rock, following its contours and in places incorporating it. The interior of the nuraghe is filled with backfill earth and large blocks that belonged to the masonry. The nuraghe stands in a commanding position on the coast with a broad view over Tavolara and Capo Ceraso. It is a watchtower of which five courses of stone survive on the outside and about two metres of masonry inside.

189af447aee1de03.text: Cave used during the early phases of the Nuragic civilization, known for the discovery of three, older, "Mother Goddess" bone statuettes.

18a1514d22f4e619.text:
The nuraghe stands on the summit of a high watershed whose north and east slopes are very steep, while to the west, a few metres from the nuraghe, the hill ends in a high cliff.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, 10.30 m in diameter. Very little of the nuraghe survives because of the substantial collapses it has suffered over the centuries.

Further reading:

Bibliography: E.E.M. 1922, p. 104; MERELLA 1996-97, vol. V, pp. 770-773, fig. 37, pl. XXIII.

18ae647dad975c9f.text: It is buried in a cucuzzolo, a sardo cucuru. The upper part, certainly the top of the main tower, is accessible. We observe concentric courses of large stones. At the summit, small openings are visible; if dug, they would lead into the structure.

18c1ff4ccd6e451e.text: Typical domus de janas with a façade featuring a carved arched stele on the calcare wall.

18c82d393866d2c9.text:
Remains of a nuraghe and traces of a Nuragic village.

Built on a granitic rise, this nuraghe is not currently discernible among the remains of an extensive village that persisted into the Roman and late medieval periods, as evidenced by fragments of pottery, bricks, and jars.

18efb1b53c2c0729.text: On the remains of the nuraghe Crixionis, during the Second World War, a concrete fortification was built, protected against small arms fire, serving as an observatory for the Coastal Battery positions in the area.

190942347351f410.text: Probable dismantled nuraghe located to the north-east; nearby there is a megalithic wall.

190ba7503fefe9bd.text: A massive single-tower nuraghe, of imposing diameter, built with large, roughly worked granite blocks. The entrance faces south and is three-quarters covered. The tholos is almost intact. Inside there are as many as three niches, cut into the wall thickness. Moreover, a spiral staircase starts from the wall to the left of the entrance corridor and certainly led to the upper floor, but is unfortunately blocked by collapse; opposite the stairwell there is a further niche.

19115f523fe78db8.text: On the north-eastern tip, some alignments of small stones suggest the remains of a nuraghe tower; on the south-eastern tip, a short curved wall segment is present, and in the depression to the north, a closure wall runs between the two tips.

193426b6f3fa9108.text: A sanctuary area consisting of several rooms surrounded by an irregularly elliptical enclosure. One of these buildings has a perfectly circular plan with a floor paved with limestone slabs fitted together with absolute precision. The accuracy of the construction and the existence of an original design plan are shown by the traces of the circular layout mark of the first course on the floor, drawn with a kind of compass.

194a3d243291fe0f.text: The nuraghe Mereu or 'Intro de Padente', entirely built of white limestone with well-cut stones of medium size, is situated on a height that dominates the surrounding area. The nuraghe is of complex type, consisting of a main tower and two additional towers, further protected by straight bastions.

194d67ac48c98e6c.text: Nuraghe partially collapsed with an open tholos

1965b599887e4d98.text: A careful survey has not revealed any trace of the Lavrone nuraghe, although some old people claimed it must have existed. The site was certainly anthropogenically modified due to the presence of some human artefacts. A curious anecdote is that Giacomino, who is no longer alive, had built more than "a nuraghe", meaning by the piles of stones gathered in the field. "Nuraghe of the large laurel".

199cda66bfdefda6.text: Nuraghe reported whose category cannot be defined

19a3f0a5ed526e0f.text: Four domus de janas, adjacent to one another, dug into the arenaria. The first one contains a single chamber, while the others contain multiple chambers. The first domu is not connected to the others, whereas the latter are interconnected.

19a5759802ccc927.text: Probable proto-nuraghe with only 4 very irregular courses remaining

19c27b7195fce363.text: Small menhir placed along the road facing the junction to Rocca Doria

19c4e66d692cc1c7.text:
The complex consists of a nuraghe with a settlement, a giants' tomb, and a well.

The nuraghe, built on a rocky outcrop, belongs to the type of complex structures: it is indeed composed of a central tower to which three secondary towers have been attached on the front and lateral sides.

19cdb225b68d6b37.text: Cave currently blocked by a collapse that prevents access. Inside, some ceramic fragments have been recovered, assignable to the culture of Bonu Ighinu.

19dbfd8bf73de758.text: Single-tower built of large white limestone blocks, situated in a cleared area within an olive grove, with a direct drop to the Orune Channel to the north-northeast. Only three courses remain, with a maximum height of about 3 m.

19ee5af3eb52b9c4.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built with large polygonal blocks of local basalt. It retains about 4 to 5 courses, and the internal chamber has collapsed upon itself, being filled with collapse debris. The diameter is about 12 m. The entrance is oriented to the south-east, although it is obscured by the structures of a more recent hut attached to it.

19f0486bd21739e2.text:
The accessible area consists of numerous rooms adorned with concretions, stalactites, and stalagmites (the highest measuring 11 metres), columns rising up to 15 m, crystals of aragonite, and underground lakes.

Inside, remains of some oil lamps used in votive offerings, of Nuragic origin, as well as Phoenician and Roman artifacts, have been found.

1a182ce9b31b0d48.text: The nuraghe Ola is a single-tower nuraghe about 12 m in external diameter and 10 m high, dating to the Recent Bronze Age. What is particularly striking is the use of different building materials: on the outside the base consists of 12 courses of granite blocks, while above them sit 13 courses of trachyte.

1a3d4c8101454dae.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument has recently been uncovered after the vegetation that had covered it was cut away. In addition to the corridor, composed of stone courses, the lower partition of a large stele remains.

1a5d5732c79156b6.text: According to the map shown in the publication "L'Altare preistorico di Monte d'Accoddi" by Ercole Contu, the correct name of the nuraghe should be "Camusina", a name also recorded in the IGM as "Camuscina". It is in very poor condition and completely surrounded by dense vegetation.

1a7003dce6225389.text: Series of natural caves used in the Neolithic for collective burials. Remains of the Monte Claro culture.

1a73323809d16c07.text: Completely dismantled. Probably partly still present beneath the vegetation, which shows stones placed without order.

1a7ce61396ce08f8.text: It is an artificial cave cut into tufa and modified over the centuries, very likely by a domus used as a winemaking building or as a storage for agricultural products or as a tool shed. There are many indications pointing to such a use. mu

1a9d186422cc9b31.text:
Although reduced to a level of great ruin, it is still possible to discern the significance of this emergence, which should be classified within the group of nuraghes with a subfloor chamber, still partially accessible.

Literally "nuraghe of the cows' urine". See Pìsciu 'àccas.

See MAURO MAXIA, I nomi di luogo dell'Anglona e della Bassa valle del Coghinas, ed. Il Torchietto, Ozieri 1994, pp. 73-74 for the entry "Anglona".

1ab05918631277c8.text: Single-tower nuraghe with access to the collapsed tholos.

1abb2d8959283740.text: The interpretation of these buildings suggests that during festivals the Nuragic (and not only) would trade various goods, taking advantage of the large influx of people. In addition to the "stalls" there are two circular huts used for gatherings and a sheepfold enclosure.

1adefc98184c9bfa.text: Six domus de janas in the locality of Sas Concheddas de Pianu Edras, carved into a cliff face composed of trachytic tuff, are located within the Prehistoric Subterranean Necropolis of Pianu Edras, among which the Domus delle Cappelle stands out.

1af8fb46c3364bef.text: The nuraghe is named after the location situated on the south-eastern slopes of the Giara di Gesturi. It is mentioned by Taramelli in his study of the prehistoric monuments of the Giara; however, the census conducted in the 1980s did not record any trace of it.

1b06e27d1ccc01bf.text: The complex system of structures comprising water sources and water-collecting features, with ingenious channels, and a rectangular building in isodomic masonry.

1b0871d1fe0bfca0.text: It is the largest and most important cave of Bonu Ighinu. It has recently been connected with the overlying Grotta del Pozzaccio. Morphologically the cavity can be divided into two main parts: the fossil branch, which is the initial one, and the active branch, crossed along its entire length by a stream; the large hall in the innermost part is also fossil. Overall the cave is 740 m long and its spatial development is 1500 m.

1b2b53f96f5f4554.text: Near the village of San Salvatore, within a private property, the nuraghe is in very poor condition, but the remains of a significant Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.

1b2f99fd4882b019.text: One of the nuraghes located within the territory of the comune of Villa Sant'Antonio is the 'Genna sa Pira' nuraghe, fully encompassed within the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC), although its construction has seen numerous later additions over the centuries.

1b611ff15d0b31fc.text:
Nuraghes that have disappeared completely or almost so, among them is this one, and it is located near Morimenta, not far from the Santu Sciori nuraghe of Pabillonis.

In other records it is mentioned as the remains of a small chapel, but there is little evidence of a church.

1b9ce89bd8ab176e.text: Quadrilobate nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and three additional smaller towers. The diameter is about 11 metres. The central tower is composed of large stones, while the front addition is made of smaller stones.

1bc2e0965747f77d.text:
On the hill of San Giovanni a Punic fortified complex has been identified on the remains of a pre-existing Nuragic village.

Opposite are the Domus de Janas of Burdaga.

In Giuseppa Tanda's recent publication it is stated that, among the various types of Domus de Janas, there is one characterised by the fact that the necropolis is carved into pre-existing rock shelters, perhaps enlarged by artificial excavation, almost as if the overhang could provide shelter for the sacred remains of the dead.

1be4ec75757a1d61.text: The nuraghe is completely hidden by the earth and vegetation, which give it the appearance of a humble hillock (in Sardinian "cuccuru") several metres high rising above the waters of the State salines; the material conceals the millennial structure.

1c366008c7eda9e9.text:
It is a medium-sized single-tower nuraghe. The building style is the one typical of the sites in the area.

It stands on a small rise a short distance from the Pardu river and commanded a good view over the lower part of the valley formed by the same river.

The site is not in very good condition. The entrance side is intact, but the interior has almost completely collapsed. Only the corridor and the internal staircase can be made out. The vegetation is dense, making the site difficult to visit.

The necropolis consists of four multi-chambered domus de janas, cut into a tuff hillock and characterised by the presence of long entrance dromoi.

It was used from the 3rd millennium BC until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC;

2487810d71df2a9c.text: Single-cell domus de janas located near Riu fruscu

248d1f1eb313a900.text: The nuraghe and adjacent village are situated behind the hill that hosts the Nuragic sanctuary of Santa Vittoria di Serri.

248dc61e2bd8c4c2.text: Situated at 140 m above sea level, a Nuragic complex partially damaged by the construction of the Ussana–Donori provincial road. Barrali. The ground plans of the structures belonging to the Nuragic complex were to be brought to light in order to define their structural characteristics and assign a precise chronological date; although the owners granted permission, the excavation campaign was not carried out.

248eac800a0add05.text: Remains of the megalithic construction were revealed during a survey at the nearby Perdu Lodde nuraghe by a local shepherd.

2494ee1ef8eced3b.text: Nuragic hut with the remaining ground-level circular enclosure. Located at the edge of the plateau above the hill, Monte Crastu, it dominated the area of the probable village of Badde Cannalza.

2499c3e9ae452ae3.text: Dolmen with a lapidary slab on megalithic walls

249c013a6dd47b8c.text: Bitorre nuraghe, collapsed and inaccessible, faces north and dominates the entire northern coast from Stintino to Isola Rossa.

249fb1e41dc75f3d.text: It is one of many nuraghes scattered across the Torralba area; this one is located near the railway line connecting Mores to the Torralba station. It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower with a frontal addition of two further secondary towers, connected by a robust curtain wall. It dates to the period between Middle Bronze and Late Bronze (1600–1000 BC).

24a645214bde9b19.text:
The Nuraghe Murruzzone or Thiortorro is difficult to spot because it is surrounded by brambles, but it is located almost at the valley floor near some springs. A surviving wall measures about 4 m, and inside there is a circular niche whose entrance faces east, accessible from within and measuring about 2 m.

It is most likely that part of it still lies buried.

24cbd0cec5c9e77c.text: Built of calcareous and marly blocks, the nuraghe features a quadrilobate plan with a central tower and four external towers aligned with the cardinal points... surrounded by an outer curtain wall, and the remains of four additional towers. Inside the complex there is a sacred well.

24d7c8fb523cf0b4.text:
It is in very poor condition.

Probable location.

24f120d6f0394afa.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Some courses are visible. In the area, large clumps of clay are present, along with other wall structures suggesting the existence of a residential zone inhabited by huts.

25150e9d3687abc8.text:
Important giants' tomb near Sant'Antonio di Santadi.

It appears to be in good condition.

I do not know its name, but it is certainly of great historical significance. Discovered by cross-referencing data from several maps.

2517546202e187a1.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers, connected by straight walls, with a courtyard in the centre acting as an integration space. Nearby, the remains of a Bronze Age stone quarry can be observed.

2517f09500153dfb.text: Single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by Indian fig trees and vegetation. It retains the fine entrance portal with a cracked lintel and dangerous condition, the tholos and the staircase leading to the upper level.

252aca0711584de7.text: The monument, located near the Borore cemetery and a short distance from the Nuraghe Pischedda, is reduced to a few courses of the elevation, which nevertheless allow it to be identified as a complex nuraghe of the “a tancato” type, consisting of the central tower to the north-west, joined to a smaller opposing tower to the south-east by two straight wall wings that enclose a trapezoidal space; the whole is bounded by an outer wall. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

252db24617366b24.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe; in the surrounding area the traces of a quarry and a settlement can be seen.

253f7dda11006ad1.text:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Marrubiu (OR).

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe with an elliptical plan, accompanied by a large settlement of circular huts.

2540396e6e335f3e.text: The cave is about 130 metres long and is mainly composed of three "rooms". Important archaeological finds have been made inside, especially some human remains dated to about 20,000 years ago, which represent the earliest evidence of Homo sapiens in Sardinia. This cave was the refuge of the famous Sardinian bandit Giovanni Corbeddu, after whom it is named.

25686d0ae3c755a6.text: Area around which, besides the dolmen Su Crastu Covaccadu, there is also the giants' tomb Sa Pedra Coveccada, of which only the arched stele remains, broken at the base.

2598f934b6145747.text: While still a student, Giovanni Lilliu reported the presence of twenty circular and elliptical huts, some of which were later excavated, yielding ceramic materials of various kinds such as large jars, bowls, copper beads, and a bronze figurine depicting two oxen found during agricultural work. Despite the destruction, the emerging remains of some walls, large fragments of furnishings, and large fragments of basalt querns are still on the ground.

259b00e8cb14e998.text: Of the Olai nuraghe in this pile of stones, currently only the foundation is visible.

259e1180def35830.text: Of the corridor nuraghe, possibly with a sub-elliptical plan, only some fragments of granite walling from the first course of the base remain.

25a8ba726df17693.text: The cemetery of Coroneddu (Bosa – OR) consists of three underground chambers, two adjacent and one more separated. It is situated on a rocky cliff on the southern slope of a calcareous hill that extends into the Modolo valley. Probable location

25c83b32612c8a67.text: It is an interesting Nuragic structure featuring the corner junction between the perimeter walls. Experts describe it as a megaron Greek type.

25f1bd3df7758cf8.text: The domus de janas was cut into a rock outcrop situated halfway up the hill known as Serra Nuarxis. The tomb has a Greek-cross plan and consists of a rectangular vestibule, a quadrangular doorway leading to the actual chamber, and the chamber itself. The chamber, semi-circular in plan, contains three niches, slightly raised above the floor level, oriented to the south-west, north-west and south-east. The niches have arched walls and rectangular bases.

25f786cd919c5da1.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers connected by bastions that enclose a courtyard.

25fc3ba5c1ff99c4.text:
The nuraghe Paddaggiu, "pagliaio", lies less than one kilometre from "dall'elefante".

It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe but is in fact a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and a bastion with two lateral towers that are barely legible. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is the presence of a chamber set above the entrance corridor, originally reached by a staircase inside the right-hand niche of the main chamber. The tholos and the staircase leading to the upper floor survive intact.

260516b3e7e18d52.text: Piles of ashlar characteristic of an ancient settlement abandoned and covered by dense forest vegetation, and various fragments of walls, most of which are circular: on the southern side there is a wall about 5 metres long, almost straight, and a smaller circular wall lower down, while on the western side of the settlement there is a circular wall made of large blocks of 2 to 3 courses, suggesting a Nuragic origin.

26387c63c18f3852.text:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.

2659310d391d0370.text: Small nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins.

26c6fa6ed7924510.text: Currently, nuragic huts remain with very little, only heaps of stone in circular and square shapes, probably the result of clearing works.

26eea7bcc5fa288b.text: It faces the road from Alghero to Uri; the tomb is very ruined but still retains within it the typical elements of the false door and the overhanging parts, possibly bull's-head protomes.

27038db9f7a4b601.text: It is elliptical, extends for about 30 metres in length, has a diameter of about 22 metres, and survives to a height of about 4 metres. In the north-west section of the curtain wall, an entrance connected to an internal corridor can be observed; this corridor served as a passage between the two main towers and originally had a roof composed of powerful slabs laid flat.

2763b907711be301.text:
It consists of an apsidal corridor set on an exedra with a narrow bench. In the centre is a small lintelled doorway with jambs and a threshold. The roof is a pointed vault.

Excavations have uncovered the remains of numerous human skeletons, deposited one on top of another, evidence of its use as a collective burial, whose size is also the origin of the name. Tradition holds that these burials must have belonged to gigantic beings.

278f11302b473912.text: Single-tower nuraghe, built of local basalt blocks. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of about 4 m. The entrance is identifiable to the south-east, from the remains of the entrance passage, with the stairwell opening on the left and a niche on the right, leading to the inner chamber. The latter survives to about half its original height and has a large internal niche facing south.

27b9df3b3b3e6818.text: The Ozzilo nuraghe is located in the territory of Aidomaggiore; it is a corridor-type nuraghe, accessed from the top, as it is heavily cluttered with debris due to a collapse. The interior chamber is occupied by the debris of the collapse, which affected part of the "naviform" vault. Nearby are two giants' tombs, one of which is partially destroyed.

27f70c0c2ece79af.text:
An interesting monument in the territory of Villanova Monteleone, oriented south-west; part of the exedra is still visible, but unfortunately no trace of the stele remains. The well-preserved corridor, built of well-squared trachyte blocks, is 7.10 m long and 2.80 m wide; two slabs laid flat still survive of the roofing.

To the left of the monument a setting of stones covered by a slab can be seen, perhaps a dolmen.

280fae6b5ea13ec9.text: It is a Nuragic village on Monte Tiscali inside a doline, destroyed by the Romans and by tomb robbers; the bases of the huts can be seen, and of one a part of the walling still stands. It is very difficult to reach — 45 minutes' walk — because you have to climb a steep mule track strewn with stones and pass through a fissure in the rock if you come from Oliena; in compensation you will enjoy a view over the limestone mountains of the Supramonte.

281652cf92bcd8b8.text:
Partially incorporated into a dry-stone wall, it still preserves only three orthostats in situ (0.35 x 0.22 thick – h. 0.50; 0.80 x 0.30 thick – h. 0.50; 0.60 x 0.15 thick – h. 0.50) and the capstone (1.70 x 1.52 x 0.52/0.40 thick); another orthostat can be made out beneath the wall.

Numerous slabs scattered around the burial on Sunday indicate the existence of a peristalith of which no other trace now remains.

281715da0da7b322.text: The tower, almost completely destroyed, can be easily accessed from the inside, where there are three niches; the most intact part of the tower is about 4 metres high. Accessible from the road, it is located about 300 metres away. Around the nuraghe there is a magnificent garden of Indian fig trees.

2821f0e96d34da7c.text: Very little information is available about the Serra Su Parone nuraghe, as the nuraghe has been almost entirely dismantled. Possibly a single-tower nuraghe, only faint traces remain, with the tower's curtain wall preserved in fragmented sections, consisting of two courses of trachyte stones. The state of conservation is very poor.

2822972d1f0e9ddc.text: Damaged nuraghe, overshadowed by a firebreak post with only a few visible remains. Excellent panorama stretching from the Seruci nuraghe to the large beach Porto Paglia/Punta S'Arena/Plag'e Mesu/Fontanamare to the Pan di Zucchero.

2837ef5d2855c263.text: Nuraghe no longer existing. The nuraghe is mentioned in documents, in Spanish, by the Bishop's Chapter (12 October 1720), as a reference point, under the name "Nuraxy de Condiazzus/Candiazus". It is also found referenced by Angius as "Nuargi de Candiazzus" (1840), in the IGM maps (1897), by Taramelli (1910?), and by my native Pinuccio Orlando, "Nuarxi de su candiacciu" (Toponyms of the Island).

284075d8613e335e.text: The nuragic well/spring was built at the edge of a rocky outcrop using trachyte ashlar; it has an ovoid shape and extends to a depth of approximately 2.50 m. The northern wall continues from ground level up to a height of about 2 m, with the same width. In recent times, a livestock water trough has been constructed nearby.

2861bfe9edfbe77f.text: The nuraghe is located in the territory of Riola Sardo, adjacent to the marsh; the nuraghe was not recorded and appears even less in the maps.

28644f6a7c8fa6e8.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

The monument is in very poor condition of conservation and it is not possible to define its constructive type. On the ground a line of stones (probably belonging to the exedra) is visible, while the final section of the corridor is barely discernible, buried under a thicket of brambles.

2895f228802d9dc2.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Of considerable size, it retains a height of about 5.40 m. Built with polygonal basalt blocks of local origin, it is well preserved in its western portion, while in the eastern part it is partially collapsed and covered by vegetation. The entrance can be identified on the eastern side, though it has collapsed and is reduced to a simple opening.

28bf27f57e2a5d62.text:
It is a coursed Nuragic construction that rests on the rugged profile of the hill, which dictates its irregular plan. At the top a small chamber filled with collapse is visible; no entrances or other structural elements can be seen.

It should be noted that building on this rocky spur, where movement is extremely difficult and dangerous, is hard to understand: it looks more like a lookout post than a defensive structure.

28c4595d6989e06f.text: Nuragic village where 32 dwellings were found, excavated deeply into the ground, a nuraghe, a silver mine, and pre-Nuragic artifacts. The site was covered with concrete in the 1980s to create a reservoir for irrigation, which has never functioned.

29461d807716c006.text: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including a pair known locally as Is ogus de monti, "the eyes of the mountain". A majestic staircase of about sixty steps cut entirely into the rock leads to the summit, from which there is a broad view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating to the 7th century BC, with an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.

29462dc8d53b38bb.text: A shelter characterized by various rooms, one of which was inhabited from the Early Neolithic, later used for funerary purposes. The artifacts found can be attributed to the Cardial culture.

29688efbf6b92c37.text: It is located within a military zone, access to which is forbidden to the public.

29870d4978ff4e56.text:
It is a circular single-tower nuraghe (diam. 13 x 13.50 m) with a corridor niche and a provisional chamber of two niches; the existence of a staircase is probable but not certain.

The tower survives to a maximum height of 5.54 m and is built of medium-sized blocks, roughly dressed and laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

A corridor 4.25 m long leads into the circular tholos chamber (diam. 4.20 x 4 m), now reduced to a maximum height of just 3.10 m with 7 courses.

2989d004b880a992.text: The walls are composed of rubble masonry of varying and medium-sized stones, roughly shaped, with cyclopean stones cut and embedded in the ground closing one end. The coverings are megalithic, some of which remain in situ while others have been removed due to land improvement works.

299998810d52fe0f.text: At a point on elevated ground relative to a natural depression, a circle of stones is visible, which could be the base of a partially buried nuraghe.

29afe399cf8cba98.text: Nuraghe consisting of a primitive central tower and several towers. The interior of the central tower is filled with earth and fallen boulders. On the east side a lintelled corridor is visible, interrupted by collapse after a few metres. A short distance from the central tower there is a curvilinear wall that probably enclosed a peripheral tower. To the NNW, adjoining the nuraghe, an oval chamber is visible. Numerous pottery fragments of various periods lie on the surface in the area.

29ba1aa9c9fe745b.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers connected by bastions and featuring a courtyard. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

29c19ade7c2a9223.text: The site is located in the area of Boe and is completely destroyed; only some courses of the foundation remain visible.

29c1e6e5f280f7cc.text: Sacred well temple, one of the most refined in Nuragic Sardinia, follows the layout with a vestibule leading into a stairway that connects to the well chamber. The building is constructed of perfectly worked limestone ashlars laid in regular courses. The vestibule, rectangular (width 2.70 m; depth 1.88 m), with a perfectly paved floor, has two bench-seats along the walls, each formed from two worked blocks.

29ce18b1938e4e99.text: Or at least what remains. During the reconstruction of the Sibiri road, the structure was partially destroyed to allow a more direct route.
