In practice, the curves of the original alignment were removed and the tomb was destroyed. Today, only a section of about two metres remains. In short, a victim of "progress".

29d55015ea86006a.text: The nuraghe, located in a pastureland area, is completely covered by vegetation. Due to the conditions in which the nuraghe lies, we have been unable to identify its type, and the possible presence of an entrance or lintel.

2a003accff479ad0.text: The site is named after the fact that there once stood a nuraghe, of which no trace remains. It was demolished around 1960, during the construction of the present-day road Castelsardo–Santa Teresa Gallura (SP90); the stone material was reused for this work.

2a69ef6b5cc3d80c.text: At the site of Sa Brèca two buildings are currently clearly discernible: the Temple with Well and a sub-circular hut with seating along the walls. The entire complex appears to be enclosed by a temenos that would have separated the Sacred Area from the adjacent inhabited zone (not yet subjected to excavation).

2a8b94eff43b625e.text:
Proto-nuraghe of sub-circular shape (D. Carta 2010)

The single-tower nuraghe dates to the Middle Nuragic period. The building is unusual; its chamber is partly cut into the rock.

Investigations by G. Ugas led to the identification in 1981 of a Punic settlement at Is Argiddas, on the border with the municipality of Sanluri.

The Punic centre, of which stretches of walling in small stones bonded with mud have been identified, overlies a prehistoric and protohistoric settlement.

2a8e3f93acb1456c.text: A burial chamber of about 11 m in length remains. The tomb is missing its top. The exedra and the abside are still visible.

2a91217903f49cd4.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The entrance is completely blocked by collapse debris; the inner chamber is visible from the top of its summit. It stands on a hill covered with wild olives near the springs of S'ena Ruia.

2ac062285fc4bce4.text:
Seen from a short distance it looks like a rubble hill that hardly suggests a prehistoric monument. We are facing a colossus that offers several readings and which I personally classify among the infrapiano type.

Nuraghe del (terreno) chiuso del re. The presence of the term re almost certainly indicates that in the giudicale period the site belonged to the personal or family estate of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro. See Tanca de su re. mu

2ada4441f4526532.text: Nuraghe with staircase in good state of conservation.

2b0c7e78aa481d32.text: Nuraghe in basalt blocks. Unfortunately, the high residual volume is not properly exploited and the site is neither legible nor accessible, also due to dense vegetation.

2b1adf0d9ae7b3c5.text: The main sacred building consists of two rooms: a sub-rectangular atrium (originally fitted with a bench) probably covered by a gabled roof, and a circular cell accessible from the atrium, originally with a tholos (false dome) roof. In the centre of the cell are the remains of a hearth showing several phases of use, and against the wall face a bench-like embankment.

2b20bb375f01e18b.text: Single-tower that remains half-submerged, completely buried.

2b2996673d2bd0b9.text:
Nuraghe immersed in vegetation. Nearby lies the homonymous Nuragic burial.

Of the monument, on the west side, a short stretch of wall tangent to the main tower remains partially visible, while in plan the outline of the external perimeter can be observed.

The entrance to the tower is linted, with a trapezoidal cross-section, and leads into a passage with a flat floor.

2b4220bd1558a9b2.text: The entrance was later modified by the construction of a wall to form a kind of shelter for domestic animals.

2b53bcd8e165a5f6.text: From its position on the ridge of Badde, it dominates the right bank of the Rio Giunturas and is exceptionally aligned along the edge of the cliff, almost as if to assert its position of dominance. The internal chamber can be identified by its orthogonal cells, and the chamber is covered on its sides by organic debris.

2b54572189410afd.text:
It lies to the north-east of the village, a short distance from the nuraghe Luas and the proto-nuraghe Friarosu, and is visible from the provincial road that leads to Ruinas after the turn-off for Villa Sant'Antonio.

The plan of the nuraghe is decidedly unusual in that it has two circular structures joined by a corridor.

What makes the site even more interesting is the presence of a large granite boulder, oriented to the east, placed there presumably in the pre-Nuragic period.

2b57b0677613c95e.text:
Structures belonging to a complex nuraghe of the three-lobed type, built of polygonal basalt blocks. The building has been heavily robbed; only two or three courses survive in elevation, depending on the stretch.

The bastion, three towers and part of the curtain wall can be made out, against which large heaps of rubble lean. In place of the central tower a large excavation dug by mechanical means is visible. The whole structure is covered by a considerable depth of soil.

2b6d534c554929e3.text: Uncertain structure, appears to be a Nuragic foundation.

2b712f45f0c1688d.text:
From IGM. The aerial map suggests the polygon is occupied by a modern cottage.

The nuraghe today is probably destroyed or at least not identifiable.

2b7c190f04407a2e.text: Apart from a large worked slab, nothing of the probable tomb remains, except a heap of stones.

2b83cae71ededa63.text: Complex corridor-type tholos nuraghe with a main tower clearly visible and two additional towers. One is clearly visible, although covered by vegetation, while the other is only discernible beneath the dense undergrowth. The main tower is preserved in good condition and features an architraved entrance oriented to the southeast. On IGM maps the nuraghe is listed as Serra Crastula.

2b89debe6b0aeb9f.text:
The site is located on the summit of a steep hilltop, whose lands, partially covered by a dense forest, are used for sheep grazing. The simple-type nuraghe has suffered a collapse on the eastern side, obscuring the entrance.  

It remains standing to a maximum height of 5.50 m and a minimum of 1 m, with wall facings constructed from granite blocks arranged in irregular courses.

2b8a25eb84bc4fb0.text: Cyclopean masonry circuit with typical features of Nuragic sources

2ba002d3d62a4560.text: Small domus whose entrance was once walled up for use as a sheepfold.

2bde1637a93c6027.text: It retains the tholos intact except for a few upper courses.

2befc409de2b8db0.text: They lie on a slight rise at 184 m. The four rock-cut chambers are hewn in sandstone and each consists of a single elliptical cell with a vaulted roof. The many artificial cuttings, clearly visible in the rock face that flanks the domus de janas on the right-hand side for a stretch of 12 m, are clear signs of ancient quarrying that has largely destroyed the original layout of the site.

2bf1706a89cef968.text: Destroyed nuraghe, of which only a small amount remains

2c3d0e089c61b4f8.text: The probable Nuragic village consists of several huts, from which only fragmentary remains survive. In some cases, walls composed of multiple courses (3–5) of stones of varying sizes remain. Most of the structures are overgrown by vegetation, which has compromised their integrity through growth; when the structures are located in open field, the remains are indistinguishable to the naked eye.

2c6aa8eb8c98c26f.text:
Su Nuraxi Serra Manalgiu, about one kilometre from the old railway station of "Ortuabis", in the territory of Meana Sardo.

Around the nuraghe there are many fallen stones and many leccio plants, which grow alongside it.

One can observe an interesting wall built with rows of stones of the same height and a chamber with a collapsed vault.

2c6add6a4030ee68.text:
Elliptical corridor nuraghe, built using polygonal masonry with trachytic red stones.

The southern short side is preserved to a height of about 3 m and houses the entrance, topped by a granite lintel, from which access to a small sub-circular chamber leads to a second room via another entrance also featuring a granite lintel.

2cc76b793ad093c3.text: The tomb, located about 300 metres to the north of the homonymous nuraghe, is in good state of preservation. The entrance, facing east, provides access to a rectangular chamber about 10 metres long and 1.20 m high, composed of well-shaped ashlars laid in regular courses.

2ceb9eb2019afb3a.text:
The single-tower nuraghe, set within the Mediterranean scrub, is a prehistoric building constructed with dark basaltic stones of fairly regular dimensions.

The internal chamber, accessed through a well-preserved corridor, features two lateral niches and a terrace situated at about eight metres in height, reachable via a staircase ramp.

2cf20a6a5a9eec02.text: Single-cell domus de janas carved out of granite

2d2eab78f5bed382.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Pozzomaggiore (SS). It is a large proto-nuraghe, almost destroyed. There is a covered entrance covered in debris and a corridor of about 10 metres in length with a height of 2 metres. At the upper part, a further entrance is still visible. Numerous stones are scattered around the structure.

2d400a2cb6dd090f.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Pozzomaggiore (SS). Partially destroyed, about 2 metres high, covered with debris.

2d5bdaf1216a0b69.text: It is in poor conservation condition. Position verified with GPS.

2d81cc7110c916d5.text: Nuraghe with a sub-rectangular plan (13.40 m long along the NS axis and 10.60 m wide along the EO axis), characterized by straight long sides and convex short sides. The nuraghe is completely destroyed and practically illegible. It is located in the territory of the comune of Ittiri.

2d8646652f2d29d5.text: The building has collapsed on the south side and dense vegetation conceals its full extent. The central tower measures about 12 m in diameter and its present height is 7.30 m. At present a short stretch of the stairwell is visible on the north side, where the facing survives and may be the remains of the bastion of a complex building. The nuraghe stands on natural outcrops of trachyte. Around the nuraghe lies an extensive settlement that was also occupied in Roman times.

2d9aa91fb9cb45f3.text:
On the plain there are two massive rocky outcrops that emerge, more or less 200 metres long, 30 m wide, 6 m high.

I only saw Site I from a distance, but they are clearly visible and the landowner confirmed that there are several domus de janas.

Site II has about ten domus de janas all facing perfectly west, all very small except for two with several chambers. They are set at different heights in the rock, from 30 cm up to 4 metres above ground level.

2dec371728af03d9.text:
The area includes a dolmen, a domus de janas, and remains of a megalithic circle.

Particular area defined by the megalithic enclosure within which the dolmen is situated. About 20 m from the dolmen lies the single-chamber domus de janas with a dolmenic corridor, added in a later period to create an additional tomb. Dated between the 3rd and 2nd millennium BC, according to the Municipal Sign.

2e0849e9ae894069.text: Second domus de janas. in poor condition due to the overgrowth of brambles.

2e17ee27bc545c2c.text: Nuraghe about 9 m high, built with large basalt ashlar blocks. Corridor entrance about 5 m long with stairs on the left and a niche on the right. Intact tholos, diameter 5.30 m.

2e1a73900b6f060d.text:
It consists of three small tombs. It is located in the territory of Montresta.

Probable location.

2e28b475883570fb.text: The nuraghe is a complex type, with a central tower at the centre of a four-lobed bastion with a straight-curved profile enclosing a vaguely rectangular open-air courtyard. The whole structure measures 22.00 x 20.00 m (W-E / N-S axis), while the maximum surviving height is 6.20 m to the south-west and the wall thicknesses are 6.40 m to the south-west and 2.80 m to the north. Of the towers, only the one to the east is detectable, accessible from the courtyard through a corridor with steps visible in the final stretch.

2e5f18f957451fe4.text: The monument has collapsed in several places and is not altogether easy to interpret: it appears to have been a single-tower nuraghe, yet curvilinear wall outlines are visible around the main building. These could be dwelling units (huts?) or additional structures attached to the main body, in which case it would be a complex nuraghe.

2e6377a134963077.text: The corridor nuraghe, with a rectangular plan and constructed of large granite blocks, survives to a maximum height of 4 m; it features an entrance topped by a lintel leading to a flat-topped corridor, from which a semicircular niche and a long, elongated chamber open.

2e830284bef5b032.text: Nuraghe completely immersed in vegetation and partially eroded due to this. Structure not easily legible

2e8d610ac03ec8e6.text: Multi-lobed, with a central tower of which only the basal course survives; this breaks off to the south and south-west for a length of 8 m, where the foundations of four peripheral towers appear, originally joined by straight curtain walls, forming a basal platform supporting the main tower, which has a diameter of 9.60 m. About 11 m from the central tower the basal walling of a circular hut 8.40 m in diameter is almost entirely visible. The structures of the complex are composed of sandstone blocks.

2e90859e2bce06d4.text:
The building is a single-tower nuraghe that retains its chamber, accessible via a corridor with a stair and a niche, and provided with three subsidiary chambers.

The tower is built in its lower courses with large blocks; above these are set smaller boulders, carefully dressed and laid in regular horizontal courses.

Several light openings, triangular or quadrangular, arranged almost in a spiral, are visible on the outer wall face.

A short distance from the nuraghe a domus de janas has been cut.

2eae93d2fb0e1c97.text: Few remaining walls and many uncertainties: frequent help from the historical memory of the elders and the presence of only a few basal remains of the homonymous nuraghe. mu.

2eb432fa7664c163.text: The necropolis includes 4 domus de janas.

2ec1bcee2317d756.text: On the limestone plateau of sas cudinas to the north-east stands the single-tower nuraghe of roughly squared stones, of which only a few basal circles survive. It overlooks the whole valley of the rio Iscanneddu, the plain of Mamucada, and the fertile Orria Pitzinna.

2ed8c1ffd6feea10.text: The exact name of the nuraghe (with the mezzanino above the entrance corridor) should be S'Olteri.

2eea640cf5a14c63.text:
The monument stands in the marly basin of Coni at the foot of the Valenza hill, in the historic region of Part'e Alenza, between the Marmilla and the Sarcidano. The sacred well of Coni, built of basalt blocks in pseudo-isodomic masonry, although lacking a vestibule, follows the classic architectural scheme of Nuragic wells.

The monument consists of a descending staircase protected by a corridor (2.60 m long) and an underground chamber that encloses the spring vein.

2f2730a0871acc77.text:
It is located within the municipal territory of Orani (NU). It consists of 17 domus de janas and 2 tunnels (probably used as burial sites). In a text by Chiara Chisu, it is stated that there are 15 domus, but I have recorded at least 17 (some may have escaped my notice due to dense vegetation).

Do not confuse them with those of Oniferi, which are known as Sas Concas.

2f3bfc056f452299.text: Cemetery composed of domus de janas repurposed in the Roman period.

2f457cdea927d1c8.text:
North-west of the Muntone nuraghe, from which they can be reached by a path, lie first a settlement and then the megalithic tomb of Tanca Noa.

The settlement, which appears to extend for about 400 sq m, consists of the remains of structures whose ground plans are not easily defined; the wall structures, of which only the basal course survives, are built in the double-skin technique, using trachyte and dry-stone construction.

2f6b60eebd54dc07.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is adjacent to the tomb of Battos I and repeats both its typology and the high quality of its basalt elements, which are well-cut and finely finished, though the site is not equally well preserved. Among the fallen stones, the corridor and the exedra can still be identified, while in the apsidal area two monolithic arches are present. On the ground, dentilled ashlar is visible.

2f6ee3dbfa7d2283.text:
Completely buried externally, it retains internally a small tholos that extends into a dead-end corridor.

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.

2f77325898f9dc0a.text: The Ruinas Nuraghe is described by Giovanni Lilliu as the tallest in Sardinia. At an elevation of 1,205 metres, it offers a magnificent panoramic view of the surrounding landscape and of the ruins of numerous circular huts that surround it (at least 200).

2f8c3039ce83990b.text: These are the remains of a nuraghe that is difficult to classify typologically; the collapses and the dense shrub vegetation growing on the exposed masonry do not allow a proper survey. However, the data gathered during repeated inspections of the site, which among other things made it possible to locate the entrance facing north-west, lead me to hypothesise that it may belong to the class of so-called corridor nuraghi with an associated settlement.

2f94c70b86d28c57.text: The cista is formed by medium-sized stones set vertically into the ground. There is a single stone that closes the cista; previously, the presence of a baetyl is noted.

2fbac5c8d12403fb.text:
Megalithic tomb consisting of a burial corridor bounded by two parallel rows of orthostats.

A single large, well-finished quadrangular slab of the roofing remains, resting on the side walls at the far end of the tomb.

For the enhancement and public use of the monument, the surrounding pertinent area has been fenced and linked to the municipal road network by a path bordered by dry-stone walls.

2fc51abef626148c.text: The Suttaterra rock-cut is located on the limestone summit of "Punta Su Nuraghe", where you can admire not only the natural arch but also a megalithic wall situated at a short distance, giving you a sense of the distance separating you from the Codula di Ilune and from other beauties of the area.

2ff88629cf7002e7.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe is almost completely dismantled, and the remaining structures consist of the first two courses of the base, built from locally quarried basalt blocks. The maximum remaining height is about 1 m, while the diameter of the nuraghe is about 12 m. The entrance must have been located to the south-east, where a hut was constructed.

3005d1570a09ff73.text: The complex nuraghe, of which ruins of the central tower and two curtain walls on two different levels survive. The original tower retains its outline almost intact. The two curtain walls are visible on the side facing north-east of the central tower; they follow a curvilinear course for several metres, interrupted from north-east to north-west by a substantial collapse that starts from the central tower.

30097d8a28f31060.text: It consists of six single-cell domus de janas.

300bf2a5a0fc89e6.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of three towers erected in a linear arrangement, built on the rocky tip of Monte Sirimagus, one of which features a well dug into the rock. Surrounding the site is a village with dozens of huts, enclosed by as many as three curtain walls. The site has been extensively disturbed by excavators. At the foot of the mountain is a perennial pond used during the Nuragic period.

3011ec213a57fe6f.text: A single-tower nuraghe with ten courses of porous basalt still in place. It lies in the territory of Sorradile (OR); its present position is curious, for after the Omodeo artificial reservoir was built the monument stands on the lake shore, subject to the continual fluctuations of the water level.

303239c12eb265ab.text: We find it at about 30 metres perpendicular to the secondary road of SS 131, in a state of complete abandonment.

303c82f0dc5a0b1b.text: Unidentified nuraghe. Area with finds attributable to a settlement with a nuraghe, the nuraghe has been demolished. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

3065746ff76fba8c.text: The Santu Millanu nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe surrounded by a four-lobed bastion barely discernible.

3070f2fa2f3ad42b.text: The most well-known nuraghe is undoubtedly the one discovered in the Santa Maria area during excavations carried out beneath the sacristy of the rural chapel; the foundations were uncovered in 1843, and some nuraghe stones are incorporated into the fence wall of the church courtyard. www.aserramanna.it/storia/ www.serramanna.altervista.org/storia.htm

30712b0761b34c11.text: It is located in the territory of the comune of Buddusò (OT) at a lower elevation than the road passing through the granite quarry.

3079ad8117f3c27c.text:
The dolmen has a burial chamber of a vaguely polygonal shape (1.51 x 1.20 x 0.71 m high) and still preserves six orthostats in their original position, on which the large polygonal covering slab, worked with some care, rests (2.20 x 1.90 x 0.50 m thick).

Around the monument, among numerous overturned stones, three orthostats still in situ can be seen maintaining an alignment parallel to the perimeter of the tomb and forming part of its peristalith.

30831f9bc26811aa.text: The Costa nuraghe, commonly known as Sa Reggia, comprises a complex nuraghe, an adjacent village, and a powerful outer wall. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bastion with four secondary towers, containing an inner courtyard. The central tower (14 metres in diameter) is built with polygonal basalt blocks in the lower section and finely worked blocks in the upper section.

308690c5e25226f9.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only the base survives, controlling the valley of the Rio Gutturu Mannu to the east. Taken from the archaeological map of Sant'Andrea Frius drawn up by Roberta Relli and Antonio Forci.

308a2f3a9e1be906.text: Very ruined, yet large blocks of hard limestone, roughly shaped, remain, highlighting the construction layout. The entrance to the south-south-east is visible, with a lintel on the ground near the two piers. The type of nuraghe refers to the sacred character of the site, linked to the union with the god, as the monument is seen as an extension of the mountain in the form of a conical trunk. mu

308f718ea684ede2.text: The tomb shows a rectangular chamber completely blocked by fallen stones and covered with vegetation. In the space immediately in front of the tomb are stones clearly belonging to the exedra wall, some in their original positions. Given its current state, it is difficult to determine its dimensions.

30b14ea8cef9275b.text:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.

30e74538a18ee09f.text: It is a nuraghe of which only a few or no traces remain.

30eb33bb99935e9b.text: A rural penetration road runs along the hillside, though one must still climb uphill on foot (no paths or trails are present).

3103656d09c41070.text:
Site where a proto-Sardinian healing god was worshipped.

Rectangular-plan temple built of large blocks, with a spring that collected in a round well. Taramelli judged that all the elements of a sanctuary with a healing character were present: a therapeutic spring and a temple to the healing deity, where the most remarkable find in Sardinian archaeology came to light. The bronze column base with inscriptions in Greek, Punic and Latin dedicated to the god Eshmun.

31163f7356630ac9.text: This is Domus I, the most important and easily visible of a prehistoric necropolis consisting of 7 hypogea. The other tombs lie on private land, about 600 metres away as the crow flies to the south-east. Two of the hypogea mentioned above are more properly burials in rock shelters. Prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia (1800–1600 BC), the so-called Bonnanaro Culture.

311d84200c0f45c7.text:
The nuraghe has a sub-elliptical plan, with its long sides aligned east–west. The masonry is roughly polygonal.

The entrance faces north and has a lintel resting on a few large blocks that form the jambs; it is surmounted by a smaller ashlar, which in turn is set within a semicircular ring of blocks that diverts the weight of the superstructure onto the jambs.

311ebdf056fb98c5.text: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.

3136580e158b1093.text: Reduced to the extreme act of ruin. Only some basally arranged stones, variously shaped, remain, all set within a large mass of mastic wood.

313aeb43f6ad9fe9.text: Known as Nuraghe de su casteddu de Monte Maria, possibly a strongholds-type nuraghe, built on a granite base. Difficult to access, it was already visited and recorded by Lamarmora in 1830; it is said that a lightning strike reduced it to its present state. The northern and southern towers are accessible; it seems to be a corridor nuraghe adapted over time.

31581427f1a11ebe.text: Four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the central tower's entrance.

3161fdbc287ab7a2.text: It is a simple tholos nuraghe, whose external plan is not visible as it is completely buried. The layout of the corridor (maximum length 3.40 m) and the nearly circular shape of the chamber, with a niche on the left side, can be understood. The structure is built with courses of granitic blocks, each course being progressively smaller than the ones above.

316d3eee248bce05.text: A short distance from the megalithic circle are the basal remains of a simple circular nuraghe of the advanced Nuragic period, and a little further downhill the Ochila domus de janas, some of them richly decorated with symbolic and architectural elements in relief. The megalithic enclosure consists of ten (plus an eleventh lying overturned in the centre of the area) irregularly parallelepiped megaliths set side by side, forming a semicircle 9–10 metres in diameter.

318ab94ad193c26f.text: Several remains of circular constructions, terraces, and robust curtain walls in megalithic technique are visible, while at the highest point stands a complex structure built of granite blocks, featuring a quadrangular tower. The settlement is crossed by the torrential Riu Bidd'e Mores, a tributary of the Riu Gutturu Mannu.

31a42914f2483654.text: Single-tower nuraghe greatly modified by agricultural mechanization in the 1950s.

31d70928501aaeb0.text:
Built of granite blocks, it consists of a circular courtyard, a vestibule – a small space linking the courtyard and the well – and the well itself, reached from the vestibule by several steps; the spring lies 17 steps down.

Excavated completely in 1938, the sacred well of Sa Testa has an overall length of 17.50 metres. It was a place of worship for spring waters. Numerous finds came to light during the excavations, such as Punic-period incense burners.

31dc0f43b6392d53.text:
The underground chamber is cut into a schist rock, and on the side opposite the entrance—i.e., the northern side—there is a clear indication of a previous excavation, likely from another underground chamber. Access to the domus de janas is via a door with a drainage groove cut into the threshold:

the door is characterized by the presence of a frame surmounted by a lintel, formed by carving the rock, to highlight this architectural element.

31e247234d5a7ad2.text: Its entrance was narrowed and adapted in the Nuragic period so as to make it hard to find and extremely easy to defend in the event of an outside attack. The rather steep dromos, with a final drop of 8 metres, was altered by adding a retaining wall and creating an access via a narrow, steep staircase of 18 steps. Inside, traces of Nuragic-period use are clearly visible.

31ebd232396a7903.text: Known as a nuraghe, it is instead an excellent example of a giants' tomb with an associated ceremonial circle. Facing east is the dolmenic exedra that opens into a rectangular lithic cist. From the sides of the exedra extend large stones cut to form a circular arrangement used for ceremonies.

31eefa9b0d874fc9.text: This domus de janas belongs to the larger complex of Abealzu-Calancoi, which includes dozens of domus de janas. It is situated on the half-slope of a limestone hillside, exposed to the south, and is difficult to reach on foot. It is notable for its state of degradation due to limestone weathering and subsequent human use.

31f28ea0bd272ee7.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village, the structure of which cannot be defined.

31fec4807eaacd9a.text:
The monument consists of an atrium and the spring itself from which the spring water flows.

The atrium is a rectangular space measuring 5.15 by 1.80 m, bounded on the sides by two benches of equal length built of basalt blocks and, on the left side, by a section of walling 2 by 3 m made of well-squared ashlars laid in regular courses. The floor is paved with blocks of the same kind.

320766da9ccee450.text: Submerged single-tower nuraghe in the waters of Lake Cuga. It was detected by archaeologist Ercole Contu during the period preceding the construction of the dam on Cuga. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes in the Chessedu–Cuga valley.

321cefb7695150cc.text: It is a vast area of archaeological interest and is located near the ruins of a rural chapel, which are visible in the territory of Sanluri just beyond the border with our village. It has witnessed successive settlements from the prehistoric Middle Bronze Age (16th–14th centuries BC) to the Iron Age (9th–8th centuries BC).

325a5bf026d9f36f.text: Group of seven or more domus de janas located on the pass, near L'azienda Mariani, from which one has a view of the Santa Lucia plain and the underlying necropolis of Sant'Andrea Priu, as well as the valley of the nuraghes of Torralba. The tomb seven, featuring a double spiral in red ochre, has recently been restored.

3299010eb6ab75ae.text:
The nuraghe stands on the northern edge of a modest trachyte plateau, from which it overlooks the whole valley below. Not far from it lie the Runara dolmen and the Pittigheddu nuraghe.

The nuraghe is in very poor condition, having been used as a stone quarry to build several enclosures that stand right up against the building, making it extremely difficult to follow the plan of the ancient structure.

32ca612e6014a921.text: The cemetery consists of 33 hypogea of domus de janas dug into tuff and divided into two groups. The site, datable to the Neolithic, was used by the peoples of the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, the Vaso campaniforme, and Bonnanaro cultures, as well as by the Nuragic people of Iloi in the early Bronze Age, with later medieval reuse.

32d3576b0851e5e1.text: The cemetery consists of five hypogea and numerous cavities that were probably domus de janas, but now appear to have been destroyed or incomplete. One of the domus (the first) features in its main chamber an interesting column.

32d8b37953b33ecb.text: Not recorded, it is located on private land.

32f02fa66b99660a.text: Completely buried... and overlooked. In the village it is said that originally it was the largest in the area and that part of the upper tower was removed for building material.

32f62beb1095ea26.text: The nuraghe is situated on the summit of the hill. Single-tower with a staircase. Completely with its top missing.

32fff02ff6c99fa2.text: The Giants' tomb is located about fifty metres to the south of the Nuraghe Figu. Part of the tomb's structure and a small portion of the exedra are visible.

331e99c6b0bfb7c5.text: A very unusual menhir, pierced at multiple points, possibly artificially.

3320fc699e192ee2.text: It consists of several single-room units, some with an antechamber and two or three small internal rooms. It is reasonable to think that others exist, not yet evident in the womb of Mother Earth. Almost all of them stand on the ridge of the mountain and on the gentle slope of sa pala de s'Ozastru. On the plateau are the remains of the eponymous nuraghe, with a clear link between the two sites of different periods and reasonably an example of cultural and religious syncretism. mu

3328571419e638b7.text: It is an isolated wooded hillock shaped like a cone on a plain, upon which various stones of different shapes are placed, ranging from conical prism to parallelepiped forms. The setting is striking and it is said that events and occurrences take place within sacred or initiation-propitiatory ceremonies. mu

332aa681d407c33b.text: It is located in the municipality of Florinas and is composed of three hypogea.

332d19abb2ec57ff.text: The nuraghe Franzesu stands in a commanding position on the Spiritu Santu plateau, with a wide view ranging from the Gulf of Asinara to Corsica, controlling important access routes. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bilobed frontal bastion without a facing. The bastion is built of large trachyte blocks; it is thought that some of these may be reused menhirs, and at least one certainly was.

3349bf13298a31c7.text: Only the lower part of the nuraghe remains, used also as a sheepfold. Likely elliptical in shape or at least non-circular. Diameter at the top is about 10 m.

336694de11079cf5.text: In a precarious state of conservation, it is surrounded by patches of rowan and shrubs that may compromise its stability.

336af29ca3582be2.text: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure is difficult to define

33882dd1dbc2becf.text: Large megalithic circle a short distance from the Sacred Well Mitza Salamu.

339b795a4e72da67.text: In total ruin, only some of the basal circle stones remain, which help identify its belonging. The stones are of large dimensions and the chamber has collapsed together with numerous debris that have accumulated over time. Fichidindia plants and thorny shrubs have colonized the site.

33b70cca9edb29b2.text: The complex consists of six hypogeal tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.

33bb6bd20ecc0ce1.text: Not easily accessible due to its position on a particularly striking elevated ridge, it includes a complex nuraghe. The structure, partially collapsed and difficult to interpret because of abundant debris, shows rows of limestone blocks.

33d3e2d7e470fb51.text: Composed of a pseudo-rectangular trench about 1 m deep, lined with three courses of stones. Closed with a flat band of three slabs of slate, each 25 cm thick. Single burial with Monte Claro ceramics.

33e4721797cb5ad2.text: Village without a nuraghe. From the same area comes a Neolithic dagger with a leaf-shaped blade, as well as a trachyte rose basin with a diameter of 70 cm at the mouth. A bronze storage chamber is noted at Sant' Elia, reported by Giuseppe Atzori, now dispersed.

3400100038e5a5bc.text:
Of the monument, practically destroyed, only the funerary corridor remains, consisting of a depression in the ground, and numerous shaped ashlar stones that indicate the tomb was of a coursed type in isodomic masonry.

Among the ashlar stones, carefully worked, one can observe the so-called dentilled ashlar of considerable size, and a monolithic arch related to the apsidal area.

341f1e0b0ed05c85.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four towers. The outline of the walls of the original tower survives almost entirely; its interior is filled with earth, collapse debris and vegetation. Three towers added laterally stand to the south-east, north-west and north-east, all overgrown with vegetation that makes their structure hard to see. The fourth tower lies to the south-west, detached from the main body. Traces left by illegal excavators are clearly visible.

345fc7c154b7400b.text: Complex nuraghe. Traces of at least three towers, probably added concentrically, can be identified. The original tower retains its wall outline, broken to the south by a small opening. The interior is partly blocked by soil and collapse debris. To the south and south-south-east there are two triangular corridors whose outlines, interrupted by collapse, are visible for several metres; one suggests the presence of a stairwell. Clandestine excavations are visible.

347c6509c15da260.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period built in courses of polygonal limestone blocks.

Although partly covered by vegetation and fill, the ground plan with its apse and exedra, whose arms run in straight lines, is clearly legible. On the façade, in front of the entrance doorway, a rectangular slab lies on the ground and may be the lintel of the entrance.

347e39d08ef341ae.text: The building, a circular single-tower nuraghe about 10 metres in diameter, adapts to the plateau, incorporating rock outcrops into its basal structures. The external wall face, made of roughly dressed limestone blocks laid in regular courses, survives to a maximum height of 8.10 metres. On the west and south-east sides, at a height of 3 to 3.5 metres from the ground, a restoration carried out in antiquity is clearly visible, made necessary by the subsidence of the masonry.

34b75d2417ce8148.text: Corridor nuraghe particularly eroded. The corridor is composed of a flat band with stone slabs. Transversal niches have been carved.

34bf7c128e23a3a0.text: Two nuraghi (no longer existing and/or buried) located in the territory of Ussana and reported by Taramelli (see "Ussana - Scoperte di tombe di età incerta in territorio del Comune, regione di Salomea", in Notizie degli Scavi, 1906, pp. 57-58). The first was probably situated in the centre of the village at Bruncu Sa Turri, more or less corresponding to the old municipal aqueduct (Via Aldo Frau).

34d4ffd77b9af2e1.text: The hypogeum lies at the southern edge of a small plateau, characterised by dense woodland. The burial is cut into a block of heavily fractured granite, so that part of the antechamber has completely broken away and now lies right next to the entrance. The entrance to the cell is about 0.70 m above ground level; it has jambs and a lintel carved in relief, with carefully finished surfaces.

34e812783c92679c.text: The probable Nuragic village consists of several huts of which linear wall remains survive, formed by several courses (in some cases up to five) of stones of various sizes. They were probably rectangular structures. Unfortunately, dense and tangled vegetation conceals most of the structures. To the north, about 100 metres away, lies the Noccus pond, a water reserve for the villages in the area.

34f31a32abbbe4dc.text: The monument, about 300 metres north-west of the Nuraghe Su Figu, is now almost completely buried under rubble from the clearance of the surrounding fields, a fact that makes the plan of the nuraghe extremely difficult to read. It appears to be a circular single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, visible where the top is missing.

351c3c255bb7c2bf.text: These are domus belonging to those with complex architecture. The development of the rooms cannot be fully understood as Mother Earth has preserved almost the entire site intact. Access is possible through the collapse of the roof of one of the chambers. Inside, clear construction details, accessories, and petroglyphs are visible. Mu

352bc0de8dd017fa.text: It is a report by an enthusiast, verified by an archaeologist. It appears to be a giants' tomb or a corridor dolmenic, hitherto unknown.

3532d8801c1337ec.text:
It is more precisely a proto-nuraghe.

In the vicinity there are also a special giants' tomb and a domus de janas.

355a8dacd2db9384.text: Su Putzu Nuragic village, composed of about one hundred huts surrounding a well temple, exactly Su Putzu.

356b86aea2594cd0.text:
It is located at the border between the municipal territories of Bortigali (NU) and Dualchi (NU), but belongs to the municipality of Dualchi.

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe. Around it are several cinerary urns. It consists of two megalithic walls still partially intact.

3570f36c7102d51f.text: The nuraghe, the best-visible side of which is from the vineyard in front of the pigsty, appears in any case to have been a single-tower nuraghe, built with roughly dressed blocks of fairly regular parallelepiped shape and medium-to-large size.

357cdb00e939ef38.text: It lies in the territory of Pozzomaggiore (SS), near the nuraghe (proto-nuraghe) Sinadorzu or Scale e Ozzastru; there are several huts and enclosure walls, and nearby one can see probable remains of giants' tombs and perhaps a Nuragic sacred well, obviously all in deplorable condition.

357fbab393ded136.text: The nuraghe stands on the Gullei. It is a single enormous lava flow several kilometres long. The village is not easy to reach because it is wrapped in dense wild scrub. The nuraghe is a three-lobed one whose walls are visible. For at least one or two hectares around, the village spreads out, with a furnace, a well and more besides. From the top of the towers the whole territory and the coast are visible as far as the Mariolu cliffs to the south and Cala Ginepro to the north.

3582b38b98e67b15.text: The domus de janas, carved into the basaltic hillside, number five, all attributable to the Ozieri Culture and dating from 3100 to 2900 BC. The pre-Nuragic village, also belonging to the Ozieri Culture, is located at the foot of the hill.

359808c65aa7484e.text:
In some publications it is distinguished from the village and the necropolis of Porcili Mannu, but the area actually lies in Sa Sucraxia and the inhabitants of the region refer to it as such.

Almost camouflaged among the large trees, clearly visible remains of a large stone village with various buildings, some dwellings, tomb remnants, and other structures of unknown function can be observed.

359ebb88b9f1dbda.text: Menhir / carved stele with concentric circles

35a024338b497214.text: It is located to the north-east along the provincial road near the border with the territory of Ruinas. It stands on a large calcareous foundation and is filled with its own stone masonry, which renders access impossible. According to common belief, it was composed of a succession of three superimposed rooms. Remains of a staircase are visible along a ridge.

35c2cb3f1abf45ac.text: Giants' tomb belonging to the same named nuraghe. Very poor state of conservation.

35cff6ce23ba502b.text: It consists of a nuraghe of an unusual type, built of roughly squared megalithic blocks laid in fairly regular courses. To the north-east an extensive village spreads out, mostly reduced to a scatter of stones; from the general collapse a few megalithic structures and some huts uncovered by unauthorised diggers emerge. The nuraghe, on the other hand, retains its original elevation to a certain height, but its ground plan is not immediately legible.

35e7c6b26ff19799.text: They are four small underground burials dug out in an isolated rock outcrop.

35fb788aae59037d.text: Domus de janas carved out of granite, particularly striking for its double door set between a pillar.

3604611dfbe5ca93.text:
The Nuragic complex at Serra Paulis now appears as a ruin, with four wall structures, already identified by Struglia in the 1980s.

Its dominant position over the entire landscape allows for a 360° panoramic view.

The site was probably reused in Roman times as a forge, given the substantial remains of burnt and fire-deformed materials found in situ.

3606441ecee8545e.text: The domus of Taulera is located near Alghero's civil hospital. In 1941–42, some soldiers stationed there discovered a skull characterized by a double trepanation. It appears that the individual to whom the skull belonged survived the first trepanation for at least a year, dying probably during the second procedure.

3625651afb95cb26.text: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on a rocky spur, utilizing its elevations; characterized by a powerful collapse, particularly located to the north-northeast. Situated at 418 m.

36365659deb4f519.text: Giants' tomb Sa Canna, in the Sàrrala area of Tertenia but administratively belonging to one of the many enclaves in the zone (39.61237 N 9.63864 E). This was my first encounter with a tomb built of schist, a stone used only sporadically for this type of monument. It is of the coursed type, considered more recent than the 'dolmenic' or 'arched stele' type, and has an elegant exedra — although it lacks the dentilled ashlar characteristic of the more refined examples — standing 2.55 m high at its apex. The tomb shows some gaps due to clandestine disturbance (the missing ashlar from the left arm of the exedra is clearly visible), which prevent the exact width of the semicircle from being determined, though it can be assessed as having a slight curvature. The chamber, not very large, is 6.75 metres long measured at the outer threshold and 6.40 metres at the inner threshold, and is distinguished by a perfect ogive with a descending height from 1.95 m at the entrance to 1.40 m (presumed, since the clandestine excavation has disturbed the basal paving) at the rear, where traces of ancient plastering seem to be detectable (unless this is due to a neoformation of clay caused by the loss of the corridor's waterproofing — which, on the other hand, remains intact for almost its entire length). The entrance doorway is trapezoidal (50 cm wide at the base and 60 cm at the top), 57 cm high, and easily passable. This is therefore one of the tombs in which it is clear that access from the top of the corridor was not possible, as most island archaeologists maintain (on the other side of the 'barricade' stood the great Ercole Contu, who in my opinion took a more scientific approach to the question), since there is no possibility of removing any ashlars from the corridor to allow such hypothetical access. The tomb almost certainly belongs to a settlement located about 500 metres away as the crow flies, on another saddle of the same ridge, of which only a few remains can be identified today: a non-canonical type of nuraghe and a few surrounding traces attributable to huts (the area is also known as Serra 'e Mari, and a boundary stone — the municipalities concerned are Lanusei and Arzana — was placed on the nuraghe in 1953).

3664093265f864c9.text: Wall alignments and structural remains, among which a hut with a sub-rectangular plan is recognisable, surviving to a maximum height of about 1 m, built of small basalt blocks laid dry, with a small lintelled window. Modern and contemporary enclosures stand in the area of the concentration. The area of what was presumably a settlement extends around the nuraghe Marzacche.

366d8486efdd2e7d.text:
At the foot of the hill on which the nuraghe Su Gattu stands, the remains of a granite burial are visible.

Of the giants' tomb only a portion of the apse and part of the rectangular chamber, bounded by large granite stones, remain, while externally the remains of the peristalith project.

36734870daa2d37c.text: Monument in poor condition of disintegration. It is located on a secondary summit of the Monte Nibbarone (237 m) at an elevation of 168 m a.s.l., from where it dominates the entire valley below.

367b23e5d0718900.text: Interesting giants' tomb with a bilitic arched stele, of which only the lower part with a door remains. The exedra and the burial chamber are also present.

367d02ee76ff5a86.text: An area with a small single-tower nuraghe around which there is a small necropolis of four domus de janas, in which there are decorations of carved bull's-head protomes.

36b51bf237f13772.text: Located at the border with the territory of Guasila, at the foot of the basaltic plateau of Lasìna, on the western side which slopes down towards the Samatzese territory. The structure consists of a single tower with an external diameter of 12 m and retains intact along its entire circumference the base course. The materials used are sandstone.

36c269c919b13893.text:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Santu Lussurgiu (OR), a few kilometres from the hamlet of San Leonardo de Siete Fuentes.

It is a three-lobed nuraghe with a main tower and two smaller towers, one to the south-west and the other to the north-east. Traces of a curtain wall remain a few metres from the entrance to the first tower, enclosing the complex.

36c7ac0d4b1983d2.text:
On a rocky spur stands the corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, built of pink trachyte boulders. The interior of the monument is not accessible because of the many collapses.

The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

On an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible, of which only the basal courses remain.

36db5ee2d0833f1a.text: The sacred area, dominated to the east by the striking granite crests of Monte Senes (about 862 m above sea level), was built in the Nuragic period at the Janna 'e Pruna pass, now crossed by the Irgoli–Norghio road and a crossing point (about 590 m above sea level) that has been used since very ancient times along a mountain route linking the Riu Siniscola valley with the Cedrino valley, important corridors from the coast into the interior of the island.

36e8677da1829e56.text:
The burial lies on the southern slope of a gentle incline. The burial chamber is partly visible, and about 3.50 m from it two partly buried blocks can be seen, probable elements of the exedra. The tomb has unfortunately been disturbed by illicit digging that has affected the rear part of the tomb.

As far as can be seen, the latter consists of medium-sized granite slabs, well dressed on the exposed face, and set as orthostats.

3700cdfde2e40a7e.text:
The four-lobed bastion has a rather disordered structure of large polyhedral blocks; all the chambers have collapsed vaults, while the courtyard is partly filled with rubble; the main entrance is visible on the eastern side.

A stretch of enclosure wall can be seen to the west of the bastion, but it is not clear whether it extends around the other sides as well. All the ground around the bastion has been completely cleared of stones and is cultivated, with abundant Roman pottery on the surface.

370d43a0d61267ac.text: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement, destroyed due to the construction of the railway. The exact location is not known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

372f9efc2963203a.text: It is located in the territory of the comune of San Vito (CA), inside the church of the same name.

3731d46ab3c2667b.text: The nuraghe is in a very advanced state of collapse. The full outline of the original tower survives for a maximum of two courses. Given the few remaining boulders on site, it may have been dismantled so its stones could be reused. A few metres away there are boulders that probably belonged to the nuraghe, used to build a yard for watering livestock. At present the nuraghe is completely overgrown with vegetation.

3747d1613ef62132.text:
Also known as "Sa Domu 'e s'Orku", it is built of local granite blocks laid in "cyclopean style". It has the unique feature of being oriented exactly to the north.

This giants' tomb is of the "coursed façade" type, typical of the giants' tombs of southern Sardinia; the façade and the exedra, 10 m wide, are built in megalithic masonry; on the right-hand side of the exedra there are three "ritual hearths", circular in shape.

3751186c7f0ac95d.text: Both the nuraghe and the giants' tomb are in very poor condition of conservation and are surrounded by vegetation.

375b78263209220b.text: The monolith of "La Serra" is named after the nearby nuraghe, a plurimillennial monument shaped like a truncated cone now reduced to a ruin. The massive stone, composed of multiple fragments, dates to the late Neolithic period, although no precise dates are known; it is certain that the monolith predates the nuraghe by a long time. (Pieragica)

375d31b3a5309a4a.text: The Nuraghe Sa mandra e sa Giua no longer exists; it has been levelled, and its ashlars were used to build dry walls and the Roman settlement.

3778bade1efc9912.text: Complex nuraghe, covered by dense vegetation; near the nuraghe, a menhir and several giants' tombs, concealed by the thick vegetation, are observed.

3780bc59e218f5ff.text: Damaged nuraghe of which the shape is not recognizable

37b78bde83516541.text: The nuraghe has suffered significant collapses and is surrounded by dense vegetation.

37d86c662b34635d.text: The sculptures of the bull's head can be admired, representing the head of the male god, worshipped by the populations of the Neolithic period, who buried their dead in these artificial caves.

37dd2f097faa47d5.text: Composed of two rooms of square plan dug into compact granite.

37f62d4938388b0a.text: Embedded within the vegetation of this nuraghe, only a few courses remain. It has never been excavated or studied.

37fec134d49a55e9.text: The existence of this single-tower nuraghe is assumed, even though very few remains survive.

3807d7b442520666.text: It is built of cyclopean andesite blocks and consists of a large central tower joined to three towers. Of these, two show their entire interior structure: precisely the east and the west towers. It would be possible to enter the west one to explore the inside of the nuraghe, but I had neither the time nor the wish to risk it. Up to seven courses of the central tower are visible, reaching a height of almost three metres, while up to six courses of the west tower are visible, reaching a height of two and a half metres.

3815d30b9625705c.text: Remains of a small granite nuraghe

3835535ba07fbfd7.text:
In the municipal territory of Gonnosnò stands the nuraghe Tramatza which, together with the nuraghe Emmauru, overlooked the valley of the rio Figu, a winding watercourse among the hills at the foot of the plateau.

Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain; the original structure was a single-tower nuraghe with a truncated-conical shape, built by superimposing stone blocks, and contained the main chamber inside, connected to the outside by a narrow corridor.

384427714a7b9c52.text: The remains of the Lepuri nuraghe are not easily identifiable. Of the nuraghe, located possibly to guard a stream flowing a little distance to the south, only a few discontinuous wall segments remain, suggesting a structure of elongated plan built using large, unworked or very roughly shaped stones.

387b809573e40b87.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from polygonal basaltic blocks. Of the nuraghe, only 4–5 courses of large blocks remain arranged in a circular pattern to form a structure of considerable size, very similar to other nuraghes in the area. The maximum remaining height is about 3 m. The internal chamber has collapsed and is filled with collapse debris. The entrance cannot be identified.

389114bec8664d7c.text: Single-cell domus de janas carved in limestone

38ad27a4279d8e94.text: Complex nuraghe belonging to a much larger settlement, which has never been the subject of archaeological excavations.

38b8a3c397b7bf00.text: Complex-type nuraghe with lateral additions, featuring two secondary towers added to the main tower. Built with local basalt blocks arranged in fairly regular courses. The entrance to the main tower is located to the east and appears trapezoidal, with an architrave formed by three irregular blocks, topped by an irregular-shaped window for drainage.

38cfe7e611241a37.text:
Single-tower nuraghe destroyed during the clearing of the field used for cultivation, although traces of ceramic finds are still detectable during reconnaissance.

The site is difficult to read due to the presence of ongoing cultivation; it would therefore be advisable to recover the materials found at the site and document them for a partial reconstruction of the site.

38d06e44235a0a1f.text: Complex nuraghe with a single tower and a secondary tower connected by walls, with a courtyard situated between the two towers. There are also remains of walls, bunds, and wells that were used for water collection.

38dbe0248f16e0eb.text: It is an excellent example of a fortress with a wall composed of large polygonal stones arranged in a roughly circular, broken-line pattern from north to west, extending to south. To the east it takes advantage of a steep and almost vertical cliff that overlooks the Ozieri plain. To the north there is a large, flat-topped dolmenic trilite. The entrance to the south is smaller. mu

38ea08e0f8c8a8cb.text: The Tracucu Cemetery is a beautiful and extensive archaeological site located about three kilometres from Lotzorai, along the road to Talana. It comprises thirteen domus de janas, marked by wooden signs, which can be admired by following a guided path through the granitic rocks and dense vegetation.

3906ac882af98e04.text: The site, dating to the late Bronze Age (1300–1000 BC), is a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower to which eight additional towers were later attached to form a bastion. The bastion is surrounded by a megalithic curtain wall featuring five towers equipped with loopholes. For its construction, mainly granite stones were used, a material available on-site.

390e91d803df8b32.text: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined and collapsed inwards

3911c2eae41fd967.text: In this locality the remains of an extensive settlement with an associated necropolis are clearly visible. From the material found in this citadel it emerges that it was inhabited from the earliest times of the Bonnanaro, Ozieri, Monte Claro and Bell Beaker cultures, and then by the Nuragic, Phoenician-Punic and Roman peoples. It seems the village was inhabited until 500 AD and was abandoned following a fire that caused its destruction.

39150a304d600790.text:
Along the road from Samatzai towards S. Pietro.

Collapsed complex nuraghe, situated on a gentle slope with a central tower and two smaller ones. It has an elongated plan with the three towers arranged on the same longitudinal axis oriented north to south. A short distance from the central tower the basal structures of three circular huts are recorded, certainly belonging to a small surrounding village. The structures are built of marly and basaltic materials.

391c243125b48615.text: The exedra of the Giants' Tomb was cut into pieces and used in the construction of the dry stone wall.

3940d86080ca33d1.text: It is fairly well known to the local population because the lintel of the main entrance draws attention for being made of white limestone, probably from the Giombachis or Iscala Ilvena area. Here too one must speak of an advanced state of decay owing to the many collapses that the cyclopean monument has suffered. Some constructional and architectural details are nevertheless still evident.

39424b270b286720.text:
The tomb has three rooms, rectangular in plan, cut into the rock and interconnected.

It dates to the time of the Bonnanaro culture (1500–1300 BC).

394baff5037e2d84.text: "Giants' tomb of Torrà, near the tributary Rio Torrà of Rio di Posada; few remains of a large cist or corridor can be seen, almost completely dismantled. On land belonging to Antonio Nanu, it was Giovanni." With this brief description and some geographical inaccuracies (the Riu Thorra is not a tributary of the Posada but of the Mannu, which is in turn a tributary of the Posada river), Taramelli reported the presence of the giants' tomb of Thorra, without however mentioning the nearby nuraghe.

39530e5cecd691d3.text: Likely corridor nuraghe and remains of a Nuragic settlement

398ef4e7f1958984.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. In very poor condition of conservation.

39a2e753d31c3e59.text: It is a tholos nuraghe with an outer wall, located near the village and in a precarious state of conservation.

39ac00beb4bfda8c.text: Corridor nuraghe with concentric plan... (a short distance from the nuraghe there is another structure of uncertain nature, which, in my opinion, dates to the Nuragic period – see photo). From the top, the panorama is breathtaking! a 360° view of forest! to the east, the entire Supramonte stretches in the background.

39d2ca0e9e4676c5.text: A few blocks of the basal perimeter in white limestone. The entrance is visible and little else, all within a dense thicket of fetid anagyris (sa giolva). The name should derive from the place-name of the land. Hill of the liburni, a shrubby legume known for its hanging pods and the unpleasant odour given off by its leaves when touched. Shepherds believe that the leaves of this plant give a bitter taste to goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas. mu

39d7aee008358e34.text: The tomb retains only a small section of the first base course along the side of the colonial house; in the vicinity of the monument, two granite slabs of small and medium size are found, suggesting fragments of a stele.

39dfd2b566e7dcad.text: It is more likely that this structure belongs to the nuraghe "Tanca di Monsignori", mentioned in the nuragographic map by F. Nissardi (published by G. Pinza in 1901).

39e5347ddd12465b.text: The nuraghe has been completely levelled for the construction of the Church of Santa Greca. In aerial views, the circular outline at ground level is still clearly visible and likely represented its original foundation.

39fd17fe979c252b.text: The nuraghe is completely collapsed and only some residual stones remain of the entire structure.

39fe262bf01a8a94.text: The Nuraghe Tradori is built of black basalt. The entrance has a pointed arch and is very low. The chamber, from which two low corridors lead off, is circular in plan with a very high false dome (tholos) that is still intact. Outside the nuraghe there is a stretch of walling made of large stones; on its outer face, facing south-east, a passage opens that descends deep down and appears to reach beneath the nuraghe.

3a0608707d84e47a.text: The giants' tomb at Sa Presone 1 features a semicircular exedra with a front of courses. On the right side of the burial chamber, raised and covered by slabs, there is a small niche above the floor, used for placing offerings or a deceased person in a curled position.

3a12a687b6f5064c.text: Modest in overall scale, almost a little treasure; it consists of two walls of nearly squared stone masonry and has a roof made of large natural trachyte slabs.

3a1af257cfd583e5.text: Complex nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village, the structure of which cannot be defined.

3a27a1065abcf367.text:
It is striking that the monument is not signposted in any way, in an area where, moreover, there is a sign for every sheepfold. The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.

The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.

3a2a0e302a563785.text: Giants' tomb, dolmenic, partially collapsed, with only the perimetral orthostats and a lapidary lintel remaining.

3a3bc8be143f1a13.text: The complex, consisting of the nuraghe and its village, is today fully incorporated into the existing settlement, surrounded by a terraced park rich in fruit trees, aromatic herbs, and Mediterranean scrub. It was built during the Middle Bronze Age (circa 1700–1350 BC) on a small hilltop overlooking the valley of the Rio Carrabusu.

3a3da2d1915859f6.text: The Acchettas nuraghe at first glance appears completely destroyed; only part of the polygonal walls remains visible on the western side. During ground-breaking works, large amounts of debris have accumulated on the monument.

3a472bc477e7d2a5.text: Another nuraghe completely destroyed, but partially visible on the maps of Sardinia from 1954 and 1977.

3a4daf20ccd6887c.text: Area where ancient maps indicated the location of the nuraghe Nuraghessu; in this area one or more dolmen are present.

3a5388315849c685.text: San Leonardo is an ancient village in Gallura, situated near the church of the same name, a typical rural Gallurese church accompanied by a small cemetery. The remains of the San Leonardo nuraghe demonstrate the presence of inhabitants even during the Nuragic period.

3a9c96cb4b330b07.text:
The second giants' tomb, situated 100 m south-west of the nuraghe, instead has a narrow corridor 6.5 metres long inside, without a roof, the peristalith visible only in part, and to the left of the entrance an orthostat about 1 m high and traces of the exedra.

About 500 m west of the nuraghe there is an area where stretches of walling and surface material emerge, probably of Roman date.

3aaaa41717c6afab.text: Located on the southern edge of the Corraile plateau (480 m a.s.l.), (Ozieri Culture). The eight tombs that make it up, together with a small natural cave, share architectural features similar to those of the main necropolises in the area. Some tombs stand out for their monumentality and for the presence of symbolic elements closely linked to the cult.

3aabbbb96d6cec72.text:
The previously unrecorded proto-nuraghe Crapianu appears to represent a decidedly original example among the early nuragic buildings known as proto-nuraghe.

The most significant feature lies in the fact that it preserves, within a large rectangular chamber, unmistakable traces of a floor support (risega) that once supported the first-floor chamber, at a height of about two metres and fifty centimetres.

3abfd23540617b18.text:
Nearby lies the same-named domus de janas. The nuraghe is heavily eroded.

A short distance from the provincial road Florinas-Banari; a service track leading to a disused sand quarry allows closer approach to the site.

3ad7985c7fc6e38a.text: Nuraghe in very poor condition and hidden by thick undergrowth

3ae2babd755bcf43.text: The proto-nuraghe Friarosu di Mogorella has a sub-rectangular plan with short sides convex, as it includes, at the base of the masonry, three rooms: two oval and one ellipsoidal, each covered by a truncated arch.

3af8b1ff08e66d9a.text: The great burial at Zanchia shows the lower part of the bilitic stele still intact, while the upper part lies reclined upon the other stones of the tomb corridor.

3b0d8118df604cc9.text: This structure is marked as a nuragic well and is located near a livestock water trough.

3b398ed0228f5138.text: Cemeteries of domus de janas now integrated into the urban fabric of the city of Carbonia, where 25 tombs of different sizes and types have been identified. Following a major recovery in which the ancient Sardinian medau built in the 18th century was restored, the site is currently managed by the Mediterranean Cooperative, which allows free public access.

3b5b43b9fa7c8a46.text: It is an incomplete domus located within a granite monolith.

3b856c958141b99e.text: The TdG consists of two walls, each about 15 m long. Destroyed by tomb robbers. Location uncertain.

3ba3992273b035fd.text: The tower at Conca Santinta must have had a function extending beyond a purely strategic one, since many stone-working debris have been found on the site, and this is further supported by the fact that the minerals composing the outcrop have particularly favourable characteristics for use in stone-working and ceramic production.

3baea1947137f99c.text: Composed of stones driven into the ground that support a slab measuring 3 x 2 m, surrounded by an elliptical stone enclosure. The Elcomis dolmen appears to have been constructed about three centuries after Su Laccu, as its orientation (azimuth 161.9; declination –46°75) points consistently towards Alpha of the constellation of the Mosca, but in 2100 BC.

3bb2ca43adf39e57.text: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by undergrowth. Likely a complex. Of the monument, several courses of the wall are clearly visible. The perimeter of the central tower and some secondary rooms connected to it can be seen.

3bf9d65ea6b424b8.text: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower with bastions. On the IGM map this nuraghe is mistakenly identified as the nearby Sa Tiria nuraghe.

3c0580f9589c1f7d.text: Domus de janas to be verified, unnamed

3c1a74f597fd615a.text: It was indicated on ancient cadastral maps. Probable location, no traces are identifiable.

3c247545db2b0c60.text: Disappeared nuraghe but of which traces remain in local memory and the basal circle

3c2b0edb15364536.text:
The building dates from the 11th century. The remains of the wall enclosing the precinct are visible. The most precious part lies at the centre of the area, with the basin altar. The building was constructed of large, fine isodomic ashlars. Many are T-shaped.

Two "circular rooms" were joined by a sort of trapezoidal vestibule, provided with lateral stone benches. Like the nuraghi, it possesses the triad of internal perimeter niches, the western one larger, the northern and southern ones smaller and symmetrical.

3c5db0fb70eb3c6c.text:
The temple consists of a small vestibule, a narrow descending staircase covered by a stepped lintel roof, and a circular chamber covered by a tholos.

The standing structures are now limited to the keyhole-shaped perimeter wall enclosing the atrium and the well drum. The vestibule, partly paved, has a rectangular plan: the bench-seat is absent. The staircase leading down to the well chamber, with vertical walls, is made up of 12 steps.

3c68c7a262b61266.text: The domus de janas of Bruncu s'Allegau or Sa Domu 'e s'Orku was probably cut from an original natural cavity later adapted for funerary purposes. It consists of a single chamber extending horizontally with an irregular elliptical plan, 2.65 m long, 3.9 m wide and 1.5 m high from the present floor level; the ceiling still shows the small parallel grooves and hollows left by the prehistoric stonecutters.

3c6caecd406fd959.text:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.

It appears in the maps of the former cadastral survey and is listed as Nuraghe Piraruja.

3c6f576af95bbe1c.text: Subterranean temple in the Pitzu 'e toni area. It has a southern exposure. Along the entrance, a two-metre-long path splits into two branches: the right branch is narrow, while the left is wider. The same name recalls its function. In the early 1960s, during an inspection, Professor Lilliu found a pendant made of smooth animal bones.

3c6f6035b2c5165b.text: Nuraghe completely collapsed and buried, such that its structure cannot be defined.

3c869d0c2dd9726b.text: In the Is Noccus area there are two ponds, the first at the foot of the nuraghe and the other about 200 m away. The first, at the south-west base of the nuraghe, was created by using a natural lake basin. The pond is circular and shows clear signs of human intervention aimed at catching rainwater and increasing its storage capacity; boulders of various sizes can be seen placed around the edges of the basin for most of its perimeter.

3cc8ab5bf82c8717.text:
Single-tower nuraghe built with squared blocks of andesite, with fairly regular courses, in good state of conservation. The entrance is located to the east, but the chamber is not currently visible due to wall and roof collapses of the monument.

To the south there extends a wall with a straight-curvilinear profile, possibly belonging to a recent sheepfold, now dismantled.

3cd4e45ec88fca1c.text: The site, located in a currently pastureland area situated mainly on hills, is irreparably ruined. The external perimeter base can still be observed, as granite outcrops rise from the ground forming a circle.

3cdc28749352f5bc.text:
It has a single chamber.

Another domus de janas should be located nearby.

3d08f5a613491077.text:
Partially brought to light in December 2002, the Sanna nuraghe takes its name from the furriadroxiu of the same name that stands at its feet in the countryside between Santadi and Piscinas. The excavations allowed the Superintendency staff to discover a Nuragic complex, until then forgotten, and to find it in an excellent state of preservation and in a dominant position over the surrounding territory.

Today it is almost abandoned and damaged by the very excavations.

3d480d2c1a0602fb.text: Single-tower nuraghe no longer visible but noted by archaeologist Daniele Carta in his thesis (ArcheoArte 2012)

3d966179322c147b.text: Situated on a small rise in the countryside of the municipality, a short distance from the new provincial road "Ussana, Donori, Barrali". It is a prehistoric wall structure discovered during a survey beneath a clearance cairn. The wall stretch is straight, 4 metres long and 80 centimetres wide, built of large blocks, of which only the uppermost course is visible. It could also be one side of a tomb of the same period.

3d9aa99b30b2a128.text: A coursed giants' tomb, it stands on the south-west part of a hillock. The tomb preserves the outer wall face, the whole funerary corridor including the back slab and a head slab with a doorway (stele?), much of the east arm of the exedra, and an ashlar with circular hollows lying out of place.

3da896765ec82f91.text: Local folk belief, mixed with clear memories of old ancestors and confirmed by the regional newspaper "l'ISOLA" of that time, reports that in a small village some tombs were found. Among the artifacts was a statuette in the form of a woman (an ocarina, or Mother Goddess?). MU

3db8015321eb4cf2.text:
A spring above a travertine limestone cliff produces a constant dripping down a sheer wall overhanging the bed of the Flumendosa. The continuous flow of water has created limestone concretions and allowed lush maidenhair fern to grow.

This unusual cascade falls into a pool suitable for swimming in the summer months. The dripping is heavy in winter, gentle and tranquil in summer.

3dbbbc742435b8a5.text:
Corridor nuraghe with an indefinable plan because of its irregularity, and a profile that juts out and recedes.

The main entrance, facing south-east, is rectangular (height 1.70 m – width 1.40 m) with a sturdy lintel and leads into a corridor that cannot be traversed because of the collapse; a secondary entrance, collapsed and blocked, seems to open to the south-west.

The wall face survives to a maximum height of 3.60 m with six horizontal, irregular courses; the blocks are polygonal and only roughly dressed.

3dbd0ce8038934ad.text: The area contains the remains of numerous huts belonging to a Nuragic settlement; some of them were probably reused in later, though still remote, times. Most of the huts are circular and preserve only a few traces of the original structure: some have two or three discontinuous courses, others just a single course, of polyhedral boulders of various sizes. In the north-east sector there is an enclosure containing one rectangular hut divided into two rooms.

3dc5dcad7ae8d836.text:
Probable location.

It consists of 4 menhirs.

3dc79fd99d1c04e2.text: It lies a few dozen metres from the building. It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe in a fairly advanced state of decay. Some features can be seen, but they appear to be relatively recent additions and therefore not attributable to the Nuragic construction, which would seem to be a sacrificial altar. Nuraghe of the sprouted site. See Càcchile. mu

3ddbd73b9b2ebe65.text: The complex nuraghe is completely collapsed and buried. It is likely that the ashlar blocks were removed to build some structure nearby. All around there are traces of a village.

3de303c5422b5689.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The internal chamber has collapsed in its upper part, but still survives to a height of about 3 m. Inside it two facing niches can be made out, one to the west, the other to the east. The entrance, no longer existing, must have faced south, as can be deduced from the surviving structures. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of 4 m.

3debafb5cdc62551.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Despite poor conservation conditions, the circular plan characteristic of such a nuraghe, of relatively small dimensions, can still be discerned; it was built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks, with the external wall face retaining a maximum height of about 2 m.

3e0747a2cf02db33.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with the characteristic shape of a truncated cone and two superimposed chambers…. Access is through the central doorway facing south-south-east; it has a central chamber with corbelled courses closing the dome, and three side cells arranged orthogonally (90°) to the entrance. A clockwise spiral staircase leads up onto the nuraghe directly above the central chamber, where the superstructure of the second chamber is still clearly visible.

3e1e021c1a497a4e.text: Pre-Nuragic/Nuragic settlement. Remains of two huts were still present up to twenty years ago, but one of the two was dismantled to make room for ploughs.

3e2df9c05bc0e660.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Furtei. It is mentioned by Vittorio Angiu in the Geographical-Historical-Statistical-Commercial Dictionary of the States of S.M. under the entry Furtei as Nuragi-Ais.

3e316a92992b30a0.text: It is a multicompartments underground chamber.

3e33bbc38dfd7de4.text: The remains belong to a small complex nuraghe. The found debris suggests the presence of a small proto-nuraghe, possibly modified or demolished and then reconstructed as a classic nuraghe.

3e34530d6b2385c9.text:
A corridor nuraghe, affected by a conspicuous collapse, built with polygonal blocks of local stone. Among the collapse of the imposing wall face, the perimeters of the upper portions of some oval chambers can be made out.

To the north-west, traces of occupation from the protohistoric and historic periods are visible, consisting of short, semi-hidden stretches of walling.

Santoni mentions it under the name nuraghe Moru Nieddu B.

3e3bdc8c7d410d6a.text: The monument is in a good state of preservation. It consists of a rectangular lintelled entrance, from which a flight of four steps leads down to a dromos. The ceiling of the dromos is covered with a flat arch of limestone slabs, while the side walls are of dry-stone construction. At the far end of the dromos is the doorway giving access to the well chamber proper, which is permanently full of water.

3e7ac9a64ae5b742.text: Natural cave with a wide entrance followed by a step and an underlying chamber. Inside, Neolithic and Bronze Age material, belonging to the Bonannaro culture, has been found.

3e8f52ec67e7c5a3.text: Domus de janas located inside a granite quarry. Pruricellulare with an internal double pillar.

3eab75d4ef2fe041.text:
Situated between the Sas Pireddas area to the east and Riu Mortu to the south, the Domus di Istiolai is a hollow carved out of a single granite block, consisting of an atrium and a burial chamber with a rounded floor plan; the latter has a small, unnatural pit cut into the floor, probably used for votive offerings.
