The entrance faces north-north-west, and the workmanship is very careful, especially at the entrance.

3f152310249214cf.text: Single-tower with a tholos in polygonal basalt ashlar. Broken lintel. Stairwell on the left side from the entrance corridor. Two niches visible inside the chamber. Traces of huts in the vicinity.

3f1e2774ff8eec6d.text: Complex nuraghe of an evolved type, definable in plan as consisting of only the central tower.

3f3aade1fe520260.text: The archaeological complex of Piscina Caboni belongs to the Culture of the Circles of the Arzachena area, which, in earlier years, appeared to affect only the Gallurese region. Site occupation, in the absence of excavation data, dates back to the third millennium BCE.

3f4b1b6b1c03ce23.text: The nuraghe is composed of a seven-sided curtain wall, with a tower at each corner (partially visible), and a multi-lobed bastion of difficult interpretation, with an opening facing towards N.ghe Melas, or Fumiu.

3f613fff8c5ac5f7.text: Complex nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village

3f6b5fa41cff22df.text: Single-cell domus de janas on a rocky outcrop, isolated and rising above the terrain

3faab66df808feba.text: Single-tower nuraghe near Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and a small nuraghe, Nuraghe Jana II, stands nearby on the steep slope of the hill.

3fc226fae43de540.text: This is probably a coursed giants' tomb in very poor condition: it is almost indistinguishable from the surrounding rocks. The ashlars at the sides of the central doorway, the burial corridor, the courses to the right and left of it, and part of the outer walls can still be made out. It is clear that many of the stones that made up the central body and the vault have been removed and then scattered all around the tomb or thrown down into the central corridor.

3fdbcda5347d7f4e.text: The complex consists of a proto-nuraghe, a village, and a giants' tomb. The proto-nuraghe, of the "corridor" type, has a roughly elliptical plan and is built against a granitic outcrop. The masonry is composed of large polygonal granite blocks.

3fdc99e0b6564629.text:
The remains of this nuraghe are located on a trachytic outcrop guarding the Rio Tossilo, near the curve that the Birori–Cobercada road follows at the level of the Urighe nuraghe.

Unfortunately, only a few large stones are left, arranged in scattered patches, in just a few sections, in double rows. Any surveying is not possible.

3ffbc4b7680e7604.text:
In the Sas Seddas area, not far from the eponymous megalithic tombs site, some ceramic finds of certain Nuragic attribution have been recovered.

No structural traces are visible at the site. The owner of the pinnetta reports that during excavation work an unspecified “channel” cut into the rock came to light, of unknown length and depth; it has since been reburied. The ceramic material consists mainly of cooking-pot fragments.

40080f30db38748f.text: The three granite menhirs stand on the slope of the saddle: the first, aniconic (length 4.25 m; width 0.98 m; thickness 0.60 m) — pointed and split into two pieces — lies on the ground; the second — re-erected in the 1970s — is of proto-anthropomorphic type with an ogival shape and a plano-convex cross-section; the third, also proto-anthropomorphic, has an ogival shape and a flattened plano-convex cross-section. Two menhirs face each other frontally, almost as if marking a passage.

401866645ef8f3c3.text: Subterranean burial with 10 domus de janas. A site worthy of in-depth study, containing 10 convex chambers.

40201f34bd7c3ac4.text: The nuraghe, situated within the Girgini-protected area, is irrevocably ruined; what remains visible is only the base course, while various parts of the nuraghe have been reused in the construction of a wall in the immediate vicinity.

4036896550004b59.text:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower to which a bastion has been attached on the front—complete with full enclosure of the structure—containing two secondary towers that enclose a central courtyard.

The main tower (diam. 18.00 m) has an entrance oriented to the southeast (width 0.80–1.20 m), surmounted by a lintel with a drainage window.

404bce428885a7c0.text: There is no direct connection, yet it is identical to the contemporary Mesopotamian temples and embodies the 'orientalising' belief in the union of heaven and earth: sacred areas on hilltops were regarded as the meeting point between humans and the divine. The temple of Monte d'Accoddi, dating back five thousand years, is a ziggurat unique in Europe for the singularity of its architectural types. It was discovered in the mid-20th century by excavating a small hill that appeared 'artificial' in the middle of a plain.

406208a0b5ba7a80.text: Subterranean tomb consisting of two rooms. Reweilded in a later period with the addition of a dolmenic corridor; it was reused in the early Bronze Age during the Bonnanaro phase. Looted by clandestine individuals.

406d95e166cc0659.text: It is a complex nuraghe that was demolished to make way for the Roman settlement.

4070e3fdb3fe099b.text: Prehistoric megalithic funerary structure. Of the monument, the part not concealed by vegetation shows only two vertical slabs at right angles to each other.

4073df3c34287cb8.text:
Complex nuraghe, in which various structural elements, visible only in part, project against the central body, a tower made of trachyte blocks, with a circular plan. In the surrounding area, especially to the south-east, there are numerous Roman ceramic fragments.

The urban plan of Sassari (11 Dec. 2014) designates it as "Nuraghe Arcone II".

4078d0c636beb443.text: Reduced to a level of ruin like so many other cases of neglect. I regret repeating myself, but the disappointment of facing a cultural heritage that is not protected and that is not taken seriously places upon me a civic duty to publicly denounce this disregard.

4086b201195a7d24.text: The elongated ('allée couverte') dolmen of 'Tramassumele' is probably a monument of transition between Neolithic dolmen and the 'giants' tombs of the Bronze Age.

4095bb8c15d1e14f.text: The complex nuraghe, probably three-lobed, is in such a state of degradation that the structural elements are almost impossible to detect. Around the nuraghe over a large stretch, fragments of Punic and Roman ceramics are found, indicating the presence of a settlement.

40af5d750898f12e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined, collapsed and overgrown with vegetation

40b265dd7020994c.text: Within a farm, it is in good conservation condition and access is possible from the top.

40b9034e88c0983d.text: This nuraghe has a partially collapsed tholos; once inside you find the stair entrance on the left and three niches with "stipetti" in the central chamber. The niche on the right, at first sight a normal niche, contains a stair leading to a mezzanine above the nuraghe entrance, with an opening from which you can see the entrance corridor. The mezzanine has a window looking onto the central chamber.

40d0ac406cd8f609.text: These two menhirs are attributable to the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC) and, for archaeologists, represent the Mother Goddess and the Bull God, characteristic symbols of other Sardinian prehistoric monuments such as the domus de janas, inside which they were depicted, and recurring also in Nuragic civilisation, especially in the bull-shaped form of the giants' tombs. Over time they have kept their original position and their function as votive monuments.

40df5dde9dd135cf.text: In this area there were two giants' tombs, one of which has been completely dismantled. In the area where the burial structure presumably stood, scattered ashlars remain within a stand of mastic trees. Due to the local ground elevation, part of the tomb may still be buried.

40f2d9e9c47278f5.text: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of local basalt blocks; its outer wall face survives for about four to five courses with a maximum remaining height of about 2.50 m. The interior is completely filled with collapse debris. The building must have been of considerable size (diameter over 13 m) with several superimposed chambers. It now stands next to a modern building made of concrete blocks.

40f7ecbfcc005556.text: It is a large domus de janas necropolis, built on a mass of limestone. Around it, interesting Cart Ruts are visible. Some tombs are decorated with bull's-head protomes.

412d642c432e7cfd.text: It is in very poor condition and surrounded by dense vegetation.

4133295757a2f664.text: It preserves the intact tholos covered by a large slab. It is a complex structure with a lintelled entrance and a partially collapsed stairwell. On the left an opening leads to another tower in good condition but with the ashlars fallen from the tholos inside it. To reach the upper floor one must use the side facing north-east, from which to admire the 360° panorama over the village with huts still distinguishable amid dense vegetation and among the various collapses.

41354e317df98a75.text:
The cemetery is situated within a broader archaeological context that includes a village of dry-stone huts and fortified dwellings – located just a few hundred metres away – and a megalithic circle (diameter 3.00 m) at a distance of about 600 m.

The funerary complex comprises nine domus de janas with variously articulated plan layouts. Tomb I is multicellular and contains eleven successive cells.

41504b8b582a0c69.text: It is located to the south, near the border with the territory of Usellus. It was presumably of a simple type with a single tower. It is in very poor state of conservation, although it is not ruled out that its portion may have been buried over the centuries due to the action of atmospheric and human agents.

41529ea8dc9e0baf.text: Up to six courses survive for over two metres in height, in large worked sandstone blocks laid and fitted to give the tower perfect circularity. The perfection of the shape is not only horizontal but also vertical. What is visible is the central tower, and it was probably a single-tower nuraghe, but since there is a high mound to the south-east of the visible tower, the presence of something else there cannot be ruled out. The visible tower must have at least four or five courses below ground, judging by the height of the mound of ashlars and earth surrounding the nuraghe.

415811cf2072db82.text: Very buried but identifiable. During recovery work carried out by the Superintendence for Archaeological Heritage, funded by the Porto Rotondo Consortium. The so-called nuraghe, after archaeological excavations, was found to be a coastal watchtower of Punic period (4th century BC).

416a2f5ee47c0b8a.text: "On the Luras terrain there are giants' tombs, indeed, there are four of them in the same area, a rare and unique occurrence. This site has been known for a long time; one tomb was almost completely destroyed over the years, and both the superintendence and the municipality were notified, but no one ever took any action" (report).

4172679423d75a91.text: Single-tower nuraghe standing next to an agritourism farm, of which only three courses survive

41a203e06fae9fec.text: Single-tower nuraghe, preserved for only a few courses.

41b5d9954aa1c348.text: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including a pair known locally as Is ogus de monti, "the eyes of the mountain", a truly fitting nickname. A majestic staircase of about sixty steps, entirely cut into the rock, leads to the summit, from which there is a broad view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating to the 7th century BC, with an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.

41bb89ecfae13e49.text: Area where nuragic huts are found

41d9d04f62a1a59d.text: A multi-chambered domus de janas with false windows, defined by incised grooves bearing traces of red paint, and straight raised beams radiating on the ceiling to evoke a wooden roof. In the main chamber there is a sub-rectangular pilaster, of which only the lower and upper parts survive, the latter bearing an incised bull's-head protome. A Nuragic village can be sensed in the surrounding area.

420de3fa1b71163e.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe from which much of the plain below can be seen.

The nuraghe is completely ruined and on private land, but access is not difficult.

The courses below the lintel are buried.

The tholos has completely collapsed inwards, but through the rubble the spiral staircase can be made out on the left of the entrance, and a second staircase whose course is not easy to follow.

It is still worth a short visit.

423ac6ec0b1c6e6a.text: Probably four-lobed, and one of the most imposing in the area. It consists of a central tower enclosed in a bastion with three transverse front towers. The lintel is currently visible at the level of the collapse that fills the courtyard. From inside the chamber the entrance corridor is visible. The stair leading to the upper part of the tower, which very probably had two storeys given the extent of the collapse on the north side, must have started from it.

425e5f5780c48390.text: A dozen circular huts and enclosures.

4266f0b57e0c30e6.text: The orthostats of the large exedra without a stele stand out. It is broken and lies scattered on the ground in front. In place of the stele, an olive tree has grown. A small fragment of the exedra remains at the back, set on a pedestal, which allows an understanding of the monument's original scale.

426b88c180a4a842.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building is in a fair state of preservation despite the considerable alterations it has undergone. It has a surviving height of about 5 m. The outer wall face is clearly visible and better preserved on the north-east side, while on the southern side it is heavily altered and covered with vegetation. (Pruna on the I.G.M. map)

427297a36a4f8367.text: Single-tower in excellent condition, with walls 8/9 metres thick, internally inaccessible, with ancient oak trees surrounding it. It offers a magnificent view down to Gallura.

42c76f96b0b436b2.text: A burial of the Nuragic period with isodomic masonry. Of the tomb, partially demolished, only the burial corridor, the apse, and some elements of the left arm of the exedra remain.

42e7c676d02159c0.text:
Nuraghe today completely demolished, with only a fragment of the foundation remaining.

Among the evolved nuraghes of Serrenti, this one belongs to the type with concentric additions: it is located at Nuraxi, four-lobed, in shape similar to Su Nuraxi of Barumini (Lower Nuragic I phase of Lilliu) and to that of Bruncu Siliqua, featuring a central tower 14 m in diameter and at least three secondary towers.

42ef9cfb8a9a487f.text: Probably dismantled after the construction of the adjacent houses.

42f404f558829541.text:
The archaeological area of Cuccuru Sa Cresia Arta, in the territory of Soleminis, lies on a hillock about 40 metres above the level of the farm track that gives access to it, roughly 250 metres south-west of Soleminis, in the hinterland of the Gulf of Cagliari.

The archaeological excavation, funded by the municipal administration, forms part of a wider programme to enhance the archaeological areas of the municipality of Soleminis, agreed long ago with the Superintendency.

4306897c75dbf215.text: Remains of structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building, now almost completely destroyed, consists of some blocks from the base course and part of what was intended to be the left pillar of the entrance, oriented to the south. The construction material is local basalt. Nearby, there are accumulations of lithic material derived from the nuraghe structures.

432afe4ed89b7c75.text: The monument, built of granite stones and preserved to a maximum height of 3 m, features an architraved entrance leading to a corridor with a flat-laid roof, accessible only for a short stretch due to a collapse.

43639c75be57b7d8.text: Site completely eroded and buried. It is evident that a village, probably Nuragic or pre-Nuragic, once occupied a large area. Apart from a few scattered ashlars, only a few hut or nuraghe walls remain visible.

436b9db56b8cb563.text: Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

438c85345f112db2.text: From the top of a hilltop, the surrounding landscape is visible, where, at a small drop of the river Iscanneddu, there were two water mills. It is a single-tower nuraghe with only a few basal circles of medium-sized stones, partly roughly shaped. Its name undoubtedly derives from the medieval period, when monastic orders established themselves in the area (X–XI centuries).

439ecd3bb982c510.text: It is a singular corridor nuraghe, complex and irregular, composed of three large megalithic bodies placed side by side and various secondary constructions. It has a surviving height of over 6 metres and was built on a projecting rock outcrop using polyhedral basalt blocks stacked dry in polygonal masonry. The nuraghe dates back, in its initial construction phase, to the early Bronze Age.

43a0fee6b414e94f.text: Tall three metres, broken transversely at mid-height and cracked at the base from the impact of a mechanical vomer, it features at the top a kind of smooth sub-oval mask. The design extends linearly along the sides, and at the apex appears almost crowned by a distinct bull's head ornament. The monument represents a unique example on the island, but possibly also in continental megalithic sculpture.

43a69580d87a07fd.text: Circled giants' tomb heavily collapsed, with part of the corridor and lintel remaining. The monument features a "filari" type, consisting of a burial constructed from courses of stacked blocks, with a elongated burial chamber in rectangular plan, preceded by an entrance, followed by a dromos, and ending in an abside.

43a711757861ccaf.text: Although reduced to ruin, some basic elements can be identified that highlight the structure of the emergency. The cist is formed with a varied stone masonry, fairly squared, upon which some covering elements are placed. The presence of the exedra, composed of stones set in a cut, is also evident, although some of them have been destroyed and lie on the ground. mu

43b0722bf661067c.text: It is a complex nuraghe, composed of a central tower and four attached towers, only slightly evident. The central tower is the only one in good preservation; it has two superimposed levels, the lower one intact, while the upper one lacks its tholos roof. On the upper level there is a large window facing the entrance.

43b32e1b5d0c10f0.text:
Nuragic settlement, attested by a demolished single-tower nuraghe and Middle Bronze Age pottery.

Decontextualised and illegible site, although the recovery of the materials found on the spot, the relevant documentation, and the contextualisation of the whole are desirable.

43e37ff6ef6bb05f.text: This is a site where the ruins of two single-tower nuraghi (huts) are found; of both, the base survives to a maximum height of one metre and a diameter of about 6

44002dd70b30f08d.text: Of the monument, in very poor condition, only some fragments of the first base course are visible, in pink trachyte.

443bc1c3b50a819a.text: The Battizzone nuraghe is a three-lobed type, with towers joined by an outer wall that forms an internal courtyard at the front. At present the courtyard and the lateral towers are completely filled with collapse debris, making access to the central tower impossible; the entrance lintel is partly visible. A corridor is also visible in the courtyard area, which probably served as the entrance to one of the lateral towers and is notable for its considerable height.

444f2ff2faa1e407.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe, built of local polygonal basalt blocks, survives in its outer wall face to a maximum height of just over 4 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the remaining part is filled with the same collapse material. The entrance, identifiable to the south, is lintelled with a height of 1.20 m. The workmanship of the lintel and jambs is fairly rough, with barely dressed blocks.

44683f91e1475a87.text: Nuraghe "a tancato", with a central tower and an additional tower connected by bastions. Traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

44761aa2a6cacbfb.text: Unfortunately, the destructive actions of treasure hunters have put the majority of the sites in the commune of Chiaramonti at risk. The loss of further historical and artistic testimonies further diminishes its cultural heritage. The heritage left by our ancestors must be part of our history, to help us better understand the path we should follow for the future. mu

44837832b82bffdd.text: Nuraghe partially destroyed by quarry work. The site is of particular interest because of the discovery in the area of three swords, with pistil-shaped blades and a central rib, and a tang to which two wings with holes for fixing the handle are attached, recovered during the 1950s. This typically Iberian type finds comparisons with specimens from the territory of Baunei, and with the sword resting on the shoulder of the “Warrior” of Uta.

449a4fea021d77d1.text: Inside there is a flat-laid corridor, a semicircular niche, a staircase leading to the upper level, and a central chamber; originally vaulted in tholos form but now without a roof, it has the classic circular plan with three niches arranged in a cross. The external wall, up to 4 m high, is composed of medium to large trachyte stones.

449af16923ad1f24.text: Complex nuraghe heavily collapsed, making it difficult to determine its original form.

449dc0bdf48e6b3e.text:
The necropolis comprises 18 domus de janas, all multi-chambered with up to 12 rooms, richly adorned with pilasters, panels, false doors, bull's-head protomes, chevrons and other spiral or wolf's-tooth motifs.

Seven tombs reproduce pre-Nuragic dwellings: single- or double-pitched roofs, horizontal or sloping, with or without central beams and side rafters, supported or not by pillars, all carved in the rock. One has an architectural façade with a carved arched stele.

44afed795e140f3a.text: Nuraghe destroyed by agricultural mechanization, now no longer visible

44b0fe21de75cbc6.text: Corridor nuraghe, also known as Runalgalva.

44c31a3a2ed72061.text: Unlikely remains of a nuragic structure.

44c421e17e12b65d.text: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghe. It is very difficult to identify amid the dense vegetation, and only about three courses of the base remain, composed of large polygonal basaltic blocks. The rest of the structure has collapsed, and debris fills the lower portion. Despite the poor conditions, the features can be interpreted as a small, simple single-tower nuraghe.

450bb250ccac2834.text: At the foot of the hill, once used as a stone quarry, within the inhabited centre of Monastir, in the south-western area, near Via Progresso no. 80, a giants' tomb was discovered during archaeological excavation, yielding numerous human bone remains.

452c8b7e7d12b5e9.text: The probable Nuragic village occupies an area extending from the edges of the plateau towards the northeast slope of the mountain. Remains of various circular huts are present, with only one or two courses and partial collapses at the centre. The best preserved hut is oval in shape and likely reused in more recent times. There are enclosures with cyclopean walls.

453c90dce40fbaae.text: Located on a promontory overlooking the municipal road from Villaurbana to the locality 'S'utturu on cardu'. The tower is largely collapsed and inaccessible.

45509bd57a02c0f2.text: Built on the edge of a trachyte bastion, overlooking a natural route, about a hundred metres north of a giants' tomb situated downhill, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a stair in the corridor and a chamber flanked by three niches. To the west, in the sector not naturally defended by the vertical rock face, are the remains of a massive outer wall, while the rocky profile on which the tower stands also appears to be reinforced by coursed wall structures.

45535fc8ce5955e4.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from polygonal basaltic blocks. Despite the dense vegetation, the circular plan can be discerned and about five courses, though somewhat disconnected, on the north-northeast exposed side are visible. The entrance, identifiable to the east, shows a collapsed pillar on the right side and the lintel placed in an inclined position.

45590c0649438da4.text: It is a complex nuraghe of unclear reading, consisting of a main tower and remains of two other possible towers. The nuraghe is built with roughly hewn blocks of sandstone and shale, set in polygonal masonry. In the west/south-west area, the wall structure encloses a rocky spur.

455cd9030ec9515e.text: A burial of the Nuragic period, almost completely destroyed. On the ground surface, the base profile of the tomb is visible, along with some worked ashlar stones. In particular, a short distance away, two monolithic arches belonging to the apsidal section of the tomb are present.

4568c3e8d90dcc3e.text: It is named after the family that owned the land on which it is situated. The nuraghe is completely collapsed and certainly quadrilobate. It is located 600 m from the palace of Barumini.

456a5fd1e5c4b81c.text: During excavation, it shows 2 (possibly 3) sacred wells opening onto a large open area paved with slabs, and a hut located within the paved area, which contains a hole through which water can be seen flowing.

457b38d75045ece3.text: Sparingly visible and identifiable, completely engulfed by mastic and cisto. Presence of numerous large trachyte boulders.

45a2f98240b6d5cb.text: It appears ruined and covered by thick patches of brambles and thorny bushes.

45b4dbb0ffb279f6.text: The monument, of simple type, stands at the edge of a small clearing on a granite outcrop that is incorporated into the walls for long stretches. Its outer plan is vaguely elliptical, with a lintelled entrance leading into a corridor 3.50 m long; to the left of this corridor another lintelled doorway presumably gives access to a staircase, or at any rate to a beaten floor that in ancient times must have led to a terraced space.

45d063865911b5e8.text: Four-tower nuraghe, with towers arranged in a cross around a large courtyard. It consists of a central tower, about 3 m high, connected to two secondary towers via a curtain wall. Some studies define the complex as quadrilobate with concentric addition.

45d96ccba04c1020.text: It is also known by the place name of the adjacent land, "sas Damas", which I believe is the older and more appropriate one, since it is closely linked with sa Domos de sas Fadas which by extension becomes Dama = lady. It was found by chance during extension work on a house, now the Agriturismo Sas Damas Doneddu-Murgia, and was rich in grave goods that were donated to the local museum in Perfugas SS.

45f2b87a2b800f2a.text:
This is a three-lobed nuraghe of particular importance because of its position, size and state of preservation. It lies in the Marghine sub-region, in the territory of the municipality of Bortigali, at an altitude of 785 metres, from which a vast portion of central Sardinia can be seen.

The site stands at the foot of Monte Cuguruttu (867 metres), in a position that ranges from the nearby Monte Santu Padre (1,025 metres) to the more distant mountains

45f86053e1d08373.text: Of this burial only the stele and part of the exedra remain.

461ecc5251b21d18.text: Quadrilobate complex nuraghe. Visible are traces of a central tower and three additional towers with bastions, whose foundations remain in very poor condition. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

4653a2d52104b93e.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower, with a facade featuring two additional towers. Surrounding it are the remains of what must have been the village.

46695eddf95f9043.text: Settlement of which only faint traces remain, located on the hill in front of Monte Cannas in a place not recommended for visits because it was affected in the 1930s–1940s by quarrying activities, with dangerous, unenclosed areas. The settlement dates from the Bronze Age to the Roman period, passing through the Nuragic culture.

466b848fb94e3e14.text:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe standing in the middle of the dense holm-oak and downy-oak woodland of the Sos Paris area, Codinazza locality. Four basal courses built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt are visible, reaching a maximum surviving height of about 2.50 m. The base diameter of the nuraghe is about 13 m.

The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part and the surviving portion is covered by a substantial fill of collapse debris.

469c415559be83dc.text: Complex nuraghe of which two towers are still visible.

46ae43563a3ec92a.text: Single-tower nuraghe in relatively good condition with the tholos intact. It is located at the boundary between two fields and is accessible only through a privately owned plot cultivated as a garden.

46baf12ec3bf7a27.text: The domus de janas at Bonorchis is a single-chamber tomb, very small, with a wide and well-crafted entrance portal.

46e61f61863ac3c4.text: Nuraghe heavily collapsed, located in the heart of the city

46f2805add5ae4f9.text: The necropolis of Museddu is located within the park of petroglyphs; it consists of 18 domus de janas, with simple planimetric layouts, either a quadrangular cell preceded by a small pavilion, or two or three cells arranged in longitudinal projection.

4708cc4a0d698846.text: The cemetery is located in the municipality of Usini. It consists of three domus, one of which has bull's-head protomes and another repurposed as an underground church.

47562430129750df.text:
Sacred well, located inside the Romanesque chapel of the 13th century dedicated to Sant'Antonio da Padova.

Access is via a hatch leading to a series of stairs that lead to the sacred well, which is perfectly positioned directly beneath the Christian altar.

475fbc1687bfb2ec.text: Nuraghe apparently single-tower. It could belong to the category of "uncompleted nuraghes".

476babb9f3ef81e6.text: The nuraghe is located in the COMUNE DI MURAVERA. The entire upper complex, four-lobed with some semi-quadrangular towers, extends along a north-west/south-east axis of about 53 m and an east/west axis of about 20–25 m. The outer curtain wall can be traced only along its eastern stretch and a short southern section: it is an imposing structure with a broad wall thickness that served to close the gaps in the pre-existing natural rock bastion.

476d2ad653c9a359.text: The Phoenician settlement arose in the area of a previous Nuragic settlement, as the structures uncovered by excavation show the reuse of various elements from the indigenous settlement. Indeed, currently visible are a megalithic enclosure and a Nuragic structure adapted and incorporated into a wall trace that appears further surrounded by a fortified line.

477d09648d89619b.text: Quadrilobate nuraghe Alvu, built with squared white stones, with numerous hut foundations surrounding it. It exhibits particular architectural features in the way the corner walls are interlocked, a detail not found in other nuraghes.

477e66a822138930.text: It lies in the municipality of Lodine (NU). A single-tower nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins. It is situated very close to Sos Nuragheddos 1. Further information can be found in the book *Archeologia in Barbagia* by M.A. Mele.

477f16cae0c51c2c.text: The village that developed in the subsequent phase of recent Bronze (1365–1200 BC) is characterized by the presence of numerous dug wells located near residential structures, some of which are set into the ground, while others are built with a masonry base. Currently, after recent excavations, the area has been fully covered.

478ae26b633f9ab1.text: Proto-nuraghe partially collapsed and covered by a dense vegetation layer

479c023b2950d1f1.text: Remains of the nuraghe Sos Iscaledos, greatly damaged.

47a9825ba1c831f3.text:
The complex stands on the summit of Monte Colbu overlooking the plain of Olbia.

The nuraghe, surrounded by a wall that originally must have exceeded 5 metres in height and has two entrances (one to the north and one to the south), is a single-tower type. The entrance corridor contains a small niche and part of the stairwell that led to the terrace of the upper floor. The central chamber, which has a small well, was covered by a tholos.

47b933232bdf8731.text: Single-tower nuraghe near Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and another nuraghe, Nuraghe Jana, stands nearby on the steep slope of the hill.

47cd6e1d94784cde.text: Nuraghe in excellent condition, although surrounded by vegetation. The internal tholos is intact.

47d6391e9db51e6e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, it marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Villamar and Pauli Arbarei.

47dfca3139fdd112.text: Remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt.

480ad095cbed587b.text: The basaltic pillars are majestic basalt formations whose presence indicates a history of submarine eruptions or the existence of ancient volcanoes now extinct. Is Aruttas Santas are a typical example of these basaltic formations, located on Monte Arci in the territory of Villaurbana.

483369ec5dbd5e04.text: It is in poor conservation. At the Sassari Museum the closure door is on display, but the tomb is incorrectly named Mesu e Rios.

485244015a104d65.text:
The Nuragic village-sacred site of Abini is one of the most famous and important in Sardinian nuragic archaeology.

It consists of numerous huts and a sacred well protected by a enclosure. The huts are mostly circular in plan.

48535ab8b8715c3e.text: It is a nuraghe left incomplete, notable for the size of the lintel above the entrance.

488678acdcda55a2.text: At the level of the great ruin, only a few polygonal stones from the basal circles remain, often roughly shaped. The main entrance is evident in the south-east direction. The surrounding area is rich in ancient traces and artifacts. Of interest is a structure on bachile that may date back only a few centuries.

4898294e27b3e2c7.text: Remains of a domus de janas

48bfc2469b1278b1.text: Hidden from view behind a granitic outcrop, the nuraghe appears partially ruined. On site a menhir is present, from which the settlement and the region likely derive their name. Possible presence of a village.

48c0eb75e1307d5e.text: It is a corridor nuraghe of difficult detection due to its poor state of conservation and the rubble from collapses that prevent its reading.

48cb34d99c98d1bc.text: Part of it is periodically submerged by the level of the artificial basin of Omodeo.

48ddcce21cfd8d46.text: In Florinas, among cultivated fields, we find this small proto-nuraghe known as Urzeghe, "characterized by a corridor-like structure with parallel corridors attached to a small circular tower."

4933310016fb9bd5.text: Three metres of approach, a lintel at the west, a row of external blocks; particularly interesting is a block with a large cup. There would be another section of approach, but it is not accessible and even less documentable due to trees.

4947399464e6234e.text: The name derives from the toponym of the land, which at the time referred to the bull god's snout present in the nearby domus, but also very likely refers to a more recent medieval or even nineteenth-century period, when the sound of the waterfall, known locally as "su mummuttu de s'abba cando sicche addobat dae punta de sas roccas aintro de sa peschina, faghet unu murrunzu mannu", was heard during winter.

496e40a3934b8373.text:
The corridor tomb has been attributed to the Nuragic period.

The baetyls recovered during surface surveys date to the Roman imperial and late antique periods. Repeated surface surveys have led to the discovery of baetyls and laterite, likely belonging to a necropolis.

49a6881df945ad6f.text:
Three hypogeic tombs on the slope of a small rise (244 m). The first has a single elliptical oven-shaped cell. The second consists of an atrium, an antechamber and a quadrangular burial chamber with a niche on the right-hand wall. On the left a wider raised cell with two small niches and a relief decoration depicting two human faces.

The third tomb, further downhill than the other two, is of the more regular type with atrium, antechamber and cell.

49bc1faf89643f00.text:
At Sa Turricula the first phase of the Nuragic civilisation is recognised. The site comprises the nuraghe, the village and, a short distance away, two giants' tombs, a well, and the Funtan'e Casu dolmen.

Sa Turricula does not allow an easy reading of the structures. It is choked with vegetation but, once you reach the top of the hill on which it stands, you enjoy a breathtaking view over the whole surrounding territory.

The nuraghe probably belongs to the corridor nuraghe type.

Nearby are

49d50868707bb680.text: The Bau ' Tanca talana nuraghe rises at an elevation of 1,122 m a.s.l. and is surrounded by a village, where traces of some huts' filaments and stone accumulations used in their construction are still visible. Notable for the unusual symmetry of the village nuclei.

49d8f3ac1aa70ef4.text: Of the nuraghe tower only very little remains. The lintel and three courses. Around the ruins of a small village.

49d901b80c02bb51.text: The structure identified here has an unclear form; it may represent a small complex nuraghe built upon a previous proto-nuraghe. Fragments of ceramics from the Nur I-IIA/B periods are observed nearby. It could also be a small mixed nuraghe.

49e0e7768858b8e5.text: A short distance from the Rio Su Hannavagliu and about a few hundred metres from the nuraghe Luduruju.

49fa4a5a18aafce2.text:
A nuraghe, a menhir, a wall, and finally a domus de janas with a façade.

Ivano Sotgiu, in love with his own village, was out gathering asparagus when he reported this site where, within a couple of hundred metres, there are monuments dating from the Abealzu culture, between 2700 and 2400 BC, perhaps earlier with the menhir, the Early Bronze Age with the Nuragic wall, the Bronze Age and up to the Roman period, marked by the probable tombs.

4a368c8e43ac695d.text: The site has yielded a two-chambered hypogeum burial cut into the southern wall of the plateau, whose upper part shows a slab of natural rock that, seen from the front, gives the monument a megalithic appearance; a small dolmen; a giants' tomb; a spring; a megalithic wall with traces of later adaptations; and a corridor nuraghe. The corridor wall includes boulders of considerable size, some of which bear linear incisions.

4a3c8687dce3bea3.text:
It stands on a small rise from which the surrounding view can be appreciated. It is a single-tower nuraghe about 11 metres high with a tholos roof. Built of large blocks of dark basalt which, together with yellow lichens, give it its characteristic colouring (hence the name: in Sardinian nieddu means black, dark).

The tower has two openings: an entrance at the base, still partly buried, and, almost at the top, a large window.

4a558d6c0f23a3ca.text: Remains of about twelve huts and a perimeter wall.

4a5686e39fe22e04.text: The Prunaiola dolmen is a funerary archaeological monument situated on a small plateau in the territory of Torralba, in north-western Sardinia. It lies a short distance from the Carlo Felice state road 131 and in the immediate vicinity of the Cabu Abbas giants' tomb and two domus de janas, in an area rich in archaeological evidence documenting the continuity of human settlement from prehistory.

4a8a56abf5529198.text:
It consists of a series of chambers opening onto the western flank of a low limestone hill. The main nucleus, the result of various transformations relating to different phases of use over the centuries, comprises three large cells linked together and arranged in succession from north to south.

The chambers look out onto a narrow terrace; the rock face has two narrow flights of steps by which the plateau above can be reached.

4a94df7e259508fc.text: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with the most significant elements missing. It retains the burial corridor.

4a963b471b8faf0c.text: It is located in the territory of the comune of Putifigari (SS). Underground tomb (domus de janas) with a notably buried entrance, about two metres below road and field level. It consists of a main cell with pilasters and three smaller lateral cells. The double-slope roof is particularly noteworthy.

4ab18d99e272d056.text: Part of the nuraghe has been altered and adapted for the construction of a pinnetto.

4ab3285a2a339abc.text: The monument, with a subcircular plan, is situated almost at the summit of a steep and wooded hillside, currently used for sheep grazing. Three blocks of the left entrance pillar remain, oriented to the north, and two of the right pillar. The nuraghe, built with rough polygonal masonry and frequent use of zeppe, is composed of granite blocks of medium and large dimensions, only roughly shaped.

4adb4b1c4161cc09.text: About 200 m from the second giants' tomb there are buildings of Nuragic origin whose function cannot be determined, mainly because of later alterations carried out at different times (some of them recent) and the lack of archaeological study. The surviving structures of probable Nuragic origin consist of an enclosure with cyclopean walls built of roughly dressed boulders, and the remains of two probable huts.

4adc98a445b6d976.text: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined. Part of it lies beneath a public reservoir.

4b0789aa767d435f.text: The monument, also known in the literature as “Pranu Nuracci”, is a complex polylobed nuraghe. Two lateral towers, the perimeter walls and the central tower survive. The south-western lateral tower and the northern one survive to a height of about 4–5 courses. The central tower, in good condition, has 12 courses of polygonal masonry with large, barely dressed blocks, a south-east entrance with a monolithic lintel.

4b0ccafc5d314072.text: The dolmen is composed of four remaining orthostatic slabs enclosing a polygonal space (1.86 x 1.40 m), bounded at the top by a large slab, roughly shaped, of variable thickness and with a rounded profile.

4b1e53a8412bdd5a.text: Single-tower nuraghe in the territory of Oniferi, located just tens of metres from the necropolis of Sas Concas, is situated in the valley below near the river. Only some blocks remain visible.

4b20ae9dbb756720.text: The nuraghe, built of schist, is constructed with quadrangular blocks laid in regular courses, set in a layer of ochre-coloured clay. It consists of a main tower and an adjoining chamber joined to the first by a short curtain wall. In the inner wall face of the tower various voids can be seen that must have served to anchor a wooden mezzanine. At the foot of this nuraghe lie the huts of the Nuragic village.

4b51ccc820474459.text: Name and/or location might not be accurate.

4b59d49cec13321e.text: It is a domus de janas necropolis facing the Gulf of Carbonara, located in the area of Spiaggia del Riso. Of the entire necropolis, only one tomb has remained intact: it is a truly fascinating monument that projects the territory back in time by about six millennia.

4b69da1c8d3c5b17.text: In the fissure there is a staircase of squared basalt stone, one metre wide, composed of three flights, two visible and the third covered by debris, separated by two landings. All the steps consist of two squared basalt blocks cut 'to measure' and laid with a wedge-shaped block inserted between them. Some have circular hollows cut into them, interpretable as cup-marks with a lustral function; on others, mammillary reliefs stand out.

4b83b9c4d583fa39.text: Nuraghe completely collapsed, only some courses remain among the dense Mediterranean scrub.

4b869257cb45ac29.text:
Complex nuraghe hidden beneath a conspicuous collapse. A large village of huts in the south-southwest is entirely covered by bushes. Near the southern periphery of the village, a building with straight walls made of squared blocks might date back to the Nuragic period.

On the hill to the west of the main ridge, a Nuragic structure—already considered a giants' tomb—appears to be actually a circular building ("tower-hut?").

4b95e982e0dd7c7c.text: The front part has collapsed, while the rear part is fairly well preserved. The rectangular burial corridor is bounded on one side by a slab, while the side walls consist of a series of blocks supporting small stones. The surviving height is about 130 cm. The entire upper surface is covered with a myriad of cupmarks (small cavities with magic-sacred functions).

4bc158a807d60116.text: It retains the tholos intact except for the closure slab.

4c04b38b2dbd5038.text: The Asusa nuraghe, built around 1300 BC, consists of two towers projecting over a courtyard and features its main entrance to the east. Inside one of the internal rooms, archaeologists have uncovered a circular arrangement possibly related to a well or a cistern, still to be explored.

4c054f99ea10c8fe.text: The dolmen is located on a basaltic outcrop on the northern bank of the Riu Coraggiu, about 200 metres north of the Nuraghe Nela. The burial chamber is currently enclosed by three orthostats, on which rests a large covering slab.

4c0c22c54a3f9bae.text: In total state of ruin, it is named after the toponym of the land or the owner of the land itself. mu

4c23601116c8c738.text:
The tower, circular in plan (diam. 10.65 x 10.12 m), survives to a maximum height of 4.40 m on the north-east side, while the minimum is 3 m on the south-west. The masonry consists of trachyte blocks roughly dressed with some care and laid in fairly regular horizontal courses. The wall thickness is 3.30 m on the north-east, 4 m on the south and 3 m on the north-west.

The interior of the nuraghe is entered through a rectangular doorway (h. 1.70 m – w. 0.90 m), lintelled, oriented to the south-east and slightly splayed inwards.

4c3298150b0d7221.text: The cemetery consists of two multicellular domus de janas dug into limestone, plus a third one begun (only the dromos has been excavated) and never completed. One of the two tombs opens into the wall near the cemetery, while the second, together with the unfinished tomb, opens along the edge of the plateau to the south-east.

4c4b11526e6da6b4.text: It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe where the tholos is still intact. Continuing up the staircase, which winds clockwise, certain constructional features emerge that are similar to other sites in the territory of Chiaramonti — a distinction made today that did not exist three thousand years ago, since the territory was a contiguous extension of that of Ploaghe. m.u

4c56e72cac969fc6.text:
Practically unknown and inside a private property. The monument, excavated and cleared in recent times, is perfectly legible and defined in all its components: the corridor, which preserves its intact floor of granite slabs, the apse and the two wings of the exedra.

It lies to the west of Santa Reparata.

The structure is built on a very slight rise with the exedra clearly raised. A linear bench is present in the front part of the exedra, a feature often found in other giants' tombs.

4c65193efb369b76.text: The Maletta II nuraghe, located at 264 m a.s.l., is now almost completely destroyed due to continuous agricultural activities that have affected the entire area, one of the most intensively exploited regions of the Sinis agricultural zone, and retains only a very fragmented section of the base row.

4c6bf3553383f463.text: Single-tower nuraghe on a hilltop with only a few courses of stone preserved. From this nuraghe you can clearly see the Nuraghe su Stiddiu, Nuraghe su Bobboi, and the hill where the Nuraghe di Crabili Simoni stood, with the megalithic altar at its foot. A few hundred metres from the nuraghe lies the Mitza Aramu spring.

4c7605f05ffbb555.text: In photographs the Longu nuraghe looks like an imposing single-tower nuraghe. Unfortunately there is no detailed description.

4c777ef88695cc21.text: The Nissardi in 1901 (map included in G. Pinza's volume) indicated a giants' tomb slightly south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that is indeed located within the perimeter of the airport.

4c83f385faf0c067.text: These are the ruins of a structure built of large blocks, completely buried; only a few remains appear on the surface. Some years ago a farm vehicle removed one of the large surface boulders, revealing an opening through which it was possible to enter the structure. It is, in all probability, a silo for water storage or provisions. The shape is a truncated cone with a bulge at the bottom. Diameter at the base 1.55 m; height 2.73 m.

4cc88cf14028a810.text: Until halfway through the last century, remains of various nuraghes could be seen, together with many basaltic ashlar of different shapes and sizes.

4cdaef2525334e44.text: Damaged nuraghe of which no description is available

4ce179c7b7b16258.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period in very poor condition of conservation.

The corridor and, with difficulty, the exedra are visible in the isodomic masonry type.

4d01cd06ceed12b9.text: A tholos nuraghe, presumably single-tower, although its poor state of preservation and the dense vegetation cover prevent a full reading of the monument. Built of polygonal basalt blocks, the outer wall face on the west side survives to a maximum height of about 3.50 m. The nuraghe has been heavily robbed, as can be deduced from the heaps of large blocks on the plateau to the north of it.

4d0289164148b3a2.text: Circle of large stones but without a foundation, thus its attribution is questionable. This structure has so far been classified as a "nuraghe", assigned the function of "meda" as an entrance to the cove.

4d436e46fc4a8194.text:
The building, one of the best known on the island, is a complex type, consisting of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion with an open courtyard.

It was defended by an outer wall, recorded by General Della Marmora, which is now barely legible on the ground surface.

The bastion (height 8.80 m) incorporates four towers linked by curtain walls with a concave-convex profile, built of roughly dressed basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses.

4d4aef7ac582a335.text: Very little of the tomb remains. The baetyls are five and are located in the territory of the comune of Dualchi (NU).

4d6751270a673507.text: The summit of Monte 'E Mesu is a small oval plateau. At one end stands the eponymous nuraghe, built almost sheer on the rock. On a small natural terrace below the nuraghe there are traces of huts and other evidence of the Nuragic period, such as boulders with bull-shaped carvings, lying in a state of total abandonment and looking, one might even say, weary of the multi-millennial life they carry on their shoulders.

4d9eb5370002b8af.text: In 1942 a stonemason from Donori, while breaking up a block of granite to obtain building stones, found 53 coins beneath the block bearing the effigy of Emperor Antoninus Pius, that of Trajan, of Empress Faustina and other rulers with indecipherable names. The nuraghe must have been very large, because despite being considerably damaged and covered by shrubs and various stones gathered nearby, the quantity of scattered boulders is considerable.

4db8ce30e2a9edbd.text: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on the tip of a limestone hill featuring karst caves used from the Neolithic period onwards. Three rows of stones, up to 25 metres long, are clearly visible.

4db938a974ca561d.text: Partially eroded, invaded by vegetation, and difficult to explore. The central chamber, the entrance, and the circular corridor remain clearly visible.

4dc3f12f543471c9.text: The Seruci Nuragic complex consists of a multi-lobed nuraghe with five towers and a central courtyard, and a village of about a hundred huts covering five hectares in a strategic position overlooking the Gulf of Leone. The village is organised into small quarters with streets and central squares. Of particular interest is a hut of remarkable size, probably used for meetings of the heads of families.

4df9cca66f4864c9.text: The tomb is completely covered by vegetation; some blocks aligned can be seen through the grass. The presence of another tomb at the site is noted, possibly belonging to a heap of blocks visible among the vegetation.

4e161fa9c0595a4f.text:
These are three hypogea cut into a trachyandesite outcrop inside a private property.

Domus I has a short dromos entrance, an antechamber that opens onto two successive cells along the same axis. The Domus has no particular decoration.

Domus II and III: the first is full of water, but its wide entrance can be admired; the second is completely overgrown with vegetation to the point that it was not possible to explore it.

There are probably other hypogea.

4e223b5ffb9d58b7.text: The tomb is not in a good state of preservation. However, the large stele can still be seen in its original position, of which only the lower, trapezoidal part survives, while the arched top is missing; a fragment of it can be seen fallen inside the chamber. Practically nothing of the exedra survives. The burial chamber, also poorly preserved, is built of slabs set vertically into the ground.

4e359c4ea1c5967b.text: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a transverse addition followed the original tower.

4e579a18dbf74d7c.text: The Nuraghe Santu Juanni or San Giovanni lies about 1 km north of Villaurbana in the territory of Siamanna. It is a single-tower nuraghe built of roughly dressed basalt blocks. The entrance corridor is lintelled and leads to a chamber where the tholos is still intact. The upper floor, now collapsed, is overgrown with shrubs and prickly pears.

4e7e65aeb9f77665.text: In 1968, about 150 metres from the entrance, the Treasure Chamber was found: hundreds of bowls were stacked in three large piles. A broken stalagmitic column served as an altar: a bronze tripod, a votive boat, several daggers, bracelets and rings were placed on it. Beside the altar was the hearth, where animal bones were found, evidence of ritual sacrifices. The C14 dating falls between 820 and 730 BC.

4e8adec710a688e5.text: Damaged nuraghe of which it is not possible to define shape and dimensions

4e95a7921ae1afda.text: The Aeddos nuraghe stands at 368 metres above sea level in the "sa serra" plateau of Orotelli. The first construction dates to the Bronze Age (1300–900 BC). The nuraghe has a three-lobed structure, composed of a central tower and three concentric towers. It is built with large polycarved granite blocks from the local area arranged in irregular courses. The height of the visible wall from the central tower reaches 8.30 metres.

4e9638da32383021.text: The giants' tomb of "Sa Sedda 'e Sena", known as "Sa Tanchitta", is notable for having been built in the Nuragic period and later adapted to an even older funerary structure dating to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC) of the "Covered Alley" type. Of this funerary monument, the burial chamber, about 10 metres long, can still be observed today.

4eada115a6cc4670.text: It is a tomb with an architectural façade, greatly modified and reused in medieval and modern times, blending the features of domus de janas and giants' tombs.

4eb7dadd599d399b.text: Nuraghe destroyed by the scolopi fathers in 1730 for the construction of some buildings in Chia. Eighties-era construction further erased all traces.

4ee46e53453e5fdd.text: Different tomb nucleus scattered along the islet.

4ee4888c8f67703f.text: The monument, considered a proto-nuraghe, is in fact a transitional structure between the corridor nuraghe and the tholos nuraghe. The complex consists of a central tower with a terrace, a bastion, and various huts both inside and outside an outer wall. It now lies beneath a viaduct; indeed, only a few centimetres separate the last surviving stone courses of the monument from the concrete beams that support the road.

4efc11f3400f8123.text: "Domus de jana of Su Adu 'e Sa iana, a short distance from the village, at the crossing of Rio Minori, was formerly an underground chamber, which has disappeared for many years, but the elders of the village still remember it. In the Pasqua Sanna field was Isidoro."

4f09ceb5524d0737.text: The structural element of the building, with the top of mastio A and some wall profiles emerging for several metres, is basaltic andesite. A thick mass of mastic wraps around the exposed part of the structure, revealing a curved profile of the bastion that, from satellite images, appears at least four-lobed due to the addition of at least two secondary bodies.

4f0a772893a434d6.text: Complex nuraghe with an irregular plan. Its perimeter wall features a single, continuous mass of rubble, from which westward remnants of the central tower emerge. The complex is enclosed by a megalithic outer wall that protects it to the west and, in part, to the north.

4f35423aa7b35eca.text: Nuraghe immersed in vegetation, eroded and partially buried. The entrance is visible but buried down to almost the lintel.

4f3a1d96c07bd529.text: Nuragic spring included in a small municipal park, carved into the rock

4f4d3c2a731bf362.text: The nuraghe was in close topographic and cultural connection with the giants' tombs of Biristeddi, located about 250 metres away.

4f4da29b7d9c8928.text:
Zinnuri in a rural municipal park characterized by the presence of ancient olive and oleander trees, together with a rural refuge. Around the spring there is an area equipped for outdoor refreshment, with wooden tables and benches, and a parking area for vehicles.

Here are located the Zinnuri nuraghe and the homonymous spring.

4f535f9bb38640b8.text: At the western end of the elongated Carronca Simoi ridge, beneath the ruins of a small rectangular building, only scant remains of a probable nuraghe are visible; about 20 metres to the east of it, some stone blocks appear to belong to a circular nuragic hut.

4fa35726e94cf040.text:
Nuraghe situated on the double and secure landing at Porto Pirastru.

Currently, only the walls and a concrete foundation of a recent installation remain.

4fa84aa17cb7e47e.text: Giants' tombs not easily identifiable near the sheepfold Presethu Tortu

4fa96389c9b5db36.text: The nuraghe consists of a central tower surrounded by a curtain wall, to which several secondary towers are attached. The central tower, which originally comprised multiple superimposed levels, currently retains only the lower level and the staircase leading to the upper levels, partially blocked by collapses.

4fcba6238e4be4b8.text: A tafone of very particular construction, probably used as a burial, considering the presence of several stones beneath it, which likely formed part of the closing wall. A popular legend tells of a chest hidden/enclosed within it, containing a treasure, a "Scrixoxiu".

4fd64845a53788cc.text: Given all this, in the locality of Serra Neba, an area adjacent to the village of Puisteris had to be established, probably used for livestock rearing and possibly also for agriculture. The archaeological material recovered, unambiguously attributable to the Ozieri culture, confirms the presence of human activity in the area during the late Neolithic period.

4fde837a295386a4.text: "Almost entirely dismantled, only some ashlar and wall segments remain of the original structure, whose layout is indiscernible due to dense vegetation and widespread decay. R. Ledda notes the discovery of primary fusion residues of minerals, currently no longer in situ."

4fe04bbc3c9175ad.text:
The archaeological complex "Sa Mandra de sa Jua" – literally "the yoked oxen enclosure", a term broadly indicating a fertile area – occupies a modest elevation overlooking the Rio Mannu of Ozieri.

The site, multi-stratified, was continuously inhabited until the medieval period and has been incorporated since the 1960s into the San Nicola district, located about 4 kilometres from the village of Ozieri.

The Monument

4ff4738ec107f4eb.text: Fountain whose architectural form recalls several clearly nuragic analogies

50014d356a110f6b.text: At the level of great ruin. The basal circle of rose trachyte is visible, with stones roughly squared. Contrary to what was previously believed, we are not facing a nuraghe but an important fusional sacred circle, of which various forms are evident. One of these, of historical and religious significance, consists of three steps with a basin. Mu

5024e52f38c479bd.text: Very complex nuraghe. It has a trilobate outer wall and an internal central tower. Traces of a village outside. The state of conservation is very poor.

503981ba150ecfb1.text: Complex nuraghe, probably of the "a tancato" type with a courtyard and an added tower, built of limestone. The majestic wall faces of the main tower survive largely intact. Inside, on the SSE side, a trapezoidal lintelled opening is visible, preceded by a passage whose course is interrupted by the collapse of the structures. Tampering by looters is evident.

503cb7379a6f1bc0.text: Usanis, located at a short distance from Osidda and situated at the top of a rocky spur, was a complex structure composed of two towers.

50424d8094e33c2d.text:
It is a large village, presumably of the Monte Claro Culture (Cagliari), which spread in Sardinia around the second half of the third millennium BC. In the centre of the polygon, because of land reclamation, little of the village walling remains, while on the two far sides traces of huts with rectangular and circular plans still emerge.

The plan in photo no. 6 was provided by the archaeologist who directed the excavations.

5067e53eff30c332.text: Well, probably belonging to a Nuragic village. It is located on the top of a hill, inside a vineyard.

5078696f0296eea1.text:
The tomb was built in several phases. The first dates to the Early Bronze Age, when the Bonnanaro culture was widespread in Sardinia (about 1800 BC). At that time the tomb must have looked like a cist dolmen covered by a mound.

In the Nuragic period the site was reworked into a giants' tomb by enlarging the burial chamber and adding the exedra, composed of 14 slabs among which the central stele, with its entrance, stands out at almost 4 metres high.

508d9c2230dc1f5f.text:
It is located within the municipal territory of Bosa (OR), inside an agriturismo.

The name might be incorrect.

It should include two hypogea, partly repurposed.

50c7bcbde8e43c1c.text: Giants' tomb built of basalt ashlar

50de56ae61e06e85.text: Situated on the hill of the same name, from which it overlooks the Bechida valley and part of the coastal strip that leads northwards to the Nuraghe Artora, the structure is poorly preserved. It consists of a circular wall face of modest dimensions that appears to have belonged to a large hut, built of local granite. A large quantity of collapse debris is visible outside the walls.

51209edeb5f3f52b.text: Nuraghe probably unique because composed of two adjacent towers similar in type and dimensions.

5130c31b06994b18.text: Destroyed by the construction of modern buildings.

514561e86dc6ad1d.text:
Located in the hinterland of the town of Porto Torres, the Sant'Elena nuraghe is one of the best preserved in the municipal area.

The monument occupies the summit of a low rise covered by very dense vegetation.

The central tower has a diameter of about 12 m and a surviving height of 4 m from the present ground level.

The masonry consists of 13 courses of superimposed blocks of white limestone, carefully dressed.

51491efeb9555328.text: It is a quadrilobate nuraghe (Sardara commune) completely demolished, of which only a few courses of the mural basement remain.

516e89cc2275404b.text: The Su Nuraxi di Loceri nuraghe was built incorporating a rocky outcrop. The main tower is well preserved and was constructed with local granite blocks, partly roughly shaped and arranged to form regular courses. Its entrance is raised above the surrounding plain by at least three courses.

5184cd9aa5a132c5.text:
Position verified with GPS. The nuraghe is partially collapsed and the entrance is blocked by debris from a collapse.

It still reaches a maximum height of about 8 metres.

51b95d618efbd074.text: The chamber, roughly circular with a maximum diameter of about 1.80 m in the north-south direction, is enclosed by four orthostats, but ideally seven can be reconstructed to complete the perimeter with an entrance to the south-east; three of the four remaining orthostats support the covering slab;

51bac9d26509da7a.text: What remains of a single-tower nuraghe dating from a period between the Middle and Late Bronze Age. Diameter of about 12 m and height of about 2 m.

51bf456df245f914.text: The sacred well is in good condition, despite its basic architectural elements having been tampered with several times. It is built of medium and large trachyte blocks and has a corridor paved with regular boulders, 5.10 m long, leading to a circular tholos chamber with a domed vault that encloses the water vein. The corridor was originally fitted with benches along the side walls.

51d0d67263b7dab6.text: Of the nuraghe Niu e Crobu, only a meagre remnant remains. Indeed, the monument lies hidden among the vegetation and is cut off from its dignity by a fence that forces it to look beside a reservoir lined with its own material, thus compromising its environmental impact... ignorance knows no limits.

51d6b627a361895a.text: The Pranu Muttedu park is one of the most evocative archaeological sites in inland Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, for a total extension of about 200,000 sq m. Excavations have brought to light very numerous artefacts attributable to settled communities of the "Ozieri" culture dating to the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex has the highest concentration of menhirs known in Sardinia.

51fca9d3dee80d93.text:
The skill with which the basalt blocks have been laid is immediately striking. Swallowed by the earth and wrapped in greenery.

The south-east entrance is topped by an enormous lintel and leads into the chamber, where access is blocked by the collapsed tholos.

It must have been an elegant single-tower nuraghe, in a strategic position "guarding" a small, lush valley.

52351d1bc8c123e9.text: In the area, remains of more than ten huts belonging to a nuragic complex are present. The village area was completely destroyed, I would say devastated, during the second world war, when the structures, belonging to most of the huts, were dismantled/adapted for military use.

5295a78ecce03c39.text: Nuraghe never excavated, almost completely buried

52a34ccf0b0e93b7.text: The Ertas nuraghe is the largest Nuragic monument in the Sassari region. Fully subterranean and quadrilobed, completely enveloped by impenetrable vegetation. From the access point located to the south-east, it is possible, by crawling, to reach the main tholos still intact.

52aa0512a1d83680.text: The nuraghe is built on several levels. The oldest part is the central tower; an outer bastion then surrounds the central tower and links it to a second tower. The boulders making up this bastion are of considerable size. The only accessible part is a corridor on the second floor of the central tower, with a “donkey-back” or inverted ship’s-keel roof, whose south entrance is topped by a huge lintel with its relieving window.

52aa2a6ae94218f8.text: In very poor condition of conservation, only scant elements of the structure remain embedded within the vegetation. Location uncertain, on the left bank of the Orune Channel, adjacent to a water reservoir built during the Second World War.

52ab57bf8c2a37b1.text: Rock bench with stairs and cupolas.

52b405b0faf12c2f.text: The nuraghe is located on top of Monte Nieddu

52bf4dee261ef956.text: Single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of decay.

52d72466ef1bfe83.text:
The remains of the megalithic tomb lie next to a dry-stone wall that follows the railway line, just 200 metres south-east of Birori station.

Seven surviving slabs of the semicircular exedra (chord 9 m – rise 2.40 m) are visible on the ground, as is part of its outer perimeter (length 9 m – width 4.50 m); nothing can be said, however, about the burial corridor and the arched stele, whose existence can be considered certain.

52db4281f9d7d6d3.text: Nuragic village inhabited in Final Bronze II and Iron I, without any nuraghe.

52e545d54e96830b.text: The domus consists of three large rooms with a single entrance.

52fc1adf1ce40675.text: Circular burial circle formed by the stacking of polyhedral stones of various sizes. The upper part is composed of 10 large stones arranged in a circle, with a diameter of about 150 cm. At the edges, some stones have fallen, likely originally forming part of the structure. The circle is filled with earth and rubble.

52ffb592b35efb22.text: Perhaps a Neolithic burial site; Roman and medieval tombs have been identified there over time. Witnesses report that in the 1940s and 1950s, while ploughing with a wooden plough, numerous human bones and fragments of tegulae and imbrices came to light. This was even more evident when the same person (my father Giovanni, almost a centenarian, now deceased) ploughed with an iron Birindelli plough, which turned the soil at a greater depth.

5310a9c93c17439d.text: Interesting site in the territory of Villa Sant'Antonio. Located about 2 km to the south-east of the village, it shows probable remains of domus de janas, canaletas, coppers, basins, and a symbol that the locals believe refers to fertility. All these elements together suggest a possible pre-Nuragic cultic area.

53708d2567fb20b5.text: Tomb II, particularly imposing, features the entrance, the antechamber, and the burial chamber carved out in two distinct rocky blocks transported on-site and placed upon a carefully prepared mound; in the final stone work, achieved with a hammer, and in the architectural and plan layout, it closely resembles the domus de janas burials.

5373e27763d20793.text: The Benas nuraghe stands on a small hill at the locality 'Tanca sa cresia', north-west of the Jana nuraghe, in the territory of Solarussa, 200 m from the border with Zerfaliu. It is a complex nuraghe, with a courtyard and three secondary towers. The central tower is particularly interesting, preserving the intact tholos roof of the ground floor. Inside there are three niches and a curious staircase on the right-hand side of the entrance corridor.

538676dc621d057b.text: Like the Oes nuraghe, it does not have a traditional tholos roof but one made with wooden substructures.

539274ce292f2cac.text: The Nuragic village of Grutti acqua is located in the plain facing the complex nuraghe and consists of numerous circular and rectangular huts. Unfortunately, only ruins remain of the huts, and furthermore, almost all are completely overgrown by dense vegetation, which nonetheless allows partial identification of their layout.

53c10763af79b6d8.text: The Cala Ostina nuraghe is a low curtain wall with a semicircular layout, having a radius of 7.70 m, protected on three sides by vertical walls; the wall reaches a maximum height of 2 m, built on two to three courses of large stones.

53dd21400e343ebe.text: Group of three domus de janas of particular interest. Featuring a carved doorway in the basalt rock and a rectangular exedra situated below ground level.

53ddeda9f86a7674.text: The nuraghe Loppelìe still stands in good condition despite the collapses. The entrance, well preserved, is triangular. On the left side of the entrance chamber the intramural stairway opens. Moreover, the nuraghe Loppelìe is worth visiting for the splendid view from the top of the structure, which ranges from the village of Triei below, to the mountains overlooking Baunei, and from the bay of Arbatax to the peaks of the Gennargentu.

53f1caf60400d827.text: 100 metres to the south-east of the nuraghe, traces of a giants' tomb are present: some slabs emerge from the ground belonging to the burial corridor.

541b9b147e2877d9.text: Proto-nuraghe with a village nearby. The size and location of the proto-nuraghe at Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest they may have been the most important centres of cantons or sub-cantons within the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other proto-nuraghe complexes, they may have controlled a large portion of the area.

5420e66d0061e680.text: In the locality "Su Tiriarzu" we find two domus de janas, about 80 metres apart.

5429273543b4fb14.text: The nuraghe is part of a complex that also includes a second nuraghe about 50 metres away. It must have been particularly grand, judging by the extent of the rubble. Within the collapse covering the central tower a tholos chamber of considerable height can be made out: the upper part of the entrance passage, with the angular cross-section typical of archaic-type nuraghi, can still be distinguished in the profile of the chamber.

54374d8d833f3561.text: On the summit of the hill lie the ruins of a small nuraghe.

544383c85e5e58ee.text:
Complex nuraghe considerably buried.

The central tower, which retains intact the tholos, reaches a height of about 10 metres on the northern side.

5448f6baa078a47c.text: More similar to a stele than a menhir, having a parabolic arch shape. A dolmen is present in the vicinity.

545f29be84474734.text: Particular site having two different classification types. The first census defined the structure as "Nuraghe Crastu Ruju", the second as "Megalithic rampart of Giusei" in the style of the most famous rampart of Monte Baranta.

5483e628825c4b86.text: It is very ruined and overgrown with dense vegetation.

549e2e7e04fa83e1.text: Here there was a Nuragic village, of which only faint traces remain.

54b6d8974894ae77.text: Single-tower nuraghe located at Sa Cordiola. The condition of the external walls is good, while inside the structure has collapsed. It is characterized by having two names: the first is "Sa Cordiola", the second is "Giustalassa", the name of the adjacent locality.

54bfd0af6f9d8c84.text: More likely it is an ancient nuragic hut.

54c148ffc378f8c0.text: A badly ruined single-tower nuraghe of which only a few courses remain

54ce9dc5fae622b5.text: Located at the base of a cairn on the southern side of Berchida valley, there stands a small village composed of several huts built with dry stone masonry. Initially identified as a nuraghe, it actually lacks the defining characteristics of one.

54d0fb348ef45af0.text:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Tortolì (OG).

It consists of three menhirs laid on the ground, two broken into two parts and one small, resembling a baetyl.

They are undoubtedly the remains of a megalithic sanctuary.

54dadcabd4d40369.text:
The dolmen has a circular burial chamber (1.57 x 1.26 x 0.52 m high above the fill) bounded by ten orthostats of various sizes (measurements of two slabs: 0.68 x 0.27 x 0.50 m high – 0.70 x 0.25 x 0.52 m high), while two slabs placed on one side of the entrance, oriented to the north-east, suggest the existence of a short corridor now destroyed.

The capstone is vaguely pentagonal (2.40 x 2.25 m) and has a maximum thickness of 0.55 m tapering to a minimum of 0.48 m.

54dc5fb3bfa66dd3.text: Located in the area of Tidula, it features a corridor niche and one in the tholos, still intact.

54f6d65ebc61acb1.text: The proto-nuraghi of Monti Proceddu, Monti Tellura, Monti Acutzu and Monti de su Marchesu were very probably placed to guard the borders of districts of the Trexenta, whose most important centres must have been in the present municipal territories of Guasila or Samatzai; the one at Sa Corona (Bruncu de is Angionis Birdis) must have controlled at least the proto-nuraghi of Monti Atziaddei (?), Genna su Carru and those of Monti Cuamnaxi (Coa Margine) and Sa Corona di Villagreca.

550affd40e41d00a.text:
The hill is not easily accessible to visitors because it is wrapped in Mediterranean scrub. The car must be left about a hundred metres from the tarmac of the coastal road from Sarroch to Pula. From here you walk up to the nuraghe.

It is hard even to guess the number of towers that surrounded the central one.

However, it is certain that it must have been a multi-lobed nuraghe with an entrance to the south-east, whose central tower had the three typical internal niches.

550c3651303804f2.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber bordered by three niches, built in basalt. Traces of a settlement.

5548bc32ebc5d79d.text: Complex nuraghe with settlement, village. If this designation is incorrect, it might refer to a nuraghe without a name, listed as number 480 by van Dommelen. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

554ef184a141dc8f.text: It lies in the locality of the same name, about 1.5 km as the crow flies from the SP165. Easily reached by farm tracks, the village covers about two hectares. Among the ruins are several structures occupying the whole area within the visible boundaries of the complex. Some appear to be huts, others are larger and more like enclosures.

5554f8f74af419c8.text: Ispiene was part of the territory of Chiaramonti. About fifteen years ago we ceded two thousand hectares to the new municipality of Erula, and with it a number of nuraghi including Ispiene. That is why "I still feel it is mine", and if you want to find the character of a fortress you must come here, but even more so the imperishable sacred character that pervades the nuraghe with its cells and the sun that at the zenith on the summer solstice penetrates them to join with Mother Earth. mu

55554ba7b6bb122c.text: Inaccessible with the tholos collapsed inward.

555a0cd14ea92872.text: Cave that may have been used, in prehistoric and protohistoric times, as shelter/residence for human families. In this case, as in others, the man-made wall structures are evident, designed to reduce the opening. Nearby, at least two more are found, similar and in comparable conditions.

5584bbb34240ae50.text: At the site of 'su pranu', a complex nuraghe in poor state of conservation, hidden and almost inaccessible to visitors. Nearby, the remains of a village are clearly visible.

55ac0e01c995711c.text: Site where the oldest human skeletons in all of Sardinia have been found (8500–9000 BC).

55bf85c749bd5187.text:
You crawl through that opening; the space is tight, the ceiling low because of all that millennia-old earth, and you go on advancing on your elbows, slowly. It consists of at least 12 hypogea, cut into the limestone and provided with various decorations and bull protomes.

These are domus that move you, because their beauty lies in everything they hold.

Then, in the darkness, a shaft of light illuminates a magnificent triple-framed decoration on a doorway still almost completely buried.

562ce041722cf515.text:
The nuraghe, of complex type, consists of a central tower around which a three-lobed bastion has been built, enclosing a courtyard of disengaged space.

The towers have a curved form, as seen in the Santu Antine nuraghe of Torralba.

56380f85ff8feb63.text:
On the illustrative map of Tharros and at the archaeological site it is marked with number 15.

The tophet was established by the Phoenicians and then the Carthaginians, who had already found the Nuragic structures present.

5640b9e1a8ecb460.text: The surrounding territory has always been heavily anthropogenically modified, and sites are numerous throughout. Often, and this is the case in the few visible remains, it is difficult to determine the exact typology.
