The proof remains of the historical memory of the elders, who retain an indelible recollection of their existence. mu

56562099af8076f6.text: It consists of two menhirs repositioned in the area.

568aef748b1a3950.text:
The monument, of simple type, is located in an area currently used for sheep grazing; the entrance features a lintel topped by a drainage window, while the pilasters are composed of finely shaped granite blocks arranged in decreasing order towards the top.

The entrance leads into a passage leading to the chamber, composed of finely worked granite ashlar and a vaulted roof section.

569f9123e678ce79.text: The giants' tomb of S'Ena 'e Sa Vacca is particularly interesting for certain architectural features that in the past led scholars to regard it as a dolmenic structure. The distinctive feature of this burial is the large covering slab, completely unworked, which covers the entire tomb chamber and gives the monument the appearance of an elongated dolmen or "allée couverte".

56b73d0ec9c5a058.text: Nuraghe located in the mountain known as Punta Breigara. The locals call the site "nuraghe de s'omu e is abisi". A tholos base of about 1.50 m height is present. Vegetation has completely covered the site, making further identification impossible. Difficult access; the roads are on private land.

56bb80e01dc1f2db.text: A single-tower nuraghe largely hidden by vegetation, built on a rocky outcrop that merges with the stones of the wall structure. The site dates to the Middle Bronze Age.

56c05568b8707c84.text: It is a proto-nuraghe of the corridor type, located within an area where remains of a larger village are visible.

56f5dd41ff6feb9a.text:
It is located within the municipal territory of Nuxis (CI).

It was connected to the adjacent Nuragic well, as evidenced in other archaeological sites (Santa Vittoria di Serri, Sant'Anastasia a Sardara, Su Putzu ad Orroli, etc.).

570ef53b43478246.text: The eastern section, which enjoys an excellent view over the entire internal gulf of Olbia, is the best preserved. From the ground it rises by about four metres. The lintel is barely visible (see photo), while the entrance is almost completely buried. Traces of the megalithic enclosure are barely discernible, but the abundance of remains and fallen blocks suggests the monument's significance.

57186389eca2ada7.text: The complex consists of several hypogean tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Among them Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.

572350cab0d179ee.text: A ruined and buried single-tower nuraghe whose structure cannot be defined.

5728ad9e9633a5f4.text: One of the best-preserved single-tower nuraghi in the territory of Seneghe

572f8d97ed9ef785.text: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and bastions featuring two additional towers. On the north side there are two further towers with a wall, located at the narrowest point of the Taccu Ara plateau. Built in basalt.

57482eef30d8250e.text:
Multi-chambered tomb with a centripetal layout. It has long been emptied. It yielded material of the Ozieri culture (3200–2500 BC) and of the early medieval period (7th century AD). The former are kept in the "G. A. Sanna" Archaeological Museum in Sassari; the latter in the Nuoro Civic Museum.

Inside the domus, cut into a rock outcrop, access is through a hexagonal doorway; all around the antechamber, with its perfectly worked ceiling, five cells open where the dead were laid.

5755b06fcf8c2a69.text:
consisting of domus de janas of the horizontal-projection and pit types (1, 2, 3, 4), the other of pit-type domus de janas (5, 6, 7).

Tomb 1 is particularly remarkable, the result of several construction phases: originally of the pit type with an antechamber and a large main chamber, it was later given a long access corridor in place of the pit and enlarged to the right of the main chamber, incorporating three small burial chambers from a neighbouring tomb.

576c408f8c4b8ca0.text: The structure is completely missing its top and shows only faint traces of wall faces. Illegal excavations have severely damaged the structure.

576c84f39fcead28.text: The tomb, of dolmenic structure, is now only discernible in the funerary corridor, the entrance, and the right arm of the exedra. Just emerging from the ground, a row of medium-sized stones forms the left side of the burial chamber.

578b6614f57e17c8.text:
Complex nuraghe, possibly three-lobed, built with large blocks of local andesite.

Among the vegetation, some stone heaps and traces related to possible huts are visible.

Clear evidence of repeated occupation in historical times, with numerous ceramic fragments—especially Roman period—found on the collapse and in the surrounding soil.

57912a17b6ed65e0.text: It is a complex nuraghe to which the anti-ship battery Boggio structures were added during the Second World War. From the outside the wall face of the probable main tower is clearly visible.

57b95555641bd39c.text: Nuraghe reported, embedded in vegetation and not visible from the outside

57c3f5622311978e.text: Subterranean complex consisting of six domus de janas.

57d6b33f9eb2881d.text: The nuraghe is not marked on IGM maps and its type is undetermined.

57f0a3505f8b074f.text: Single-tower nuraghe on top of a basalt outcrop, a natural fortress. Inside, a shelter for shepherds was built. Today it is abandoned.

57f9d6cc5490e5f7.text:
The nuraghe is very large and I believe it has more than one tower.

It has suffered numerous collapses; it would be advisable to take a photo from above using a drone.

From the nuraghe one has a wide view of the surrounding territory extending all the way to the sea.

5829aa34379b4f29.text: Giants' tomb located within a large olive grove.

585a502d3257b4b9.text: Of particular importance is the cave known as "Su Stampu VI", where pre-Nuragic and Nuragic artifacts have been found.

585ce1843c0f24b5.text: The giants' tomb Sa Dom 'e S'Orcu is one of the best-preserved Nuragic monuments. Built on a slight rise in the ground, it is of the coursed exedra type. The apsidal tomb body, aligned on a SE–NW axis, is 15.20 m long. The masonry consists of medium-sized, well-worked basalt blocks laid in regular courses. In some parts of the walling the use of levelling wedges can be observed.

587ab5c4977fd0ae.text: It is a complex, three-lobed nuraghe, featuring a central tower, three peripheral towers arranged in a triangle connected by curtain walls with a straight-curvilinear profile, and an internal courtyard with an entrance facing south-east. Finds of incense-burners with female heads, draped figures, and anatomical votives indicate a probable cult dedicated to the goddess Demetra.

58900b67ce516ea6.text: Located within an area designated for sheep grazing, near the course of the river of the same name.

5890f5bcb01e4a62.text: Located in the territory of Mara, it draws attention to what appears to be a large monolith visible from the SS292 just before the junction at Bonuighinu. The nuraghe, likely a complex one, is unfortunately almost completely swallowed by vegetation; what strikes me is discovering that the monolith is the remnant of a colossal outer wall shaped like a V.

589347e6d908a375.text: Natural monument, eroded into columns and protected by rock overhang.

58999dc77deee8c1.text:
Small single-tower nuraghe completely destroyed.

The nuraghe was listed under the name Pirastu Fattu, but the owner, Mr G. Raspa, who was born and has lived in those places, states that the real name is Campo Maggiore.

589f9d42024d9df6.text: The settlement, which originally was intended to extend to integrate with that of the N.ghe Maiore, consists of numerous architectural remains whose fragments are still awaiting investigation by experts. As also observed in the nearby Maiore, there are remains of rectangular dwellings.

58ab470d149a0487.text: It consists of three domus de janas partially eroded and in very poor condition.

58ac6c77c9b2b52b.text: Inside a large enclosure at the site of S. Pietro, adjacent to a colonial farmhouse, only a small portion of the nuraghe remains. The building appears to have been constructed upon the nuraghe. The materials used are large blocks of arenaceous rock. From the ruins come hundreds of fragments of Nuragic pottery, lithic tools, flakes and microliths made of jadeite, as well as remains of food.

58d02ce8b2286369.text: Nuragic sacred well currently under study and excavation. The reconstruction is hypothetical.

58d1d3d2461005df.text: It lies in the municipality of Florinas (SS), and is a circular single-tower nuraghe with the entrance unusually oriented to the north-east. Very ruined. An old mule track passed practically alongside it, but is now completely disused.

58da18b3cb81e2f7.text: The giants' tomb S'iscra e Lottoni is of dolmenic type, from the Early Bronze Age, and is in a fair state of preservation; indeed it retains the funerary corridor almost intact, with a flat-lintel roof formed by stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele consists of a centinated monolith in which the small doorway giving access to the burial chamber has been cut.

58f7b3a62847d2d9.text: A mixed-type complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower with a partially collapsed inner chamber, a second tower on the SW side, and an imposing structure crossed by a corridor that appears to end in a small courtyard containing a further small tower. The monument is very difficult to interpret, both because of the vegetation cover and the deep deposits, as well as the unusual nature of the building itself.

58fab2fb25ba7fe9.text: Single-tower nuraghe with its tholos intact

5905066d8283229e.text:
The circle, irregular in shape, has been destroyed by agricultural work that has compromised its original form.

The monument consists of about 40 trachyte boulders of various sizes forming an irregular ellipse with a major axis of 17 m and a minor axis of 15 m. Archaeological excavations have brought to light an unspecified number of polished stone axes that have allowed the circle to be dated to the Late Neolithic, placing it within the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC).

594ebce339c4ad6f.text: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos partially collapsed inward. Located beside a sheepfold.

59b3da178c7d2ff0.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with the tholos collapsed. Only a few courses of masonry and part of the internal niches remain, although these have been used locally by herders as a place to store goods and also as a site for various plastic waste.

59b473f21b010436.text: It lacks the covering slab and is covered by vegetation.

59b7606a6de7a6de.text: Domus de janas necropolis particularly striking, located adjacent to part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen. One of the most beautiful Domus de Janas is Sirilò, until recently entirely still buried underground. From a small entrance one accesses a large chamber, within which there are three additional entrances leading to three separate rooms.

59be7d1db3aa4618.text: Stone forming part of a group of five stone blocks. It is characterized by a flat anterior surface and a convex posterior surface.

59d048470d20778f.text: Small nuragic spring with remains of the original cell built over the spring's source and faint traces of the atrium.

5a014914debd4fc2.text: In literature, as indeed observed on the ground, Su Padrigheddu is closely linked to the complex nuraghe S'Uraki, first mentioned as such by A. Taramelli in 1935. The materials recovered were immediately attributed to a village inhabited during the Nuragic period and continuously active right up to the Republican Roman era.

5a0a72c435280371.text: The site is called Su casteddu de Adeva, named after the mountain behind it, Monte Adeva or Is concas de Adeva. It is a single-tower nuraghe with an outer courtyard, bounded by a wall face that joins the tower structure, on the summit of a rocky spur with which the natural rock is partly integrated.

5a0e95888a8c4e18.text: The tomb was built with large blocks still partially buried and with exposed faces mostly straight. The exedra is no longer visible and the position of the door can only be hypothesised.

5a1763feffdfbef0.text: The S'Argara nuraghe is undoubtedly one of the most important nuraghes in Su Pranu; it is a four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the central tower. From its summit, on days when the sky is clear, one can overlook almost the entire western coast of Sardinia, from Capo Caccia to Capo Pecora in the Sulcis.

5a244ac9d2d9fe95.text: The archaeological area comprises a village and two domus de janas on a granite tor partly surrounded by the Tèscere river. The complex nuraghe is distinguished by natural cavities incorporated into wall structures. The two domus are cut into two boulders. The first, single-chambered, is reached through a raised entrance preceded by a short vestibule. The second consists of a single chamber ruined by the collapse of the boulder in which the entrance opened.

5a3a5ecfebdf07ca.text:
Destroyed nuraghe located on the summit of the hill of the same name.

Unfortunately, little remains of this monument, but it is still of considerable significance.

5a60626c84bf859f.text: The site is located at the centre of a livestock farm. It is a dolmenic tomb arranged along a north-south axis with an entrance to the south-east; the burial chamber tapers towards the back and is open at the front in a large semicircular exedra.

5a61e008e78e025b.text:
The prehistoric settlement spreads out, adapting to the rock formations, over three natural terraces, the first straight and the other two curvilinear.

These natural features have been reinforced by massive wall bastions built of large and medium-sized ashlars laid with heavy chinking. The proto-nuraghe, built of ashlars laid in irregular, heavily chinked courses, conforms to the morphology of the rocks.

5a862e1cf9b55b10.text: Remains of two sacred wells of the Nuragic period, set about 150 m apart. The first well is almost entirely buried. The second is in excellent condition, with an entrance formed by a semi-buried staircase. Its cylindrical shape has a diameter of about 2 m and a depth of about 3 m; it is built of stone blocks laid in horizontal courses. The presence of two sacred wells suggests a sacred centre of considerable importance.

5a9be3e2121d6c32.text: Together with the nuraghe Cabonu, it lies at the border between the territories of Ussaramanna and Turri.

5aa30cf4bced3b3a.text: A double curtain wall of large stones appears along the edge of the hilltop, enclosing a previous Nuragic structure, the nuraghe Diana.

5ac1cee26104b8ca.text: Single-tower nuraghe partially collapsed but with the tholos open. It offers the possibility of climbing to the last remaining course and enjoying the view over Cala Sinzias.

5acc1702867feec9.text: Located in the area of Su Fonnesu (Teulada), at about 300 metres above sea level. It is situated on a pointed promontory, locally known as "punta acuccia", which from a distance resembles a pyramid. The stones used are mainly granitic. The view is excellent, especially over the Gulf of Palmas.

5ad172dca5240d9e.text:
Cuccuru Nuraxi is the hill on whose summit a grand complex nuraghe once stood, now largely destroyed.

Even the earliest studies made it possible to grasp the nuraghe's structure. It was the first archaeological excavations, in the early 1960s, however, that gave a more precise definition of the monumental complex. The building consisted of two megalithic towers joined by a curtain wall. Inside, it comprised at least three chambers, one of which formed the main chamber.

5b173e6a82f3f246.text: The tomb shows clear signs of illicit excavation; its structure is hard to make out because most of it is covered by vegetation and soil. The chamber is rectangular and partly buried at the rear; an apse may be present. On the sides and at the back of the tomb there are fallen boulders that certainly belonged to the tomb. Even though it is hidden by the scrub, the wall of the exedra is visible, following a curved course.

5b218e1fc4a03b50.text:
It is built of medium and large boulders laid in rather rough courses; the plan is oval, and it has two entrances and two stairways leading to the upper floor.

The roof is formed of large slabs set side by side.

The east entrance has partly collapsed and was probably connected to the stairways, while the west entrance leads to the central corridor off which open a deep niche and a stairway that has almost completely collapsed. Probable proto-nuraghe

5b26e7ccccd3c98f.text: About 500 metres from the homonymous nuraghe

5b36700158c9998d.text: It is identified as a megalithic circle because it features a single row of uncut ashlar stones arranged in a circle. Diameter about 11 m. Currently it is used as a sheepfold. Nearby, two menhirs are noted.

5b3d94142e673201.text: Basically a pile of stones; at the top a circular opening is visible, forming a 2 m deep shaft, which I assume was the flat lintel of the staircase that ran along the inner wall.

5b4401594cfcec40.text: Complex nuraghe, only a few remains of the central tower and bastions are left; the structure was demolished to build the nearby state road. Many Roman and high-medieval artifacts testify to the continued use of the monument during these periods.

5b51d169ab4df0bd.text: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe constructed with medium and large-sized blocks arranged in regular courses. The nuraghe is not in good condition of preservation. The southern-eastern entrance, collapsed, leads into a corridor whose left wall shows access to a staircase (itself collapsed). The chamber is circular and survives to a maximum height of 9 m.

5b5636cad1de0592.text: The IGM lists it as Longu, which instead is located slightly further east, some hundreds of metres away. It is composed of several courses of massive, polygonal stones that impress with their remarkable precision and craftsmanship. It features an opening to the north, with an architrave containing the initial form of an arch. The surrounding area is particularly noteworthy.

5b90c961a62bffd8.text:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Montresta (OR).

At the centre of the delimited area, on a rocky outcrop, stands a structure that for a long time was considered a nuraghe. It is more likely, however, to be a quadrangular Carthaginian fortress, with traces of masonry visible at its base that completed the defensive structure.

5bb6f064c9ce92d8.text:
It is a bilobed nuraghe built of large trachyte blocks, roughly worked and laid in irregular courses.

Leaning against the central tower, which survives to a height of about (???) metres, is a second, slightly elliptical tower on the east side. From above, part of an internal niche in this tower is visible, faced with perfectly squared limestone blocks.

5bba0711db64d556.text: The Carrarzu Iddia complex nuraghe is situated on a modest elevation bounded by a curtain wall enclosing a proto-nuraghe and a nuraghe that appears to be of tholos type: between the two structures lies a small cluster of circular huts, some of which are still well preserved. A few dozen metres away lies the homonymous dolmen, and slightly further on the Pranu 'e Ruos and Tittiriolos nuraghes.

5bdd5cc4598480a0.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Florinas. It consists of two underground chambers.

5be402dbd22df328.text: The tomb was restored in 1993, using and repositioning the exedra and other orthostats, some of which were deteriorated or broken but still in situ. The monument, which shows two distinct construction phases, was built during both phases in the Early Bronze Age and was used for funerary purposes only during the first phase of occupation.

5bff8c977d8741d5.text: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas

5c21695b6d665a34.text: Complex nuraghe, never studied, located within a private property, surrounded by vegetation.

5c2b11b026b3b790.text:
Four giants' tombs, placed close to one another and in varying states of preservation. They are built with local limestone blocks and measure slightly more than 10 metres in length, except for one.

Due to illegal excavations, an undisturbed stratigraphic context has not been preserved. However, a sequence datable between late Middle Bronze Age and recent Bronze Age has been identified.

5c2ba12597f7afb1.text: The nuraghe Bidighinzu or Su Idighinzu, which in Sardinian means "dry vine shoot", is a single-tower monument that still preserves its intact tholos, located in the territory of Ploaghe.

5c3082d393017706.text: Damaged nuraghe, completely surrounded by vegetation

5cb502b2f5c302ab.text: Single-tower nuraghe probably. Completely covered by vegetation, making its structure difficult to interpret.

5cc3271110a94dd4.text: Small underground chamber in an isolated stone.

5ccdddcafed81307.text: Single-tower nuraghe visible only when the waters of the Cuga basin recede. It is one of the 20 nuraghes in the Cuga valley.

5cdb619684040110.text: Built on a rise from which it overlooks the surrounding area, it can be seen from the hairpin bends of the SP 6. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a base diameter of about 10 m, built of schist blocks. Part of the masonry on the south side has collapsed, and the entrance, also on the south, is ogival and gives access to the inner chamber, which lacks its tholos roof; a niche is visible inside it.

5cf5c5c0c97954ac.text: It is located about 500 m east of the Is Perdas Croccadas menhir. In recent times it has been reconstructed and restored from three large fragments.

5cf7f3446a0a83bd.text: The burial lies on the south-western edge of a plateau used for crops and pasture. It is about 1.50 metres north-west of the nuraghe of the same name and a few hundred metres south-east of the open-air site of Ruinacchèsos. The monument has its entrance facing north-west, with some blocks of the exedra nearby. The burial chamber is about 3.55 metres long and rectangular in plan.

5d01695078e7d200.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The external ground plan is not fully definable because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation.

The tower, about 12 metres in diameter, survives to a maximum height of 5.30 m (8 courses).

The masonry consists of basalt blocks, medium and large, roughly dressed with some care and laid in regular horizontal courses.

5d1dddce5f2534ca.text:
It is a single-tower with a circular plan (diameter 9.60 m) reduced to a heap of ruins. The wall face, composed of medium-sized stones laid in horizontal courses, survives to a maximum height of 2.20 m with 3 to 4 courses.

Due to the collapse, the internal structure of the monument cannot be known.

5d5252d91a34d630.text: It is a small single-tower nuraghe. The ruin stands at most about 2 metres high and consists of a few superimposed courses of medium-sized, roughly worked stones. The external diameter of the nuraghe is about 11 metres. It is built of mixed basalt, limestone and schist stones. The monument is in a precarious state of preservation.

5d60c694dd5f0dbb.text: The nuraghe is hidden beneath an impenetrable layer of vegetation.

5d7fff7dc905a95f.text: Single-tower nuraghe partially collapsed. Most of the walling remains on one side.

5d90f505ce192a95.text: It is also known as Su Canarzu and is recognised as Su Aijanu, which is the name of the plot of land on which it is built. Only the large closure stone and the two jambs are visible. In the surrounding area there are stones worked by man that were used to mark boundaries, and also wild olive or mastic trees.

5d98059efa231513.text: Multi-lobed nuraghe with an outer wall, a straight curtain wall, built of basalt blocks; Roman Republican settlement on the ruins of the nuraghe. Traces of the nuraghe were discovered during road construction works for the pylon foundations of the viaduct: the site has been extensively documented and is now completely concealed.

5d9f570d3b451d65.text: The nuraghe, or probably the proto-nuraghe Monte Uri given its features, appears imposing, leaning against and therefore erected in symbiosis with a large granite boulder; it preserves an intact tholos and from its position dominates the Oschiri countryside. For us it was a great surprise to see it, admire it and be able to confirm that where this place-name occurs, remains of very ancient monuments are generally found. (ArcheoUri)

5da4c9283268c34c.text: Single-tower nuraghe built on a rocky outcrop. Only a few courses remain visible, intersected by the rock, together with some lower wall structures, though still connected to the nuraghe.

5ddbbe745311d558.text: The nuraghe apparently composed of three towers; inside, three niches can be seen. On the left, a staircase leads to the upper levels, and surrounding it are the remains of the Nuragic village, with some red stones from the area. To the left of the nuraghe lies a small necropolis.

5ddf7309b956e91d.text: Situated near the S'Urri valley (where other domus de janas are found), in the Su Linnarbu gorge, on some outcropping rock faces small rock-cut chambers were excavated, of which only slight traces remain because the large natural inlet was used as a dump for inert materials by Italcementi. However, cut into the upper edges that bound the rocky plateau, a few small cavities are still just visible, attributable to prehistoric tombs of the pre-Nuragic period.

5de07489db9c618a.text: It stands on the left-hand side of the Samatzai–Serrenti municipal road in the locality of the same name, on a slight rise of the plateau. It is a single-tower nuraghe with an external diameter of 10 m and a wall thickness of about 2 m. The basal course, formed of large limestone blocks quarried from the surrounding area which is rich in such outcrops, survives almost intact all round the circumference.

5de5cd3b85a6f7b2.text: Also known as "Sa Grutta de Santu Giuanni", it presents the classic planimetric layout of giants' tombs. The burial chamber (22.10 m²), arranged along a north-south axis with an entrance to the south, is surrounded externally by rows of granite blocks of varying sizes. The façade remains partially excavated and cluttered with rubble.

5de675e096ced975.text: The megalithic tomb is located further ahead, in a small open area. Of the monument, composed of a short funerary corridor made of rose trachyte slabs, only the base course remains; the entrance is marked by two carefully worked rectangular slabs, while the external wall, following the profile of the funerary corridor, is built with vertical slabs and a fill of small stones.

5de7b84081eec217.text: Completely dislodged structure, the original form of which is barely discernible.

5df5fabd3bb31dc1.text: Ruined nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower is ruined; it has a fairly broad terrace running all round the main tower. There is a secondary entrance on the north-east. Hut bases are found nearby at the foot of the nuraghe.

5e376969432acec6.text:
A particular structure is present, which appears to be nuragic and may have been used for surveillance.

Probable location.

5e44a45e1562bdfe.text: If one considers the defensive function of the nuraghes, this one at Elighia I° is the most evident example. It stands at an elevation above 600 m.a.s.l., dominating the surrounding countryside at 360 degrees and acting as a sentinel, keeping watch over anyone who might unwise enough venture into these territories. Unfortunately, it is also in a state of ruin. mu

5e6d5e260a68f2a5.text:
Although the current state is entirely characterized by collapses affecting the entire site, I must admit that it evokes interest and respect for the grandeur of the cyclopean stones, only a few of which remain in situ. The state of devastation is evident.

Nuraghe della Tortorella. mu

5e965265339575b9.text:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower enclosed by a quadrilobate bastion with four corner towers connected by curtain walls with a concave-convex profile.

The bastion (NS axis m. 17) is well preserved on the western side and only partially on the northwest side, while it appears completely collapsed and covered in debris along the remaining perimeter.

5e9a02e98549d6cf.text: It is a well-proportioned and harmonious three-lobed nuraghe. Only part of it is accessible due to obvious and widespread collapses. The construction techniques and features of first order are particularly noteworthy. Although the name derives from the local topographic term, it nonetheless indicates intense copper-smelting activity. Numerous semi-finished bronze artefacts with a bull's hide form are present.

5eaea2a234f9aba8.text: Three giants' tombs are present at the site, all built with schist stone.

5ebe7b8b3a44a0ce.text: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a high hill, from which the view perfectly extends over the area of S'Adde 'e S'Ulumu,

5ed22969503dba89.text: It is a proto-nuraghe or early nuraghe.

5ef29c5be1f5c7c7.text: All that remains of the nuraghe are some courses arranged in a circular order that formed the base of a single-tower.

5ef5f9c9d07c4dce.text: It is a ruined nuraghe of which only little remains.

5f22a5aae6913761.text: The Nolza nuraghe is a large four-lobed nuraghe, formed by four corner towers joined by straight bastions and a central tower still standing 13 metres high. Archaeological investigations, begun in 1994 and still in progress, have made it possible to distinguish several construction phases, characterised by alterations and adaptations. In a first phase the nuraghe was built of local schist, the material of which the central tower and two of the corner towers still consist.

5f2a672b3c95e59c.text: Located on the edge of a cliff, less than 400 metres north of the "Pattada" nuraghe, now reduced to a heap of rubble, it is covered by shrub vegetation.

5f300937d2a6d5da.text: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghes, of which three to four external courses of the wall remain, with a maximum height of about 2.50 m. The internal chamber has collapsed, and the debris from the collapse fills the space. Built with locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The entrance cannot be identified. The structures are largely covered by vegetation.

5f32bb0d1d452a3b.text: On a mountain terrace located at the base of the Ischiriddé pinnacle, the village of Sas Funtanas stood, at a very short distance from the Duas Vuccas cave. Lilliu reports the discovery of fragments of grinding stones and grinders, and of a white-ware jar containing a copper chisel, and notes the presence of a small village now no longer visible due to dense vegetation.

5f3dea0954fe4515.text: One of the six coastal nuraghi on the island of Sant'Antioco — a single-tower nuraghe with an adjoining probable hut or other room — stands on the rocky outcrop of the same name, in a strategic position in the cove “Su Portu de su Casu”. A few courses of the original tower and a short stretch of walling to the east of it survive. The line of the inner face of the chamber can no longer be traced, as its interior is completely covered by vegetation and collapse.

5f43f83f3cd1bf95.text: The Menhir Terra Coccoi is located on a hilltop at about 1 km north-east of Nuraxi Figus. It has a remaining height of about 2 metres.

5f71a32876f1818d.text:
Dated to the 11th century BC. Temple built with isodomic calcareous ashlar, an achievement of refined architecture. The external walls are decorated with rows of carved notches on the ashlar. Water is channeled into the well through gutters and then into an external basin.

It shows some similarities with the well at Predio Canopoli in Perfugas.

5f77e41c033d6fb9.text:
A few courses still visible at the Peidru nuraghe, a probable single-tower nuraghe located on SP8 near the old bridge maintenance station at Oinu.

A notable stone with three holes is observed at the base of the monument.

5f79057a17ef5290.text: The nuraghe, probably of complex structure, was built on the same rocky ridge as the corridor nuraghe, to the north of it. It shows a very extensive collapse. The central tower can be identified thanks to the presence of two courses of boulders that survive in their original position. On the rocky ridge there is a curvilinear wall running from the west side round to the south-south-east side. On the south side stretches of walling, not well defined because of the collapses, appear to link the two nuraghi.

5f8e57a148de858c.text: About 150 m from the Bigozzi nuraghe, in a north-western direction, lies the giants' tomb, bearing the same name. Built on a small platform made of small stones, the burial preserves the funerary corridor composed of granite orthostats; the roof is missing and the apsidal slab lies on the ground, while only a short section of the exedra, located outside, remains visible.

5faaa1bfb25db07d.text:
Complex nuraghe consisting of a central body with a bastion and four lateral towers. Bronze Age II, 2nd millennium B.C.

A large nuraghe at the top of the hill dominating the Colostrai pond, in an area that during the Nuragic period was densely inhabited. A harbour and two inlets, partly navigable, completely controlled.

5fb476c574eef11d.text:
The distinctive features:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.

5fb4f13df6f996fc.text: It is the uniqueness of the site in hosting so many ceremonial circles that leads one to believe in an exaggerated construction effort with no specific purpose. It is instead believed that the site's significance stems precisely from the presence of so many ceremonial circles, indicating a substantial population.

5fbf0f937c924f60.text: It is a complex structure consisting of a main tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber surrounded by three niches arranged in a cross pattern, plus an addition of uncertain typological interpretation. The circular tower (diameter 11 m along the north-south axis) survives to a maximum height of about 6.50 m.

6015c9ad35beae2d.text: Domus de janas built around a central acrocoro on which the traces of a hut or megalithic circle are evident.

6026d659ae30458a.text: Base of a nuraghe near the old fire watch tower, built with schist blocks.

6043637ab6672650.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, the tomb structure, partially covered by surface soil, the funerary corridor, and the exedra are identifiable.

The construction type is coursed, using polygonal sub-squared granite blocks.

6072213d7ebf795f.text:
A nuraghe in the territory of Ulassai, in the province of Ogliastra, is the second largest after the nuraghe s'Ulimu in the same municipality. It belongs to the complex in the "Neuletta" area, where besides it there are two other nuraghi and a small megalithic village, called Nuragheddos in the local Sardinian.

The nuraghe was built in the period between the Middle Bronze Age and the Final Bronze Age, therefore around 1400–900 BC.

60bf8d0fb719884f.text: Structures belonging to a complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The central tower has its lower chamber intact and the base of the upper one; the northern part of the bastion is visible, with two towers, while the whole southern part is covered by vegetation. The other two towers, not yet located because they are hidden by vegetation, may lie to the south of the central tower.

60c4b8337286b641.text: Mainly composed of stones similar to those of the Arresi nuraghe, four towers are visible, plus one almost completely destroyed. Some elderly people still remember that the tower exposed to the north-west was intact. They say there was a well so deep that the sound of stones being dropped into it could not be heard.

60d8821446f0b7dc.text: It is a group of six domus de janas tombs, of which five, of the monocellular oven type, are in very poor condition, while the sixth features a sub-square antechamber from which access is gained to an adjacent rectangular chamber.

6109c31be6d0a334.text:
Buried and partially concealed by anti-aircraft installations from the Second World War. Traces of a Bronze Age village between southwest and east.

Chronology: Bronze Age Nuragic (for the nuraghe and the village); contemporary period (circa 1942–43: for the military post).

6152c21b393c6105.text: Nuraghe completely collapsed, of which only a few traces remain on the surface.

615e864d0e703da9.text: Nuraghe completely collapsed, its shape difficult to define

618d5b709508455b.text:
A true necropolis of giants' tombs – comprising 4 or possibly 5 burials, two of which have "a stele centinata", all still preserved in good condition.

The main burial features a broad arched exedra – with slightly suggested wings – placed directly on the tomb's body, with no break in continuity, and a wall face with a concave-convex profile.

619eadf033e61b57.text: The nuraghe is a complex structure consisting of a central tower to which a bastion has been attached, the bastion featuring three secondary towers connected by a curtain wall with a concave-convex profile: two towers are positioned on the front, the third is offset to the south (towards N). The bastion has a curved eastern face (height 5.00 m), at its centre where the entrance opens (width 1.10 m; height 1.60 m), today partially blocked.

61b02a7d2b303c13.text: Nuraghe surrounded by vegetation and eroded

61b675635fccbd53.text: Prof. Ercole Contu reports in 1992 that there are twenty large baetyls placed halfway along the coast on the south-east slope of Monte Cachile. Some geologists have been involved, and in part have ruled out a natural geological origin. The site has been known to the local population for generations, and orally passed down is a legend that women in labour were brought to the site to give birth.

61c5fc904eb19132.text: Damaged nuraghe with multiple towers, undecipherable, part of a larger settlement.

61de255ac5304d26.text:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.

Attached to the nuraghe, a boundary wall was built for a villa.

61f03582616032a1.text:
It is located near the campsite of the same name.

It consists of 25 menhirs, 22 of which are standing (but only five in their original position, as the others have been erected by the archaeological site's construction team).

620c5ccf808a9f07.text:
Megalithic funerary structure composed of three vertical stone slabs set at right angles to one another.

Archaeologists have interpreted it as a dolmen, although like all the other surrounding monuments, it requires more in-depth scientific investigation.

621d2dbeb7675245.text: Nuragic village, never the subject of studies or excavations, located within the Gutturu Mannu park, in the Assemini administrative enclave, on the left bank of the river, facing the homonymous springs. Completely surrounded by the cork oak forest, it is almost invisible from the outside.

6248aadab4ed254f.text: In the area, where a Nuragic site probably once existed, a calcination oven has been built, which in recent times has been repurposed as a dwelling. Adjacent to it are the remains of a recently constructed house. The oven's construction, likely, dates to the end of the 1800s or early 1890s: many other ovens of the same period were erected in Sant'Antioco.

625ae3ca646d6515.text: No trace of the nuraghe remains, except for the stone structures that border the properties. Numerous pottery fragments, however, are present.

626223723c7c0a65.text: It is a giants' tomb with a collapsed structure and in relative abandonment.

627fc051917f84fa.text:
The monument appears as a large sub-circular enclosure (diameter about 18 m), with a wall thickness of about 2.50–3 m and a maximum remaining height of about 1.50–2 m, featuring two courses.

The masonry is composed of large polygonal blocks arranged in horizontal courses.

From what can be seen, it is most likely a corridor nuraghe.

628271bb90ac5109.text: Complex nuraghe composed of a central mastio and two towers with a courtyard.

62a5fea14262cb0a.text: The burial, located near two nuraghe and a village, still preserves the tomb structure. It includes a burial chamber constructed with granite blocks of various sizes, shaped obliquely on the exposed face and arranged in irregular courses using wooden wedges for support.

62c88bbe66d99297.text: The nuraghe is in a state of considerable degradation, and there are artificial structures also inside the nuraghe.

62cbf61345ad9eb6.text: South of the nuraghe and near the village huts, there is a rectangular structure cut into the ground to a depth (visible) of about 150 cm, about 120 cm wide and 250 cm long, surrounded by trachyte stones of varying sizes. The interior is almost completely filled with fallen stones and vegetation, making it difficult to accurately determine its dimensions and structure.

62fadff2b58ec710.text:
It is a small artificial cave cut into a single rounded block of limestone. The oven-mouthed entrance faces south-east and leads into a longitudinally developed space, divided into several chambers, which must have formed the rooms of a hypogeal burial.

The tomb shows no decorative motifs and has yielded no grave goods. It is dated to the Late Neolithic and demonstrates the occupation of the territory from the pre-Nuragic period.

6338d1dce4862369.text: Certainly a central-tower nuraghe of note. The central tower soars, and from what can be made out it must have been a four-lobed nuraghe with a village around it. The tholos has collapsed inwards.

6347717477fdd088.text: The structure is built onto a natural rocky outcrop and forms an enclosure about 50 by 32 metres with an average height of about 3 metres. Access to the interior was through two lateral portals on the north and south sides. The entrances are followed by a walled corridor. Inside, a large granite boulder, which some say has the features of a mother goddess, leads them to hypothesise a temple function for the area.

6349de2ae427dba5.text: The Tomb of the Three Hundred is the most significant structure and part of a larger necropolis discovered during the construction works of SS131. It is named after the number of skeletons found within the walls surrounding the burial area.

634ee5dc99e94aa4.text:
It is one of many prehistoric monuments that make Seneghe one of the Sardinian comuni with the highest density of material evidence from that remote civilization.

Single-tower partially collapsed and overgrown with vegetation

634ef1fcbc9a2242.text: Monte Claro culture underground chamber discovered during works at "nuova 554". It consists of two underground chambers with vertical access shafts and various funerary furnishings.

635c6dc3311feafc.text: Dr. Aste maintains that Su Doladorgiu, in its original form, was a fortress, the reconstruction of which he has proposed, equipped with towers and a nuraghe. For strategic defensive reasons, it was built in the Nuragic period to oversee the entire valley; from the sea, incursions by enemies and invaders were feared.

638e0b2c0bc6045b.text:
Romanzesu is one of the most important settlement and cult complexes of Nuragic Sardinia, with about a hundred huts, five cult buildings — a sacred well temple and four "megaron" temples — and a large ceremonial enclosure. It is built of local granite.

The area develops around the sacred well temple, built into the rock from whose fissures spring water emerges. It has an access stair and a circular chamber built with regular courses of carefully worked blocks.

6392c7218f11e912.text: It is located above the Church of Santa Lucia. Only little remains visible, particularly a wall of the tower (I believe it is a single-tower nuraghe) on the northern side and some varied courses.

63a34e2c6de8db70.text: It has a quadrangular plan with a rounded profile and a maximum surviving height of 3.65 m on the south-east side, with five courses, while on the north-west it is 2.00 m with four courses. The masonry consists of large, barely dressed boulders laid in very irregular horizontal rows. The building has two coaxial entrances, the first to the ESE and the second to the WNW, linked by a corridor that runs orthogonally to the structure's long axis.

63e6ec33e83522ce.text: The Nissardi in 1901 (map included in G. Pinza's volume) indicated a giants' tomb slightly south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that actually lies within the perimeter of the airport.

63ef5fb02a417e88.text: Damaged nuraghe, with the upper part of the tholos collapsed. Set within a forest.

63fccd20ee293649.text: Nuragic village almost entirely covered by debris, vegetation, and stones from cleared lands.

64057d35d3f71662.text: The present structures suggest the remains of a possible proto-nuraghe. From a high vantage point, at least two rectangular rooms can be distinguished, while the rest of the structure is hidden by vegetation. Unfortunately, the various field clearing operations, followed by the accumulation of stones above the ancient structures, create doubts about the true nature of any other possible buildings.

6418fa53230d8467.text: Damaged nuraghe but with the interior accessible. The portal and about five courses of the wall masonry remain.

64194bea6a6a099c.text: The few known finds from the A1 rock shelter at Monti Crastu, used as a burial and violated by clandestine digging, are attributed to the Abealzu phase. The size and position of the proto-nuraghi at Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest that these may have been the most important centres of proto-Nuragic cantons or sub-cantons in the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other complex proto-nuraghi, they could have controlled a large part of it.

642f951df74196f5.text:
Situated a short distance from the rural church of S. Gavino and about a hundred metres to the north-west of the Nuraghe Toscono, with which it had a close cultural relationship, the tomb of Santu Bainzu is of the dolmenic type with a monolithic arched stele, aligned along the SE-NW axis and with the entrance to the south-east.

It was recorded by Lamarmora, whose drawing still shows the orthostats of the exedra in situ, whereas they are no longer present in a later plan sketch by Mackenzie.

6444c2f12129d861.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe in a state of serious deterioration. The perhaps improper description comes from the fact that these monuments speak and shout like living beings. History of our forebears, of a great people who managed to express their own culture of peace and solidarity among small shepherd-kings federated in a single great state. What was said elsewhere for the many monuments in the territory of Chiaramonti applies here.

(photo Mario Unali)

6468b1895ff850a2.text: The poor state of preservation does not allow a clear reading of the structure, which nevertheless appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical shape.

647880e609c6a9d0.text: Two multi-chambered domus de janas are cut into the limestone ridge that bounds the Baddenare plateau. Both have an antechamber, a main chamber and two side cells. One is entered through a long dromos, the other through a raised doorway above ground level. The domus with the dromos entrance preserves two fine columns in the main chamber and an incised inscription (L M S), probably Roman or medieval in date.

647f613dec78cda4.text: The slow retreat of the water, caused by drought, reveals what normally lies submerged. All around, clear Nuragic traces are visible, such as the sacred huts and other rooms typical of the period. On a small promontory stands another nuraghe, “Sa tanca 'e sa Mura”, and a little further on a third, “Tudera Alto”, of which, unfortunately, only a few of its cyclopean stone courses have survived.

64ac278d9b02f40c.text: Remains of a megalithic circular structure with an apparent entrance portal.

64e4b48052df25f5.text:
It is located in the territory of Goni (CA).

Although signage highlights the presence of a giants' tomb, the architectural type (the monument features two opposing apses) is not well attested in funerary contexts.

It could be a cult enclosure.

64f66b18309b5192.text: At first sight a single-tower nuraghe, in reality a complex one with buried structures covered by vegetation. The original tower preserves its entire perimeter circuit. On the SE side there is perhaps a raised entrance. The interior of the tower is blocked by boulders and earth. To the SE an obvious attempt at illicit excavation has exposed the outer wall face of the tower. To the S and SW circular curtain walls can be seen that may belong to two further towers.

650b0c22b492ca29.text: Domus de janas on a trachytic cliff, internally decorated with a false door and a possibly carved hearth.

651c2be9b1cfbcf4.text:
It is located within the municipal territory of Monastir (CA).

The archaeological area was discovered during excavation works for the 131.

6534a1b5e2cf9e96.text: Damaged nuraghe of which a good height of about 3 metres is preserved.

6535dcb4afbd2f4f.text:
Throughout the area, there are settlements and remains of huts dating from the Neolithic to the Medieval period.

This nuraghe is in a state of complete abandonment; no recovery works or excavations have ever been carried out to reveal or bring to light any artefacts.

6580e25bf154b7be.text: Built from limestone blocks and erected on a rocky outcrop, it consists of a central tower, an added body where traces of a corridor and remnants of some huts on the western side are visible. It is in poor state of conservation.

658374abb4ab4b59.text: Vittorio Angius calls it Fumìu: "It is a design of such a kind that no idea of it can be given without having drawn it." He goes on to state that several nuraghi make it up: "Above the door opening towards the sirocco-levante there is a loophole, and not far from it a second door opening to the sirocco and two metres high, which however, being high above the ground, looks like a window: on one side of it the gallery within the wall thickness opens, leading to the upper floors or the terrace."

65a0cdcee9399deb.text: The monument is located on a natural terraced area, in a hillside region used for grazing. About 300 m to the north-west lies the giants' tomb of Funtana Morta. The nuraghe is almost completely destroyed, and only the external plan can be observed, faintly circular.

65c6585f25731054.text: The nuraghe preserves the tholos intact, but due to the collapse at the entrance it cannot be visited. The chamber has four niches; it is one of the very few nuraghes known so far to possess this feature.

65ca6fdef2c2ee84.text:
Dolmenic burial with an apsidal corridor.

Located in the territory of the comune of Narbolia (OR)

65d441c6d88faf0c.text: The nuraghe is subterranean, probably a single-tower and single-cell structure. The external wall has parts that project. The internal wall retains three courses that completely close the circular space. The lintel at the entrance was inserted into a dry-stone wall.

65e5952e3a03e8a1.text: It is a large Nuragic village, currently only a small amount remains; only the presence of mounds and scattered stones around the homonymous nuraghe can be observed.

65edfcedaef5f094.text: Nuraghe almost completely dismantled, only a few courses of stones remain.

65ef4a53027a1bf7.text: Likely domus de janas, currently used as a dog kennel. It is probable that other domus de janas existed in the area, now destroyed due to building activities.

65f88d12f3d9a627.text:
This nuraghe has unique features, such as the three different helical staircases that led from the ground up to the upper levels.

Today, very little of what once stood remains. The height of the central tower and the massive scale of the building can be inferred from the diameter of the tower, the imposing size of the ashlars, and the extent of the whole footprint of the main structure.

In this case, too, a village of considerable size must have developed around it.

660167fb7777fe1c.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan. The nuraghe stands on a basaltic platform at the summit of Monte S. Antonio, south-west of the country church dedicated to the Santo. The monument rests on the edge of a cliff that forms a natural bastion along the western arc of the tower, gradually declining towards the north-northeast where the structure sits upon a plain.

6604a7b0274216dd.text: There are six domus de janas on site.

660fc159d3c39a44.text: It is a small single-chamber tomb, of oven type, circular in plan (depth 0.55 m – width 0.62 m), accessed through a finely carved opening (width ….. – height 0.42 m – thickness 0.12 m), preceded by a short antechamber (depth 0.32 m – width 0.75/0.48 m). The orientation is to the south; the walls are perfectly smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.

661319f1b2172355.text: It is visible from the SS131 and immediately strikes you as a special nuraghe. Special because it combines the features of a nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber and a truncated-cone nuraghe. On entering, you find yourself in the long chamber, which has two large niches and is about 7 metres high; at the far end a doorway leads to a staircase that, plunging into darkness and enclosed by the nuragic walls, spirals up to the upper floor.

66309609d4e5cb8e.text: The nuraghe, in a good state of preservation, consists of a main tholos to which other masonry parts were added later. A long corridor and a staircase lead off from the entrance. In the main chamber, where the roof has collapsed, there are several niches. The nuraghe, datable to 1500–1200 BC, stands on a hill whose slopes show the remains of circular and oval walls, probably belonging to a village.

66481ae229fabb1a.text: Complex nuraghe, quadrilobate, of which only a small amount remains

6648d6cc6bccf073.text: The nuraghe is multi-lobed, consisting of a central tower surrounded by five towers, some of which are in a good state of preservation. The towers have lost their tops; originally the tower summits must have been crowned with stone battlements, which were recovered at the base of the structures during the most recent archaeological excavations carried out on the monument following the collapses.

6649f3b1cb29415a.text: Nuraghe “a tancato” has on the front face of the main tower a wall of irregular shape that encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.

665970e04e53254e.text:
It is a nuraghe that is hard to classify typologically because of the collapse and the dense shrubby vegetation covering it.

The masonry consists of medium-sized stones laid in regular horizontal courses. The few features observed do not help to understand the ground plan of this structure, which excavation might reveal to be a proto-nuraghe rather than a classic tholos nuraghe.

669b9a3a6991872c.text: Two nuraghe towers very close to each other

66b47f91916c0a9c.text: It is a complex nuraghe, whose plan is impossible to determine because it is largely buried. A tower to the west is visible, with about five courses visible. From the other areas, scattered circular courses emerge.

66be76584516d532.text: Un ruined nuraghe never studied, of which only a few courses remain. A singular and remarkable stone worked near the proto-nuraghe, above a few rudimentary remains entirely indeterminate, might be interpreted as a fragment of a mound originally shaped and placed above a domus with a façade, or alternatively as a covering element of a giants' tomb.

66cb74c5a0fab348.text: It is a domus excavated at the base of a trachytic rock outcrop.

6700174566a64b82.text: Single-tower made of large white limestone blocks, located in the courtyard of a private dwelling. About three courses remain, with a maximum height of about 3 m and a minimum of about 2 m. Base diameter: about 15 m. The structure is in a state of collapse; conservation state: mediocre.

6713c64deb9753cf.text: There are not enough elements to provide a reasoned classification, yet despite the most recent modifications, I consider it to be a Nuragic source.

67155568138260e3.text: The tomb, because of the collapse of its side structures and the lush vegetation that covers most of it, does not clearly show its layout. However, some ashlars still in their original position suggest a rectangular plan. At the sides and in the surrounding area there are heaps of earth mixed with boulders and rubble that probably belonged to the tomb structure, clear signs of the violation carried out by clandestine diggers.

67598d2324934d65.text: We find it listed in the map of the 1844 State General Census, as Nuraghe Numassi.

677956d7acb63f5c.text: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.

67cb1ef57bf88eda.text: The monument, inside the village of Sagama near the parish church, is a single-tower nuraghe with a stair, a corridor niche and a central chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross.

67e1067a7f42000a.text: Circular single-tower nuraghe with a southern entrance topped by a stone lintel. The central chamber, elongated, is distinguished by the presence of four niches—an unusual feature—located one on the left side, one at the back opposite the entrance, and two (in pairs) on the right side. All are semi-elliptical in plan; the cross-section is trapezoidal, like that of the access passage. The remaining conical height is about 3 m.

67e9a808c544cedf.text: another nuraghe in the Segariu area, though neglected and eroded

67f504832ed0aa7a.text: Located on a plateau adjacent to the Rio Caddare, the tomb is situated at a short distance from the site of Lettu Rucratu. The burial, which prior to excavation and restoration work showed significant damage caused by mechanical equipment that had removed parts of the chamber and exedra, was constructed using an orthostat technique. The site has yielded materials datable to the early BM period.

6833037cfdc0b3b4.text: It consists of about ten metres of megalithic wall made of large boulders placed on the ridge north of Monte Zennaru, facing Runaghe Paulusedda or Palusedda, in the centre of which the Rio Murrone flows as a winter torrent. The construction gives the impression of being intended, almost, to watch over that river crossing. On close examination there are no traces of any other building in the vicinity.

6844f183f79790d5.text:
The nuraghe is a single-tower built with large, well-cut stones.

The entrance is covered by an imposing lintel and leads into a corridor featuring a niche on the right side and a staircase opening on the left; the latter is largely blocked by debris. At the end of the corridor opens a circular chamber, with the tholos vault still intact, containing three niches arranged symmetrically.

684f06e6ef141592.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of blocks about two metres high.

684fa7de19e47212.text: Complex two-tower nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

6875625bc164c04c.text: Around the parish church the remains of an important settlement have come to light, including three wells and Hut 5, interpreted as a council hall. The discovery of terracotta casting moulds in the area outside "Hut 4" proves that metal artefacts were produced on the spot. By the threshold of "Hut 1", also of the Final Bronze Age, a clay bowl containing ox-hide ingots was found, deposited in the Iron Age.

68786d9114bdf062.text: The nuraghe located at the summit of a rugged hilltop, characterized by dense undergrowth, is built on a granitic rocky outcrop that provides an excellent view of the areas below. The monument, in a severe state of degradation, is a simple single-tower nuraghe with a sub-circular plan, barely discernible due to the extent of the collapse.

6888f5cd956acb4a.text:
Small dolmen composed of two vertical slabs upon which rests a well-shaped covering slab.

The back wall is instead formed by two base stones upon which smaller stones are placed to close the chamber.

For the valorisation and access to the monument, the surrounding area has been fenced off and connected to the municipal road network via a fenced path.

68a64104c726e378.text: Single-tower nuraghe, with part of the tholos remaining and the access portal restored.

68d83c82bcdd6275.text: It consists of only a few meagre remains and some stones of the nuraghe, which is completely overgrown by vegetation.

68e5f92fcb3e8652.text: Single-tower nuraghe; located inside a military area. The tholos survives intact. The site is now accessible (it is still advisable to ask for "authorisation" at the "Bechi Luserna" Barracks).

68f8ed78d7ee1cc9.text: Only a few courses of the nuraghe remain. Located in a position of observation and signaling, it provides a view spanning 360 degrees over all the surrounding mountains and nuraghes.

6900ff05eaccf2dc.text: The menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini stands on a promontory at an altitude of about 230 m above sea level. It is a monolith whose shape is probably the work of weathering. It has the appearance of a human face. Some believe it was connected with the ancient cult of the Mother Goddess, especially given the presence of remains of ill-defined structures next to one of the two monoliths. In ancient times, and still today, it is regarded as the centre of the Island.

690fd6fbbe951729.text: The well located south of the cave and at a short distance from it has an oval shape. The well was cut into a rocky outcrop that forms the northern side and, partially, the eastern and western sides. A masonry structure made of parallelipipedal stones completes the eastern and western sides and fully encloses the southern side.

691ee05cf10ef2b1.text: The burial is located on the flat summit of Planu Borgolo, about 50 m east of the SS131 road, which separates it from the surrounding settlement context. Of the tomb, only the burial layout and the funerary corridor—formed by several large orthostats, especially at the terminal end—are still visible; only some elements remain of the exedra.

692fee2f043a86a5.text: Erased, buried, little known and never excavated, it is visible while travelling along S.S. 131.

6945f079120a1ebf.text: The tomb without a cover has an external profile of the central body with concave wall faces. The exedra has curved arms. The burial chamber is oblong. A row of infill stones along the apse is visible.

69696041360cb29d.text: Complex nuraghe with walls made of dressed ashlar stones and of similar thickness. Damaged, collapsed, and partially buried.

696d13a6d8f48621.text: Nuraghe partially collapsed, with a dozen courses still standing, located beside two rural buildings

6981ddb1ccff9f27.text: Tafone/luttoni – rock shelter probably used in prehistoric and protohistoric times, possibly as dwelling for human families. There is no certainty regarding its identification due to the lack of in-depth studies, and thus information is very limited. The only indications suggesting its identification as such are other rock shelters located nearby (exactly three) and a giants' tomb at a short distance.

6996399ccaf60c1c.text: It is a masterpiece of architecture and harmonious, sacred construction. In front of the tumulus, turned upside down from both above and below, frequently visited by tomb-bearers, there extends an exedra in two rows of roughly hewn stones. From the arms of the exedra emerges a circle of single stones with a diameter of 15 m.

69c0f776ae03b9d0.text: Simple proto-nuraghe, of which only very little remains

69e5ffa1b97081b4.text: Single-tower nuraghe of which only a very small, or no, remains. Inhabited until the Recent Bronze Age. Afterward, life ceases at many nuraghes, which have lost their original function.

69e65c7e0c766b16.text: Built of squared limestone blocks, it stands at least six courses high and has a well-defined, legible façade even from a distance. It was investigated in the 20th century with unsystematic excavations undertaken by the then Honorary Inspector Cornelio Puxeddu. About 25 m west of the nuraghe and at a lower elevation, a building of uncertain purpose was erected in modern times; it has a cemented stone wall with an iron door and an upper skylight.

6a1bac3a3c22935c.text: The archaeological site of Bruncu Suergiu lies in the Giara Park. Hidden by vegetation and hard to reach. Traces of ancient routes, a large settlement with production facilities, and defensive structures characterise the site. Besides the huge quantity of material, a broad terrace looks out over the Campidano, offering a breathtaking view. Only the panorama repays the long and difficult walk. The archaeological area, which is protected, covers about 11 hectares.

6a2121e8b343a424.text:
A particularly striking proto-nuraghe for the beauty of its proto-historic architecture, the original tholos access is preserved, integrated within the rocky mass.  

Outside the granite block, and visible, are depressions that form natural sculptures; inside there is a shelter beneath rock, probably already in use in earlier periods.

6a2bc7ccb8092782.text: There are 22 Nuragic villages known within the municipal territory, both large and small, and not all of them were inhabited simultaneously. Often they are located near a nuraghe, as in the case of the Bruncu Pubusa site; in other cases (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis, and Sa Serra) they are located without any nearby nuraghe.

6a2c8b0ba2e2ab9c.text: Neolithic burial composed of two chambers connected by a door, which has, above it, a probable bull's-head protome.

6a4214210a8b6a67.text: Nuragic hut or nuraghe base, not marked on IGM map, currently reduced to a rubble heap

6a630e9080899c09.text: A short distance from the Sant'Andria nuraghe, in the north-west direction, lies the domus de janas, which is carved into a granitic outcrop. The entrance has collapsed, so access to the underground chamber is through an irregular opening; this chamber features a small antechamber from which the entrance to the second chamber opens. Around it, fragments and pieces of lithic material are scattered.

6a69c8f17414948b.text:
The monument stands about twenty metres from a second giants' tomb and about 200 metres from the eponymous nuraghe; it is not traceable in the outer perimeter because of its very poor state of preservation.

A fragment of an arched stele (height 0.46 m; width 1.25 m) with a raised frame, 12 cm wide on the left and 15–17 cm on the right, reused in the paving of the nearby church of Santa Sabina, probably belongs to this tomb.

6a6d13e1576fabf0.text: In the area of Monte Sa Scrocca Manna, on the boundary between the municipalities of Sant'Antioco and Calasetta, there are several structures that originally most likely formed part of a Punic and/or Roman settlement. Unfortunately, during the Second World War military works irreparably damaged their walls. Some stretches of walling, still fairly well preserved, survive, together with various squared and moulded ashlars reused in the military constructions.

6aa974f09d6c166c.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe, not marked on the IGM map.

6ad28b4d97bacb67.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is practically destroyed. On the ground one can make out a course of the stones that formed the funerary corridor and blocks belonging to the exedra.

The most visible distinctive element is the terminal slab of the funerary corridor, still in its original position. The construction technique must have been of the coursed type, using polygonal blocks.

6adf301083235435.text: One of the numerous dolmen present in the Sardinian territory. Dolmen (from Breton tol-men, "stone table") are funerary monuments erected presumably during the recent Neolithic and early Neolithic (3400–2700 BC).

6ae3f76b0aa2ac2e.text: Unfortunately, very little of the tomb remains: today the central corridor of the burial chamber can still be made out, its walls once formed by courses of stones laid neatly as in nuraghe corridors; the stones that framed the central doorway are also present, together with many other stones scattered all around. Finally, a single stone slab (or orthostat) survives which, set in a row with many others, formed one of the two wings of the exedra.

6af0be8720cc9c6a.text: A burial of the Nuragic period built of polygonal trachyte blocks. Little of the tomb is visible because of the vegetation; the corridor and the exedra survive. From what the remains and the vegetation allow one to see, the two arms (running straight) that define the exedra consist of two superimposed wall faces of different widths with a set-back that presumably served as a seat. mu.

6b0429ccd1085386.text: The remains of the nuraghe are hard to make out; it has certainly been dismantled and the ashlars may have been used to build the retaining walls and boundary walls found in the area where the nuraghe probably stood. From the booklet “Ritratto di nuraghe eredità di un'isola …” by Sara Muscuso we read: “All that remains of the nuraghe is a curvilinear wall face made up of one or two courses.”

6b10177fdebe1a02.text: The Nuragic village of Neulè is located in the area of the same name, a few kilometres from the settlement of Dorgali. The site includes numerous intact huts, a sacred well, and a nuraghe.

6b131317526a1666.text: Leaving the village of Irgoli towards Onifai/Orosei, just before a small bridge, turn onto the road for Capo Comino. After only 300 m, at the junction for the bypass, a municipal asphalt road begins on the right. Follow this road for about 5 km until you see two prominent granite pillars on the left. Walk on until you reach the Domus de Janas Sa Conca 'e mortu.

6b1ef0ccd7fd1bd6.text: There is no trace of the nuraghe remaining, apart from a large amount of rubble from the collapse, hidden by vegetation.

6b48d2cdd29e2fa7.text: The monument must have been a far more complex and articulated structure than one can imagine today, looking at the surviving ruins, which nevertheless still retain a semblance of their original monumentality. The first tower, circular in plan, has its foundations set on a bedrock surface; the inner chamber has an oval layout whose elongated end joins the wall face of what must have been the main tower.

6b5078cf2a9b0331.text: Nuraghe probably a single-tower, covered by collapse and vegetation. Only a single course emerges.

6b523dfb7260d951.text: Isolated menhir, on its back bearing an alignment of cups.

6b5fd112e3ebacd6.text: In an advanced state of abandonment, the curtain wall oriented east-west is still visible, constructed with medium-sized stones set in cut joints. Only faint traces of a possible exedra remain. Notably, a baetyl stone is present, bearing several holes whose meaning is unknown, if not linked to a female essence. mu

6b8a29d5d9bbe4eb.text: It consists of 6 hypogea, of which 4 have been destroyed.

6bab7ec9df851d13.text: In a dominant position relative to the Riu Liscoi, on a granite outcrop, a corridor nuraghe of elliptical plan, built of granite and pinkish trachyte, is visible; it is not accessible inside due to collapses, and is accompanied by the remains of some circular huts.

6bc21beaa72f5dff.text: It is a proto-nuraghe or early nuraghe.

6bd8a79bac96bb6b.text: "Nuraghe s'Omu e s'Orcu", is located near Santa Giusta. The nuraghe fortress consists of a bilobate central tower, characterized by a lateral tower and a second tower situated in the central part of the complex; the towers are circular, with a diameter of about 7.50 m, and are composed of quadrangular and polyhedral ashlar stones of medium and small size, arranged in a tightly packed manner according to regular wall courses.

6bdc801fc57ea11f.text: Structures belonging to a nuraghe, presumably of the archaic, corridor type. The monument lies inside a private courtyard on the northern outskirts of the present-day village of Bonarcado. Four or five courses of polygonal basalt blocks can still be seen among recent structures of small blocks and cement that lean against the nuraghe. The building technique of the few visible remains would suggest the nuraghe's antiquity.

6bde8a1bfaf5b013.text: At the entrance to the Bari Sardo settlement, in the hills of Su Pranu, lies the cemetery of Funtana su Rettore, composed of three domus de janas. The domus, of the double-cell type, date to the recent Neolithic period, 3500–2800 BC. The burials, well preserved, are arranged at nearly the same height along the rocky wall and retain traces of the tools used to dig them.

6bef691fe3324eb4.text: Stele with an arched stele placed at the post for a metal gate

6bf7d017e3025723.text: The site is located in the Planu Is Ciaexius plateau, in the Sarcidano, central-southern region of Sardinia. The megalithic tomb of Aiodda, which follows the classic layout of giants' tombs, was discovered during agricultural works. The entrance, facing east, is preceded by a large semicircular exedra composed of calcare orthostats, about 6 m in width.

6bffb266d4c180bb.text: The central tower is elliptical, typical of a proto-nuraghe. The towers are more regular in shape, suggesting they were built in later phases, as was the curtain wall of the courtyard, which encloses a system of stairs and silos (presumably for storing agricultural produce). Some parts of the towers show a smaller-scale fabric in the curtain wall, with flatter, more regular stones.

6c03ef37b8a6ac62.text: Single-tower nuraghe of trachyte blocks; three courses survive. It appears destroyed and completely hidden. It takes its name from the mountain on which it stands, where a convent of nuns stood in ancient times.

6c079978b2c6249f.text: Lacking any visible structures or vestibule. It is composed of a linear sequence of steps (28–29 steps) and a water chamber that together form a rectangular void measuring 8.12 m in length and 1.25–1.10 m in width. The bottle-shaped section of the well, elliptical in plan (1.82 m x 1.25 m, height 5.12 m), distinguishes it from the well temples of Sardinia. The internal masonry is of polyhedral type.

6c2670cfb1612d42.text: “Sa Pedraia” consists of five hypogea set close together on a short rock face. One of them has an antechamber with a sloping roof and grooves showing the run of the beams. In the same chamber two bull’s-head protomes have been carved naturalistically to show that the fertility god would guarantee rebirth in the new life. The adjacent domus on the left has a cell with a central pillar and a raised lying-in floor.

6c4016261d4b20c0.text: From the second giants' tomb, moving 450 m north, one finds an area where the presence of polyhedral stones of various sizes, only roughly shaped, suggests that it was a site dedicated to cult practice.

6c44e8ba58b7a295.text: Svettated tomb with walls emerging only a few centimetres. Width of about 4.50 m, calculable length of about 7 m. A burial chamber, an apse, and an external perimeter wall are discernible.

6c520e10a6c9f7cd.text: Proto-nuraghe of sub-triangular form, built of basalt. It is located a short distance from n.ghe Su Pranu in the westward direction.

6c537bf64dd5f25b.text: A jewel set among the mountains of Padria, where the Ancient Sardinians carved the rock and sculpted extraordinary bull's-head protomes across an entire wall, enigmatic guardians watching us in silence.

6c7422dd3dd0ee20.text: Powerful, captivating even under a grey winter sky, the Nuraghe Sa Dom 'e S'Orku rises above a rocky massif amid a magnificent landscape, offering broad views over the entire Parteolla down to the Gulf of Cagliari and the mountains of Iglesiente. Dating back to the 2nd millennium BC, it is the main monument of the Dolianova area, where numerous other prehistoric remains are also present.

6c75f2cf0e4c437b.text:
It is completely covered with earth and vegetation; one would not even notice that it is a nuraghe were it not for a few limestone blocks laid one on top of another visible on top of the hillock.

On the side away from the sea, a few metres from the summit where the central tower stands, inside a hollow one of the towers of the nuraghe can be seen, in which its tholos, sectioned in half, is visible, built of sandstone and limestone blocks.

6c864ee046e23017.text:
It is a complex nuraghe of which the central tower and three other perimeter towers are visible (the presence of a fourth on the WSW side is not ruled out), joined together by a wall following a straight and curvilinear course.

The last excavation campaign ended in 2009.

The masonry is built of cyclopean basaltic andesite boulders, averaging 3 quintals each, with small stones and mud mortar also used in the interstices.

6c931c087da53fb0.text: Two giants' tombs adjacent, from two different construction periods. The first is of dolmenic type, the second is coursed (with opposed courses).

6cb510b92060149b.text: Location of the remains of the Tattari Pizzinnu nuraghe, of which only the foundations remain, a Roman villa built with stones from the nuraghe, and the remaining Roman-period settlement.

6ce39dae2e5193a4.text:
The “Domus de Janas” is cut into a modest, irregularly rounded granite outcrop that barely rises above the surrounding plain.

The plan is reduced to a single cell of modest size; the entrance, which opens to the south, is preceded by a short dromos cut into the rock face, characterised by a sub-trapezoidal plan and bounded laterally by vertical walls that decrease in height from north to south.

6cf84c1648258f8d.text: Single-tower nuraghe, around the traces of a settlement. At this site the famous bronze tablets of Tzricottu were discovered.

6d12c9ac6baff369.text: The village, lying east of the two nuraghi, occupies a broad flat area and consists of several structures. An apsidal hut is visible, rectangular in plan with a forecourt vestibule, in good condition, together with a probable circular hut and two enclosures. The area covered by the village is currently being excavated, bringing further structures to light. The structures were certainly reused up to recent times.

6d234b2b67f8516d.text:
These natural cavities are among the largest and most beautiful in Sardinia: their rectangular entrance is set in a lush holm-oak forest.

The caves, easily visited, were according to ancient legend the dwelling of three janas (fairies) who were turned to stone by God for killing a friar.

The cave walls are covered with marble-like flows and draperies. From the ceiling it seems almost as if a storm of white stalactites hangs over the visitor.

6d2512265670dcde.text: The village of Sa Muralla, whose name comes from the late medieval walls built around the village and the Castle in 1365, may be linked to the ancient toponym "Nuragonnos" on the northern outskirts of Sanluri; the latter probably referred to the hills on which the present town stands, perhaps already inhabited during the pre-Nuragic Monte Claro phase, as indicated by the Cukkuru Poddinis hypogeum.

6d345b4e8dce70a3.text:
