Funerary structure of the Nuragic period.

Entry form to be completed.

The monument is located in the territory of the comune of Norbello (OR).

6d38c3197717aaf3.text: The oldest nuraghe in the Villa Sant'Antonio area is Nuraghe Spei, a corridor nuraghe with a central body consisting of an ellipsoidal structure measuring 22 x 7.5 m, on whose eastern side open the three lintelled entrances of the internal tholos chambers, which are connected to each other by intermural passages. On the opposite side a second, larger ellipsoidal body abuts it, also with three lintelled entrances, now blocked.

6d3cb00219d5b31f.text: The remains of the nuraghe "CULZU" lie in the municipality of Torralba (SS) in the Su Segadu area, a few dozen metres from the nuraghe Longu, in the so-called Valley of the Nuraghi; it is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt with a chamber flanked by three niches. It has the entrance and the entrance corridor to the chamber; the tholos is missing its top and various trees growing inside the central chamber protrude from it.

6d421014769de527.text:
It lies west of the village centre, along the boundary with the territory of Villaurbana. It is a simple, single-chamber type. It is undoubtedly the best preserved and presumably among the most recent nuraghi in the municipal area.

Oral tradition holds that this nuraghe suffered a dynamite attack in the 1930s; the arrangement of the dome's ashlars and the condition of the western side would support this theory.

6d4b3a357404fc66.text: Near the remains of a church dedicated to the saint after whom it is named stands this nuraghe. Built from basalt blocks using polygonal masonry, it has a residual elevation of about 3 metres. It is surrounded by several thickets that prevent the identification of the entrance.

6d7d0fdb313cc7b0.text: The Anulù nuraghe belongs to the homonymous settlement, a large village dating to the late Nuragic period, and is composed of about thirty circular huts of medium and small size, separated by several walls.

6d8e25da80977a40.text:
Of this megalithic tomb, which must have been closely associated with the homonymous nuraghe, only a fragmentary upper portion of the arched stele remains.

The monolith, currently embedded within one of the many dry stone walls interweaving near the Serbine nuraghe, measures 1.68 m in height and 1.15 m in maximum width; the outer border defining its profile is 0.11 m wide.

6d8f56e551596e0a.text: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, reduced merely to some courses.

6db0af65fe88df78.text: The monument, in very poor condition of conservation, does not allow the identification of the original layout of the structures; one can only hypothesise, considering the alignment of some wall sections on the south side, where two courses of granitic blocks are preserved, that it might have been a simple tholos nuraghe.

6dcbd768492bf225.text: Nuraghe completely destroyed by agricultural improvement works. Possible location.

6e2c2a4eef76c29f.text: A short segment of slightly concave wall composed of stones not particularly large is certainly worth observation because the builders constructed it to meet a family-oriented need, either for residential use or for hunting. Within the context of Sa Mesana di sos Pianos and the adjacent Cudinatos of similar period, contemporaneous with or following the domus, it would assume a different identity. mu

6e40ae5d1d908406.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, visible under a dense canopy of olive and mastic trees. In addition to a scattered concentration of stones, some base courses of the structure remain, built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The remaining portions of the structure are filled with rubble from collapse.

6e59bebbf9b43caf.text: The Bruncu Mannu Nuraghe at Villa Sant'Antonio is located on a hill at a short distance from SP 37. At first glance it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe whose top is missing and overgrown with the foliage of various shrubs. Along the perimeter, the entrance can be identified, surmounted by an interesting lintel. The interior is cluttered with debris from collapse.

6e6301488d8136df.text: Group of domus de janas hidden in the undergrowth

6e6e58187e87a064.text: Extensive ruin remains only a small portion of masonry, composed of medium-sized stones arranged on two or three circles.

6ea5d8590fedd235.text: Located at about 176 m a.s.l., marked on the topographic map as Nuraghe. This dry-stone complex consists of walls varying in height between 40 and 110 cm. The layout of these wall sections shows a circular form in some areas and a squared form in others.

6ebf32dc5cc4e514.text: Random location. Tomb mentioned in the Master's thesis by Annalisa Uccheddu 1995, UNICA, located within the Villa Siotto Park. The tomb is svettata and buried. Original length probably about 10 m. Illegally excavated with removal of the covering.

6ed77c025a78a2f8.text: The cemetery consists of four domus de janas, among which the "tomb of painted architecture" is particularly notable, characterized by relief and painted decorations. The underground chamber, with a plan shaped like a "T", is composed of a long "dromos" ending in a rectangular atrium, an antechamber, a central chamber, and two lateral chambers.

6edd1fa3f0129621.text: Complex nuraghe of the lateral-addition type. A main tower is visible with a secondary tower alongside it on the east side. The entrance to the main tower, facing south, is lintelled and buried for more than half its original height. The entrance corridor, with the typical ogival section, is about 4 m long and built of perfectly worked basalt ashlars, showing a level of construction skill rarely found in other nuraghi in the area.

6f00c4bd48e27299.text: Right next to the village of the electric company there are two nuraghes and this exceptional giants' tomb, belonging to the site known as Pira Onne. Here too there is a stele with three recesses for housing the three figures of the Trinity, which usually stood on the exedra of a wall composed of horizontal courses; the stones are slightly squared.

6f1adb74dc4b36ed.text: Complex nuraghe with uncertain plan layout, featuring a very large tower and a series of wall structures of uncertain function connected to it. The site was also occupied during the Punic and Roman periods.

6f2f0737aa6cb203.text: Three or more granite menhirs placed near the homonymous nuraghe

6f99d23c5b92fec4.text: The cemetery consists of six domus de janas in poor state of conservation. One, however, features two pillars carved into the rock with fish-spine decorations. The ceiling is also carved, depicting the roof of the hut.

6fdc79a1fbf208fc.text: Unfortunately, the nuraghe Longu does not differ much from the state of extreme emergency observed in most of the nuraghes of Chiaramonti. Interesting is its study and architecture, which places it at the centre of attention as belonging to those with a subterranean chamber. Mario Unali

6fea63746dc425af.text:
It stands on a high rocky spur whose shape has strongly influenced the appearance of the monument, which in its surviving part shows a portion of an internal room with a sub-rectangular plan and rounded corners.

The surviving wall face of this room is about 3 m long and 1.55 m high.

For the rest, the whole nuraghe is reduced to the collapse alone, which is very extensive and located mainly on the southern slope.

701530fd1b68960d.text: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only a single ashlar with a curved profile belonging to the apsidal area remains, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.

7028bac9da2f2b1a.text:
The monument, a complex structure, consists of a central tower and a bilobate bastion.

Access to the central tower is via an entrance with a lintel. The bastion likely enclosed two towers, one to the east and one to the south-west.

703cb7e5c0919145.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a bastion with three towers. The original tower survives, filled with earth and collapse. To the south-east stands a tower of which part of the wall structures can be seen; the inner wall face is barely visible because of collapse and vegetation. A curtain wall links this tower with another oriented to the north-east, of which almost the entire wall outline survives. A third tower oriented to the south-west preserves its external perimeter almost intact.

707bb43abefc7022.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a diameter of 9.90 metres, whose entrance, still intact, leads into a corridor now uncovered, with the passage niche projecting from it and still preserved. The circular chamber (diameter 3.50 m) is missing its top and stands 3.50 m above the current floor level; it has no niches, and access to the staircase leading to the upper levels was provided from the ground surface.

707c5cc433c39ac4.text: It is a couple of hectometres from the church of Santa Lucia. At first glance it looks like a single-tower nuraghe, but it could simply be the top of a large complex nuraghe buried inside a hillock formed over the millennia. What is visible is somewhat ruined: a few courses, a cavity that may be the top of the central tower or the end of the stairwell.

70a6588391fca3f7.text: Preserves the tholos intact. There is a Nuragic settlement around the nuraghe.

717d7ff25025e857.text: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age with a likely Bilitic stele belonging to the giants' dolmenic tomb, partially buried

71878b3f5eb591bd.text: The nuraghe is partly collapsed and likely destroyed during the works for the construction of the municipal road.

71adc4d1ceccabd1.text: Among the heaps of stones the main tower emerges at the highest point, where the entrance is topped by a bare lintel. The open-air entrance has the niche on the right intact and on the left the collapsed stairwell, passable up to the upper floor from which the interior of the tholos with its two side niches can be seen. On the north-west side a double chamber, partly underground, is entered; it probably connected with the central tower in the lower part, which is now below ground.

71d00273eabf764b.text: Domus de janas entirely excavated in shale, consisting of a single chamber with lateral benches.

71e851cb303a26d2.text:
It is located within the municipal territory of Nule (SS).

The nuraghe is a single-tower with a staircase, a passage niche, and a chamber surrounded by three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower is circular in plan, while the roof has collapsed.

71ed755c83a04f0b.text:
The massive excavation work, the architecture of this monumental hypogeum, dates to the period of the first spread of metals on the island. In this "domus de janas" one sees the result of an evolution and it denotes the consequences of the formation of powerful family nuclei under tribal chiefs, capable of imposing a greater volume of work on their dependants.

The cells opened at a considerable height above the flat rock floor, inaccessible without a ladder.

7200116fa8425f07.text: The monument has been badly damaged by a thorough and indiscriminate clearance operation. Beneath the many piled ashlars that cover the structure, the corridor and one wing of the exedra appear to be distinguishable. Among the ashlars (which show that the tomb was of the coursed, isodomic type), made with great care, the so-called dentilled stele and several curvilinear-profile elements belonging to the apsidal area can be observed.

722159a4b0613854.text:
The nuraghe stands on the edge of the Corte plain, south-west of the town. You follow the Nuoro–Orani farm track and stop at the little bridge that crosses the Rio Su Saju.

On the left, about 200 metres away (near the shepherd's hut), lies the nuraghe. The site occupies a dominant position over what was a possible access route to the Corte plain and made use of the water from the nearby stream, which in ancient times was much more abundant.

Altitude 510 m a.s.l.

7221cdd7a824ba6a.text: The nuraghe, of which only a few remains are left, is at an elevation of 599 metres.

7235748baa4d59db.text: Nuraghe to be verified as it might be a enclosure.

7264c64df7e2756b.text: The sacred well of Sa Brecca is located in the area of Sàrrala é Sùsu, Marina di Tertenia (Ogliastra). The site is named after the river Sa Brèca (in IGM Sa Brècca) and the associated sheepfold (Coìli 'e Sa Brèca) which stands on the remains of the proto-Sardinian settlement. The river is one of the most significant in this region and flows into the beach of Fògi Mànna.

72961311a5e39289.text: Corridor nuraghe, hypothesis supported by the shape of the entrance (lintelled). Site easily accessible and usable. Traces of ceramics found outside suggest non-regular excavations. About 200 metres away there is a giants' tomb in the style of an allée couverte, of which some scholars speak as an incomplete work.

72bec0280606cc5a.text: The Giants' Tomb is located beside a river and is largely destroyed. A portion of the open corridor is still visible. The area is interesting because it is rich in springs. Nearby the Giants' Tomb are several nuraghes. It is situated at the foot of Bruncu Salamu, where there are numerous springs, sacred wells, and the Nuraghe Sa Dom'u S'Orku.

72d09f537fca2a8f.text: Only the external perimeter of this nuraghe remains clearly visible. The rest of the structure is barely discernible. Its plan is rectangular with very rounded corners, and its maximum height to the north is 4 m, with six courses of roughly hewn stones. The western façade is formed by a rocky cliff that drops directly into the valley.

72d9c66bf0b8cd2e.text: Single-tower nuraghe, preserves the tholos intact. The lintel above the entrance measures approximately 3.30 m x 0.90 m x 1.85 m, weighing about 16,000 kg.

72dec1afdab3dbff.text: Built by the Sardinian Nuragics, the well is estimated to be about 2,700 years old; it was discovered in 1883 during land clearing for railway tracks, and it is believed that valuable artifacts were lost. Of the original 40 steps, only 22 remain. Various artifacts, including rings and coins, were found and are now preserved at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.

72e6751bfcb9859e.text: Very eroded nuraghe with a tholos and collapsed walls

72e9cf6fe89a1532.text: Immersed in the dense vegetation stands the sacred well “Su Presoni”, so named because tradition says it was used as a prison in past centuries. The sacred well is a building linked to the water cult, composed of an underground part (well chamber) and an above-ground part (atrium) connected by a flight of steps. The monument at Cardedu is well preserved; the side walls of the atrium are still clearly visible to a surviving height of more than a metre;

72fd7f2db1d22296.text: Corridor nuraghe. The structures are completely covered and hidden by dense palustrine vegetation. The building stands on a small alluvial elevation between the Rio Cispiri and a parallel stream. As regards the structures, only a few courses of polygonal basaltic blocks can be observed.

73334df075f2d40f.text: Giants' tomb immersed in vegetation and eroded

734086524c8fca93.text: Single-tower with the tholos collapsed inward

734d66bde75261ec.text: Nuragic well concealed. It has been completely sealed with bricks and cement to make it undetectable.

734f9bcf152baaa5.text: It is a anthropomorphic rock whose appearance is likened to the face of the Egyptian sphinx.

736d818f2d07e30d.text: Three domus de janas. Featuring an imposing column inside and carved bull's-head protomes on the walls. Very difficult to locate.

737672d5524245fe.text: Nuraghe coincident with a medieval settlement

7386479130ff1b77.text: Nuraghe partially collapsed and invaded by vegetation, located at the edge of the village, near a rural chapel.

7399d94471fe4e98.text: Simple to find and difficult to understand, due to its cover in REINFORCED CONCRETE, which only the local administrators can comprehend, plus its pitiful state of abandonment. It appears the giants' tomb was used as a powder magazine during the construction of SS131; hence, it was equipped with a reinforced concrete cover and a metal door, now no longer present.

73b2467c836df360.text: There are the most important domus de janas in the Pozzomaggiore area. The cemetery consists of at least 20 tombs cut into the rock, some of which are incomplete and not finished, while others are buried or heavily damaged.

73b490dbe7f35f16.text: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and surrounded by vegetation

73c77e5d4bec9280.text: Provided with a corresponding Nuragic settlement.

73cd4faee7ca9591.text: This nuraghe has also been completely destroyed; only traces of a single course of a single-tower nuraghe about 9 metres in diameter remain. Many potsherds and basalt lava querns were found on the surface.

73df64cfff64c8e4.text:
Originally there were three, but only one remains standing.

Probable location.

73e9cf8690369397.text: The cemetery is located along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula and consists of 11 domus de janas, characterized by the complexity of their planimetric layouts and decorative patterns. Only one of these is monocellular, while the others are composed of multiple cells arranged according to increasingly complex designs.

73f39e579f8c6456.text: Within the archaeological area are Nuragic period burial circles located at 990 m a.s.l., as well as constructions from a later period, including ancient cow pens and ancient sheepfolds known as "Pinnetus".

73f579e1cc7b2851.text:
The megalithic monument, 13.5 m long according to the 2005 survey, does not depart from the traditional model. The long corridor was entered through a doorway cut into a generally arched stele, flanked on either side by stelae of decreasing height joined together (exedra).

Despite the collapse of the vault, the corridor is still preserved; the tomb entrance, however, is covered by a dense mastic bush, which prevents verification of the stele's integrity.

74329d8506d9cc99.text:
The necropolis, located along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas characterized by the complexity of their planimetric layouts and decorative schemes.

The tomb of the water clocks, on the other hand, comprises 10 rooms, whose walls feature relief geometric motifs.

7434a3e7350da766.text: Nuraghe partially buried with a special lintel, worked and currently broken into two. Nearby is also a dolmen of the same name.

743eac0415527a97.text: Single-tower nuraghe, whose shape is difficult to determine due to collapses and the dense vegetation present. Nevertheless, the external wall of the central tower can be identified. In the western part of the central tower, a possible infill remains, with partial traces of about two-thirds of the courses still visible.

749b7cedce716136.text:
Single-tower nuraghe now called “Su Nuraxi”, though it was once better known as “Cocconi”.

A second tower is suspected to have existed in the past. A distinctive feature is that a Byzantine burial complex has been brought to light inside the central tower: a sacred use from which the monument evidently never strayed. Indeed, another of its long-standing names was “Sa Parrocchia”.

74c86c6f6e5f9fed.text: The Furcadizzo nuraghe stands on the small promontory. The monument has suffered heavy collapses. Around the area, wall structures of mixed curvilinear and rectilinear plan can be identified.

74c8837cacc4c8ac.text: Of this nuraghe only a small amount remains, just a few large stones arranged in a circular form. Perhaps the first course of stones from the foundation.

74e3d56d62179238.text: A Chalcolithic necropolis discovered by chance during public works for the new Cagliari aqueduct. Three oven-type tombs were identified and investigated: of the first, found on the lowest part of the ridge on which the site extends, only the cell cut into the sandstone bedrock survived; 5 m to the west of the previous burial a second tomb preserved the vertical shaft and the oven-type cell with an elliptical plan intact.

74e4d95cbbbd6044.text: Of the monument only the corridor tomb remains, which has five courses of stones to the west and six to the east, with a maximum length of 7.40 m and a width of 1 m.

74ece7918ca5c915.text:
Single-tower, single-cell. Svettato, with the chamber completely filled with collapsed debris. The southern-eastern side of its outer wall, where the entrance opened, is entirely collapsed. The highest point of the monument reaches about 3 m in height and is composed of six courses of roughly hewn stones.

The lintel of the entrance, well-crafted, is found isolated on the ground a short distance away.

74f038de5b807b48.text: Single-tower nuraghe consisting of a chamber with an intact tholos roof and an internal staircase connecting the various levels that form the complex structure.

74fea0fd06c9c81b.text: The highest part of the Posada cliff was occupied by a corridor-type nuraghe, and on its southern-eastern slopes, at a significantly lower elevation, there stood also a village, probably arranged on terraced levels. The village began at about 90 m as the crow flies from the nuraghe and extended from an elevation of about 42 m down to about 25 m a.s.l., covering a drop of about 17 metres. (Sanciu 2010)

75026ecfadd78c0b.text: At this site, within a short stretch of about two hundred metres, monuments dating to the Abealzu culture, 2700–2400 BC, the early Bronze Age with nuraghic walls, and the Bronze Age up to the Roman period, marked by probable tombs, are present.

7526a2b2655ec8b6.text: In 1788 the community council of Villaputzu complained that the cove of Murtas, where the sea penetrated a long, deep inlet, was unguarded. Corsairs hid "behind large boulders at an ancient nuraghe called Nuraxi de moros", which they used as a base for raids: in 1767 they enslaved two farmers; in 1779 two peasants; in 1781 four; in 1788 two men who were making charcoal for their own use.

75325c73b8774128.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a small village adjacent.

7536faae0508f20a.text: Village of which only little or nothing remains due to construction, down to the immediately surrounding areas.

7548806599755d66.text: Nuraghe known from ancient writings (Taramelli) and in the toponym recognized by the elders of the village. Noted by Costantino Corongiu.

754db59ab6b1fa5a.text: Single-tower nuraghe, of which megaliths remain, regularly "arated" in which few cossi of the Late Bronze Age.

755308bfc2bedf30.text: Arched stele of a Giants' tomb known as “S'Artare de su Moro”; the base of the stele remains in situ, while the upper part has been broken and incorporated into the wall of the hut.

75557b4f530c409a.text: Damaged nuraghe of which it is not possible to indicate the form

75562bb2d7f67371.text: Sos Monimentos has a circular plan, with a chamber measuring about 1.80 x .100 m, surrounded by a dry-stone wall of granite. At the entrance to the structure two rectangular slabs, about 0.60 m high, rise. On these slabs rests a circular lid slab measuring about 2.50 x 2.25 m. Its possible astronomical orientation has not yet been identified.

75cb095abb7e67dd.text: The two domus, between which a large tree stands, are located about 1 km from the village of Goni and are carved into a rocky formation situated about 4 metres above the walking surface.

75d63320cb24a1fd.text: Nuraghe whose southern side has collapsed but still retains the tholos intact

762889fec822b8ae.text: Single-tower, it is a newly identified feature because the central chamber has imploded and the wall face has collapsed to the west. Some characteristics of the Nuragic masonry can be observed. Nuraghe of San Pietro. Local tradition does not recall a church dedicated to San Pietro in this place. It probably refers to a property linked to the church of San Pietro that stood in the village located at Elva nàna, the name of which has not survived. Mu

762d5a39bab34bce.text: The remains of the funerary structure are completely covered by a layer of mastic. A circular hut built in the contemporary period on top of the tomb's remains is visible, with part of an exedra composed of five basalt stones arranged in a semicircle.

7645cfa7b9052a0c.text: In its upper part the corridor appears to have been cut by excavating into the sandstone rock. Below it is covered with soil; the depth is unknown but the distance between the walls is certainly greater further down. Of the conical structure of the well proper, parts made of worked ashlars are visible, especially on our left and in the upper part straight ahead, while the part on the right and the central lower part seem to have been emptied of ashlars, as if they had been taken for other uses or had collapsed. The lower part of the spring is covered with mud.

76d0d21c8da19546.text:
At present a circular tower (diam. 1.50–2 metres) can be seen at the centre of an irregularly quadrangular fortified bastion that follows the rocky contour of the hill.

The entrance to the bastion, on the south-east, has a rectangular opening (width 0.80 m – height 1.05 m above the fill) and is topped by a massive lintel. This doorway leads into a short corridor (depth 2.50 m – height 2.05 m – max. width 1.75 m) that turns left and then stops where it has collapsed.

76dd18c64282c2b5.text: "Giants' tomb of Araene, of the long cell the dense stones of the sides and large slabs of the roof are seen. In the land of Carta Luca, it was Luigi." From Taramelli's description, the tomb of Araene must certainly have been the best preserved among those in the territory of Lodè; unfortunately the monument was destroyed in relatively recent times, as a result of the usual land-reclamation works, which spared practically nothing.

770c3144182a3f41.text:
In an initial phase, several villages of square huts were established in the area, belonging to the Ozieri culture, which included a necropolis with hypogean tombs of domus de janas and a probable sanctuary featuring a menhir, stone slabs for sacrifices, and stone spheres.

It consists of 8 hypogean tombs, among which the "Head's tomb" stands out in importance.

77132f8bf28e67e7.text: Nuraghe of undetermined type. The nuraghe features an unusual staircase that, at about halfway along the entrance corridor, projects diagonally from a height of 2.20 metres above the floor level, extending over more than 5 metres with an exceptionally steep vertical rise that breaks out onto the terrace. The ceiling of the chamber remains intact.

77221d85049ccaa6.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a tholos, unfortunately in advanced state of degradation, protected by a large outer wall with a deep underlying drop, of which today only a fortress remains inaccessible.

772fafe891d8aba8.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a guard niche, a probable stairwell, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower, circular in plan (diam. 12.70 m), survives to a maximum height of 5 m on the west side, with 7 courses, while the minimum height is about 2 metres in the section affected by the entrance, to the south-east, which has completely collapsed. The masonry consists of roughly dressed trachyte blocks laid in horizontal courses with numerous packing wedges.

777912f696f381d4.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a primitive tower and a bastion, perhaps four-lobed. The entire outline of the central tower survives, although hidden by vegetation and collapse. The structures of two chambers belonging to the central tower survive. A curvilinear curtain wall forms the link between two peripheral towers oriented NNW and ENE. The NNW tower is connected by a curtain wall to another tower oriented WSW, of which much of the outer outline survives.

77b642f048942d06.text: The giants' tomb at Sas Melas is located about 200 metres by air distance from the homonymous nuraghe. The tomb is completely buried and is in very poor conservation condition; only a few orthostats emerge, barely a few centimetres above the surface.

77cd0f541baea384.text: On the edge of the named height: a very ruined tomb, possibly the only underground chamber remaining from a small necropolis.

77d7ef31279f1b32.text: Domus de janas of which no photographs exist and whose condition is unknown

77e316e2b1deef19.text: Artificial grotto with access, pseudo-quadrilateral and large.

77f9091d57ea9e86.text: The area preserved the settlement, which was uncovered in the early 1980s. The land was expropriated and archaeological investigations were launched, revealing a series of residential areas used at least up to the late medieval period, traces of a complex nuraghe, and what has been identified as a sacred well, still to be excavated.

78061533a1471bce.text: It is a complex nuraghe located on the hill known as Pettu 'e Murtas, from which it takes its name. Nearby are the remains of some huts, all of Nuragic age.

7837da5987240a5e.text: Single-chamber domus de janas located underneath an artwork on the S.S.131 heading N.O.

7856b2c653c33ea3.text: Remains of a nuraghe, of which only the bases remain.

786a396bedadd1c2.text: Single-cell domus de janas especially eroded

7895017e9863cd80.text: Probable proto-nuraghe consisting of a tower section attached to a rock outcrop. Probable entrance to the south-east. From the top of the rock face, the panorama extends over the archipelago to the north-east and over Rena Majori to the north-west.

789517f4e77023b6.text:
Nuragic settlement with Middle and Late Bronze Age pottery. Following deep excavations for industrial purposes, the site has recently undergone profound changes.

The single-tower nuraghe has been demolished and the building stones have been set aside; the materials are still visible.

7897702b29e37dd4.text: The archaeological site was discovered in 1985, entirely by chance, during land clearing works for the installation of a vineyard. Investigations, continued until 1988, allowed the identification of the main nucleus of the sanctuary, consisting of the sacred well, a round structure that characterizes a portion of the large building constructed in isodomic masonry, and two cylindrical structures, interpretable as altars.

78b3cdc10c3a2202.text: It is a nuraghe with a square chamber that remains unfinished, as only the base has been constructed, and an architrave has been placed at the entrance. Interesting because around it, stones are already ready for use on the nuraghe, making it valuable for understanding the construction techniques employed.

78b5930da4036ea9.text: Partially hidden by the Mediterranean scrub, the tomb is oriented in a north-south direction, with an exedra facing south, of which about three courses remain, composed of large granite blocks in a quadrangular form arranged in alternate rows, with a surviving height of 90 cm.

78e50c766a67248a.text: Complex nuraghe with settlement; no traces remain on the surface.

78e9b4c1e2b973b9.text: Group of domus de janas situated on the calcareous escarpment overlooking the Bunari valley (Abealzu culture)

78f049c42021dc2d.text: Large area belonging to a probable Nuragic village. In the surrounding areas, fragments and other surface finds are easily recoverable. The village extends over a considerable distance to the south from the indicated point and towards the west stream.

790aa9345e001bb1.text: Nuraghe of the same name, near the singular monument composed of two superimposed towers, stands alone on an extremely high and impressive cliff dominating the large valley of the Rio "S'Acqua Callenti", right at the junction with the valley of the Flumendosa.

7915c504c9bfedce.text: Catalogued as a probable Roman-period burial, with a facing. A surface portion of the monument is visible alongside a depression in the ground, featuring a granite lintel and, beneath, three walls composed of small and medium-sized ashlar stones forming a dry masonry. It resembles the shape of a well.

792587ac94812cec.text: The giants' tomb of Iscrallotze is particularly eroded. In appearance, what remains suggests it belongs to the category of dolmenic giants' tombs.

79426168b6fc1f48.text:
The Santu Scioni, San Lussorio nuraghe stands in the countryside of Pabillonis, on a hillock from which much of the Campidano plain can be seen towards Monte Linas and above a bend of the Flumini Mannu.

Originally it must have consisted of a central tower and a series of other towers that are now by no means easy to identify, since all the wall structures have been levelled and covered by human activity around the sacredness that the site still retains today.

7960b0b5eef0f3d1.text: The nuraghe is almost entirely collapsed. Only the entrance with lintel and traces of two corridors remain. A niche is also visible in the rear corridor. The Budas nuraghe is an example of a proto-nuraghe.

796168d124b3fa96.text: Well of undefined period, often indicated as Roman but possibly Nuragic.

797cbbbec8758aa3.text: Small domus de janas with two cells

7983e112784784c1.text: irregular and buried, whose structure cannot be defined

7993b044e93c4d44.text: Single-tower, collapsed and stripped, with only the ruins scattered on the ground.

799c8d9699757d1c.text: The Abba Noa nuraghe, on a granite outcrop at 178 m above sea level, is characterized by mixed masonry: part of the construction uses local granite, while the rest employs basalt obtainable in the surrounding hills. The plan, complex, consists of two towers diametrically opposed, joined by a bastion that is straight to the west and curved to the east, running along the edge of the summit.

79bdbc0867b5f32e.text: Nuraghe of which only very little remains externally, collapsed and never studied

79fb5ddd50813cb9.text: Remains of the nuraghe Sa Domo Ezza

7a2a8949e802a487.text:
Small nuraghe, located on a high cliff of Monte Dominigu.

Nearby, to the west of the nuraghe, the megalithic circle of Monte Dominigu. On old cadastral maps it is listed as Nuraghe San Leonardo.

According to the current Regional Catalogue (CTR) of Sardinia, it is now known as "Nuraghe Sa Pedra Pertunta".

7a69d3c5dede37cd.text:
The Lu Brandali nuraghe is of mixed type, with features of both a corridor nuraghe and tholos nuraghi.

The entrance opens in the north-western part of the latter, its length marked by several watchtowers that make use of rock outcrops.

Outside the curtain wall the village extends; Michele Careddu's 1967 survey recorded 36 huts, mostly circular. Period between the 14th and 10th centuries BC.

7a6ba66d84024f55.text: Nuragic megalithic enclosure of probable defensive use, later repurposed in the Roman period, as evidenced by the presence of pottery fragments on the ground.

7a708dbaa573f236.text: Single-tower nuraghe in very poor condition, only two courses remain.

7a80b5407e370cc2.text: Nuraghe/proto-nuraghe characterized by a robust and wide central tower and the remains of two other towers barely visible. The nuraghe is situated on top of a hill, in a natural rocky outcrop from which it offers a magnificent view, allowing the naked eye to easily spot the ruins of the Las Plassa castle... traces of Punic/Roman ceramics suggest the superimposition of multiple civilizations.

7a814efc9da6f91b.text: Nuraghe, probably a simple tholos type. The structures are very difficult to interpret because of the dense vegetation, the poor state of preservation, and the presence of recent structures leaning against the remains of the building. A few aligned polygonal blocks can be seen, while the rest consists of a heap of jumbled blocks overlain by small stones.

7abf865f400ffb57.text: Discovered by the great cartographer A. Lamarmora in 1840. It is covered in dense mastic vegetation, has collapsed inwards and filled with earth over time. The stones used for the construction are white with yellow patches of dry moss. The surviving height of the tower exposed to the north is about three metres. If visited in summer, the desert-like landscape of the area adds to the fascination of this imposing megalithic monument.

7ac8e088bc943c00.text: Giants' tomb, nuragic, with a corridor and a partial portion of the exedra.

7acd6817ab200e1c.text: The Nuraghe Su Guzzu is a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone blocks with basalt reworkings. It lies about 7 km south of Paulilatino and, together with the Nuraghi Forreddos, De Mesu and Codas, forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. The lintel giving access to the inner chamber is very interesting; the tholos is intact but unfortunately the chamber is cluttered with a good deal of collapse debris.

7ace1279234d0420.text: The area, located on the north-western slope of the comune of Giave, includes the remains of a nuraghe, possibly a giants' tomb, and an attached settlement.

7acf68154aa7ae6c.text: Single-chambered, carved out of a granite monolith.

7ad6153a4bdef6a7.text: Single-tower nuraghe incorporated within Medau Su Conti. In recent times it was used as a support for the masonry of a house. It is partly stripped of its outer stones but overall retains a good height. It is the only accessible nuraghe in Carbonia, even though it lies inside a fenced plot.

7aed96d632277f10.text: Likely three-lobed, with only the base courses remaining.

7b0b30d92fac3c58.text: This nuraghe is just one of the countless ones found throughout the territory. Its condition is commendable, but maintenance work was required by the municipality due to several landslides.

7b28191e0ed2bf32.text:
Complex nuraghe, with a bilobate bastion.

The central tower is equipped with a mezzanine.

7b530fcbc5b7f3f3.text: The tomb is svettato and consists of an orthostatic structure in courses. Part of the exedra, the architrave portal, the funerary corridor, and part of the apse are visible. Length about 12 m.

7b67b06be8f19eb5.text: Nuragic settlement area. A nuragic station has been identified with clear signs of human presence (about 1300 BC).

7b90345baaaa84cc.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Collinas. The Regional Commission for Cultural Heritage of Sardinia, by its own Decree no. 155 of 14 December 2017, has declared the site known as "Nuragic tomb of Sa Terra de Su Muru" of particular archaeological interest.

7b971a19d6a9316d.text:
The nuraghe is of the single-tower with tholos type, constructed from roughly hewn trachytic stones and has a circular base with an external diameter of 12 metres, a remaining height of about 6 metres, and wall inclinations ranging from 7 to 11 degrees.

The entrance, oriented to the southeast as in most nuraghes, is topped by an architrave composed of two separate blocks and leads into a passage covered by transverse slabs.

7bb5d84b33f249d2.text: The stone of Sant Eliseo is a large erratic boulder on the lower slopes of Monte Santu, in the territory of Mores. Used in various periods, it was first a Prehistoric Tomb of the Neolithic, then adapted by the Romans, and finally became a Byzantine church dedicated to Sant Eliseo. The domus has a ground floor and a first floor, reminiscent of the houses of the fairies (in Sardinian, precisely, Domus De Janas).

7bfebc9880a6962f.text: Single-tower nuraghe, the entrance is not visible; its diameter is about 9 metres. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes at Su Padru.

7c14da6520431c61.text: The monument, built of limestone, has an internal diameter of about four metres, dimensions relatively small compared to known standards, but not insignificant when considered in relation to the width of the promontory on which it stands, which extends over slightly more than six metres in width and ends at the edge of a cliff.

7c38ca4975ec7cb6.text: Masonry of barely rough-hewn blocks alongside others that are well shaped, of various sizes. The side towers: the one on the left is better preserved than the others, rising from the ground for four courses of blocks of considerable size; the tower on the right is barely visible on the surface, with two courses partly buried; the third tower, its footprint covered by collapse, stands opposite the entrance.

7c3cb4e9daccceb9.text: Nuraghe that might belong to the category of "uncompleted"

7c58d30eb6130184.text:
The monument is in the Mandras locality (Campeda), 600 metres north-east of the Mura Sauccu nuraghe and less than 300 metres west of the Mura Sauccu B nuraghe.

It is a single-tower nuraghe surviving to a maximum height of about 6.50 metres. The masonry consists of large and medium-sized blocks.

7c918c0968785213.text: Of the monument, of the coursed type made of polygonal granite blocks, the corridor and part of the external profile of the burial chamber are visible.

7cc1c6b8018f93d3.text:
Despite the very dense vegetation and the collapses suffered by the monument, the ruins of a central body flanked by two towers can be identified, built with trachyte blocks of rose colour.

At a short distance, in the south-west direction, traces of some circular stone constructions are visible.

7cd6235b2c1e7848.text: Complex nuraghe. Access to the upper level via a staircase passing beneath the SE tower.

7cd870a56f53943d.text:
The monument has a complex plan in which at least two bodies can be distinguished, one leaning against the other, developing along a north-east–south-west axis 16.50 m long.

The perimeter of the north-eastern body, which has almost completely collapsed and is partly buried, can be traced only at the point where it joins the other tower and in part on the western side.

It may have been an elliptical element whose major diameter measures about 7 m.

7cddc2b81b58910e.text:
It is a two-cell domus, oriented to south-east, with a roof widely collapsed (opening 1.06 x 0.86 m), lacking the diaphragm that once separated the two chambers, which was recently destroyed to create a single, more spacious chamber.

Access to the subterranean level is through a square opening (height 0.44 m – width 0.50 m – thickness 0.22 m), finely carved, featuring a triple molding for the insertion of a door latch.

7ced4863bf2b3751.text:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale. A picturesque and colossal tower of bizarre shape, at the base of which stands the eponymous Nuraghe. The nuraghe, though imposing, appears incredibly tiny compared to the immense rock that looms over it.

This single-tower nuraghe is built of barely dressed megalithic blocks, even larger at the base. Around the rocky mass it is possible to make out the huts of a small village.

7cf73674873c1848.text: It is a domus that probably suffered the collapse of the antechamber, and of which only the access opening and the internal chamber remain.

7cfe7e178bba8f0e.text:
A rather massive towered structure can nevertheless be distinguished. This tower stands off-centre in relation to a kind of walled “enclosure” that appears to have been very thick and abuts it on the northern side, while a facing of large blocks involves the western sector of the tower.

Another outer wall is visible from north-west to south-east, almost doubling the tower’s perimeter.

7d05c4e0d889acec.text: Nuragic settlement or sacred site, reused up to the Roman period. Basements of different structures from various historical periods are present.

7d0c7098ff859ee7.text: On a rocky granite outcrop of irregular shape, two single-cell domus de janas have been excavated. The surrounding area is characterized by a dense forest of oaks. The two subterranean burials, separated by about 1 metre, are respectively dug into the northern and western sides of the granite outcrop.

7d233f1cd7313ba6.text: Nuragic settlement with particular attention to lithic industry. Here, among other finds, axes, hammers, and stone mace heads have been discovered. One of the most remarkable discoveries is a depiction of a dagger on ceramic.

7d28584c1acddc63.text: The site consists of a three-lobed nuraghe, still mostly buried, and of structures probably dating to the Roman period.

7d3c1bb3a802b614.text:
The complex consists of a "cromlech" and other menhirs. In the surrounding area, an underground necropolis attests to the intensive occupation of the territory in prehistory.

The "cromlech" is made of large rounded boulders (trachyte, grey granite and pure white quartz) transported from considerable distances.

The complex is attributable to the Final Neolithic (3200–2800 BC, Ozieri culture) and the Early and Middle Chalcolithic (2800–2400 BC, Filigosa and Abealzu cultures).

7d3d3a06ff742cd1.text: It is located in the territory of the comune of Nuoro. It is a single-cell domus, well finished internally. Difficult to identify due to dense vegetation. It opens onto a low granite bank.

7d443d672f585b48.text: To the north-west of the nuraghe there is a small pond containing spring water, which is present even in summer, though in small quantities. The pond has an irregular triangular shape entirely natural. The deepest point reaches the overflow level at about 120 cm.

7d59e78cab0ec01c.text: No official documents have been found, yet in the village it is said that beneath the hill there lies a complex nuraghe and a very large village, as would emerge from the traces left by tomb raiders.

7d5a807ad5898dc0.text: Quadrilobate nuraghe, the central tower (with a mezzanine) retains intact the tholos roof of the chamber.

7d863c6c44e1f7b7.text: The artifacts indicate that it was used from the Middle Bronze Age until the Recent Bronze Age. It is built with large blocks of limestone and originally contained a chamber with two niches and a staircase. Now the collapse blocks access to the chamber. Nearby the nuraghe, remains of a hut are visible, consisting of a circular room and a courtyard.

7d86a2c7e08394af.text: The tomb is in excellent condition, both inside and out. The façade, built of well-squared medium-sized blocks laid with care, has a low rectangular entrance doorway at the centre (about 50 cm wide and 60 cm high). The burial chamber reaches a height of about 1.80 m at its highest point; the apse that closes the rear of the chamber is also very well preserved.

7dbe34d1a0d27d5a.text:
His Majesty the ERGULIS, the largest of the nuraghi in the Cuglieritano area, is a single-tower nuraghe standing 106 m tall and is intact both in its walling and in its vault.

It features two niches directly opposite each other just beyond the entrance lintel, and two more inside the chamber, while a niche at the front of the entrance is notably absent.

The lintel is equipped with a drainage opening directed to the south.

7dc188d410891d65.text: The Golunie nuraghe is located on land owned by the Guiso family (ancient barons), precisely at the border between the territories of Orosei and Dorgali, in the Cala Osalla area, and it overlooks both the Marina beach near the second Osalla mole (Orosei) and the adjacent beach of the same name (Dorgali).

7dd0a845dba3da57.text: Typical nuragic well with stakes made of ashlar stones and a lintel closure. Interior features a water collection basin.

7de53b7e6aedb211.text:
The small necropolis of Ovau consists of three small domus de janas. The first one is the one with the largest chamber and the most prominent door frame. The third, on the other hand, is very small inside.

Nearby are two remarkable, superimposed menhirs, very well crafted. The first menhir

7e133945f8f3d096.text:
Single-tower nuraghe of which only the ground-level courses remain.

Twenty-two Nuragic villages, large and small, are known in the municipal area, not all occupied at the same time. They are often found near a nuraghe, as in the case of the Bruncu Pubusa site.

7e48b0377f887cc4.text:
The nuraghe, collapsed internally, shows a fairly irregular plan, typical more of proto-nuraghe than of true tholos nuraghe.

For further details:

eprints.uniss.it/9371/1/Merella_S_Indagini_territoriali... pages 339-340

7e6486e20e39b408.text: It spends most of the year beneath the waters of Lake Cuga. Destroyed single-tower nuraghe; only a few courses of the original structure are visible. During the excavations before the dam works, the archaeologist Contu found an important Nuragic model boat here.

7e6f797e2c77924c.text: In the territory of Sanluri there are remains of as many as 15 nuraghe, three of which are complex nuraghe with multiple towers: Corti Sa Perda, Geni, Nuraxi Candelas.

7e79bafee054cb25.text:
THE PISCINA'E SALI SITE. The archaeological area is reached by following an agricultural track that starts from Via Cimitero, continuing straight on at the junction at Gedilis and crossing the Pranu Corongiu plateau until the right-hand side road.

The area certainly played a prominent role in the past as regards religious manifestations; no fewer than ten menhirs have been found in the valley and are associated with the funerary contexts of Pranu Corongiu

7e7a3b0c5a011c65.text: The Pastoris nuraghe is of simple type, located to the north-east relative to the inhabited centre, near the municipal water deposit, and in close proximity to which, a few years ago, some structures related to a livestock farming company were built—though in reality these do not harmonize well with the presence of the nuraghe.

7e93987d182f67e6.text: It is a powerful nuraghe made of andesite with a three-lobed plan, resulting from the addition of two secondary towers in front of the central tower, connected by walls enclosing a central courtyard. Nearby stands a large hut; adjacent to it is also a well carefully lined internally, which is also likely dated to the Nuragic period.

7e95ee0ad54c1ce7.text: Partially destroyed and located near the industrial zone of Portoscuso.

7ed0bdad34442b0c.text: Dolmen with a collapsed and buried structure, whose layout cannot be defined.

7eeeb7d33221049c.text: The tomb is considerably disturbed in parts, also due to illegal excavations; it preserves (a rare case for the area) a (likely) large fragment of the central stele of the exedra.

7ef45367926eb7d6.text: Of the two giants' tombs, both relatively eroded, the burial chamber and the exedra are identifiable.

7effd430be5af0ab.text: This complex nuraghe, with five towers and a curtain wall measuring as many as 450 metres, rises prominently at the eastern edge of the Abbasanta plateau. The general plan of Santa Marra nuraghe is complex and three-lobed, with a concave-convex perimeter, typologically similar to Santu Antine of Torralba and Losa of Abbasanta, but reinterpreted in an original manner.

7f04ce2fd6363de6.text:
Nuragic well in the territory of Guasila, for which no significant information is available.

It is noted simply that the structure is built of isodomic masonry and features on its upper surface a T-shaped ashlar course, a feature observable only in more renowned and highly significant monuments.

7f1f971cc3192b6e.text: Here also a mezzanino and a subsidiary staircase, elevated within the right niche of the chamber. A nuraghe that reminded me, in layout, of the Crabia at Bauladu.

7f27d3e53b5a77ef.text: This nuraghe was identified through a letter sent to Nurnet by a reader of the page. The nuraghe appears to have been destroyed and incorporated into a large rural building. This is the origin of the name "Medau Mannu".

7f5a2c7d36d4204f.text: The site is characterized by a quadrangular courtyard, which originally served as the main chamber now collapsed. Access is provided through a granite arch of rare beauty, from which one reaches what remains of the original domus; two rooms, one quadrangular and aligned with the entrance, the other irregularly shaped to the right.

7f9098052b19ca61.text:
The necropolis consists of 14 domus de janas, considered among the most beautiful in Sardinia for their architectural conception.

Twelve of them are cut into the rock in a horizontal row, the other two opposite the first ones. The façades are striking for their monumentality and the precision of the workmanship: in particular that of tomb 3. A drainage channel cut into the rock, still visible, protected the burials from rainwater infiltration.

7f9de465cff952e7.text: Megalithic enclosure with inside a toppled menhir.

7fa413f806fde21c.text:
A single-tower nuraghe (mostly remains) is present on the ridge of the hill Cuccuru S. Eremilis, very close to the road.

Position to be verified

7fade875b4639b87.text: The nuraghe is not visible on the ground due to the presence of a dense thicket covering what may have been the site of destruction. However, the abundance of ceramic material still indicates Nuragic origin for the site's occupation.

7fe710208d526fe5.text: Giants' tomb with a bilitic stele, of which only the lower part remains; the monument damaged over the years by clandestine diggers and vandals.

7ffa59388d9f37e9.text: Perhaps it is the same nuraghe referred to as Thorcodossile in some books, located about 500 metres further west. Only a few ruins remain at the top of the hill.

8013714e42ae323f.text: Nuraghe Artòra dominates the Capo Comino promontory at a height of 120 m above sea level and once fulfilled the role of a watchtower, equivalent to the current traffic light. Located at a short distance from the lighthouse that overlooks Capo Comino, it is described by Relli as a complex nuraghe situated on the summit of the same name; however, it is very difficult to distinguish due to being covered by a concrete platform built for military purposes during the Second World War.

80170f61eb05eec7.text:
Single-tower nuraghe, preserves almost intact the tholos roof of the chamber.

It is one of the few nuraghes equipped with a mezzanine or mezzanine floor on the entrance corridor.

80195b3358c48d7e.text: It is a complex structure composed of a central tower (or mastio) and two additional towers situated adjacent to the south. Its entrance is partially collapsed, making access difficult.

806567e0252adb7f.text: Possible origin of the name: nuraghe della scolca, which in the time of the Giudicati served as a guard post. On a small relief of 70 m.l.m, there are a heap of stones and basaltic boulders, traces of burials and Roman pottery, and fragments of obsidian.

8078fc654046dcab.text: Small and single domus de janas

808526370313d697.text: The nuraghe Thorra, like the nuraghe Sas Melas, stands on a low hill rising at the bottom of the valley, surrounded by higher ground; from this position it closely controls an important ford on the Rio Torra, a tributary of the Rio Mannu. Three hundred metres away to the west lies the eponymous giants' tomb, recorded by Taramelli who, strangely, makes no mention of the nuraghe at all.

80d4e25584c8fd57.text: It should include at least five hypogea.

80e2883b898d197b.text:
The construction is extensive and complex. The area outlined in red is the highest and is well enclosed by typically Nuragic walls up to two and a half metres thick.

All around, however, the existence of other walls can be discerned; they defined a much larger surface, with terraces stepping down towards the impluvium to the north.

The building dominated the valley, now completely built over, which takes its name from the little church of Santa Barbara.

80e7bd9418e716a6.text: Single-tower nuraghe, near which traces of a settlement and a sacred well are found.

8100fe508a82a8f9.text: Given its dominant position over the surrounding countryside, it is presumed to have been a very important and complex nuraghe. Unfortunately, at present only two curved sections of wall remain: one towards the north and the other towards the south. Nearby, many basaltic lava pebbles have been found.

810ef39c5126548e.text:
The monument stands on the edge of a steep rock face that drops sheer to the south, in an area of particular interest for the presence of numerous archaeological monuments, both prehistoric and Nuragic.

The building has a roughly quadrangular plan and is crossed by a through corridor flanked by opposing pairs of large niches; the corners are rounded, the walls where the entrances open are straight in profile to the ESE and slightly concave to the ENE.

81302f5d3c8147a7.text:
Probable location.

It consists of two underground chambers.

81310aa1c1f00435.text:
The monument consists of a central tower against which, on the north-western side, a second ruined tower leans.

The main tower, built of basalt blocks of various sizes, survives to a maximum height of about 8 metres. An internal staircase leads to the upper level. An extensive village, indicated on the surface by stone rubble and numerous ceramic finds, extended around the nuraghe.

813f62f6f295eba7.text: The context is special because the quarried stone appears "isolated", surrounded by holm oaks that blend it into the surroundings, the entrance faces south-west, the chamber is circular, and the walls feature square niches; the surrounding ground slopes gently, and a striking rocky outcrop is visible a few metres away to the west.

8147ae29e3075826.text: Complex nuraghe, it cannot be confidently assigned to any defined type due to the state of degradation or the significant burial of the structures.

8162d36833239887.text: The Sisini nuraghe stands on the summit of a hillock in the countryside at the entrance to the homonymous hamlet. It is characterized by an original and rare plan, which reinterprets the model of temple with a well. Indeed, it consists of a circular tower preceded by a massive bastion of square form.

8180ead9bf5b3806.text: The nuraghe, built from basalt blocks, is in fairly good condition. It consists of a central tower and two others attached to it, though the structure of one of them is not discernible due to collapses. Access to the main tower is via an entrance featuring a lintel. Inside the tower, a niche and the remains of a staircase are identifiable. From the nuraghe, one enjoys a magnificent view of Cea Bay.

81a5237036541632.text: One of many nuraghes, hidden beneath the earth, in the Oschiri area.

81a76b2df2c6da79.text: It lies on the south slope of Monte Lerno. The structure is in a state of serious decay. Nevertheless, part of the wall is easily recognisable because one of the entrances is still in good condition. At first glance this could be mistaken for a dolmen because of its particular structure, with a massive flat stone resting on the walls. A short distance further downhill there is another building, resembling a hut.

81b03c7500ded028.text: Village – scattered throughout the area are several stretches of wall that could belong to the huts of a village; unfortunately, the dense vegetation prevents a clear view of the area and makes it difficult to identify the structures.

81b3ae51a8171068.text: The domus de janas, existing in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe, marks the continuity of human occupation of the site over the millennia.

81b4bce6e8ad73f7.text: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and three additional towers with bastions (four-lobed). Around the nuraghe, traces of a settlement.

81b76175724dd560.text: Excavated in an amphitheatre of trachyte rock on the southern flank of the 'silent' hill of sa Pranedda, it consists of over 40 tombs of various sizes and plans, aligned along the rock face in a symmetrical arrangement that appears pre-planned. The necropolis of Montessu is one of the most significant and fascinating pre-Nuragic testimonies on the Island, in use for a millennium and a half, from the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC).

81b8c07b765b0153.text: Significant difficulty discouraged by the ascent. Several abrupt drop-offs. At certain points, walkways and ropes are provided to serve as handholds.

81c3177e971c93d1.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, 11 m in diameter, preserved to a height of about 2.5 m over three courses. Cyclopean walling of barely dressed boulders. The entrance, to the south-east, lacks a lintel and leads into a corridor about 2 m long.

81d209ea94cd6f19.text: The menhir, known as Su Furconi de Luxia Arrabiosa, stands alone on a short rise. The menhir is quadrangular, thinned at the top in a nearly conical shape, and measures 3.60 m in height. On the main face, facing east, 12 small cups are carved.

81e28b0675eef0dd.text: In the area of Baratè, on a modest elevation in a zone partly used for olive groves and partly for vineyards. On the north side, 4 courses (h m 1.80) of trachytic blocks remain; on the south side, the remains of the raised portion are covered by vegetation. Boundary walls attached to the nuraghe.

81e5e27fbac886f3.text: The structure remains only with traces; the site is neither accessible nor easily legible at present. Following the incursion of the Greek Church, Greek-Orthodox monks and hermits taught the inhabitants the production of crude bricks in the Eastern style, made from mud and straw (ladrini), which were used for building houses, with the rubble from the Nuraghe Zira serving as the foundation.

81e6856957d28340.text: It stands on a hilltop, at a panoramic point that dominates most of the Olgiastrino territory. Of the structure, in poor state of conservation, only some courses of limestone blocks are legible.

81fcbc280e6a9834.text: On a hillock along the provincial road Atzàra-Belvì, blocks of granite, almost entirely buried and arranged in a circular pattern, have been found, which are presumed to belong to a nuraghe.

822541bc6b7ab710.text:
The Maiore nuraghe (14th–9th century BC) is a single-tower type, currently standing more than eight metres high, with a clear taper towards the top; it has a single entrance on the south-east side. From the entrance a corridor leads to the central ground-floor chamber, which has a tholos roof, while on the left a stairway gives access to the upper level.

Because the tower suffered a major collapse before the 1980s, restoration work became necessary.

8227992fceab608b.text: Complex nuraghe or nuragic fortress, apparently earthen and completely levelled to the ground, with only the low courses partially buried remaining. From it, a large part of the Marmilla could be seen.

8237978d36df3440.text:
The domus is cut into a limestone face that is almost sheer above the valley below. It has a façade 2.60 m high depicting a simple stele. On the stele are the three typical recesses.

Like most architectural-façade domus created from scratch, it has a single chamber; this has a semi-elliptical plan. Inside, on the left, a wide niche opens whose function is unclear but which was presumably used for depositing votive objects.

824022900d8905f7.text:
The nuraghe consists of a main building with a three-storey central tower accompanied by a bilobate bastion arranged on two levels, enclosing a courtyard and two secondary towers. It is surrounded by an outer wall featuring towers and a sacred area.

Its tower is the one with the largest diameter among the known nuraghes.

825207b3af858e70.text: An enormous, tall building of huge, very dark basalt blocks, cyclopean, worked just enough to fit them together and give the structures perfect circularity. The central tower, very broad, and two other towers are visible, one to the south-east and the other to the north-west, plus a stretch of wall linking the central tower to the north-western one. The maximum visible height of the tower walls reaches 3 metres. The eastern part of the complex is covered with earth and vegetation.

826c34e947bdec43.text: Dolmen I consists of a large slab resting on stones that originally must have been set on edge to support the roof. Of Dolmen II the ceiling slab and a few wall boulders survive. In the same area about sixty hemispherical hollows are also recorded, clearly artificial and perhaps linked to ancient cult practices connected with the prehistoric monuments just described.

82837c38a2c5482d.text: Settled village already in the iron age. According to the report, the site continues to be affected by quarrying activities, particularly by a large dump of equipment and inert waste. Quarry where approximately 10,000 tonnes of toxic waste from Portovesme S.r.l. have been illegally dumped.

8297d6a6d955ba1d.text:
The presence of the village, belonging to the nearby homonymous nuraghe, is attested by the existence of some circular huts and other alignments of stones emerging from the ground.

The settlement is located within the territory of the comune of Macomer (NU).

829ace6260d3f0ab.text: It is a "corridor nuraghe" located at the centre of a large outer wall within which the ruins of a vast settlement are found. The monument is situated on the basaltic upland extending between the settlements of Dualchi and Borore. About 180 metres to the northeast, the remains of the corresponding giants' tomb are preserved, while to the north-northwest lies the giants' tomb of Putzu Iu.

82bfa9476bb00be5.text: Complex nuraghe with traces of a village surrounding it, featuring significant collapses on the slopes. From here there is a prominent view and control over the village, which includes a temple at Irru.

82cb39628fc500a7.text:
Built entirely of granite, it is of the central-corridor type, with a mixed layout that combines the plan of corridor nuraghi and tholos nuraghi with a central corridor and paired chambers; the structure is massive and irregular. The tholos is intact.

The bastion is reached by a staircase accessible from the courtyard. The entrance leads into a central corridor, covered by an ogival vault, which runs the full length of the building and opens onto a large courtyard.

82d2b69b360ef99f.text: The area is heavily anthropogenically modified and rich in evidence. The presence of this wall, constructed with medium-sized polygonal stones and others only roughly shaped, does not follow a pre-determined direction, but appears entirely random. The surrounding territory is rich in surface features, from which its significance can be inferred. The freely interpreted layout represents an idealized partial view of the sites in that region. mu

82f0d84e6ad28898.text: The site consists essentially of two parts: the first, formed by the well temple, a sacred well dating to the Nuragic period, with structures attached to it: a meeting hut, an enclosure, and other smaller huts. The second part of the complex, about two hundred metres to the south-west, consists of a single-tower nuraghe, some elongated stone huts of uncertain date, and a Nuragic village, still to be excavated, of which only a few emerging elements are visible.

831e367f36eaec84.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an attached village. The original tower survives, its interior choked with collapse and vegetation. About four complete courses of the original structure remain. To the south there is a curtain wall with an entrance topped by a lintel; because of collapse and vegetation its function cannot be determined. To the north-west of the tower a cyclopean wall is present, breaking off abruptly, apparently the north wall of a corridor.

833bf4c6f2f60103.text: The nuraghe was built in the advanced phase of the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1400 BC) on a granite base surrounded by a series of massive boulders, adapting the building to the irregular shape of the hill. It is a four-lobed nuraghe, with a central tower and four other towers added concentrically. Access is made easy by a ramp leading to the entrance, which in turn opens into a long corridor with corbelled walls forming a pointed arch.

8342c3ac24f9e115.text: Oral sources insist that a nuraghe stands on the summit of Bruncu Zinnibiri, without specifying whether it is a single tower or a more complex structure. Immediately below the few ruins of the “nuraghe” the village extended, also the target of continuous illicit digging; one of the surveys carried out led to the discovery of a cultural deposit near which charcoal remains were observed and where abundant ceramic material was collected.

834e76b0e7970f6d.text: Nuraghe currently under excavation. It is thought to consist of a central tholos and four surrounding towers enclosing a courtyard. An extensive village of numerous huts, also used in Punic and Roman times, spreads around it, protected by a massive system of walls up to 6 metres thick. Great importance attaches to the discovery inside the village of a glass-working workshop. The site is not open to the public.

83513fcd96d1c93f.text: The necropolis consists of eleven domus de janas, both single- and multi-chambered. The largest originally had five chambers, now a single space after the partition walls were demolished. It is distinguished by two distinct phases of use: the first in the Neolithic and the second in the Middle Bronze Age (1700–1300 BC), when at least three hypogea were converted into "domus a prospetto architettonico".

8367345caeb83466.text: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain standing, embedded in natural rock masses.

8375f645498b8e92.text: The tomb is small in size and built using an orthostatic technique. It was destroyed by illegal excavations; during the excavation and restoration works carried out in 1996, fragments of a uniquely shaped, carved bowl were recovered, a type not previously known in Sardinia. In 2008, several vitreous paste beads were also recovered.

838be6dc8474df98.text: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a small portion remains at the junction of three borders.

83ced32001881340.text: Cemetery consisting of four domus de janas dug into erratic boulders

83d1d8a64e2f75cf.text: This site is located in an olive grove and was previously studied. Today it is completely destroyed, and it is unclear whether there are still remains of a village underground. Some forms of hut or nuraghe are recognizable. The agricultural land is covered with squared stones and fragments of stone. Most of the stones of various sizes have been incorporated into the numerous dry stone walls surrounding the site.

83d512f6de506d9b.text: In the immediate area behind the mouth of the Mannu River, the complex nuraghe Monte Aiveghe remains with a height of about 1.2 m, consisting of three courses of calcareous blocks corresponding to the top of the two towers. Surrounding it, the remains of at least three huts are identifiable, likely belonging to the associated settlement. There is also evidence of ceramic material dating to the Roman period.

83f3894ad6fcd03c.text: This underground tomb, cut from a block of erratic rock, is located about 300 m from the village's sports field. Nearby, other rock blocks with cups can be observed.

83f477bc8ff4d066.text: There are three giants' tombs, of which the first is the most important and in the best state of preservation.

84026b5e5d9ca8e0.text: The investigations have identified traces of human presence at the site dating from the period between the Late Neolithic (3300–2700 BC) and the Chalcolithic (2700–1700 BC). The most monumental evidence consists of the menhirs present at the site: single, in pairs, in triads, in spectacular alignments formed by as many as 20 menhirs, and in circles. Walking through the site one can see menhirs lying on the ground everywhere, whole or in fragments. The site must originally have been larger than it appears today.

844719993f47d5a7.text: Nuraghe apparently a single-tower, freed from vegetation in 2022. Previously classified as a single-tower, it is now more likely to be quadrilobate. Around the nuraghe a considerable amount of Roman-era pottery (sealed) is present.

845d3ca5e4e1ea1a.text: The Lorenzu Origa nuraghe partly incorporates the pink granite spur on which it was built into its wall face. The monument appears as a truncated-cone tower about 11 m in diameter, preserving a surviving height of at least 2.80–2.50 m. The other opening, topped by a lintel, leads into a space that is actually a sort of corridor roofed with blocks laid in steps and may be part of a stairwell.

846642c6282f93ab.text: Single-tower nuraghe in partial good condition, located on the slope of a small hillock.

84b15019b36fb12a.text: The site is very difficult to identify. To the visitor it appears as a heap of buried ashlar stones, only partially exposed. Accessible via the half-coast path behind the Capoterra settlement.

84b557dfaff9d7b0.text:
The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

In an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible of which only the basal courses remain; in particular a wall stands out that encloses a roughly rectangular area, inside which there are traces of various types of rooms, some semicircular but mostly quadrangular.

84c8f552e740643e.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an addition not easily legible. Surrounding village.

84cf04d8b566f687.text: Enormous single-tower, inaccessible, built on a rocky outcrop, with earthbound walls remaining up to 4 m in height. It can be reached on foot via the forest ranger's lookout road. One of the highest points in the area offers a magnificent view.

84e9f853f83d1907.text:
It has a single entrance oriented to the northeast.

It is now covered with soil and sand, although at the top of the nuraghe the top section remains, from which part of the internal walling is visible.

84ff8079e9fb8de0.text: The cave is reached by a staircase built with Nuragic technique and covered with lintels for sixteen steps, very similar to the one used inside nuraghi. The cave consists of two large chambers and a small single-cell room at the top of the cavity. On the floor of the cave there are ceramic fragments of the Nuragic period. The site is generally classified as a hypogean temple or as a refuge.

8518e13c448dbcaa.text: The layout is quite imposing: it measures a total of 22 m; the exedra has a circumference of 18 m and almost all the stones remain, set in a sharp, pointed fashion, some of which are very tall. The funerary corridor is 16 m long, 1.30 m high, and 1.40 m wide; it is covered by horizontal slabs, one of which is missing, revealing the interior of the tomb, which has a rectangular cross-section.

852acd05cc7c6024.text: The village lies at the foot of Monte Perdas de Fogu, in the locality Sa Costa de su Lurdagu. The structures survive as disordered wall remains; in some cases two rows of boulders are arranged in a pseudo-circular form. All the structures contain fallen boulders and rubble inside, making it difficult to determine their original perimeter and shape. Numerous potsherds of various kinds are visible on the surface throughout the area.

852f16d8d985536b.text: Complex tholos nuraghe. Completely enveloped by vegetation, it is a large nuraghe whose features can only be vaguely guessed. It appears to consist of a central tower and two added towers, with an internal courtyard now filled with collapse blocks. Built of large blocks of local basalt, it survives in good condition, although it is hard to observe because of the bushes that envelop it.

85401d129d2ca0de.text: In the area of Funtanazza, within the lands of the Lampis family, lies the giants' tomb of Bruncu Espis, a site where in ancient times a Roman village stood. Well preserved and maintained by the landowners, it features a corridor about ten metres long and slightly more than one metre wide, and is completely covered by soil, upon which some ancient constructions still appear.

85629a0f51e8b232.text: Single-tower nuraghe, covered by a layer of vegetation, whose tholos is still intact

8589650ab91db3fd.text:
Practically in the town, on a ridge overlooking Tossilo, this completely derelict single-tower nuraghe stands out. Its layout is the most classic one, with a niche to the left of the entrance to the south-south-east, and the staircase to the upper floor on the left. Inside the tholos, though completely covered in brambles, the three typical niches can be made out.

A splendid spot for sunsets of nostalgic meditation.

858992b85b1c16dd.text: Once one "slid" inward, the tomb reveals itself in all its splendour: columns, bull's-head protomes in low relief, chambers, antechambers, the door of the beyond, symbols and signs of an ancient devotion that intoxicates body and spirit.

85a1c349b9085472.text: The village includes three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of medium-sized blocks of local schist, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. Access to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The tholos has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.

85f2a426195c131d.text:
Inside a pastoral farm, at the centre of a circular sheepfold bounded by a dry-stone wall, stands a unique and exceptional proto-anthropomorphic menhir fixed in the ground. The pillar, 1.77 m high, shows a summary rendering of a head set off from the body below by a short neck, and may symbolically evoke the phallic symbol.

It lies 500 metres north-west of the hypogeal necropolis of Monte Ozastru.

8606324f17341d23.text: The temple was built in isodomic masonry, that is, with basalt blocks skillfully squared and shaped as needed with appropriate inclinations. The rocks in the surrounding area are mainly schist or granite, while the volcanic rock used was transported to the site from relatively distant locations, probably from the Dorgali region.

860f89d966f4035c.text: The archaeological area lies on the edge of the Santa Lucia basalt plateau, east of the Monte Arci massif. It includes two complex nuraghi with a village, set about 50 metres apart. The nuraghe to the east is also complex, in better condition than the previous one; it preserves the central tower chamber, with its top missing, with several niches in the walls and the stairwell opening off the entrance corridor.

8623547e0c115955.text:
Corridor nuraghe.

The main tower currently preserves the chamber, which has a sub-circular plan, partially filled with rubble from the tholos and the upper part of the wall face; a first block is visible marking the start of the corridor. To the south, at a distance of about 8.50 m, there is a secondary tower that remains standing for 5 courses, arranged with polygonal technique and irregularly.

865687fd2c3fbc54.text: It is possible to assume the location of the nuraghe indicated by Taramelli on the slope of the hill. The nuraghe was already demolished at the time of Taramelli and is no longer visible today. Exact location not established.

8693d32834b08d93.text: It currently appears as a modest height. Likely a complex nuraghe of "tancato" type (two towers with an intermediate courtyard). Remnants of walls remain. Destroyed by the opening of the municipal road.

8694c5b4aa5867a2.text: easily visible, adjacent to the municipal road, almost destroyed at the top of the tower, there is a covered entrance surrounded by bushes.

86c0086b33f07f97.text: Nuraghe Abbaia (Acquaviva); it is situated halfway up the slope of this mountain, near two abundant springs; this nuraghe, which remains with only a few traces, served as a coastal watchtower in relation to the nuraghe Ottiolo.

86dab82870f7f473.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 12.50 m) and an entrance facing south-east; the tower survives to a maximum height of 4.80 m on the south-east side, with six courses, while the minimum height is on the north-west side at 2 metres with three courses. The masonry consists of carefully worked blocks laid in regular horizontal courses.

In the surrounding area the circular structures of numerous huts from the Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.

86dc75140485e089.text: Giants' tomb in miniature, very small

86dd54fc1a0e946c.text: Single-tower nuraghe. About 100 metres from the monument there is a Roman hypogeum, partly cut into the rock and partly built of brick with a barrel vault.
