86f42518434a190d.text: Location according to ancient maps of this nuraghe, of which today only scattered stones remain.

8710668f7587c7cf.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, though partially concealed by vegetation, retains a discernible external profile, the funerary corridor, and the right arm of the exedra.

The construction technique involves regular courses using polygonal blocks that are slightly squared.

8724fa70b12fc476.text: The central tower, which has a diameter of about 8 m at its top, is clearly visible. It retains nine courses in height, built in regular sub-square masonry with medium-sized blocks set with rubble in scalloped patterns. The internal upper portion is completely blocked by collapse. Some added structures, hidden by vegetation, are discernible, though only with difficulty.

873f78d54a0f0148.text:
The nuraghe, almost completely demolished, is traceable in its entire ground-plan profile (diameter 11 m, surviving height about 2 m).

Near the nuraghe, scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of a great many circular structures (generally more than 7 m in diameter) and rectilinear ones can be seen, attributable to the ancient settlement and probably also belonging to a sacred area.

8746908ae8c291f0.text: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.

874f380519baa735.text: It is located on the slope to the north-east of Monte Sozu, directly beneath Su Casteddu where the homonymous nuraghe stands. It is the largest giants' tomb in our Chiaramonti area. The lithic burial cist is about 15 m long and is composed of stones of various shapes, roughly shaped, and is covered by large trachytic slabs laid flat. Mu

87521610f8d1f860.text: It is composed of at least four domus de janas, still under excavation.

8771bb3ddd23d00b.text:
It is in poor state of conservation.

This is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

Within a radius of 400 m there are 3 giants' tombs, one nuragic spring, and 5 baetyls.

877260810e55e77c.text: Two opposite dolmen tombs. One has been excavated and consists of two chambers, with the entrance facing south. The other tomb remains unexplored; the covering slabs are visible, and the entrance faces north.

878d15915ef7aefb.text: With the filling of the artificial basin at Oliai, it is found on the summit of a small island.

8799c12b16150fc1.text: Small Giants' tomb, belonging to the Appiu village context. Never excavated, it appears to belong to the cyclopean type of giants' tomb, despite being located in an area where dolmens with arched stelae are predominant.

87aa554490418714.text: It is a two-cell house with a short antechamber cut into a trachytic outcrop. The rooms are arranged along the longitudinal axis and have walls carefully smoothed and ceilings slightly hemispherical; the entrance faces south-east.

87aba838b149e43b.text: Between 1950 and 1960, a calcination oven was built, whose structure was very likely constructed using stones belonging to the village.

87de76843d0aca7d.text: It is a complex nuraghe, with at least the upper courses of the walls skillfully dressed in arenaria. Unfortunately, it is difficult to visit and document due to the vegetation.

87e7eac82f9a7341.text: The nuraghe Su Cuttu stands on the Alghero–Ittiri provincial road. It is a single-tower nuraghe that has suffered considerable disturbance. Only a few boulders remain in their original position. It belongs to the complex of nuraghi in the Cuga valley.

87f660e9a29263e0.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are completely enveloped by vegetation, appearing as a small natural rise covered with moss, bushes, and debris. Although the type of monument can only be barely discerned from observation, it is plausible that, once freed from the vegetation, it might reveal itself in good state of preservation.

881647d8baa379be.text: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral extension, featuring a central tower and two additional towers with bastions, and in the middle lies the courtyard as an integration space.

8819c63e5660577a.text: The Prunittu necropolis is in the Sorrana area. The complex consists of two clusters about a hundred metres apart and contains 27 domus de janas in total. Most of the hypogea are easily reached, but some, cut into the vertical face of a trachyte bench with their entrances set well above ground level (up to four metres), can only be accessed by lowering oneself from the plateau above.

882028d065d86e04.text: A few remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

883743940e5fb5a3.text: It is uncertain whether the site dates to the Nuragic period.

883f034a05109c58.text: Collapsed remains of a probable single-tower nuraghe

884b762848e5cda8.text:
It is located at the highest point of Florinas. (517 m a.s.l.)  

Today, unfortunately, it has collapsed inward.  

It features a main tower and two additional towers.

884f7669f49de708.text:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks.

The building is completely covered in brambles and climbing vegetation, so that only a few stretches of the external wall face can be seen. From above one can observe the collapse debris filling the inner chamber. Modern and contemporary structures, enclosures and shelters, lean against the nuraghe on the west side.

8853127344c1c3a9.text: Complex nuraghe: the central tower is visible, inside there are three niches. It has been extensively modified due to agricultural mechanization and the constant activity of tomb diggers. It once had an extensive village attached, extending to the giants' tomb of "Sa pedra Longa".

885842d1e767c62e.text: The nuraghe is built of soft trachyte blocks, not very large. The foundations rest directly on the bedrock, which also forms a natural bastion that was then finished and completed by the nuraghe's builders by adding large blocks. Nearby the base of a Nuragic hut is visible. Single-tower nuraghe with village and outer wall with probable seven towers

8861785dd22406a5.text:
Popular memory reports the existence of a complex nuraghe beneath the Forte Su Pisu.

In the regional reconstruction of the Sulky Fenicia, a Nuragic village is reported situated at the top of the dominant hill, overlooking the port and the ancient city.

88726d1720fb1b71.text: Noted as a nuraghe, it appears as a large heap of stones. Very useful for hiking purposes, as it marks the turnaround point when coming from Magola, following the edge of the cliff, before descending along the path beneath the cliffs. Caution with shepherd dogs!

887589c464cd286d.text: It consists of three baetyls of truncated-conical shape, about 1.5 metres high and with a diameter of about 60–80 cm, located on the right side of the tomb. The central baetyl, from an undated period, was overturned and transformed into a basin.

8875f87e19b01d2f.text:
The site dates to about 3000 BC and was used for about 1500 years, from the time of the Ozieri culture to that of Bonnanaro.

It takes its name from the large number of skeletons (more than 200) and the rich assemblage of weapons – datable to about 1650–1600 BC – consisting of swords and daggers in arsenical copper (19 in all). The swords, with triangular blades, range in length from 27 to 66 cm and show some similarities with the swords of the El Argar culture (Spain).

8878fdebdd388f78.text: Single-tower nuraghe, it faces the Nuraghe Su Nuraxi on the other side of the Rio su Gaffu.

88914d40bc7fe058.text: The name would suggest a possible three-lobed structure, almost entirely destroyed, of considerable dimensions. Above the main tower there is an entrance covered by bushes.

88976154d099e122.text: Natural cave composed of a single chamber within which prehistoric fragments are visible. The cave has been severely damaged by illegal excavation activities.

88be519d1323c5f2.text: Nuraghe with a large village and giants' tomb of attachment. Damaged and overgrown with vegetation. The shape is difficult to identify.

88c05bce9563fc54.text: The “Tittiriola” at Bolotana is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, bounded by an outer wall and set within a village whose traces are still appreciable. It has an internal stair chamber that is currently impassable because of collapses, and on the upper part, corresponding to the entrance, a large window surmounted by a lintel is clearly visible. Near the structure a sacred well is visible that appears to have been covered over in relatively recent times.

88d9a109ae8cda4c.text: Two domus de janas sites located on the slopes of the mountain known as "Sas Monzas". Excavated in Miocene limestone.

88e19494d38a8f3b.text: Giants' tomb, cut-down, belonging to the same named nuraghe and village

88e84835013e9645.text: Located in a picturesque natural rock outcrop near the nuraghe Nieddu. It is partly eroded and difficult to read due to the few courses remaining in situ. The main tower and a smaller secondary tower, likely added at a later date, are visible.

88f044de5f09228d.text: It has a well-preserved tholos and features, at a height of about four metres, two niches that undoubtedly communicated with the staircase leading to the first floor. The boldness of the construction is evident, as the two niches would likely weaken the vaulted structure, which instead appears solid and strong. Part of the first floor, accessible from the outside, is also visible. mu

890eb5f7a40d4579.text: The nuraghe is in a state of complete abandonment. Partly buried and completely overgrown by vegetation.

890f048030b5196c.text: It consists of the ruins of a site and a settlement that originally must have had medium to large dimensions. Indeed, the central tower, which was likely imposing, remains only with its base, lateral walls, and lintel at the entrance; at least three other towers and extensive fortifications along the entire perimeter of the small hill on which the site is situated.

8919634a7358cc2a.text: Remains dating to the Nuragic period located on the Red Island, about one kilometre from the coast of the commune of Teulada. The area falls within the Capo Teulada military zone.

891b4f5102377522.text: The Pranu Narbonis cemetery consists of a group of three domus still in excellent conservation, dug out from a single large granite block emerging from the ground.

89494ba1f15853ac.text:
Of the megalithic burial, of isodomic type and oriented south-east, the funerary corridor can be measured (length 4.20 m – width 1.05 m), consisting of four blocks per side and one at the end, all finely worked; the layout of the exedra and that of the tomb body are less clear.

Among the scattered stones in the exedra area lies a dentilled ashlar: it is trapezoidal (1.85 x 1.15 x 0.75 m high), has a slight rebate and the usual three vertical notches.

894b96583b2e93c0.text: The village consists of three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of local schist blocks, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. The entrance to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The latter has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the well's entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.

89723364ff0f6be4.text: Eroded by the force of water

8974fcab08c004b0.text: Remains of a possible Nuragic settlement currently located at the centre of a road ramp.

8987b76e41c3ac78.text: The entrance, tall and flat-topped, leads into an interior space that was intended to be a protected area, built at the edge of a cliff. On the left as one enters there is a circular chamber; on the right side of the corridor only the perimeter wall remains.

898cca40919711f4.text: It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower surrounded by a quadrilobate bastion that includes four angular towers and an open-air courtyard. In the north-eastern area, the remains of the outer wall and the ruins of an attached dwelling are visible.

89af1ba9e7a5d05a.text: Neolithic huts of circular form characterised by large stones up to 1.00–1.20 metres high, resting on the rocky stratum.

89d315f30a378464.text: A short distance from the underground tomb of Putzu, beyond the agricultural road passing through the area of Busola, two menhirs have been identified. One of the menhirs still stands firmly in the ground in its original position. A second menhir, with a sharp lateral profile and an elliptical cross-section on the major side, is embedded within the post of the entrance to the field.

8a0be753a7a08799.text: The tomb is covered by enormous flat lithic slabs, including one longer than four metres.

8a225f2452816252.text: The monument, a complex (four-lobed) structure, includes a central tower to which four secondary towers have been added, connected to the north and east by straight curtain walls, while the connecting wall to the west follows a curved outline.

8a27f8c2f1d48fa2.text:
The monument lies about 200 metres from the nuraghe of the same name.

The tomb has been partly demolished with the removal of all the worked ashlars that faced the burial chamber.

Nevertheless, despite the very poor state of preservation, the usual ground plan of this tomb type can still be read on the ground: a rectangular body with an apsidal rear, a semicircular exedra at the front, and a rectangular burial chamber.

8a3351f43e8a2410.text: Among the few remaining elements of the nuraghe, the lintel deserves special mention, appearing almost suspended in the air.

8a3b9b687f111427.text: The tomb opens just a few metres from the remains of a small single-cell domus de janas (Tomb III); it is very likely that Tomb II was originally a small domus de janas, later transformed into the form of a tomb with a façade. The stele is currently missing its upper part, including the lunette border, which lies on its side just a few metres from the entrance.

8a56c6f0dc294e96.text: Nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghes in the Cuga basin. Apparently bilobate, but a third, partially destroyed tower submerged beneath the lake cannot be ruled out. All around the remains of a large Roman settlement are clearly visible.

8a5b8384ad6b11f8.text: Probable complex nuraghe completely collapsed and fallen.

8a63e89d8447490e.text: The Ortei nuraghe is a three-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, still in a good state of preservation, and two lateral towers whose remains are almost completely buried and overgrown with vegetation. The peculiarity of this nuraghe lies in the fact that the chamber of the central tower, which has a circular plan, is provided with three particularly deep niches, especially the central one, which has a large lintel with a small window above it.

8a6d1a32de3d8926.text: They are three underground cists dug into a low limestone cliff face.

8a7b1f979b75dcd9.text:
The tomb is built with coursed masonry. The tomb body contains a rectangular funerary corridor, closed at the far end by a single shaped head slab with an arched top.

The exedra survives only in part: the hemicycle is bounded by orthostatic slabs of reduced size, at the base of which runs a low bench-seat, also incomplete, intended to receive offerings.

The rear wall face of the exedra joins the tomb body without a break.

8a878bf830ca952c.text: It consists of five hypogea, one of which is buried and one of which is difficult to identify.

8a8e71474c221cfe.text: Domus de janas at the edge of the village, next to which a dwelling has been built.

8a9226598ad04adb.text: Small dolmen closed on three sides with a single covering slab.

8a98614405b54f31.text: The reliefs at Sa Icu in Dorgali are on the basalt cliff overhanging the Cedrino, 1.2 km east of provincial road no. 38, and are attributed to the Chalcolithic. They consist of 57 geometric figures covering an area of 10 x 12 m, carved mostly in high relief (only one is incised) on three basalt blocks that protrude on average 30 cm above ground level. The figures depict: simple parallelepipeds, truncated terraced pyramids of three tiers with simple rectangular plans or with a semicircle on the longer side of the base parallelepipeds.

8aa6fdb28e3d2888.text: Nuraghe named after the locality: "Sa tanca 'e su padru". Of imposing dimensions but completely ruined and not discernible anymore. Until a few years ago it allowed access to the interior.

8ab6d8af7af45de5.text:
A large cave, extending about 40 metres, shows an archaeological layer disturbed by guano diggers and illegal excavators.

From the disturbed layers come ceramic materials dating from the second half of the 5th millennium B.C. to the republican period.

8ab7ddf510c88b29.text: It is probably the door closure of a domus de janas.

8ad5ddc43032f1e4.text: The cemetery consists of three domus de janas.

8ae20d05fb32a010.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which only a few courses survive

8ae99d90f8b5aadb.text:
Possible single-tower nuraghe; the doubt arises from its small size, but it could be a small nuraghe placed on a height with the sole role of a lookout.

Near the structure there are two tombs, perhaps of Roman date, built of limestone slabs; inside, two skulls and other human bones can be seen.

8aeb7b39fc9ca14e.text: It is one of many nuraghes in the Thiesino area, of which today only a few remains can be identified.

8affd99fff66cae1.text: A tomb circle built of large, semi-worked slab-like boulders of various shapes, mostly triangular. It differs from the others in the size of the slabs. The circular structure is broken on the north-west side, where presumably three or four boulders are missing. Nine boulders remain in their original position, covering three-quarters of the construction. Some recumbent slabs lie at the edges and very probably originally closed the circle.

8b1387a597181fc3.text:
In its current state of preservation, it is possible to speculate—based on only a few identifiable wall segments— that the monument extended over multiple levels, following the different elevations of the rocky peak on which it was built.

Its main axis may have been oriented north-south, but the position of the entrance or the planimetric layout of the chamber remains undefined.

8b1e1b4b21858f01.text: Complex nuraghe of difficult definition due to its state of degradation and the significant burial of its structures. Located on the summit of Capo San Marco, with panoramic views in all directions.

8b45b03db155062f.text: The Nuragic spring of Su Musuelu lies about 600 m east of the Nuragic sacred spring of Is Molineddus. From the little information Spano was able to gather, its temple consisted of a rectangular building with the entrance on the western side, built of large blocks laid dry. Behind the building a spring rose from the rock and collected in a round well, also made of large stones.

8b60279ab8ed73bb.text: Complex nuraghe with three towers, probably added. Calcare ashlar. Nearby are the remains of a village and two giants' tombs.

8b65044db8954ac9.text: What remains of a giants' tomb located in the wooded area of Santa Barbara's pic nic zone

8b848d0934b4810f.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. A monument of considerable dimensions, in good state of conservation, fully legible in all its components except the entrance area, which has now been restored and contains two residual fragments of the original stele.

The construction technique is of the coursed type, using polygonal granite blocks.

8b84d0c8cd626ed5.text:
Two domus de janas, separated by about 2 m. The antechamber has a semi-elliptical plan and an irregularly flat ceiling. In the back wall of the antechamber there is a square opening, also with a recess, providing access to a room with a flat ceiling.

A rectangular light opening with a recess for the shutter provides access to an antechamber with a sub-elliptical plan and a flat ceiling.

8b88e15ab7753425.text: The Cuccurada archaeological complex stands on the southern tip of the Mogoro basalt plateau of “Sa Struvina”, in a position commanding a wide view over the Campidano plain and the Rio Mogoro valley. Excavations carried out from 1994 to the present have revealed the presence of monumental structures attributable to different periods: a megalithic wall and a cyclopean structure with an elliptical plan (Cuccurada A), attributable to the developed Eneolithic (Monte Claro Culture, 2700–2200 BC).

8b88f17f0e5c676b.text: Man-made structure submerged by an artificial lake

8b951ea2a36be01d.text:
The Nuraghe Biriola lies at Dualchi, about four hundred metres from the Nuraghe Piddio. It is a complex nuraghe that looks like a veritable fortress of considerable size (about 38 by 22 metres). The central tower contains a large circular chamber with a corbelled roof; niches, partly accessible, are set in the central part of the structure.

A village once stood around the nuraghe, and traces of it are still visible.

8bb010f32a356bd4.text:
It stands on the summit of a hill in the Marmilla. The structure is a complex type, formed by an original central tower built in the Middle Bronze Age, to which four more towers and a bastion were later added. One of the four towers was subsequently sacrificed during a further building phase that presumably also saw the construction of the massive hexagonal outer wall.

In the Early Iron Age a new village developed on the site.

8bf5479ed3f26aac.text: Menhir located about 40 m from the Nuraghe de Chirigu. The menhir has three faces: the two opposite ones are approximately semicircular and have a flat surface, while the third, the rear one, is convex. Natural cuts and grooves are visible, along with smooth areas that appear to be artificially shaped.

8bf9062aaddc2558.text: Built from basalt blocks, the structure features a three-lobed layout, with a central mastio and three secondary towers arranged around a courtyard of falcon-shaped plan. The site was surrounded by a powerful outer wall – traces of which are clearly visible – composed of five towers and straight curtain walls, except for the northern side, naturally protected by the slopes of the Giare.

8bf9cfba40da64a7.text: The alignment of closely spaced stones at Serra Pillonadori stands on the south-western slopes of the Su Niu de is Crobus ridge and west of the Baccu Ungroneddus, in a position from which the valley of S. Barbara and the Rio Solanas can be taken in at a single glance and which is visible from practically every point of the inner ridges and valleys below. The five granite stones of which it consists are arranged on a north–south axis and face east.

8c163f822bfa4e7a.text: Large natural cave, on the eastern side of which open several smaller cavities whose morphological features would suggest they should be classified as domus de janas; this hypothesis would be strengthened by the presence of channels and cups on the top of the cave, used both functionally and ritually.

8c27698951ab5b79.text:
It is probably a corridor nuraghe against which various elongated huts and numerous dry-stone walls were later built, making it particularly difficult to survey.

From this heap of rubble overgrown with vegetation a circular tower (diam. 11–12 metres) emerges, with a surviving height of 4 metres.

At the top, where the tower is missing, short stretches of corridor can be made out, but they cannot be defined because of the collapse.

8c5cd6af648a6110.text: The Dom'e Biriu nuraghe is located about 1.5 km north of Genoni. In large part eroded, a tower in masonry with a nearly square plan can still be seen, with horizontal courses and nearly squared blocks.

8c86be6426246128.text: It is reported in historical memory of those who worked on the construction of the artificial basin at Madau in the second half of the 1900s. There are no on-site evidences of other types of constructions or foundations.

8c8f592a10901388.text: The largest nuraghe in the territory of Illorai, mentioned by Taramelli, G. Lilliu and Angius-Casalis, consists of a central tower probably of two storeys with its tholos still intact; on the south side is the courtyard with the entrance partly collapsed; on the north-east and north-west sides are the two lateral towers (with collapsed tholoi) but their internal walls are in excellent condition. Collapses inwards are minimal, while those outwards are substantial. Contact AGRIS for access to the area.

8c973c77e93b2b08.text: Originally it was intended to form, together with that of the nearby N.ghe Ena Ortu, a single extensive settlement.

8caaefdddd31f327.text: Giants' tomb in very poor condition; the chamber is still clearly visible, the exedra is partially incorporated into the boundary wall. Located inside a small enclosure a short distance from the country church of Santa Cristina. Easily accessible.

8cd5a56b1dad06ee.text: Complex nuraghe built of slates (stintino stone). Three towers remain, with a powerful outer wall enclosing the structure. Around the nuraghe, traces of huts and collapses of related structures are clearly visible. It preserves a tholos almost intact, except for some courses.

8ce5f57c95f85a72.text: Complex nuraghe of which the central tower and a bastion, perhaps three-lobed, survive. The original tower retains almost its entire outline. The interior of the tower is filled with collapse and vegetation. To the NNE there is a curving wall that reaches its maximum height to the ENE, where five courses survive; it may be a tower. To the W–SW a wall can be made out, probably belonging to a lateral tower. A further tower was probably located to the SE. Ceramic fragments are present, attributable from the Nuragic period to the medieval period.

8d0a7646f05f6dfb.text: Complex nuraghe, partially collapsed and surrounded by vegetation. The tholos is intact, surrounded by a significant outer wall.

8d13d1896fa9e569.text:
A collective burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, hidden beneath a mass of mastic trees, only the apsidal area and the terminal section of the corridor remain visible.

8d1566ec6f57aab9.text: Single-tower with its top missing and buried

8d1c6dd59b61d075.text:
Santa Vittoria constitutes one of the most important ritual complexes of the Nuragic Sardinia. Extending over more than 3 hectares, it is protected by a natural cliff to the S/S-O and by a wall to the N/O following the rocky margin.

The sanctuary features four main groups of buildings: the two temples and the "hut of the priest", the "festive enclosure", the group of the "double baetyl" enclosure, and the eastern-southern-eastern group.

8d38456f080a447a.text:
What is visible is only a small portion. The rest is completely buried and covered by vegetation. Structure with a circular form on multiple levels.

A little lower down, an ancient wall cut from the rocks and composed of very large stone blocks.

8d640e1766c944c5.text: Located within the municipal urban plan. There are no authoritative studies on the structure. Local oral traditions state that it has an entrance on an inclined plane/slope for a few metres, leading to a base, after which one descends vertically by about 20 to 25 metres. The landowners of that area sealed the entrance with a large stone/ slab.

8d84d4ec05e26245.text:
In a wooded area, carved into trachytic rock. The interior is decorated with a false door and a probable bull's-head protome above.

It includes 7 hypogea in total and known.

8da24ee84bd04f1b.text: Of the practically destroyed monument, the outer outline of the tomb body and the exedra are still visible on the ground. Shaped ashlars worked on their exposed faces lie on the ground, showing that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry. During the last site visit (Jan. 2012) it was found that the two so-called dentilled stelae that lay next to the burial are no longer present.

8da6e04882651802.text:
Nuraghe "CASTEDDU" located in the hamlet of Pozzo S. Nicola (municipality of Stintino).

It could be a three-lobed or four-lobed nuraghe, currently buried.

L.L.

8db28d14ca80c3bd.text: In this area, for many years used for cultivation, eight monoliths were discovered during ploughing works; five of them are still present on the ground today; these menhirs, all made from a single local trachyte block, have an average height of 180 cm and feature a flat face and a convex opposite face.

8db4146460198c4b.text: Submerged nuraghe in the basin of the lake on the hillside

8dc6449e6dbd4c13.text: Only the central corridor of the structure remains. Surrounding it are scattered ashlar stones, but not immediately assignable to the tomb.

8dd09721ba09b137.text: The monument retains a large portion of the internal corridor. It is possible to identify what was the external wall face up to the exedra, whose right side is visible, while on the left only two vertical stones remain near the entrance. At a short distance lies the megalithic stele, unfortunately cut, and what appears to be the closure portal.

8dd38400d708d7e6.text: Of the monument, the wall structures related to the central tower, plus other towers, and possibly one more, are clearly visible. The outer wall, equipped with an entrance lintel, is clearly visible. The mastio retains a structure of as many as seven courses.

8de61a176bf25107.text: Nuraghe destroyed during the times of the local land reclamation. In the area large stones (not found in the surrounding region) remain, used several decades ago to build terraces. In the area, fragments of pottery, probably Nuragic, and pieces of grinding stones from the same period have been found. It remains impossible to determine their exact location and dimensions.

8df16460ebc746a0.text: About 250 m from the Nuraghe Noccus, on a rocky outcrop, there are: a very unusual tafone, now partly collapsed; three large monoliths (about 250 cm high), set a short distance apart, which could be menhirs; numerous boulders of various unusual shapes, in some cases next to the monoliths, in others scattered without a clear order but close to them. In the opinion of a (female) archaeologist, the menhirs do indeed seem to mark out the funerary space.

8df50dc3c051752a.text: The shape of this single-tower nuraghe is still clearly visible, although only a few stone blocks have survived.

8df74754790fb377.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure has been largely destroyed, as well as covered by vegetation and rubble.

8dfb25bdc5b6cd09.text: The ceramic artifacts found date to the Monte Claro phase and correspond to those from the nearby nuraghe Trobas. This site is located on a rise flanking the prehistoric route to Villanovaforru and has an atypical plan with a large subterranean chamber and four adjacent rooms.

8e01f05f032248d9.text: The collapses and dense vegetation prevent a clear outline of the structure, which nevertheless appears to be elliptical and of mixed type: a corridor nuraghe, probably adjacent to a tower built at a later date, to which may have corresponded an additional circular tholos structure.

8e738b76d5b88de5.text:
The complex consists of an extensive settlement defended by a wall (length 120 m; maximum height 5.00 m): the north-eastern end is better preserved, where a tower is incorporated. In the central sector, probably protecting the entrance to the acropolis.

Halfway up the slope are the remains of a second fortification, built of large squared blocks. The village extends over the summit of the plateau and has numerous huts; the complex is datable to 1400–1000 BC.

8e74eb40453f5d72.text: The nuraghe Santu Antine, also called Sa domo de su Re ("The King's House" in Italian), is one of the most majestic nuraghi in the whole of Sardinia and also one of the most important of those still standing. The entire complex is a major example of prehistoric Mediterranean architecture, and its original height is thought to have reached between 22 and 24 metres, the tallest for that period after the Egyptian pyramids and the central tower of the Nuragic palace of Arrubiu, which measured between 25 and 30 metres.

8e789743acc61c92.text: Complex nuraghe of quadrilobate type, the central tower is surrounded by bastions with four towers enclosing a courtyard. Around it, traces of a settlement and a wall remain.

8e7a61f892f2d6df.text: The Nuragic village of Perdu Isu (one nuraghe and traces of about 11 huts) and the cistern storage known as "Su scusorgiu" are located at an altitude clearly above 1,000 m a.s.l. The village is situated on the crest of one of the ridges, with visual contact to the well-known site of Serbissi and to the valley where the complex of "Is Tostoinus" is located.

8e8e19bab6ae95b3.text: Complex consisting of 9 domus. Probable location.

8ea0f582168973b8.text: The structure of the nuraghe is clearly complex; the compact mass of the monument is immediately apparent, dominated by the central tower. To the north-west of the nuraghe, about ten metres away inside the enclosure, stands a large stone which, because of its shape, is thought to be a stele; its presence gives the site its name, and also the name of the Nuraghe Istelai, or "place of the steles". All around, traces of the ancient human settlement are evident, ranging from the pre-Nuragic period back to the Neolithic.

8ea4155b10d13fa7.text: Generally known as Su Corrazzu dessu Estiu, it is so large that its circuit measures no more than a hundred ordinary paces, and it is built of enormous stones with the wall about 30 palms high on one side and half that on the other. Inside and around there is a great mass of ruins. The simple folk who live there believe an evil angel dwells within, so many fear to approach it, and only the most courageous dare go there in September to search for some marvellous flower of prodigious virtue that benefits whoever picks it. But all who have gone have laboured in vain, because the spirit of the place hides it. This place and this spirit are the subject of wondrous tales among the people of Fluminimaggiore, and anyone who tries to dissuade them speaks in vain.

8eca328bde420779.text: The nuraghe is named after the light colour of the lithic material used in its construction.

8eca6f87337bc156.text: The Diana Nuraghe, of complex type, consists of a tholos and two smaller towers connected by a curtain wall, forming a general triangular shape. At the centre there is an open courtyard in a quadrangular form, providing access to the various rooms.

8ed62323df7f05e0.text:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Buddusò (OT).

It includes at least 10 hypogea.

8ef2a9e9dcffab73.text: In a state of ruin, only a few medium-sized stones from the basal circle remain, within which the entrance facing south-east is visible. Due to the absence of the main nuraghe structures, the site is likely classified as a burial tomb.

8eff65e9a28f886d.text: Nuraghe with a central tower and an additional tower facing it. The nuraghe is located near the cemetery where the large statues of Monte Prama have been found.

8f123f5d4bd877c2.text: The probable Nuragic village occupies a large area on the eastern slope of the channel called S'ega Langonis. Despite the dense vegetation, more than 30 circular and rectangular huts can be counted. All have collapsed or imploded, partly because of illicit digging; even so, several courses of the perimeter walls survive on some of them. All the structures were built of small- and medium-sized polyhedral boulders, laid dry in more or less regular courses.

8f297746da765c2b.text: Nuraghe in poor state of conservation.

8f3399b222075658.text: The nuraghe is located in a dominant position above the wide valley of Modolo, in the region of Planargia, in north-eastern Sardinia. The structure, of particular interest and grandeur, is of the corridor type. It has an irregular elliptical plan, crossed longitudinally by a central corridor passage with opposite entrances.

8f4533db60aaeca1.text: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghes. The building stands on a modest elevation in a dominant position over the surrounding plain. Three to four courses of the external curtain wall, constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks, are visible, while the internal chamber is destroyed and not observable. The maximum remaining height is about 2 m.

8f5296aa02bb0459.text: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghes in the Cuga valley. Currently almost invisible and impenetrable due to the thick vegetation.

8f5333befdd60973.text: The slabs of the burial chamber and a small portion of the outer wall face on the east side are visible. The chamber has been partially dug out by looters, who also excavated in the mass of fill making up the tomb mound, between the left wall of the burial chamber and the course of stones of the outer wall face, wrongly believing that the two walls enclosed a second burial chamber adjoining the first.

8f6a608f41bfbc8b.text: It is a small, still intact dolmen.

8f72432eac5bb9ab.text: The nuraghe, an archaic corridor type, built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt, has a quadrangular–elliptical plan. It shows two communicating entrances, on the north and south sides respectively. The entrances are lintelled and vaguely trapezoidal. The internal corridor is visible and in excellent condition, with the usual roofing of slabs laid flat.

8f7e1a42f3276baf.text: Complex nuraghe with a unique plan. Known in the IGM incorrectly as "Giaga 'e Puliga" (which is the name of a nearby nuraghe).

8f8d74d0e7dad6c6.text: Domus de janas reported via the Nurnet page by an anonymous contributor. From the photos it appears to be a two-cell tomb, used by the landowner for storing livestock.

8f8e009bda3ff2c1.text: It consists of four domus de janas.

8fa275bd68008dfc.text: The nuraghe is located in the middle of a field cultivated with grain, with very poor visibility. The nuraghe's structure is visible in the field, but not the extent of the village area.

8fcec670daeff6e9.text: Domus de janas on the junction of SS125

8fe8ecdf9272df21.text: Impressive nuragic site. Various hypotheses and recent analyses suggest the remains of a quadrilobate (or pentalobate) complex nuraghe. Currently open to the public, the northern tower is accessible. A central well leads to internal chambers and extends through narrow, precarious tunnels, suggesting a complex and intricately structured layout.

8feecb0754c99fc0.text: It consists of at least 19 tombs, including one barely outlined.

8ff526154df5fcef.text: The monument, made of trachyte, has a rectangular plan (12 m x 7 m) and includes an 'elbow'-shaped corridor inside. It shows significant collapse along both the western wall and the southern side.

9014b538e4d75611.text: The chamber, monochambered, with a sub-elliptical plan and entrance offset to the left relative to the central axis of the chamber, features a flat floor and a curved vault, almost like a oven. It shows two phases of construction: in the original layout, the chamber and the rectangular door were excavated, marked by a groove; in a later phase, a small dolmenic corridor was added.

9016bebfa285818c.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of large dimensions, is barely legible in plan as it is almost entirely buried. Parts of the orthostatic structure visible include the external wall face and the exedra, together with fragments of the large arched stele scattered over the monument.

903f87564829e2ec.text: A prehistoric burial of the Nuragic period. Unfortunately, the tomb has been partially demolished by herders to build a sheepfold.

90433b495cfeccb9.text: The central tower is visible for 4 courses in cyclopean blocks. It is probable that at least 4 courses lie beneath the surface. To the east and north, the remains of two secondary towers are visible, only partially discernible. Superficially, some wall connections can be seen.

90462dcd1344d596.text:
The Punta Unossi complex is one of the most important in the Florinas area.

It consists of an extensive settlement within which a large circular building stands out (external diameter 11 m, internal diameter 7.60 m) displaying typical features of the so-called "meeting huts": a circular bench against the walls and a central circular base on which a tower baetyl originally stood.

905f903cfdb0c8de.text: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, known as the Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, among which the domus I, the most important, is located about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the hypogea mentioned are more properly described as cave burials.

90675713a5eeb406.text: Village attached to the nuraghe Lu Padru

90b795e9b0d619c0.text: Two giants' tombs stood in this area, about 100 m apart. The second is the one that survives in a more legible state, although for most of its extent it is covered by vegetation and its walls are blocked by collapse. The tomb whose structure is harder to make out very probably has a rectangular chamber built of large boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed.

90e7d468da4a7a3e.text: Nuraghe completely stripped and immersed in vegetation, never studied

910cc10955f6a78a.text: The village is located on the slope of Capo Su Moru, northwest of Torre Canai. The area is scattered with trachytic stones of various sizes, and in some patches, where the Mediterranean scrub is less dense, fragments of rectangular and circular walls can be seen, indicating the probable presence of a village, if not a temple.

912e0703133e795e.text: Multicellular domus with a dromos probably collapsed. Inside the main chamber there is a pillar with carved capitals.

9151136b1ec96d72.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Located on a rocky spur dominating the entire western slope of Montiferru down to the sea, it is almost completely hidden by forest vegetation. It is constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks and stands about 2.60 m high. The internal chamber has collapsed, and the remaining portion is filled with debris from the collapse itself.

915bfb3f8ccb410b.text:
Domu de Orgia di Esterzili is the largest known Nuragic "megaron" temple to date.

The building is enclosed within an elliptical enclosure (48.50 m x 28 m; wall thickness of 1.50 m), reduced to only the base course, with entrance to the north.

These and other details:

915d0c91ee2e0f3c.text: Bronze Age materials (mainly fragments of pottery and shallow bowls), almost entirely belonging to the S. Cosimo cultural phase and recovered from the surface, mostly come from Crastu Mountains, Atziaddei Mountains, Ibera Mountains, Porceddu Mountains, and Acutzu Mountains. Materials from the Monti Mannu phase are found only in the Serrentese locality, which gives the phase its name; further specific studies are needed to fully understand this assemblage.

9177b7d35323f85e.text: Of the monument, in isodomic masonry in courses, the funerary chamber, a corridor defined by some dentilled ashlars well connected, the apse and part of the exedra remain. A dentilled ashlar, though probably damaged, might constitute the so-called "dentilled stele".

917bec6392c243bf.text: Should be brought to the attention of a specialist. They appear scattered in location, and if any had been used, it would not be the one currently in place. It is clear that their function was related to pastoral needs.

9183aaf2d0c28f7b.text: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age (14th century BC). In very poor condition of conservation, located very close to the homonymous nuraghe, better known as N.ghe Gorroppu.

91861ba699349247.text: Unfortunately, the nuraghe is covered by vegetation. It is believed to have a well-preserved tholos.

91cbfd040ec11032.text: The original nuraghe was likely quite tall. Currently, the tholos has collapsed inward. Note the presence of two giants' tombs located close to the nuraghe.

91dd3e2ff3286bf2.text: On an isolated hilltop located about 40 metres south-southwest of the Su Sonadori nuraghe, the remains of a complex nuraghe were observed; currently it is concealed by heaps of rubble stones.

91e8215f49e1c0c3.text: Sacred well nuragica, located a short distance from the complex nuraghe of Ardasai.

91ebd5489bf92219.text: Dug into a calcareous rock outcrop stained pink by iron veins. Single-chamber tomb.

91ec6d17ae29125c.text: Located on a trachytic plateau at 152 m a.s.l., from which a vast expanse of territory can be seen, Monte Baranta is a pre-Nuragic settlement characterised and protected by a enclosure-tower, a long and powerful wall enclosing a group of rectangular huts, separated from a sacred area by menhirs and a megalithic circle.

9231b56b5be94a7e.text:
At the base of the hill, a short distance away, there is a lake basin, an important source of water for the nearby village.

The shores show clear signs of human intervention through the deliberate arrangement of stones and blocks that form a border around the so-called "nuragic lagoon".

928bc523cf95f081.text: The nuraghe structures, of the simple tholos type, are buried and covered by dense vegetation. Partially emerging at the top of the small ridge formed by the structures and the soil covering them are some courses composed of local basalt blocks.

92963658cd635194.text: Complex nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation, of difficult definition

92992ea3ffc4f7b3.text: The only evidence of this megalithic burial is the presence of numerous shaped ashlars of various forms incorporated into a dry-stone wall for a length of about 200 metres. All these monoliths are remarkable for being perfectly worked and shaped, indicating that the destroyed tomb was of isodomic type. Among these stones, most of which have lifting recesses, a monolithic arch is of particular interest (arch span 1.72 m – rise 0.80 m – height 0.68 m).

92b7e1311fafbdba.text:
It is a domus in basalt. It consists of a vestibule and an adjacent chamber.

On the right wall of the vestibule, a small niche has been carved. The floor features a "fireplace" of notable craftsmanship.

Located in a low basaltic coastal area shaded by some holm oaks. Easily accessible just a few dozen metres from the road.

92b8f542c02f1e10.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which is vaultless, has on its left a wide staircase about 1 metre in width. Nearby is a nuraghe known as Lobaos II, visible in the photo.

92d13efddfc09cce.text: It is in a state of complete abandonment. The structure, built with limestone and shale, shows part of the tholos wall face, as well as some additional features suggesting a complex monument. Around the structure, there is a noticeable dispersion of materials emerging at the surface, almost certainly related to the presence of a settlement attached to the nuraghe.

92da30c0c5539ad0.text: The nuraghe stands on a small hill beside the church of the same name (17th century). It is in fair condition, rising to about 4 metres, with a south-facing entrance that is partly blocked. Inside, two pointed-arch niches can be seen. Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks.

9313192255aa9230.text: Single-tower, of which only a small portion remains.

932fc80fe057dbbf.text: Single-tower nuraghe used as a quarry for the construction of walls and "pinnettas". Today, only a partial row of stones is visible.

935b8f161d91e7bd.text:
The Nuraghe of Nuraxeddu stands on a promontory currently isolated at the centre of a plain used for grazing sheep herds.

The masonry works are made of roughly shaped blocks with parallelipipedal form arranged in fairly regular courses.

937371254f2b6caf.text: It is a complex nuraghe, partially eroded, located at the centre (mesu) of a wide valley bordering the Alto Oristanese plateau.

937387a72cd20ab9.text: It is a monument likely of Nuragic origin, featuring the remains of a cistern, possibly originally vaulted in tholos form, and an adjacent rectangular elongated building constructed with sack masonry.

937a7e105a9b6c1f.text:
Complex nuraghe difficult to read in its planimetric layout due to dense vegetation and the prominent collapse, composed of large blocks of andesite.

Traces of a settlement of nuragic huts are visible, especially to the south-east, and of a Neolithic open settlement in the area between the nuraghe and the Neolithic underground necropolis of Serra Maverru.

937c79d04faa2ddc.text: On the main summit of the rocky ridge, beneath the remains of a modern rectangular structure, the ruins of a probable nuraghe are visible, almost unrecognizable.

93842d727701f562.text: Only faint traces of the nuraghe remain.

938b7a79c4dc5f2d.text: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at Su Padru. Partially destroyed

938d2770ae9116b9.text: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.

939f7f03cfa84d1e.text: The cave contains internal wall remnants and artefacts; it is not ruled out that it was used as a smelting site.

93a123e18f17d748.text: Structures that are hard to read because of the dense vegetation, probably belonging to an archaic corridor nuraghe. A few blocks of the upper part can just be made out among the vegetation. The plan appears vaguely elliptical, with a straight section facing south, in which a doorway with a monolithic lintel opens onto a flat-roofed corridor about 4 m deep. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. A

93eb3a9b9186a786.text:
About twenty metres north-west of the large tomb described in record no. 50 lie the remains of a second megalithic burial that has been largely destroyed by a dry-stone wall cutting across it transversely.

Only a short stretch of the rectangular body can be measured (4.30 m long – 3.20 m wide); the construction technique uses orthostats, while several large overturned slabs inside show that the roof was flat-laid.

94008f683adf8508.text: It should have been a perfect three-lobed structure.

940dc700349a00d4.text: It is one of two hypogea in the Campu Marinu area. In the past, a dolmen (presumably destroyed) also existed at the site.

941d8f0905efc825.text:
The Barrancu Mannu giants' tomb, also known as "Sa Tuerredda", displays the classic ground plan of giants' tombs: an apsidal tomb body, a covered corridor, and an arched exedra.

The outer wall face consists of large, roughly dressed blocks of yellow-pink granite topped by irregular courses of variously polyhedral stones of large size.

Of the apsidal circuit, originally finished with ordered rows of tailed ashlars, two or three courses survive.

942732c849dc9b1c.text: It consists of only a few remains.

945856e0777d3643.text: The San Pietro nuraghe is located on the summit of a hill in the immediate vicinity of the village of Ussaramanna and is named after a church of the same name, now disappeared. It is a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a quadrangular bastion with towers facing the four cardinal points.

946316e3e9105740.text: The archaeological site, dating to about 3500 BC, lies near the provincial road and consists of three tombs. The first, isolated, was cut into a rock outcrop that rises behind a small building; the other two, close together, are instead situated further south in a granite monolith that runs alongside the road. All three domus de janas are of simple type without an antechamber and have a rebate in the entrance doorway.

947db635af230088.text: The nuraghe, datable to the Middle Bronze Age (15th–14th century BC), has a single-tower structure and a truncated-conical shape with a diameter of twelve metres and a surviving height of ten metres. It is built of well-worked limestone-schist blocks laid to form the tholos, which has lost its top courses. The entrance leads into a corridor four metres long, equal to the wall thickness, which opens into the main chamber, circular and over five metres in diameter.

949463f2cde0ca6c.text: The Perda Lada nuraghe is located on a hillside used for grazing and farming, near the Crastutorro nuraghe. What remains of the monument are large granite blocks, which unfortunately do not help in identifying the type of monument or its various features, possibly also due to the work of erosion caused by the elements.

94e2de9e0bb7fccf.text:
It appears as a large heap of rubble covered by dense shrub vegetation that in no way allows the ground plan of the monument to be read.

The surrounding ground is strewn, over a wide area, with the remains of the Nuragic settlement, which was also reused in Roman times, as shown by the potsherds scattered on the ground and several cippi.

The nuraghe was defended by an outer wall that still survives for about sixty metres in length and to a height of about 1/1.50 m.

950adef3a4e753b4.text: The Nuragic village lies at 1200 metres above sea level and is one of the highest in Sardinia. Part of the village is fenced, but the gate is open. The three-lobed nuraghe is surrounded by springs and mountains and set in an unspoilt landscape. Inside the nuraghe a staircase leads to the upper floor and the central tower, whose tholos is intact. The remains of the circular huts that made up the village and the nuraghe are of granite.

952ce4bfe4fbbe2a.text: The basal courses of the single-tower nuraghe are visible among the bushes.

952e397bd74fd3ab.text:
This nuraghe lies on the edge of the Teulada military training area.

The geoportal shows that walls still survive around the nuraghe of Monte Idu, built for who knows what reason. The place is magical, both for the presence of the monuments and for the breathtaking scenery it offers the visitor. Its landscape value is exceptional.

The nuraghe appears to be a single-tower nuraghe

953d90fcfaaa5476.text: Hundreds and hundreds of ruins, huts, and towers, joined together by narrow paths, transport us back millennia, showing how imposing and significant this site was during the Nuragic period. Two things stand out in particular. The first is a kind of amphitheatre, a majestic construction in the form of a horse's iron; the second is the well.

95461be8e9c55172.text: Located about a hundred metres south of the Provincial Road Borore-Sedilo, the enclosure of Pedru Feghe has a vaguely circular shape, with a remaining height of 2.45 m to the north-west and 2.05 m to the south-east, respectively, with 4 and 3 courses; the wall thickness varies from 1.45 m to 0.46 m. The masonry is composed of polyhedral blocks of medium and large size arranged in fairly regular horizontal courses.

9554ca352a2eedab.text: Nuraghe no longer visible; a house was built on the site in the early 20th century, now in ruin, using basalt blocks from the original nuraghe.

9555966dbc5b54b6.text: Of the aforementioned tomb, only a few foundation stones remain, together with a nearby stele, suggesting that there may have been a giants' tomb.

9570634998d88661.text: STESSEI, indeed, almost adjacent to the nuraghe on the eastern side, the remains of a Nuragic village are clearly visible, extending over an area of at least ten thousand square metres, composed of numerous huts partially hidden among stone heaps. Among the huts there are at least three wells (or cisterns).

957d58e2eba5cc86.text: On the Monte Narcao plateau, the remains of some prehistoric huts, built with large stones, still stand. Around the area, fragments of obsidian are frequently found.

958e9151f93ddc17.text: What remains of the probable nuraghe rests on a granite outcrop, of which some stretches were very likely incorporated into the wall face. At present only half a circuit of roughly dressed, medium- and large-sized granite blocks survives in plan. At the base of the outcrop, at a slightly lower level, two short wall stretches survive, whose function cannot be determined because of the monument's state of preservation.

95932cc7fa2380cf.text: The building consists of a central tower and a quadrilobate bastion with an internal courtyard. The external face of the main tower, of which only one course attributable to the first-floor chamber is visible, is constructed in isodomic masonry with sandstone blocks. Inside, at S, the projection of the staircase landing is identifiable.

95bc847b5b4b3dd1.text: Short antechamber (depth 0.45 – width 0.77) leading to the door (height 0.48 – thickness 0.18 – width 0.40). The chamber measures: depth 0.98 – width 1.16/0.90 – height 0.44/0.80.

95e293449ded00c4.text: A few but clear remains of a giants' tomb. The mound still partially in situ, together with two pillars embedded in a dry-stone wall. The surrounding area is rich in Nuragic remains. mu

96185f56c6428c27.text: Giants' tomb, of which only a very small portion remains, almost completely destroyed.

96320b36e2c78eec.text: Two giants' tombs located near the homonymous nuraghe and the nuragic village. A dolmen is attested nearby.

9649095589d69c6c.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, almost destroyed, only the funerary corridor remains, composed of two parallel alignments of ashlar stones projecting from the ground. Other ashlar stones are visible in the immediate surroundings.

The construction technique of the tomb was isodomic, made with finely shaped ashlar stones.

966466032dce8576.text: They are located on the left bank of the river Oloitti. They extend in an L-shape, consisting of three chambers with antechambers. The photo showing the throne "sa trona de su Re" is nearby and intriguing for its shape, which ergonomically fits the posterior of a commander.

96adc973d72f6645.text: It is a simple nuraghe with a typical troncoconical shape, probably a single-tower with a tholos. It is composed of large granitic blocks. At its highest point about seven courses can be counted, but it is clear that there are others below the level of the floor.

96c902fd7bbc0f4f.text: Nuraghe on the SSW slope of Monte Arbus, on the hillside facing the S'Acqua sa Canna area. Complex nuraghe with a three-lobed bastion and an internal courtyard. The towers of which traces remain are positioned to the N, SSE and SSW. Because of the collapses and the vegetation it is difficult to make out the outline of the walls clearly. By contrast the outline of the courtyard is well defined; at first glance it appears pentagonal; in some stretches up to three rows of boulders of various shapes and sizes survive.

96e5587ef33337c7.text: Remains of a single-tower nuraghe and village.

971268343aa5b85e.text: The complex, datable between the Late Neolithic (Ozieri culture, 3200–2800 BC) and the Chalcolithic, stands on a broad outcrop of tuff and consists of 26 domus de janas. The domus de janas are arranged on the ridge at different levels and are multi-chambered, i.e. composed of several rooms; most have a dromos entrance (a corridor cut into the rock) while only a few have direct access.

971c203326a000b7.text: The Murartu or Sa Menta nuraghe is located in the territory of Silanus, about 2.2 km from the village. It is almost completely hidden by vegetation. As a complex nuraghe, a portion of the central tower rises about 2 metres in height.

9728cc5bed969357.text: The Cae Nuraghe is a complex type, featuring a central mastio and at least two towers connected by a bastion, with probable evidence of two additional towers on the south-eastern side, and references to a subterranean gallery. A small village is also present, along with signs of area reuse during the Roman period.

973427de639f24b2.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches.

The tower cannot be fully defined in its outer perimeter because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation, but a circular ground plan about 10 metres in diameter at the base is to be assumed. The surviving height is 6.50 m on the south-east side and 4.80 m on the north-west side. The masonry consists of medium and large basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

9776820ce0919735.text: Structures belonging to a giants' tomb built of local basalt. The funerary structure stands on a small rise overlooking a small river valley, between the nuraghi Campu Scudu and Piricu (Santu Lussurgiu). Some blocks of the funerary corridor and part of the outer wall face remain visible. The tomb is oriented east–west and survives for a total length of about 8 m. In the front part a few displaced blocks can be seen that originally must have formed part of the exedra.

97d6c1ae4babbb06.text: It lies near the country church of San Pietro, about one kilometre from the village. Its name, S'Acqua 'e is dolus, means "the water of sorrows", from an old folk belief that the water in this small cave has miraculous powers; a legend also tells that during one of his journeys San Pietro took shelter in this artificial grotto and prayed there for so long that the imprint of his knees was left forever in the rock.

97ddf9d39b4f4ae5.text: Nuraghe built into a stone masonry and tholos structure between emergent rocky masses.

97fb05255399cd25.text: A complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The structures are overgrown with vegetation, but a central tower and an added tower with a courtyard can be made out, of the so-called tancato type. The added tower appears to be smaller than the central tower. From the top of the latter the interior of the chamber can be seen, still well preserved except for the collapsed upper part.

9807c62f2b2f7f00.text: Six hypogea of the domus de janas type. The immediate proximity of a tuff quarry, on the edges of which a few traces of other hypogea can be seen, suggests that the site originally extended further than it does today. Of the six domus present, one is almost completely destroyed, three were converted into farm buildings in historical times after substantial alterations to their plans, and only the last two (Tombs V and VI) have preserved their original structure.

984110b7f75960f3.text: In total ruin, only a few large subsquared stones remain. The older inhabitants of the area recall its existence, though only a few basal circles are known. When the Sassari Tempio fast-moving road was constructed, excavation work affected more than one site, in total disregarding their immense historical value, in order to serve as a foundation for the road network.

984d0b545b996e5d.text: Complex nuraghe with the tholos intact. Part of the external wall face has collapsed.

9857cbf3930176e1.text: Area where ancient maps indicated the location of the nuraghe Evrassu, in the countryside of the commune of Pozzomaggiore (SS); what remains of the nuraghe Frassu (in the countryside of Pozzomaggiore)

98728b59823cac15.text: From the aerial photograph it appears to be one of those nuraghes belonging to the category of "uncompleted" ones.

98971556fcd91c65.text: From the second giants' tomb, moving 50 m westward, one finds an area containing polyhedral stones of various sizes, only roughly shaped, suggesting the presence of a cultic zone.

98a0a109dcffcf2d.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period, of dolmenic type. Of the tomb, now completely destroyed, only part of the exedra and the apse remain legible, while some fragments of the arched stele are present both on the front and in the surrounding area.

98a5d6480ff422b3.text: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a hilltop, from which the view extends over the surrounding landscape and especially over the valleys below and the Rio Mannu river course. It is situated within a cultivated area dedicated to olive groves.

9944ae4e3107961b.text: It is a simple nuraghe, evidenced by only a few stones scattered here and there inside and outside a centuries-old lentisco thicket. The stones are of medium size, and some appear slightly rough-hewn. Only a few circles remain, which do not provide sufficient clarity for proper assessment.

9947264f248248f9.text:
The necropolis of Sos Laccheddos is an archaeological site in the territory of Sassari, in north-western Sardinia. It is divided into two groups of tombs lying a short distance from each other, located between state road 127 bis and the new provincial road to Anglona a few kilometres east of the town, in the direction of Osilo.

To the 32 tombs recorded in the aforementioned work, another 19 were added following more recent investigations.

995a951a0cd8dff0.text: Single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition. Corbelled entrance corridor with a left-hand intramural staircase.

995afcf67463d1ff.text: Four-lobed nuraghe, largely covered by vegetation. The central tower is still accessible from above. It shows to be a much larger complex than it appears at first glance.

9960cc61577055d6.text: Complex nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation. Its outline is difficult to define. It could be four-lobed.

996a77d73e3e2a70.text: The Su Mamuccone nuraghe is today completely ruined, standing on a calcare monolith near the homonymous sheepfold, located in a position optimal for having an elevated view of the entire area.

9973278cbb9d9f92.text: Su Putzu Nuragic village, composed of about one hundred huts surrounding a well temple, exactly Su Putzu. The temple features a long ramped vestibule; there is no staircase leading to the spring source.

99c1e22e591c37bb.text: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia but under deletion. To be verified.

99d6d4e14f3f5c60.text: Nuraghe and structure of uncertain definition

99dc44e5b0a78132.text:
The monument, located in the immediate northern outskirts of Birori, has a circular plan (diameter 12 x 12.30 m) with an average residual height of just 2.75 m and two courses; the stones, polygonal and roughly hewn, are arranged in horizontal courses.

Due to its extremely poor state of conservation, the internal structure of the monument cannot be identified.

99e792ae088a8d86.text: The I.G.M. lists it as a nuraghe, yet strong and well-founded features raise doubts about classifying it as such. It stands at the border between the territories of Chiaramonti and Ardara, in the area known as Pittiri, at an elevation of 440 m a.s.l., and at the boundary with the territories of Truncu Nieddu and Serra di Monte Pittu. The structure is atypical and difficult to classify: it is not a nuraghe, but difficult to categorize as a hut.

9a2aa32bfa878587.text: A place of rare beauty. The site, particularly evocative, includes a complex nuraghe with an attached village, a cave with two entrances, two giants' tombs, and two single-tower nuraghes.

9a377e93d37c99d1.text: Now only large stones have remained, moved and reused in the nearby retaining walls.

9a5f2be3240ab10f.text: Nuraghe of undefined structure. Unfortunately, only faint traces remain of the nuraghe, as it was completely demolished to make way for a RAI antenna. At the base of the antenna, several stones are piled haphazardly. At the edge of a recess, adjacent to what may have been the base of the nuraghe, remains the probable footprint of a hut.

9a6830d5b17e778e.text: Nuraghe with extensive collapse on the eastern side, difficult to read in plan. Adjacent huts belonging to a probable village.

9a88f3364762788d.text:
The monument lies less than 900 metres south of the Nuraghe Suerzu.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular, slightly flattened plan, with a surviving height of 2.15 m over four or five courses of medium and large stones, only roughly dressed and laid in irregular courses.

Because of its very poor state of preservation, the collapse and the shrub vegetation, it is not possible to determine the position of the entrance.

9a951394f9210566.text: Complex nuraghe, severely collapsed and never studied. Completely enveloped by vegetation, it is difficult to interpret. It shows a possible internal staircase and remnants of external walling of secondary rooms.

9aa1569e53343429.text: Nuraghe in very poor condition and completely covered by undergrowth.

9ab0bbbdf395f200.text:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building stands on the summit of a bend in the Rio Cispiri and rests on a solid rocky base partly incorporated into the structures, as can be seen on the north-facing side.

The nuraghe is well preserved on the north and north-east sides, with an external wall face of large polygonal basalt blocks reaching a maximum surviving height of about 12 m, while the south and west sides have collapsed.

9abc03a3ee40f8c4.text: (16th–13th century BC), it is built of trachyte. It has a corridor with a spiral staircase on the left and a guard niche on the right, and a vaulted chamber, perfectly preserved, with three niches arranged in a cross. The entrance jambs of the nuraghe are 1.52 m and 1.24 m high respectively. The tower reaches a maximum height of 8 m and consists of seventeen courses of stone. The entrance faces east; its perfectly worked lintel is 1.60 m long, 0.70 m high and 0.80 m wide.

9acb5d49ca0a45b3.text: The monument is a single-tower, single-chamber nuraghe. Its entrance and the whole of its base are badly damaged, although clear traces of a staircase and a guard niche remain. The north-western wall face is the best preserved, standing about six metres high with eight courses of roughly dressed blocks. Along the corridor, itself practically destroyed, the traces of two facing niches can be seen.

9ae30688b5fe4be4.text: The nuraghe stands on the summit of an isolated, modest elevation. The area is covered by vegetation that is almost impenetrable. Some alignments of granitic blocks are visible.

9ae454109cd71a92.text: Damaged nuraghe of which only a buried chamber built in masonry can be observed.

9ae83b043a68868e.text: It is slightly elliptical, with a diameter varying from 20 to 30 m. Some stones no longer stand in line along the perimeter but lie fallen inside or outside the circle; however, most of them are still well aligned with each other and some are still perfectly upright. It is astonishing that, despite thousands of years having passed, the state of preservation is still relatively good.

9b25e4f96699414c.text: These are the remains of a sanctuary built in megalithic technique, set in the centre of the saddle about 100 metres from the other site to the east; at present the dense vegetation allows only four or five menhirs lying on the ground a few metres apart to be visited. I remember from a visit I made to this site many years ago that the menhirs were far more numerous, but now the thick vegetation makes it impossible to tell whether any others survive.

9b33042eb3f6000c.text: Fortification or nuraghe also called Staderis or Giolza. It lies in the Montiferru, near the summit of a high spur of bare, rugged rock facing Monte Urtigu, where the remains of an imposing megalithic wall survive with seven courses of roughly dressed basalt boulders. The straight line of the ruin suggests an original quadrangular defensive structure around the level top of the rock, rather than the wall face of a hilltop nuraghe.

9b505a166440da3a.text: Inside there is a pillar on which a bull's-head protome is carved in high relief.

9b506c319214dcf3.text: Only traces of the structure remain, as it has been completely dismantled.

9b5e1cd47b9576f4.text: Ruined nuraghe. The central tower is clearly visible for 10 courses. A possible trace of an outer wall preceding the north tholos is present. The south-east turret has completely collapsed. The nuraghe appears to have imploded on itself in non-recent times. A short distance away a structure can be identified that suggests it may be a dolmen.

9b625cc5768c4579.text: In Serrenti, nuragic villages are often located near a nuraghe, as in the case of the site of Bruncu Pubusa; in other cases (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis, and Sa Serra) they are located without any nearby nuraghe.

9b6d926e25cfdebb.text: This complex nuraghe consisted of a central tower and three towers joined by a bastion, today only poorly preserved. The central tower, however, is in perfect condition and has a remaining height of 14 m, only slightly less than its original height. It is built on two levels, both intact, and each with a tholos roof.

9b793c1c6d2cc40a.text: It is a corridor proto-nuraghe built of basalt.

9bb23c1d423d4667.text: The church was built on the remains of a nuraghe called Nuraxi Mannu, and Nuragic remains are found throughout the village. The decision to build the church stemmed from a desire to give sacred continuity to a particular place. The church is a small building with a rectangular plan and a single nave. In the white façade, a round-arched doorway with a frame opens, surmounted by a small circular oculus.

9bd3c30675e59d05.text: Nuraghe along the road. Partly collapsed. The tholos is open and essentially visible in section, showing its constructional features.

9c0791fab6b72aa3.text:
150 m from the second group of domus de janas, at the foot of Monte Corru Tundu, stands a colossal monolith of trachyte tuff with a truncated top (surviving height 5.75 m). The menhir, one of the largest in Sardinia, is strongly tapered, with one face flattened and the other rounded; on the latter three circular cup-marks appear to be visible.

The monolith and the necropolis served the settlement of Monte Padrillonis. (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC).

9c14bc9ade3fb27b.text: The Norampè nuraghe is literally almost entirely vanished, only a few stones integrated into the rock remain, testifying to its excellent and prominent location.

9c2ba2e623a1bbb4.text: Between Tratalias and S. Giovanni Suergiu, near Is Loccis. In very poor condition.

9c2fab168b6f39f7.text: The remains of the nuraghe are located inside the Orguglioso Castle.

9c31f6f263cb272e.text: The nuraghe is located on the hill of Cala Francese, in the area “Serra is tres portus”. The nuraghe may originally have been of a complex type, built using limestone blocks. The original tower's outline is preserved only in fragments, its interior being covered by collapse and vegetation.

9c5539f745cb7e73.text: Single-tower nuraghe built of large blocks, situated on top of the hill. On the hill slopes there are tall wall structures of the same period. The site was used from the Bronze Age to the Roman period.

9c5dd88b9ad951aa.text: Built on a slight basaltic outcrop less than 200 metres south of Riu Corte, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, now largely demolished along its outer perimeter. Due to the collapse, the details of the corridor and chamber are no longer discernible.

9c83328b5ed8a4da.text: The construction was carried out in two phases. In the first phase, dating to the Bonnanaro culture period, a covered allée tomb—a type of elongated dolmen—was built; subsequently, around 1600 BC, it was transformed into a giants' tomb with an exedra and stele, some traces of which you can admire.

9c91609f5e0be651.text: Well constructed with stones of different sizes; the external structure is completely ruined, probably belonging to a temple of a spring-water well.

9ca85495547a9b07.text: Situated within a picturesque forest of monumental olive trees, the nuraghe is a complex, quadrilobed, corridor-type structure with a ramped access path located at the upper part and a well from which one descends into a subterranean chamber. The only accessible lateral tower is the one situated to the north and is visible from the upper part of the central tower.

9cabd3f3436a4bba.text:
This domus came to light during the flood of 18-11-2013.  

Until then, it had been covered by vegetation and was likely known to the local herders. Above it lies a road.

9cd8f95aed53c105.text:
The giants' tomb is covered by dense scrub, and only one covering slab leaning to the north can be seen outside.

Rock shelter opening in a huge granite boulder, a spacious cavity with a wide main entrance flanked by two orthostatic slabs and already partly closed. The main interest lies in the geometric figures on the exposed rock that forms the shelter floor, and schematic anthropomorphic figures on the back wall.

9ce54b7a9816c9ad.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, like the other tombs in the area, is in very poor conservation conditions. It is possible to identify the corridor formed by two parallel rows of stones and to detect, in some sections, the external profile. Some regular ashlar stones, inserted into the dry-stone walls surrounding it, may belong to the tomb.

9d092b238d67b5e1.text: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, partially hidden by vegetation and collapse debris, only the outer perimeter, the funerary corridor, and part of the exedra remain visible.

9d0ec0666288c646.text: Complex nuraghe forming part of the nuraghes of the Cuga valley. The associated village and its external structures have been extensively modified. It allows access to the interior, where the tholos remains perfectly intact.

9d2b34a98e9be4ab.text: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe, and it is circular in plan.

9d4607b08ddb23c6.text: Probable location. In a pasture area, hidden behind a large thicket of mastic, in poor conservation state, some stone blocks are visible. Adjacent to the wastewater treatment plant it may have suffered damage during recent installation works of the structure.

9d4e70031a153abb.text: Through a wild gully carved by a stream in the porphyritic granite, access is gained to the Nuragic village of Praidas. The remains are in severe disrepair and have significantly collapsed.

9d61a90994db4b00.text: "Monte sa Perda" – it is thought there may have been another nuraghe dominating the entire Gulf of Palmas, probably destroyed during the construction of "su forr'e sa cracina" (limestone furnace) located in the immediate vicinity.

9d7d519b7b353b6d.text: Its position relative to the terrain's topography is truly odd! Or rather, it is clear as the sun, since the fortified wall facing it on the Zennaru hillside clearly indicates its function as a control and surveillance post.

9d96625f0ea60afb.text: From the early photos, the section of the Tolos is visible but partially collapsed. The splendid niche is also evident. It is easily accessible, although it is located on private land. It is situated just a few hundred metres from the Romanesque Cathedral of Sant'Antioco in Bisarcio.

9d9ba7bdf8b76bfd.text: Small circular structure, built using Nuragic technique and classifiable as atypical nuraghe.

9dc6a44e930ff657.text:
The monument appears as an artificial hill at the base of which the material produced by clearing the surrounding fields has been piled up.

Its very ruined state, the fact that it is buried, and the rubble that partly covers it do not allow a correct reading of the building's ground plan; nevertheless, it must have been grand and of complex type, as the very name Tresnuraghes attributed to it also suggests.

9dcbf1992a366b49.text: It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe with a collapsed but easily accessible tholos chamber. The nuraghe displays a variety of constructional and architectural features. Facing north is an entrance that was clumsily walled up in recent times; it lies about 2.00 metres above the present ground level.

9dd4319bac171a78.text: Complex of 5 domus de janas in the Canyon of the Rio Mannu. Carved into Miocene limestone. Some have suffered collapses.

9ddb3e32fd24a92b.text: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition near a small agricultural farm

9dedb873ade9ab03.text: Monte Claro culture underground. The site was used during the Nuragic, Roman, and medieval periods.
