9def887a26b97392.text: Originally built with medium-sized basaltic blocks, it makes use of the rock as a foundation. Currently it is almost illegible due to a conspicuous collapse, retained by vegetation composed of olive trees and Indian figs.

9dfce14b398f1197.text: Nuraghe Alvu di Nulvi: "alvu" = white. A four-lobed nuraghe, very beautiful, although in a fairly degraded state of preservation. Human and institutional neglect, together with the harshness of the elements, contribute to its deterioration. Let us remember that present-day municipal boundaries make no sense when referred to the Nuragic period, and future generations will have one piece fewer with which to reconstruct the historical and cultural period of our forebears.

9e1aa6394e2b7549.text: Also known as "nurarchei" according to A. Tarameli (1915).

9e1efba9f53094b7.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan, the layout of the nuraghe is difficult to read.

9e2b9d2e742e296c.text:
Nuraghe that features an inscription carved on a stone slab, attesting the boundary line between the territory of the Iliensi people and the Balari.

The inscription reads "ILI IVR IN NVRAC SESSAR M C", meaning the rights of the Iliensi of Nurac Sessar. Its significance also lies in being one of the earliest testimonies of the name given to Sardinian towers.

9e3f337d5dd372f8.text: Near the nuraghe there is a Nuragic spring. It is located in the Pedruitta plain. It is immediately evident that it represents an extremely ancient Nuragic feature.

9e3f5320dd1e3661.text: A rectangular niche cut into the sedimentary rock, set against a quadrangular space bounded by four large upright stones with dry-stone walls. In the lowest Bell Beaker levels three cist structures were identified, sealed by limestone slabs and containing human skeletal remains attributable to several individuals. Above these lay further deceased individuals accompanied by grave goods such as objects in ceramic, metal, stone, bone and a gold necklace.

9e4ac7177d26a911.text: A small single-tower nuraghe; around it is a small domus de janas necropolis, in which there are decorations of carved bull's-head protomes.

9e784daf54e7ae26.text: It stands on a basaltic spur accessible only from one side, west of the village of Sagama. It has a polygonal plan with a straight, slightly convex façade to the north-west where the entrance opens. At the centre of the main wall is the main entrance, featuring a rectangular opening and a lintel. Entering, we find a straight corridor; at the right end of the first section, two adjacent niches open.

9e7cd1e25b672454.text: Reduced to complete ruin, only the base circle remains, where we can observe an opening to the north. No structures are sufficient for a precise classification of its typological affiliation; it is presumed to be a corridor nuraghe. An interesting area due to the presence of large stones arranged in a cut pattern, giving the impression of facing a giants' tomb.

9e86ee25dfd3ad6a.text: see sacred well Bau Crabas I

9ebba98be615d7ec.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Guasila, inside a private plot planted with Mediterranean scrub.

9ec3f7b3bc0c5966.text: Two blocks of the exedra are visible, the inner right wall of the chamber. Illyscavated illegally and damaged.

9ecc85edb37ec0f9.text: The “rotunda” of Sa Corona Arrubia in the territory of Genoni, also known locally as “Santa Maria S'Ungroi”, is a unique sacred building of the Nuragic period at Sa Corona Arrubia-Genoni. Of the monument, mentioned by Taramelli who considered it a Nuragic sacred well, the entire base ring survives, consisting of an isodomic basalt wall face with two and in a few places three courses preserved, with a small niche and a few blocks belonging to a bench.

9ecedd7c3aeea508.text: See Giuseppa Tanda's book “L'arte delle domus de janas”, page 97.

9ef4c48e64361d27.text: The tomb is missing its top; it has a rectangular plan and shows no traces of the apse. Its length is about 12 m. Currently, some blocks of the left arm of the exedra, the entrance, and the perimeter wall can be identified.

9f0729673a25d122.text: Around the structure extends a large settlement of circular huts, while at a short distance two giants' tombs are present. There is also evidence of an ancient well, of which today no trace remains.

9f0c5b089b59bfab.text: The "Domus de janas" are hypogean (underground) burials of the pre-Nuragic period, datable to 3500–3000 BC, consisting of one or more chambers and used up to the Nuragic age. On Monte Arista, in the municipality of Cardedu, there is a necropolis composed of ten carefully made tombs in an excellent state of preservation. The tombs are cut into isolated blocks of granite. The hypogea are of two types, single-chambered and double-chambered, and have a longitudinal layout.

9f146dd60d8e8856.text:
It is hard to interpret because it is not clear whether it consisted of a single tower, which in that case would have been of a large diameter, or of several towers on different levels.

All that can be seen are high walls of massive construction, built of roughly squared blocks and spread over a wide area.

It also appears that the wall faces of the monument enclose a space already bounded by rock outcrops that are incorporated into it in several places.

9f1d5729c9463f00.text:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Quartu Sant'Elena (CA).

Of exceptional form, the nuraghe is now almost completely destroyed.

9f1de417e1c03ec6.text: Located in the Bèrchida valley, it shows use and occupation from the Nuragic period, with a significant area of surface fragments dating to the medium to late imperial era. The site was inhabited until the 1950s. Among the habitation remains, the ruins of a small religious building stand out; this structure is documented as early as the 14th century.

9f2c4361ac2bfdd4.text: Proto-nuraghe subsequently restructured into nuraghe. On the summits of the highest hills of Serrenti, overseeing the valleys leading to Trexenta, we find the simple proto-nuraghe of Monti de su Marchesu, Monti Acutzu, Monti Ibera, and Monti Proceddu.

9f425edca8a431f4.text: Complex nuraghe: due to the state of degradation and the significant burial of the structures, it cannot be securely assigned to any defined type.

9f7f605d50b16afc.text:
It is of tufaceous trachyte (L 5, W 2.50, H 2.70 m), consisting of a rectangular chamber (4.18 x 1.14 m) bounded on the sides by two orthostats, by a front slab with an entrance hatch with rounded corners facing south-east, and by a flat covering slab.

Inside the western lateral orthostat a rectangular niche opens (L 1.22, W 0.88, D 0.50 m). To the left of the monument's front slab there is a small niche, cut into the thickness of the western orthostat.

9f86d081884c7d65.text: Nuragic hut. It is circular, built of flat stones of various sizes laid one on another in courses that corbel inwards towards the centre. The wall is conical: about 60 cm wide at the base and about 40 cm wide at the top, with a surviving height of about 130 cm. To the south-east the wall breaks off for about 100 cm (perhaps the entrance) where the structure has collapsed, probably because of wild olive and mastic trees.

9fa1161b074af6b6.text: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure is hardly observable because, in addition to being embedded within the usual lentisco soil, it is also covered by small stones resulting from the erosion of the surrounding terrain.

9fbf26d21d1083c2.text: It seems to belong to the category of "uncompleted" nuraghes, yet the dense vegetation cover prevents a precise definition.

9fc5a0b4cae6015f.text: The site is partially eroded. Only the entrance corridor and part of the staircase remain. It is thought that the use of the nuraghe may date back to 1550 and continue until 900 BC.

9fc7922b96a500ea.text: The Paiulu (IGM) or Paiolu nuraghe is located on a basaltic bastion at Costa Pisu, on the western slope of Monte Arci, at the border between the municipal territories of Oristano, Palmas Arborea (Tiria) and Villaurbana.

9fc9469ad2883f6c.text: Single-tower nuraghe, the few remaining fragments are covered by dense vegetation.

9fe70c616d486780.text: Probable nuraghe tower, of which only the lintel of the entrance and the rubble heap remain.

9fff7918ad9d973c.text: June 2021, report. The foundation has collapsed and the stones have been propped up with iron rods; if you enlarge the image, the rods can be seen.

a01d5a61f973e98a.text: The sources available to us report that the proto-nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Ercole Contu, before the construction of the Cuga dam, around the 1950s/60s; unfortunately the same texts tell us that the body of the nuraghe was dismantled for study precisely because it had unusual forms. Subsequently, with the approval of the Ministry, it was used as a foundation for the Cuga dam. The tower was 6 metres high.

a0203407efef8981.text: Single-tower nuraghe, with traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

a02fdd30f0459c89.text:
Located on an acrocoro from which the valley where the Nurritani people lived could be monitored. Bounded by the Roman cippus found in that area by Professor Mastino.

The region south of Tirso extended between Orotelli and the sources of the Tirso to the east of Benetutti, bordering the Goceano to the north and the Barbaria to the south.

a03dd77413b10cdb.text: The site includes an undefined structure (WHAT COULD IT BE?) at the edge of a sheer drop; on the front it once had (now disappeared) a hollowed-out boulder like a holy-water stoup, a tiny domus de janas, the giants' tomb of Pascaredda; a dolmen, the Monti Di Deu nuraghe, the Agnu nuraghe, and the Nuragic spring of Li Paladini. The Pascaredda tomb and the Agnu nuraghe are easily reached; everything else has been left to itself and is hard to locate and reach.

a0548905676bbea4.text: Nearby and closely associated with the Miuddu nuraghe, no more than a hundred metres to the south-east, stands a giants' tomb displaying the usual architectural layout of this tomb type: a semicircular exedra (chord 10.05 m – sagitta 2.25 m), a slightly apsidal rectangular body (length 9.75 m – width 2.50 m) and a rectangular burial chamber (length 4.60 m x 0.80 m wide x 0.75 m high above the fill).

a055d01b83acae13.text: It is named after the terrain's toponym. Like most of the nuraghes and other features in Chiaramonti, it is in a state of degradation almost irreparably compromised. Several features stand out that lead me to consider its belonging to the nuraghe type with a flat floor.

a05787575fb7ec0e.text: Beautiful necropolis of domus de janas consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5–6–7–8), the fourth is located near the group of four tombs, the third is about 200 metres to the south, and the first and second are situated near each other, about 100 metres east of the third.

a06d0de84771c63b.text: Single-tower with circular plan (diam. 12.80 x 12) and a maximum remaining height of 2.55 m.

a0907cbaa62bc212.text: The Bia nuraghe now appears as a ruin. It is not a single-tower nuraghe (although the most visible tower is very probably the central tower), since other walling can be made out to the south.

a09ce11fd8a88c30.text: The few remaining fragments of the nuraghe have been lost, as a result of land clearing and agricultural improvement works, now covered by brambles and other shrubs, and behind a wire fence. Nevertheless, traces of the monument are still visible through large basal circle stones. mu

a0aab8069f58e5a0.text: A few surviving courses of the Crastu nuraghe, located within the village of the same name

a0ca319a0baab44c.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The monument preserves three to four courses of blocks of the outer wall face, reaching a maximum surviving height of about 2.60 m. At present it is not possible to identify the entrance, partly because brambles and mastic partially cover the remains of the nuraghe. The inner chamber has collapsed and the material that formed it completely fills the remaining parts of the monument.

a0dd61818557c0d5.text:
A monument of exceptional value belonging to the final phase of the Nuragic period, when towers were no longer built and various "federal sacred sites" were established, often incorporating sacred wells constructed with isodomic ashlar and enriched with sculptural architectural elements.

La Fonte is unfortunately not properly maintained and is not kept consistently clean.

a0f0f4b7d02c7863.text: Single-tower nuraghe. On the IGM map this nuraghe is confused with the nearby Nuraghe Molas. Around the nuraghe there are traces of a village or settlement.

a137fbf519536e09.text: The De Planu or Don Micheli nuraghe has a diameter of 12.50 m and a wall thickness of four metres. The circular chamber, 3.80 m in diameter, is reached through a corridor 4.50 m long, blocked for two metres. At a depth of two metres fragments of vessels with handles of different shapes and a mould hollowed out in the centre came to light; at a depth of one metre fragments of tableware, human bones and a cremation burial were found.

a15ac0e12e9a2ed9.text: The proto-nuraghe Bardalatzu is located at the western end of a basaltic tableland, in a remote and difficult-to-access area, dominating a narrow and deep valley where the Riu Murtazzolu and the Riu Cuguttu meet. The monument appears to be of considerable size, with an irregular planimetric form that fits the triangular profile of the hill on which it was built.

a15e673b881e195e.text:
Complex nuraghe.

Although listed as Brundette Nuraghe, it is instead known (even by the local elders) as Chentucheddas Nuraghe, and it is situated on the edge of the named rock.

a186769eb41f771a.text: Complex plan, it is built in basalt with a structure composed of well-cut blocks arranged in regular horizontal courses such that the joints of the upper blocks fall in the centre of the lower ones. The fortress is probably composed of three towers enclosing a small courtyard with an entrance to the south-west.

a1962477e723448d.text: The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of about 90–100 huts, spread over five hectares. Due to its extensive size and the number of buildings, the site is considered unique within the Nuragic context of Gallura.

a1a633c8cf9f4a4c.text: Single-tower nuraghe that re-emerges from the lake only during periods of drought

a1f5e21914697d41.text: Probable nuraghe (Ugas 2022), located beneath the remains of a 18th-century fort, later used as a signal point. For some archaeologists it would have been a quadrilobate, Nuragic royal residence. Others consider it unlikely. Further studies are pending.

a200db2ae7441a62.text: It is located on the summit of a hill, precisely at the intersection of two watersheds. From this fortunate and strategic position, the nuraghe dominates the entire surrounding plain.

a2021f270b30daeb.text: Four-lobed, whose excavations have yielded many intact artefacts. The lifespan of the nuraghe appears to be very short.

a235b92de614ffdc.text: Four-lobed nuraghe in which a bronze figurine and the hull of a boat, also bronze, shaped like a four-tower nuraghe, were found.

a238e0b37b7948e8.text:
Of this monument nothing remains, as it was buried over time and subsequently covered by houses and roads.

Some sewer excavations and local narratives indicate the presence of a complex nuraghe and a settlement. The site is also about 300 m from the location of the tomb of the warriors of Sant'Iroxi, known for its two hundred skulls and swords.

a258913f11c4f353.text:
The Written Boulder, carved.

Giants' tomb at Santu Micheli whose stele is framed, precisely, by a low-relief border.

a2713c40ca6b9ee2.text:
nuraghe, probably a complex, with a village.

In the area, successive occupations after the Nuragic period are evident, evidenced by the dispersion of historical-era fragments in the soil.

The complex, difficult to access, is currently covered by dense vegetation that conceals the huts, making a correct planimetric reading and the full understanding of its layout extremely difficult.

a28e51b6e1b27115.text: Wikipedia identifies this nuraghe as one of the last to be built, with progressively less pronounced external wall slopes. It retains the tholos almost intact, except for some courses.

a2ab2cd36492bf70.text: Located in the same locality, in the countryside of the village, a Nuragic well temple, of which only some remains are visible today. The monument is isodomic in type and thus exhibits very refined craftsmanship. Numerous blocks of the sacred structure are scattered near a recently constructed well, which in fact has replaced the ancient one.

a2af53bb761abfd0.text: Complex nuraghe of Mont'Elva with attached village. It is in a state of ruin due to works carried out in the 1950s for the high Nurra aqueduct water network. The central tower, partially buried, remains with a residual height of about 2 m; a secondary tower located to the south-west of the main one has been reduced to just two surviving courses, hidden by the dense Mediterranean scrub.

a2c74cb5dced0fee.text: Structures related to a complex nuraghe of mixed type, consisting of a proto-nuraghe of corridor type connected to a tholos nuraghe of single-tower type. The complex, overall very imposing, is composed of a large elliptical – slightly quadrangular – building with rounded corners, about 22 m long and 17 m wide, slightly more than, oriented N–S.

a2d779d329297f14.text: The Nuraghe of Busurtei stands on top of the hill of the same name, from which there is a breathtaking view. Near the nuraghe, in the medieval period, stood the small village called Busurtei, Busateri or Buzarcheri, which belonged to the diocese of Santa Giusta in 1224. About a hundred metres north of the nuraghe there is a spring whose water is said to be the best of all the springs in the territory of Sedilo.

a2d97e0949b1db55.text: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral extension: the added bodies are arranged not only in front, but also laterally relative to the main tower. The smaller towers are two, connected to the main one by curtain walls; in the centre lies the courtyard as an integration space.

a325ecd50ff446dd.text: Multicellular domus de janas containing carved decorations depicting a bull's-head protome. At the centre there is a pillar cut out by removal of rock.

a333a7b48d4e9021.text: Nuraghe Busoro lies in the municipality of Sedilo, about 1.5 km north of the village. It is a single-tower nuraghe, built of basalt; the internal tholos lacks its uppermost courses.

a3622f4944227ffe.text: In the area there is a large amount of pottery fragments. Amidst the dense vegetation, a hut is still intact; a first tower and a second, possibly a remnant of a four-lobed structure; a magnificent well or cistern with a basalt grating at its entrance.

a367867eb4cf1ba0.text: The Tomba di Bau su Matutzu (3rd millennium BC) is located within an olive grove inside the Ecoserdiana dump.

a3696c5f3c602360.text:
The S'Ulivera nuraghe is of mixed type, as it features corridor structures, and above it rises a tholos chamber with niches, though partially collapsed.

Around the nuraghe, some remains of what was once a village are still visible; at a short distance, several basalt stones well-cut remain, which likely formed part of a culturally significant building.

a3772359fd80eea1.text: Approximate area of the Nuragic village Codula Manna

a3adaf466c6d2ba6.text: Complex nuraghe completely collapsed and buried.

a3d0c272f5bdf880.text: It may be a nuraghe whose construction was never completed.

In Tomb VI, which has seven chambers, a false door of trapezoidal shape is carved into the back wall of one of the cells. In Tomb VIII, the main cell has a double-pitched ceiling and, on the front wall above the hatch giving access to one of the secondary chambers, double horns are carved in low relief, now barely legible.

a3ec0c6ce86b892e.text: In this case one is faced with a critical situation because the remains of the nuraghe form an irregular heap of stones, although certain constructive features of the structure are still discernible. a41013587fac6505.text: Around it one can see the remains of the ancient village and the granitic rocks in their varied shapes. Near the building, of which only a few courses and the lintel facing Monte Novo remain, the traces of the granite quarries are very evident. Within an area of 1 km there are nine domus de janas; some lie near the Nuraghe, the others, on the same granitic outcrop, lie near the Sau family farmhouse.

a416d6f46532c891.text:
It is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

a42b5c6c31af1f74.text: Next to the provincial road remains a low row possibly belonging to a giants' tomb, whose typical structure is clearly visible.

a42c02195677bf69.text: It is in a state of complete ruin. Some of the basal stones, though barely visible, are discernible and embedded in the natural rock, forming a single unit with the entire structure.

a43f83f30dfb7440.text: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Other wall sections of undetermined function are present. The site was also occupied in Roman times.

a44bb6177309ed64.text: Single-tower enclosed within a bastion. Four courses of massive arenite blocks from the wall are visible, with a height of almost 2 metres. Climbing the wall, the top of the tower is seen to be ruined.

a45c5c3c68787a2c.text:
Only shaped ashlars of the monument can be identified, from which it can be established that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

Some of the ashlars (perhaps those belonging to the exedra) are incorporated into the walling of a recent hut, and others lie scattered nearby, hidden by vegetation. In particular, the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size is present.

The baetyls now placed in the forecourt of the Church of Santa Caterina appear to come from it.

a45e3017c8916a0f.text:
On the summit of the limestone outcrop at 191 metres above sea level stands a monumental Nuragic complex that makes use of the natural rock ledge to the west and a sheer drop on the eastern slope.

The monument covers an area of about 1000 sq m and extends in plan along a longitudinal axis oriented north-west–south-east, with a probable entrance to the north.

From north to south the following can be identified: a tholos; a sub-rectangular block; a semicircular room; walls following a curvilinear course.

a460a7f7bcfbe647.text: Visitable, collapsed upon itself, central tower with a tree inside, large walls of calcareous tufa. Used in Roman times, evidenced by the presence of broken amphorae. In the nearby rocky outcrops, laccus are present. Traces of a village nearby.

a47bec8478559f00.text: The monument lies about 200 metres north-east of the Nuraghe Figu and less than 350 metres south-west of the Nuraghe Bighinzone. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, a wall thickness of 4.00 m on the east side and 3.60 m on the west, and a height that varies from 3.05 m to the north-north-west, with six courses, to 1.75 m to the south-south-west with three or four courses. The masonry consists of polyhedral blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

a490349148fb125f.text:
Complex nuraghe, of which only some of the curtain walls of the towers and possibly a outer wall remain evident. The collapse and dense vegetation make it difficult to interpret the spatial layout of the complex.

A modest Neolithic village develops to the south-west.

The complex shows interesting superimpositions, including the remains of an old medau with buildings constructed with dry stone walls.

a4b7ad5569f87ebd.text: A few megalithic stones indicating a probable nuraghe, perhaps a circle. Certainly, witnesses report that many stones ended up forming a vespai during the reclamation of the marsh. Marsh nuraghes, wetland nuraghes. See Paùles and Cunvéntu nòu.mu

a4c2703d195d189b.text: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.

a4d47b8acf558a1d.text: Group of domus de janas, the most important of which features a checkerboard motif, bordered on one side by a zig–zag band, representing the depiction of textiles found in the dwellings of the living and re-presented in the tombs of the dead.

a5015661dbdb7053.text: The nuraghe, as shown on the maps of the former cadastral survey, is listed under the name "Chessalzu". Only a few buried courses remain.

a50d659dc67aa32d.text: A ruined nuraghe of which it is difficult to say whether it belonged to the category of unfinished nuraghi or single-tower nuraghi

a54e87c6d8b49cca.text: Reported by a resident of Osilo. The domus is not photographable, hidden by brambles and shrubs. To be verified.

a5931941e0916b3d.text:
Nuraghe consisting of two towers and a courtyard on the south side. Built of large roughly dressed blocks of red trachyte. A megalithic double-faced wall runs south from the nuraghe, of which about 35 m of the basal courses survive. To the north, and partly to the east and south, a village of huts extends, of which various basal circles remain.

A few metres west of the nuraghe there is a well now blocked by collapse debris.

a594f789c493731a.text: It is one of the many nuraghes destroyed over the millennia due to vegetation, ploughing, land reclamation, and other uses. It should have been quadrilobate, possibly with a double anterior addition. But it is difficult to say for certain without a thorough cleaning and excavation.

a5a283e691e0407e.text: Located within a private property, among the numerous domus of the Ozierese area, they are the largest present in the region and not only; but they are also the only ones to feature symbols of the bull god carved in such a conspicuous manner.

a5ea087f180e766a.text: The Su Nuraxi nuraghe of Gonnosfina is located about 400 metres east of the village, near the industrial area. It is a single-tower nuraghe, largely destroyed and covered by its own debris and vegetation. Only a few courses remain.

a62e22d864f0c50a.text: Located at a short distance from Sa Unta and Sa Tumba, in the area of Sculta 'e Muru, it appears as a heap of stones in complete disuse.

a6875cf62fb69713.text:
Proto-nuraghe Mura Barbaros: the monument consists of an outer wall enclosing, for at least three-fifths, a building of rather irregular form. On the surface of the top, a short corridor to the south-east is visible, partially closed by four flat slabs, while to the south there is a glimpse of an entrance with a lintel belonging to a second corridor.

Almost a continuation of the previous.

a6946ce0bc088ff4.text: It has an elliptical plan and is built on a bed of granite rock. During clearance work, several early medieval ceramic finds decorated with "stampiglia" were recovered.

a6c7c5a6c2f87d12.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe that still has its tholos intact. It almost certainly belongs to the type with a sub-floor chamber, which is easily recognisable. The entrance has collapsed but it can be entered carefully by sliding over the lintel astride the guard chamber.

a6e4b0b0f775a0a3.text: Only a few traces of the completely collapsed settlement remain to the south. Excavated by illegal diggers. Remains of the wall faces are visible.

a77fb27ddf71f730.text: Remains of a complex nuraghe built in basalt.

a797b386e0eeba7d.text: Remains of a giants' tomb, of which the base courses remain.

To the south-southeast lies a trapezoidal entrance to the monument. There is a narrow passage with an ogival cross-section that leads directly to the chamber of the central tower.

a7acefc6b503fc1b.text: The monument is built at the foot of a rocky outcrop where a spring vein is present. The structure is made of trachyte boulders of various sizes expertly worked. Access to the well is through a vestibule leading to a staircase that ends in the well chamber; this has a façade preserving a rectangular entrance opening surmounted by a lintel. Because of collapses and its precarious state the site has been fenced off.

a7d18f784698fc37.text:
Impressive four-lobed nuraghe with two towers partially collapsed, but with the main tower in good condition, although largely buried. a7f2b566d648084d.text: It is a nuraghe more than partially collapsed. It appears as a haphazard heap of stones, which, on its least damaged side, retains three courses of the original foundation.

a7fe1104a67ce84b.text: In this underground chamber dating to the Middle Neolithic (4600–4000 B.C.) several interesting artefacts were found, including a tetrapod plate made of limestone with a bull's-head protome. This is described as one of the earliest depictions of a bucranium in Sardinia. A bucranium refers to a figure of an animal's head with horns pointing upwards. a804c5e55978b832.text: The sacred well was excavated by diggers using a backhoe, and they found numerous bronze objects sold on the black market. The current state of the well is very poor, covered by moss and mud.

a80847fd522ab682.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure has been largely destroyed. Some alignments of stones relating to the corridor and the exedra help to identify the layout of the monument.

a855b80e52e55cb2.text: It is a pair of hypogea: a two-cell domus and a three-cell domus.

a8afd9564c737464.text:

The monument, built with isodomic masonry, features an exedra with courses and an architrave entrance, repeats the common planimetric layout typical of burial monuments: a rectangular body with an apsidal rear section and a semicircular exedra in front.

a8f07125c272d1e5.text:

a8f18cf3de392617.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Sassari. It is heavily eroded and surrounded by dense vegetation.

aa35f0a49e8beb58.text: The nuraghe is situated on the summit of a granitic rock massif; it is a small single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of degradation, and the dense vegetation prevents access for visitors.

aa82885afd42cbac.text: On a hill composed of a central tower and a bastion, featuring a large village hidden almost entirely by dense vegetation. Two large huts remain, one identified as the 'meeting hut', and at least four others are visible in the undergrowth.

aa972c1dfc3a4ef3.text: Contiguous with the area where the corridor nuraghe of the same name stands, it consists of dozens of quadrangular huts, sometimes divided into several rooms and apsidal, bounded by blocks set on edge. Sometimes affected by illegal excavations, the fragile pre-Nuragic dwellings are located both inside the wooded area owned by the municipality and, in greater numbers, outside it, in a large area used as pasture.

aaa9206e973c7fe0.text: Coursed tomb, the shape of which is difficult to determine.

aacf88cccc3080cf.text: Only some stones remain of the tomb.

aaf0a133c0400de7.text: It stands on Cuccuru Cireddu at 130 m above sea level. It is not in good condition and is almost completely covered by mastic. It is in visual contact with the Nuraghe Monte Eghedda about 1 km away and the Nuraghe S'Omu e S'Orku about 2 km away as the crow flies. Documents from the Municipality of Maracalagonis also report a necropolis, perhaps "Roman"; indeed, a large amount of material is present all around the nuraghe over a wide radius.

aafd007f48f2d40b.text: Single-tower with its top missing and a collapsed vault inside. The best-preserved section is four metres high and has eight courses. To the south-east the entrance is preserved with an architrave and a window for drainage.

ab0dc26fa59379d1.text:
Domus de janas currently repurposed for other uses.

Should include 9 domus de janas.

ab0e6175a7ff3822.text: Nuraghe Mannu stands on the summit of the beautiful beach of Cala Fuili. The significance of this site is mainly due to the Nuragic village of Nuragheddu, which is one of the largest in Sardinia and comprises more than 200 huts of various shapes and sizes.

ab11d6aac44a8857.text: Noted to the Superintendent of Ca’ Or on 17 May 2021 by the Nurnet Foundation

ab172037023d8e3e.text: This domus de janas is named after the bas-relief sculpture of a bull's-head protome carved on one of the internal walls. The other notable feature is the dolmenic corridor located in front of the entrance.

ab285e36cbef122d.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe roofed with a tholos, still in good condition: it survives on the N-NE and N-W sides to a height of 10.50 metres, while the SE side, corresponding to the entrance, has collapsed.

The external wall face, of 26 courses of stone, is formed by large polygonal blocks in the base, which has a diameter of 14 metres, while in the upper part the blocks are sub-square and of modest size, becoming more regular as the height increases.

ab3ae37d49394b68.text: The building stands in a strategic position on the limestone plateau of Sas Seas (482 m a.s.l.), from which it dominates the surrounding territory. The ground plan of the nuraghe cannot be clearly defined because of the collapses. Inside the structure part of a rectangular chamber survives that was probably originally roofed with a truncated ogive. The same roofing system has been hypothesised for the Fodde nuraghe at Bolotana.

ab5306207025dee8.text: Vast and complex archaeological site, comprising at least two villages, a probable necropolis with an associated building that may have been of cultic use, and nearby also a furnace.

ab7d2bf27b431c4b.text: Mixed nuraghe, of which only little remains, partly covered by vegetation. Possibly enlarged and restored.

ab7e0a4908ac304d.text: Of the megalithic tomb, very well preserved until the 1970s, only the northern façade and the right arm of the exedra remain, partially; a short section of the burial chamber is also discernible, while at a few metres' distance some enormous slabs, which formed the flat-laid roof of the tomb, are visible.

ab89dd9a84d34442.text: It now appears as a single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by well-cultivated fields; it is imposing, with free-standing walls about seven metres high. To the right a steep helical staircase leads up to the top of the nuraghe; to the left a niche overlooks the entrance area. Inside the circular chamber three further niches can be seen, clearly defined. The view from the terrace takes in the woods and the well-tended lands of the industrious people of Samugheo. It deserves to be visited and enhanced.

abb8b0f8b18c338f.text: Apparently detached from the adjacent tomb, it must certainly have been built in relation to it, or vice versa. The site is also known as Culu de Muru. mu

abc1a6b035f3aa2e.text: At the foot of the nuraghe of the same name – in the east-south-east sector – wall remains probably belonging to the village are visible, though partly hidden by the scrub. One can clearly make out: the entrance to an enclosure; the remains of a rectangular hut; cyclopean walls adjoining the hut structures and the nuraghe itself. The structures were almost certainly reused in relatively recent times.

abc430a475acfcfa.text: The giants' tomb Su Niu de su Crobu is located on a rocky elevation, not far from the sea, in the area Sa corona de su crabì. The burial, of the "coursed" type, consists of a funerary corridor with an apsidal end, about 10 m long and averaging 1.20 m wide; the stones forming it are only minimally worked, arranged in irregular files and consolidated with numerous pegs.

abd2e5da6c30fc78.text: Located near the homonymous nuraghe, some giants' tombs are observed, concealed by dense vegetation that also partially hides the nuraghe.

abe29e6bf2912d65.text: Situated about a hundred metres north of the Rio Merchis and less than 300 metres west of the proto-nuraghe known locally as “Nuraghe Magossula”, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.70 x 11.70 m) that survives to a maximum height of 2.00 m with four courses on the north side, while on the south-west there is only a single course and on the south-east, where the entrance must have been, the wall face is entirely absent.

abe3cb188b09c769.text: Complex nuraghe, apparently four-lobed with the tholos of the central tower intact

abee9d7422c12098.text: Unusual rectangular plan with a probable entrance on the south side, which has collapsed completely. The north, west and east sides remain visible. Built on the edge of a steep slope, it is probably a temple dedicated to the water cult, as suggested by two springs (long dry) at the foot of the structure on the south side. One spring is covered by an almost intact tholos with its entrance partly blocked by a collapse, while the other, triangular in plan, shows clear traces of a spring at its apex.

ac30d8b330f5adb9.text: “Nuraghe Sas Melas, a short distance from the hill called Fruncu Sas Patatas, at the ford of Rio Minori. It is the best nuraghe in the municipality; it still has two storeys; solid construction, accessible doorway like the corridor and the lower chamber; shepherds’ refuge; the stair leads to the upper storey, with a domed cell; windows wider than they are high. In the lower chamber a stone table. On land belonging to the heirs of Luca Piras, son of Angelo.”

ac60de420955cb0e.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of two towers joined by a corridor, built in basalt.

ac905da6ed6aab7b.text: Nuragic huts along the south-west coast within the municipality of Arbus. Very little remains visible, but it is an important testimony of this civilization.

aca7110d2b1d00dc.text:
Dug into a tuff cliff and located in a narrow valley gorge fed by a tributary of the Rio Mannu, just outside the village, to the right of the road to Allai.

The domus are situated in a private property, enclosed and secured by a gate; the owner is often seen working in the garden and will readily let you enter and guide you to the site.

acf7fbeeecede4e6.text: Pluricellular, extensively modified and used as a shepherd's shelter.

ad169d6781c351c7.text:
Small observation tower.

Nearby is a hut with a "rotonda" equipped with a bacile.

ad3404b285e4dd5d.text: The tomb is built in isodomic masonry with a faceted wall of courses. The funerary body is thick and symmetrical, apsidal, and slightly tapers to a semicircular exedra marginated by seats, exposed to the SSE. Of the monument, in local basalt, the following remain: the base course of the funerary chamber, parts of the base slabs of the façade and the seat bench, and a good portion of the external vaulted cover composed of monolithic arches.

ada7409facdba3a2.text:
The dolmen lies about 250 metres north-west of Nuraghe Arghentu and less than 500 metres south-east of Nuraghe Interenas, on stony ground with abundant shrub vegetation.

The tomb, built partly on a basalt outcrop, now consists of three orthostats that enclose a quadrangular space (1.16 x 1.26 m; height 0.92 m) and support a large covering slab, now slightly tilted to one side.

adbcbd704c58fdb4.text: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation, near which a dolmen is reported.

adbf3e18078c98fd.text:
It is a single-tower with a circular plan  

(axis SE-NO 11.75 m; axis East-West 11.50 m) with a thickness of 2.70 m to the north-west and 3.85 m to the west; the maximum remaining height is in the north-west, measuring 3.60 m on 8 courses of basaltic stones, well-worked, of medium and large dimensions, laid in regular horizontal courses.

adc9676e8f088f8e.text: Nuraghe type undetermined; it features a tower with the tholos still intact, surrounded by remains of collapse within the dense undergrowth.

adef3851df435ef0.text: The tower is missing its top and the perimeter has an irregular shape. The internal diameter varies from 4.2 to 5.6 m. Presence of clandestine excavations.

ae01d19c24a3ba42.text: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined with its tholos collapsed and overgrown with vegetation

ae0bbc681c522b0f.text: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a five-lobed bastion enclosing the original tower and a courtyard. The central tower, circular in plan (13 m external diameter), survives to a maximum height of over 12 metres. The wall face is built of blocks laid in horizontal courses. The lower chamber is filled with rubble, laid transversely to the helical staircase — also blocked — that started from the ground floor.

ae218d79e1243485.text: The Orgono nuraghe at Ghilarza is a remarkable monument whose structural development tells the evolution of Nuragic architecture: from the archaic nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber to the truncated-conical tower with a circular tholos chamber. The consolidation and excavation work carried out so far has allowed at least partial recovery of the monument, which was already seriously unstable and in danger of collapse.

ae312519fed91a26.text: Of the monument, in large part covered by an agricultural access road built directly over it, only some large stones remain, which formed the base row; from these it is possible to infer that the original layout was circular.

ae38f105abd43da6.text: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.

ae5a0ceb36b37b66.text: Located on a rocky spur near the road between Thiesi and Romana, it dominates the landscape below, where in particular the nuraghe Majore is situated.

ae60012e460b9a03.text: Complex nuraghe with a village and sacred well in the vicinity

ae6ea4a9ac070e0b.text: Domus de janas reported to the Nurnet editorial office. From the video it appears to be a rocky massif where a larger necropolis may be present.

ae759644c7006e86.text: The nuraghe located on a rocky cliff to the west of the Domus de janas is completely hidden by dense vegetation. However, the mastio's course is difficult to identify, though some visible filari suggest its structure was that of a single tower.

ae7c21c6f9727706.text: Nuraghe located within the urban centre, single-tower, partially collapsed

aec5d2cd9d74183a.text: At the end of the Geometric phase the number of occupied sites continues to fall: evidence for the 7th and 6th centuries BC is found only at Monti Crastu, Is Arruinalis and Monti Angurdu, where decorated sherds of the Archaic phase have been observed. In this later phase it is likely that the centre of Is Arruinalis grew to a “proto-urban” level, as is known to have happened at other settlements in the Campidano and Marmilla (Tuppedili, San Sperate).

aec7e336cd75948c.text: Nuraghe almost entirely destroyed, with only a semicircular stretch of masonry remaining.

aed3b993e8b02f21.text:
It stands imposing in the locality of Pauli on a limestone plateau. The monument consists of a central tower almost 7 metres high, against which two further added structures lean, now almost completely collapsed. From the entrance you enter the main chamber, partly covered by collapse debris.

The nuraghe is surrounded by an outer wall and the remains of a village, whose huts are used as goat shelters. A few hundred metres away lie the remains of two giants' tombs.

aee75268adeb333c.text: It had a very complex plan.

aee7e191c7488f95.text: Diroccated nuraghe, it is distinguished by its proximity to several other Nuragic megalithic monuments.

aee90228c89f101e.text: Two giants' tombs located a few tens of metres apart.

aefad4ebd990fda5.text: About 100 metres west of the nuraghe, a small settlement has been recorded, consisting of the remains of a cluster of at least five circular huts and a rectangular building. South of the nuraghe, about 500 metres away, the basal courses of two circular huts and other short stretches of curvilinear walls in trachyte are visible, while about 400 metres south-west of the nuraghe lie the remains of a circular hut.

af1cca68f83765ad.text:
A pre- and proto-historic complex comprising a modest Early Neolithic village, a complex nuraghe enclosed by an outer wall, and its village of huts. Inside the village a well for water supply has been dug, of uncertain date.

The buildings are constructed of blocks of local andesite.

Above the Nuragic hut village a fine sheepfold has been built, bounded by dry-stone walls.

af207b243c1b42e0.text: The monument located at a short distance from the Giants' Tombs of Su Piccante and Su Ittichinzu and from the nearby village of Lettu Rucratu is situated at the foot of a hill where it appears as a small well carved into the ground, where presumably the water table naturally emerged, and lined with rough basalt blocks.

af475417d567f1bc.text: It is a sacred well almost entirely buried and partially damaged by illegal excavations. It can be identified in the midst of a dense and invasive vegetation, which nevertheless does not prevent the recognition of masonry structures forming the upper part of the tholos of the well and the upper structures of the vestibule.

af5ccc6c740c54ff.text: The nuraghe, located in land used for pastoralism and partly for viticulture, is irrevocably ruined due to illegal excavations that affected the area. Only a short section of the wall remains, which, however, does not allow us to define its further dimensions or the type of construction.

af601c4ae20f7af7.text: Noted to the Nurnet editorial office by a resident of Osilo. Single-cellular, situated on a calcareous pedestal from which it takes its name, located near the settlement of Santa Vittoria.

af623f91f0934921.text: Simple single-tower nuraghe, built with polygonal basalt blocks of local origin. Of the structure, camouflaged in the dense vegetation and overgrown by a stand of Indian figs, only about 6 courses of stacked blocks remain. To the south-east the entrance can be identified, featuring a large monolithic lintel well-cut and squared. The blocks forming the uprights also show a fairly precise craftsmanship.

af64eac4e2fa0335.text: The nuraghe is completely collapsed, probably known also by the name Tostoinus.

af6bf30c757e0870.text: Simple dolmen, with a rectangular plan and entrance facing north-east. The right wall is formed by a single rectangular slab, while the left wall is composed of two roughly worked stones resting on natural rock. The covering slab is flattened on the lower surface and left natural on the upper surface. EPOCH: Ozierian culture (3500–2700 BC).

af7a186c5b7f4668.text: Nuraghe of which only faint traces remain

af7bedb82930f301.text:
Not easily accessible, one reaches it after a rugged climb, through arid and rocky pastures, among emergent stones that reveal the ancient presence of a large village.

Nothing has been excavated from this monument, and only the tholos of the second level is accessible.

Completely overgrown with stones and brambles lies the courtyard opposite the main tower.

af8d3bc9984c50ab.text: The territory, today almost entirely devoid of vegetation, must have been greener and richer in water at the time of the nuraghi: the springs, now neglected, were clean and well kept until thirty years ago. Even then it is likely that small circular structures were built around many of them, made of large blocks and covered by small vaults with an opening for the water, to keep them clean, as we can see in the remains of Funtana Gureu.

af9c3e6af131c1da.text: The complex is located within the territory of Villaputzu and includes two towers known as N.ghe Monte Arrubiu I and II, which should be considered part of the same structure, together with the Nuragic village that develops in the adjacent plain. From the summit, a magnificent view is enjoyed. There are several rocks that take on particularly distinct shapes.

afb4d83418826461.text: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and bastions, possibly including a second tower. Nearby are the remains of a settlement and the Giants' tomb of Li Mizzani. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

afc7e0e6fdd224e3.text: One of the most important and nearby historical testimonies to the commune of Arbus is the nuraghe of Cugui, one of the most original in Sardinia. Located on the summit of a hill facing Fluminimaggiore, the nuraghe of Cugui is easily accessible from the Canau area, known for its spring. The nuraghe has three towers, one of which is accessible, although the taller ones may present considerable difficulties for visitors to enter.

afe8a4a0f729ece4.text:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Cagliari.

Final section of a domus de janas (Neolithic underground tomb), near the cave of the same name, destroyed by the limestone quarry.

afed8acf6ff6f247.text:
Should preserve the intact tholos.

Complex nuraghe, today appears as a wooded hill.

On top, a staircase provides access to the internal areas, probably the central tower.

I do not recommend an internal visit, as the nuraghe is very unstable due to the large roots of the vegetation that inhabits it!

affe51a749d174b0.text:
The mastio dates to the 15th–13th centuries BC, while the bastion, the outer wall, and the curtain wall date to the 13th–late 12th century.

Already in the Early Iron Age, the findings show a gradual decline in site occupation, though the site was not entirely abandoned.

It was also used for funerary purposes, as evidenced by the remains from the 7th–8th centuries BC.

b0477bb27e92831f.text:
The remains of what appears to have been a classic-type Nuragic sacred well lie against a dry-stone wall marking the boundary between the territories of Birori and Borore, a few metres from the Bau Cannas hypogea.

At present only the circular base profile (diam. 1.40 m) and a masonry of two courses of well-worked stones are visible; the bottom, as far as can be seen through the standing water, seems to have paving slabs.

b076ad8ea62a58d5.text: Only the floor, composed of large stones, a few peripheral stones, and clearly visible exedra remain.

b08189b4cc9575e7.text: A circular single-tower nuraghe with three niches. It stands on an island in the middle of Lake Cuga, which was spared when the dam of the same name was built. It cannot be reached by land; the only access is by boat or canoe after a journey of 20–25 minutes. Each time one lands there after the winter season, the rebirth of the flora and fauna is revealed anew, forming a natural frame for the archaic shapes of the nuraghe. The quantity of incisions and cupmarks is striking.

b0974ea8b643c694.text: Located on the side of the canyon of the same name, where during the rains the same named torrent flows, it originally stood on an isolated spur raised above the valley below. Some courses of medium to large stones are present. A few metres downstream, large amounts of rubble are visible, and the structure is now almost completely destroyed.

b0ba63faaca93405.text: Three-lobed nuraghe, reused in the Roman and medieval periods. The village surrounding the tower, now almost entirely vanished due to agricultural mechanization, is one of the largest in the Uri region.

b0cb5ddcfbcce376.text: Composite nuraghe. At present it is impossible to read its plan because the whole site has been churned up by mechanical diggers, even though until a few years ago it was possible to go inside by lowering oneself from above. One thus entered a long corridor with corbelled walls; a further bulldozer operation has probably piled more material against the nuraghe and blocked the entrance. The hope is that the burial has protected it from this devastation.

b0fa6b8bbf288f0a.text:
A. Sanguinetti, who in 1970 complained that, among other things, it was partly buried under stone dumps caused by the reclamation of the surrounding farmland.

The author nevertheless described a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan and an entrance facing north-east, and hypothesised a straight access corridor.

b10def6f34c38df9.text:
Situated just outside the town of Arzachena, it appears as an imposing structure, although the upper floor has partly collapsed.

It is built of large blocks of granite and dates to around the Middle Bronze Age (about 1600 BC) on the basis of the numerous finds recovered during the excavations.

The walls of the nuraghe lean against a large granite boulder; for this reason the nuraghe has an irregular plan that gives it a "pseudo-nuraghe" appearance. (MIBACT)

b1139bbdfa02be4a.text: Site accessible only by traversing a difficult path. The ruined monument, difficult to read, retains a section to the east with 11 irregular courses of the wall.

b1377630f0c0325f.text: Nearby are also some nuragic huts.

b137f9b29d3b3a16.text: What remains of a small nuraghe near Santu Sciori. A church has been built upon it. Mentioned in the writings of Vittorio Angius for the discovery of some giant bones.

b14861155ad2eb2a.text: Structure of uncertain interpretation built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building stands on a small natural rocky spur and has an elliptical plan. It measures about 17 m in length and about 11 m in width at the central point. The northern, western and eastern parts consist of one to two courses of large and medium-sized polygonal blocks, while the southern part has three courses built with the same technique.

b15bc2089f6f2adf.text:
Situated at the foot of a hill along the course of the Rio Caddare, in an area covered by dense vegetation, the remains of wall structures belonging to the village can be seen emerging from a section of the hill eroded by the elements; these are not, however, the only evidence relating to this settlement.

Venturing into the vegetation it is in fact possible to identify the presence on the ground of numerous circular structures.

b163f4ed2018f712.text: Near the homonymous nuraghe on the slope descending towards the Stupàra stream there is a giants' tomb built with flat slabs of shale. The tomb is about 7 metres long and about 2 metres high. No exedra is visible. However, the state of conservation is nonetheless good.

b17749259b5508b2.text: It was the earliest settlement in the Villanovaforru area. A short distance from a spring, unfortunately no traces of it remain. A Bonnanaro Culture tomb was found, dated to the Early Bronze Age between 1700 and 1600 BC, together with fragments of a tripod vase and obsidian arrowheads; no osteological remains or tomb structures were recovered. The isolated find is to be interpreted as an open-air site or a funerary deposition.

b18d7aa2733daec4.text: On 10 July 1205 Maria de Thori, wife of the nobleman Pietro de Maronju and aunt of Comita, judge of Torres, gave the church of S. Maria di Orria piccinna, near Chiaramonti, together with the nearby church of S. Giusta, with servants, houses, woods, lands and animals to the hermitage of Camaldoli, and for it to the prior Martino, granting, among other things, to him and his successors the free election of the rectors of the donated churches and the burial of the monks.

b199f0dec53fa729.text: In the historical dictionary by Goffredo Casalis, the nuraghe is listed as Sa Corti deis Bacus.

b1a35b3931d0d0a9.text: Nuraghe built with calcareous white ashlar laid upon a rocky massif emerging from the dense forest. The walls remain to human height.

b1af3f1ace8db3cc.text:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale – Orune. A village built around the picturesque and colossal tower of bizarre shape, at the base of which stands the eponymous Nuraghe. The nuraghe, though imposing, appears incredibly tiny compared with the immense rock that looms over it.

This single-tower nuraghe is built of megalithic blocks only roughly dressed, of even larger dimensions at the base

b1b28c638d2cd2c3.text: Serra is Araus is a multi-layered site, known for a rock-cut necropolis (domus de janas) of the Neolithic (Ozieri Culture), Chalcolithic (Monte Claro Culture) and Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro). The 2013 excavation brought to light two new hypogea and the first evidence of the Nuragic village. In particular, traces of a building were found inside which a large model of a nuraghe had been placed.

b1e43aaec3ab3e9b.text: Nuragic wall (200 m long, with double wall face). It enclosed a Nuragic village.

b1e70ef0ea9c93b8.text:
The nuraghe still has an accessible tholos, although its top is missing. The entrance lacks its original material all the way up to the top of the tower, perhaps because of a collapse that affected the load-bearing structures of the wall in the past. The masonry has been rebuilt.

The nuraghe was almost certainly used both as a shelter and as an animal pen, and this has allowed it to be preserved in good condition.

The monument has the stairway on the left, with 13 steps still in place.

b22e099dd645b905.text: Remains of a simple single-tower tholos nuraghe built with basalt blocks from Montiferru. The structures are preserved to a height of 5–6 courses. The nuraghe stands on the summit of a dune that, until the 1950s, was part of the desert of Is Arenas. It has a direct line of sight to the large quadrilobate nuraghe at Tradori, located on the opposite side of the road.

b23ae3d818bd84a2.text: Archaic corridor nuraghe. The nuraghe stands on a hillside and is laid out on two different levels, adapting to the lie and slope of the ground. The structures are largely covered by vegetation, but the north-west and west parts can be seen in particular. The north-west part follows a semi-circular course, while the west part consists of a massive wall that extends in a straight line towards the south.

b24a2111bcb1276b.text:
The nuraghe has been dated between the 14th and 12th centuries BC.

It is notable for the use of large basalt blocks carefully squared, in particular the jambs and lintel of the entrance.

At the entrance, on the left, is the ramp that led to the upper terrace, while on the right there is a niche in the walling. In the chamber one can see the three large ogival niches in the walls, the central hearth, and the tholos that forms the ceiling, still intact.

b25bd43329214241.text:
It is cut into an erratic limestone boulder, worked on the outside as well, roughly trapezoidal in shape. On the main façade, which has an entrance, an arched stele almost 4 metres high was carved, on top of which three small baetyls were originally placed. On the rear façade another small entrance can be seen, perhaps from an earlier period.

The material culture found during the excavations is of the Bonnanaro type (Early Bronze Age).

b2662ba178526c3a.text: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade

b27804e5b11675c0.text: Nuraghe almost completely destroyed, of which only a single course remains visible. Almost entirely covered by the collapse and vegetation, its plan cannot be established.

b283ffcb72a32112.text: The site consists of the nuraghe, composed of the central tower and two other towers, various structures arranged around it that would suggest the presence of an important settlement in antiquity, and finally a structure that may represent an ancient sanctuary.

b28649a52ddf91e8.text:
This nuraghe rises on a hillock facing the village of Mara.

It is well marked but also completely overlooked. To reach this monument one must wend through tall, thorny scrubland that makes it almost invisible. For this reason it is difficult to describe, especially by a non-specialist.

It appears to be of corridor type.

b298512c9614edbf.text: A ruined nuraghe, buried and covered in vegetation. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe.

b2ae0631cc6284fd.text: Nuraghe composed of trachyte blocks; only the lintel remains, the rest has been destroyed, probably its stones were used for the dry-stone walls in the area.

b2b1c3fa13dbbed8.text: The nuraghe, likely of a complex structure, is currently covered by dense vegetation and preserves only a few courses of the original structure. Associated with the nuraghe is a circular cyclopean wall with a diameter of about 10 m. The state of conservation is very poor.

b2c0b85275518823.text: It is largely buried. One can thus make out a central tower with an irregularly circular perimeter, containing a central chamber, also circular. Along the outer perimeter of the monument stretches of walling can be seen that suggest something about its more complex articulations; for example, to the east-north-east one might hypothesise terracing works, if not the actual presence of huts or enclosures.

b2c1d1358d15e4b2.text: The probable nuraghe stands halfway up Monte Sa Corona Arrubia. Its structure cannot be determined: a large quantity of collapse boulders lies in disorder, and dense vegetation prevents an overall view. A few courses with a circular alignment are still visible in their original position, probably belonging to the central tower. Numerous potsherds lie on the surface in the area.

b2fc02b92143f7c7.text: Nuraghe completely dismantled according to S. Ghiani in La Trexenta Antica.

b31138f4dad3343d.text: The discovery of the Monte Idda hoard (Decimoputzu), which took place towards the end of 1914, was described by Taramelli as “perfectly accidental”, and on this subject the famous archaeologist wrote that “two shepherds from Desulo, who were grazing their herds on the mountain known as Sa Idda, found under some loose granite boulders, inside the remains of a terracotta vessel, a mass of bronze weapons and tools, together with ingots and ingot fragments, slag and scrap pieces of the same metal…”.

b33a3f2f89abfed4.text: There should also be a corresponding Nuragic settlement at the site.

b380a2551a7678eb.text:
The megalithic complex consists of a central body, built of rubble laid in irregular wall courses; vaguely quadrangular in plan, it contains three small circular chambers.

These rooms, enclosed within the wall face (about 2.10 m high) that defines the central body, quadrangular in plan, have been subjected to conspicuous illicit excavations carried out at an unknown date by looters.

b391a3030a57e989.text: Domus de janas with architectural façade, interesting the graffiti.

b39e9eb95a75a722.text: The cemetery of S'Isterridolzu occupies a flat area, crowned to the east by a steep rocky cliff. It includes 10 hypogea dug into low calcareous outcrops, one in an erratic boulder, and a final, unfinished one on a rocky spur: they are distributed across a large area (about 10,000 m²); the distance between each hypogean varies from 10 m to about 0.200 m.

b3c25d057f71bc68.text: Reduced to a great ruin, it still shows some constructive features of that period. Clear traces of the foundations and part of the masonry apparatus remain. Land improvement works have significantly contributed to its disappearance through the piling up of stones.

b3c5a01a4ea1f821.text: Of the monument, only the first two courses of the base remain. It could belong to the nuraghe Nuradorzu.

b3dc6718fb005ebd.text: Single-tower nuraghe covered by sand. In its surroundings are visible traces of habitation and a well dug into the rock.

b3e2c959989680e0.text: The nuraghe is almost entirely collapsed. Only the entrance with lintel remains.

b3ebb824a4a2f647.text: Initially, probable subsoil shelters have become domus de janas as needed, through the addition of related modifications. There are other examples to be noted. The surrounding area is rich in fossils and calcareous formations. Photo Mario Unali

b42104e8706113a4.text: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe. Survey is difficult because thorny shrubs have colonised the whole structure. Traces of the Nuragic village huts are clearly visible, scattered around the central tower in a limited area, not as incorrectly reported by others.

b44a3a147b8e82dc.text: On the maps of the former Catasto, the nuraghe is called "Mesu 'e Tancas Paulis".

b44bc02630bdbd94.text: This domus is single-cell with a pseudo-quadrangular plan and curved walls. The domus is located adjacent to the perimeter wall of the cemetery, with an opening facing that wall. The nature of some apparent "reliefs" on the ceiling should be investigated further. Adjacent is a second tomb.

b44d6a9460e6fefb.text: The complex nuraghe is composed of three parts built in different periods: the mastio, whose construction phase dates to about 1000 B.C.; the quadrilobate bastion with the courtyard, built between the 9th and 7th centuries B.C.; and the antemurale with the four external towers, raised between the 7th and 6th centuries B.C.

b482c041cd668c55.text: Prehistoric underground cemetery composed of 6 tombs.

b484d9134af30598.text: A striking dentilled ashlar with three teeth is visible, upon which, likely, the three baetyls representing an unidentified Sardinian triad were set.

b496248a64bfbaa0.text: It lies to the south-east of the village, not far from the Tirso River. Its state of preservation is very poor, being almost completely destroyed, like the Jana nuraghe. However, the extent of the rubble, about 25 x 18 metres (1), suggests a complex of considerable size. Nor can one overlook the fact that the very long fence enclosing the field in which it stands is built entirely from the stones of the nuraghe itself.

b498f505e9b14da3.text: There are four (but one is destroyed).

b4cb22658db8ff92.text: Single-tower with a large diameter, of which only the courses remain up to about 2.50 m in height, with the entrance and lintel.

b4e7e5ebc2f00c1a.text:
This is an archaeological area that cannot be defined because of the collapses and the vegetation. However, the data collected lead me to determine that it is a complex nuraghe, consisting of an ancient tower surrounded by a massive wall (bastion) with a continuous, concave-convex profile that probably encloses a courtyard, and some minor towers.

All around, the remains of walls (outer wall?) built with blocks of considerable size are visible.

b4f865834e3685b4.text: General location in the area of Li Casacci

b4fa73fdb0633674.text:
Complex tholos nuraghe, of the tancato type, with a central tower, a small courtyard and a secondary tower. The complex is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, but is distinguished by the extremely careful working of the entrance blocks (jambs and lintels).

The central tower has a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, while the added tower has largely collapsed and survives to a maximum height of just over 3 m.

b5002cb8a36c2233.text: The probable Nuragic village, about 200 metres west of the nuraghe, appears to consist of about 10 huts, two rectangular and the rest round. Unfortunately all the structures are in very poor condition and in some cases barely distinguishable. The huts were built of small and medium-sized polyhedral boulders laid dry. Several pottery sherds are present in the area.

b536e9d0e623f4b4.text: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.

b55c7ac33bf53602.text: Usanis, located at the top of a rocky spur, was a complex structure composed of two towers.

b561753331cde68c.text:
The monument lies less than 200 metres south-east of the giants' tomb of Santu Bainzu, which must have been the reference funerary area.

It is a single-tower nuraghe at the centre of a large village bounded by an outer wall that can only be traced in part. The tower, circular in plan (13.12 x 2.75 m; diameter at the top of the surviving masonry 11.90 m), with wall thicknesses of 4.30 m to the east and 3.60 m to the north-west, survives to a maximum height of 7.25 m and 12 courses to the south-east.

b57fb9db9546f400.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and a remaining wall face reduced to 2–3 courses.

b599844b55326968.text:
Domus de janas necropolis particularly striking, located adjacent to part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen.

One of the most beautiful Domus de Janas, until a few years ago it was entirely still underground. From a small entrance one accesses a large chamber, inside which there are three additional entrances leading to three separate rooms.

b5d2555313ccb4cc.text: Few remains of TdG. The site, heavily anthropized from distant epochs, is presumed to be very rich, like the nearby Pisciu Accas. mu

b5e56f79fea033a5.text: The proto-nuraghe Su Cannuju (ex S'Alzola Trigale) has a quadrangular plan, with a single longitudinal corridor.

b5f2218df15baf31.text: It is almost certainly a single-tower nuraghe standing on a cliff, as if to emphasise its impregnability against a probable enemy attack. About twenty courses of ordered stones are visible in the circles. The inaccessible tholos is probably intact.

b5f2a87a61169839.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.30 x 13 m): the wall thickness is about 4 metres, while the surviving height is 1.75 m with three courses.

The entrance, facing south-east, leads into a corridor (length 4 m – width 1.50/1 m) in which the existence of the stair and the opposing guard chamber can be discerned.

Of the circular chamber only the base diameter (5 m) can be measured, while it is not possible to determine whether it was lined with niches.

b5f707ded2265e66.text: Sacred well of probable Nuragic date and probable sacred use, located at 70 m east of the quadrangular tower. The well is built with well-shaped ashlar blocks of limestone and basalt, and has a notable depth of about 30 m, having yielded a large amount of material dating to the Nuragic, Punic, and Roman periods.

b6009d8cbfd2bc64.text: Near provincial road 25 to Aidomaggiore stands the tancato nuraghe called “Sa Jua”, shown here in the fine photographs of Nicola Castangia. Professor Pittau derives its name from the Latin “iuga”, meaning a herd of cattle. I would point out that in ancient Egypt cattle were also called “iwa” (jua), plainly similar to the term “ju” or “juale” used in Sardinian for the yoke.

b623d284c47f8927.text: Only known burial in the Dolianova area belonging to the Bonannaro culture and dated to 2200–1800 BC. Here, ceramics, two tripods, and a cup were found. The tomb was destroyed during quarrying operations.

b6646c39246810b5.text: From Tharros.info. Position not precisely defined

b6875af4e1757122.text: The tomb is hidden by vegetation, blocked by fallen boulders and earth. Despite the collapse, the entrance can be identified and faces east. The exedra and the apse are hard to make out, also because of the violation by looters. For the exedra, the few clues are some semi-worked stones still in their original position at the sides of what remains of the probable entrance. To the rear, boulders arranged in a semicircle formed part of the apse.

b697711008f0584b.text: Domus de janas located on the hill facing the Ortali 'e su Monte complex, beneath a smaller nuraghe similarly named.

b6b1f1f32a82e8a0.text: To reach it, follow the SP 63 from Sindia towards Scano di Montiferro for about 4 km until you see the beautiful single-tower nuraghe Serrese on the right. The dolmen lies 750 metres north of the nuraghe.

b6b2607db4c8eff5.text: Sa Turricula is recognised as the first phase of the Nuragic civilization. The site includes the nuraghe, the village, and at a short distance, in the territory of the comune of Osilo (locality Funtana 'e Casu), a dolmen.

b6bd886326ae10b5.text: The actual nuraghe no longer exists, though a section of the perimeter walls is still visible at the summit of the hill. The hill's shape suggests it may conceal more than what is presently apparent.

b6e1f369ea042d41.text: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif

b6e9959de4932da6.text: This tomb, dug into trachyte, shows — in the antechamber and in the main chamber — a painted ceiling designed to imitate the roof of a hut according to two different typological schemes. Particular attention is drawn to the "lattice" motif appearing along the walls of the main chamber.

b73a96cce9b209b8.text:
The monument stands on the summit of a low hillock, in an area currently used as pasture.

Of the simple nuraghe, which rises on a granite outcrop, only the outer wall face is visible, for 1.50 metres.

The chamber plan is sub-circular and rather irregular because a roughly trapezoidal rocky spur, projecting slightly into the chamber, has been incorporated into the wall face.

b73ef0fcbb8604fc.text: In the Nuragic period, during the Final Bronze Age, a small sacred well temple dedicated to the water cult was built. The building follows the ground plan typical of this type of monument elsewhere on the island, consisting therefore of a vestibule, a stairwell, and an underground chamber. The circular chamber, originally roofed with a tholos, and the stairwell, which survives with six steps, have wall faces built of perfectly fitting isodomic sandstone ashlars.

b73fbbe2d6b417bd.text: The structures, very likely to be interpreted as remnants of a single-tower tholos nuraghe, are literally concealed by a mass of mastic. Some base courses can be seen, composed of locally quarried polygonal basalt blocks, on the south side. The nuraghe is practically destroyed.

b75fb1760cb89a24.text: Single-tower nuraghe. Only visible on the side facing west, the lowermost 3–4 courses of the base remain, constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The structures are completely overgrown with vegetation and are only observable from the agricultural penetration road that runs alongside them.

b790cf1a85079e43.text: The nuraghe is largely invisible due to vegetation, but mainly because its lithic components have been dismantled and reused to build dry-stone structures nearby (themselves now abandoned). Because of this, its location is difficult to determine.

b7a67eea03190549.text: It is a domus carved into a flat rocky outcrop and consists of two rooms with a vaguely circular plan, aligned along the same axis and both opening to the south-east, separated by a partition with a door; the walls are finely finished, while the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.

b7a8baf260042eb4.text: The Lu Brandali complex nuraghe consists of a nuraghe with an outer wall, a village, a giants' tomb, a series of "tafone" tombs, and shelters beneath rock. To reach the Archaeological Site of Lu Brandali from the traffic light on Via Nazionale in Santa Teresa Gallura, one turns left towards Capo Testa, after about 700 m; on the left-hand side, the main entrance is accessed.

b7caa24aab685c50.text:
They are located in the territory of the comune of Busachi (OR).

At least 4 domus de janas are visible.

The necropolis should include at least  8 domus de janas.

b7cc65d96dc11247.text: Baetyl with two concavities almost on the "head". Probably for the attachment of lithic horns.

b7d38f312df38140.text:
The collapses affecting the Nuragic monument make it impossible to identify the entrance.

Collapses are also visible in the upper part, preventing any view of the inner chamber.

In this area a few courses of stones can be seen leaning against the bedrock.

On the northern side, next to the central tower and a rock outcrop, there is a structure with an entrance that appears to belong to a courtyard or a Nuragic hut.

b7de56d28c2cd368.text: It is a sarcophagus similar to those of Su Cannau and sos Terrelas. Ready for burial, or simply ready to be carried to the deceased? Roman period or merely medieval? Or belonging to the period of the Giudicati, as part of the personal or family heritage of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro.

b7e327308f520206.text:
The complex currently comprises 15 domus de janas.

The underground chambers, located at a considerable elevation above the plain (ranging from a minimum of 0.60 m to a maximum of 4.00 m), were originally accessible via stone steps; today, collapses and fractures in the rock wall make access particularly difficult.

b7ef931dfa0bbebb.text: Stunning single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed. It features an intact tholos and an anti-clockwise staircase.

b7f1c8a020d7e56d.text: It is located near the Nuragic spring on Musuleu. It appears to be a Nuragic-period structure.

b80afdadd84c0c8e.text: The Aresti Nuraghe lies on the border between the municipalities of Narbolia and Seneghe and is located about 1 km northeast of Narbolia, near the SP 11. It is a complex nuraghe in good state of preservation. The main tower is accessible and features a fine entrance with a covered corridor and an intact tholos in the internal chamber.

b8189615e83deb90.text:
It consists of a few basal circles that nevertheless define its construction character precisely; this character belongs to a broader human context in the surrounding territory with numerous other features close by. Its function as a lookout, or if you prefer as a defensive post, is paramount.

- Nuraghe del mestolo. In the matter of kitchen utensils it is curious that this nuraghe lies about one kilometre as the crow flies from Nuraghe Cogàlzos (see entry) which means "spoons (of bone)". See Truddàriga.mu

b8202a3e98db4c54.text: De Chirigu Village, the one to the north-west of the nuraghe of the same name, even though immersed in dense vegetation, shows several clearly distinguishable wall stretches belonging to probable huts, mostly rectangular in shape. At the far end, to the north-north-west, there is a circular structure (diameter about 10 m) that probably served as a meeting hut, against whose south side a rectangular structure is abutted. Numerous pottery fragments from various periods are present.

b82058234bfe80e2.text: The tomb is covered by vegetation and can only be found by following the dry stone wall on the western side.

b826d2f5a9e8b964.text: It was a smaller tower (diameter of about 8 m) compared to the Susu nuraghe. It probably served as a watchtower. It was certainly repurposed during the Roman period, as evidenced by terraces, pit tombs, and lithic material found in the area. After the bulldozer operations during reforestation, very few traces remain.

b84a7e8f942c5906.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan that reaches 29 m in length including the collapse debris closest to the monument.

Its state of preservation allows the structure to be followed in general around its entire outer perimeter, which was not affected by any refacing of the masonry. It is difficult to identify where the entrance opened, probably to be located in the southern quadrant.

b85b7fd8cefe8b12.text: Diroccato, only the first courses are visible. It must have been of considerable size, having a base diameter of about 15 metres.

b87ef8467826af4b.text: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.

b87fa4e0f4ec2130.text: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, in poor condition and partly hidden by vegetation, only the funerary corridor, the exedra and numerous shaped ashlars remain, showing that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry. The ashlars, very carefully made, include the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size, and an element of uncertain definition on which one face has a framed, raised boss.

b897a50228feb0fd.text: Around the monument extends the Nuragic village over a large area, with in particular two huts in good state of preservation. To the south-west there is a pond (Paule – from which the site gets its name) that very likely served as a water reservoir.

b8c1cac5d496a796.text: Remains of a nuraghe, possibly never completed

b8cec15197d60037.text: A singular funerary monument, a prehistoric tomb entirely cut into the rock. Discovered not many years ago, archaeologists regard it as a collective burial datable to the end of the Middle Bronze Age and therefore include it among the Nuragic-period giants' tombs. Its structure, however, is completely different from the usual giants' tomb types, both the coursed ones and those with a stele.

b8fa8812ed2f0d80.text: Scant remains of a small nuraghe
