b9353b2353f3610b.text: Two other domus de janas are visible in the vicinity.

b93e81cf7ec8f9be.text: Tomb with corridor and semicircular exedra

b93fa229a94c87b6.text: It lies about 300 metres below the associated nuraghe. It is built of isodomic ashlar blocks. In the vestibule in front of it there are stone benches, and in front of the entrance a hole cut in the rock acts as an overflow for the threshold level. The spring is still active and functioning. A temporary structure of concrete blocks has been built all around the spring to protect it from the weather, vegetation and animals.

b94e51cc9956ff4e.text: The Tutturuddu nuraghe is located on the first promontory after the Nuridda nuraghe, guarding a path descending towards the village of Tuili. Of this Nuragic testimony, only faint traces remain. The name Tutturuddu derives from the Sardinian word tutturu (mattarello), referring to the shape recognizable in the remains of the ancient structure.

b957464684163884.text: Nuragic settlement with a single-tower nuraghe built of sandy limestone blocks. Middle Bronze Age pottery. The landscape setting of the nuraghe has been radically altered since the site was recorded; nevertheless, traces worthy of protection remain.

b9952e66bd57cb10.text: The domus de janas that make up this necropolis, one of the most extensive and significant in Sardinia, are carved into the vertical face and the plateau of a trachytic outcrop – about 10 m high and oriented to the south – and are arranged in about twenty burials, mostly situated at a certain height above the countryside level.

b99dce64c1e7ee15.text:
Reduced to a state of complete ruin, likely due to road excavation works and land improvement projects. It is confused with the one slightly farther away at Pedru Canu.

Nuraghe of the smilace (Smilax aspera). It is very likely a paleo-Sardinian term. It indicates that at the time the name was first used, the monument was covered with smilace, a thorny climbing plant.

b9acef5c068dddc1.text: Domus de janas with a chamber having a collapsed ceiling.

b9aeceb16c7814fc.text: The Orconale complex features a bastioned tower with a courtyard. The main tower has an ogee profile. Surrounding it are the remains of a large Nuragic settlement, including a megaron temple where a model of a nuraghe was found, possibly belonging to a basin similar to that of Su Monte Sorradile.

b9bc25c9d33a3bd1.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The entrance, opening to the south, is lintelled and gives access to the corridor; to its left opens the stairwell of the helical staircase that led to the upper chamber, which no longer exists. The inner chamber is well preserved except for the top of the false dome, which has collapsed. Two facing niches open inside the chamber, oriented respectively east and west.

b9cd9a454a25f28a.text: It was a large stone cist, dug into the ground, oval in shape, with walls lined by stone slabs; inside it contained the remains of 15 inhumations and various items that formed part of the funerary equipment, typical of the Early Bronze Age (Bunnannaro culture).

b9e345ce7d81c0fb.text: Built of local granite boulders, it has a roughly triangular plan and shows mixed features of corridor nuraghi (the most archaic type of nuraghe) and tholos nuraghi (an evolution of the former). The central chamber with its tholos roof is still intact, while the side chambers have partially collapsed. The building has two entrances, one to the south-west (the main entrance) and another to the south-east.

ba0596bed0707867.text:
Collective tombs of the Nuragic period, 1600–1800 BC, built in the final phase of the Middle Bronze Age, 1500 BC, and used until the Final Bronze Age phase, 1100–900 BC.

The elongated burial chamber has side walls of limestone blocks laid in corbelled courses, closed at the far end by a slab set on edge. The outer wall face is apsidal at the rear. The entrance, facing east in Tomb no. 1 and south-east in Tomb no. 2, is preceded by a semicircular exedra space.

ba08a618a34f0d16.text: Unfortunately, numerous damages—often unconscious—have been caused by human activity aimed at reclaiming a few square metres of pasture.

ba1064d73c69c007.text: Archaeological area comprising various remains among which Cart Ruts; menhir; different types of cairns.

ba121513dfb54522.text: The central tower, almost completely destroyed (maximum surviving height 2.70 metres), is built, like the rest of the visible structures, in polygonal masonry, using exclusively granite blocks. On the south side a trilithic structure survives that could be interpreted as the remains of the entrance to a mural staircase giving access to the tower's terrace or to a possible second chamber.

ba15d29618f3ad6f.text: An allée couverte is also present at the site of Chinzana. It is a tomb composed of a rectangular corridor with a remaining length of 5.20 m and a width of 0.95 m, formed by slabs set in a coltello fashion, seven of which still remain in situ; the covering slabs are missing. Around the tomb, on the north-west, south-east, and south sides, some stones of the peristalite project.

ba39eeb662820204.text: Granite nuraghe, composed of large and medium-sized blocks. It appears to be a corridor nuraghe with two towers, with documented remains: a section of the central tower's wall on the northern side, consisting of three courses, and the interior of the upper part of the secondary tower.

babf7ecc86d213bf.text: Single-tower nuraghe, attached to a colonial-era farmhouse. Very close to the asphalted road.

bad298d783bce6e4.text: Built of granite blocks quarried on the spot, the nuraghe consists of a circular tower about 4.5 m in diameter and an added pseudo-elliptical body (with a major axis of about 12 m and a minor axis of about 8 m). No traces of huts are currently visible, but it is likely that some structures were built against the site's perimeter and that the natural tafoni were exploited for various uses.

bad5820016839520.text: It includes at least eight domus de janas, of which only three are detectable in plan.

bae16389dbc7aac8.text: Remains of a probable quadrangular fortification built by the Nuragic people. It survives as a large megalithic wall running along the eastern edge of the plateau that forms the mountain summit. The wall is broken by an entrance leading to a corridor parallel to the wall and roofed with basalt slabs laid flat. The place name “Sa Rocca 'e su Para” given to this mountain may refer to the use the Camaldolese friars made of the fortress in the Middle Ages.

baf0cf45ff29ed69.text: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.

bafe6ef79e8a34ff.text: The tombs number about ten and vary in form, from the simplest single-cell tombs with an antechamber and a single chamber, to those with circular plan and various recesses, a hearth, and pilasters that separate the small chambers. They are cut into the soft tuff rock. Threatened by unauthorized archaeological excavations.

baff369c9d99db4a.text: Semi-diroccato. Twelve courses of stones remain, with a breach to the south-east, possibly the entrance. The prism-shaped stones easily interlock, allowing precise connections between them, though they are not arranged in horizontal layers. The external wall is vertical and difficult to access, making it hard to enter the interior.

bb46772a7f080c00.text: It is four-lobed, with a central tower surrounded by a bastion against which the other four towers are built. In places it is quite ruined, yet it still reaches a height of more than ten metres; the ground floor is well preserved, while the upper floor lacks its roof although the masonry survives to a certain height. As often happens in multi-storey towers, the upper floor was characterised by a large window.

bb6b4981a20909cb.text: The cemetery consists of two groups, comprising 7 and 31 units, of hypogean domus de janas; only one is monocellular, while the others have more complex floor plans, and one of them contains up to eleven chambers. They are of the "vertical and horizontal projection" type, meaning accessible either through a vertical shaft or via a descending corridor, the latter usually equipped with steps leading into the vestibule.

bb6cf49935423a21.text:
It is also known as Sa Pinnettedda.

The circumstances of its discovery and the materials recovered place the monument chronologically at the end of phase II of the Nuragic civilization (1500–1200 BC),

bba03d5d90e849d5.text: Giants' tomb marked in an article by Gallura Oggi, already included in the Geoportal, alongside which a windmill has been erected.

bbc059560b397eee.text: Single-cell domus de janas located near the municipal road

bbc4d1b409b31f3a.text: Nuraghe covered with ficus indica plants and disturbed by a structure that has developed beside it.

bbcec42aa2c704fc.text: Located in the San Simplicio valley, on the ground surface only a few fallen stones remain.

bbe01eb28c39fa97.text: The excavation revealed a rectangular building divided into two rooms and set inside an enclosed area. It is thought that the building had a religious function. The excavations yielded finds datable between the 8th and 7th centuries BC. The setting is bleak and typical, with abandoned military structures (built inside the sanctuary), an abandoned restaurant and a large tarmac car park.

bbfcfab4cd667700.text:
The Margone nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill and is largely hidden by dense vegetation, especially prickly pear and wild olive.

Its important function is emphasised by the complexity of the structure: it is a three-lobed nuraghe with a central tower 12 m in diameter. Around it one can trace stretches of polygonal masonry, built of medium-sized limestone blocks, that link three secondary towers to the main tower.

bc0c588d1554968f.text:
The archaeological site stands on a rocky cliff of granitic nature, bounded by three spires lying about 30 and 50 m apart.

The area covers about 2.0 ha; the settlement is hard to read in plan because of the vegetation and its very poor state of preservation.

The site is surrounded by an outer wall that encloses the nuraghe, the two watchtowers and, in the centre, the Nuragic huts, while other huts lie outside the wall on the east side.

bc1e4dabbe316ead.text: A row of subterranean wall face remains.

bc425ca14ddccfa5.text:
The site where Sa Murta 'e Pizzus stands, at 520 metres above sea level, is beautiful and evocative, set in the greenery and silence of an area little touched by man. Numerous grey-pink granite rocks sculpted by time are present, and the Gulf of the Angels can be seen from the hill.

Near this funerary complex there are some stones marking the circular perimeter of several Nuragic huts,

bc44d6fcf3e3cc38.text: It has a particular form, because part of it is built upon a huge stone that has been partially cut out and adapted to a funerary function.

bc6e8b697ddd1934.text:
There are nuraghi that are not only grandiose in themselves but also for the landscape in which they stand.

The nuraghe Iscolca is one of these: it dominates the Semestene valley and those of the surrounding villages. Not easily reached, it is accessed after a steep climb through dry, rocky pastures, among protruding stones that hint at the ancient existence of a large village.

Nothing of this monument appears to have been excavated, and only the tholos of the second level is accessible.

bc704cb0d407c6de.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe and is in an advanced state of decay. Some elements of the construction are still visible, however. For the moment it shelters a few domestic animals right on the main entrance. I want to exorcise the situation by thinking of the great people of the nuraghi… "from the stars… to the stables" if institutions and civil conscience linger and persist in abandoning our monuments. mu

bc914836ef57d764.text: Dug in a low trachytic formation, it features a bull's-head protome in the antechamber.

bc9c4009dd4aed35.text: "Domus de janas of Gianna Oria Porru or Solottos; a short distance from the Rio Mannu or Rio Posada trench, on the opposite side of Nuraghe Eritta (no. 5). Two small chambers cut into limestone, each with a low doorway and border. Empty. In the Antioco Sanna ground" (Taramelli, 933).

bd31e143145d02c6.text: The nuraghe, near an agricultural farm, features a small tower added.

bd31fe65032d4215.text: Probable Nuragic well in poor condition and relatively isolated. It still has an active perennial spring. Noted and photographed by Sergio Melis.

bd3efac46119921e.text: A proto-nuraghe later transformed into a single-tower nuraghe,

bd666f58ec88dfc2.text: Not far from the three domus de janas of the same name: an elongated chamber structure with walls built of courses of medium-sized stones, small ones, and a roof formed by the rock into which it is cut.

bd89cea477199659.text: Nuraghe with village almost completely covered by soil and vegetation. The most visible part has been destroyed by excavations. Surrounded by greenery and numerous streams, other nuraghi such as Sa Dom' e S'Orku are visible from here.

bd8a26fff2c72351.text: A village composed of several circular huts of which only a few courses and the collapsed structure in the centre remain, plus two of complex structure. Of these two, the first, rectangular, consists of five rooms: four roughly circular ones at the four sides and one rectangular one in the centre, perhaps a courtyard; the second, oval, has four rooms, three of them round and the fourth formed by the wall joining the three rooms, perhaps a courtyard. Enclosures with cyclopean walls are present.

bd8adc19a336be54.text:
The nuraghe is surrounded by a square curtain wall, within which circular remains of huts are visible, possibly forming a small settlement.

The perimeter of the enclosing wall, at its upper section, features several stretches of a path carved into the wall thickness.

bd949709db071e94.text: It was marked on the IM map but is now completely vanished.

bda639a19c1d7913.text: Collapsed nuraghe covered in vegetation. Probable single-tower nuraghe.

bda6be9db0252fb1.text: It is a tower with a circular outer perimeter, a maximum diameter of about 10 m, and an internal chamber that is approximately elliptical, as far as can be judged from its present state of preservation. The whole northern sector is badly damaged, and the east and west sides have been affected by illicit excavations that caused further gaps in the perimeter, later patched by an attempt to “restore” the masonry in the eastern quadrant carried out by the Sisters of the Good Shepherd.

bdb2b91d16001669.text:
It is located to the south, near the border with the territory of Usellus.

It is a simple type and is very damaged.

bdb701105df8dd5f.text: Single-tower nuraghe built of chalky sandstone. Nuragic settlement with finds of ceramics from the middle Bronze Age. The site is neither accessible nor easily readable at present, and a study for a philological reconstruction of the site would be advisable.

bdc49df8637c89ca.text: The domus has an ESE-facing entrance and a cruciform ground plan. The tomb structure consists of a trapezoidal doorway leading into a sub-rectangular antechamber and then into a rectangular main chamber, on three sides of which are three raised parietal niches. The niches are oriented SSW, NNW and NNE. Originally they were decorated with small pilasters set in the centre of each niche.

bddbcd9c9189ca2d.text: Curtain wall of uncertain function, of clearly Nuragic craftsmanship. At the centre of the site there is a singular structure consisting of a kind of silo cut into the rock, with straight walls except at the end (at 2.65 m), where it narrows; the edge, partially worked and squared externally with notches, features some irregular cups.

bddf50e93c0348a7.text: Of this monument, noted by Lamarmora and other authors, but not by Taramelli, no trace remains. It seems to have been located near the railway and destroyed during the works related to the construction of the Borore railway station.

bde94254e20a320e.text: The nuraghe has an irregular elliptical shape; the total circumference is about 50 m. This massive structure is crossed lengthwise by a corridor 15.2 m long, running right through with opposed entrances and lined on both walls by wide openings that lead to large niches — that is, cavities — or to the stairwell that gives access to the upper floor. The straight corridor has a trapezoidal section with a flat ceiling formed by 11 slabs.

bdf51dd330ca05d4.text: Complex nuraghe, cannot be definitively classified by its state of degradation or by the significant burial of its structures; in the vicinity, traces of an inhabited settlement, village.

be11dcce95c72723.text: It consists of a façade and a small courtyard. On the façade there is an architrave lintel opening for the collection of water. The space has a semicircular plan and walls that gently slope inwards.

be1da0546fea6195.text: In this sacred well, of which no further information is available and which probably went completely out of use, some bronze figures of great importance were found, including the banner above the votive sword and the warrior with a shield and four daggers.

be2d63c873279540.text: Nuraghe in good condition, built of red granite stones. Equipped with a spiral staircase. Likely part of a complex nuraghe.

be5f807049fc0485.text: Nuraghe of which only a small amount remains due to construction in immediately adjacent areas

be6253725e0803f3.text: There are numerous sarcophagi, each made from large trachyte and basalt blocks shaped into large rectangular prisms of considerable dimensions (2.50 x 0.90 x 0.90 m). Since the blocks are placed here and there without any defined or logical order, it is inferred that the site was a place where these sarcophagi were constructed.

be7ff15717b10bc4.text:
The nuraghe, situated at an altitude of about 794 m, is of mixed type, featuring elements both of corridor nuraghes and tholos nuraghes. It consists of a central tower to which a three-lobed bastion is attached.

Around the nuraghe is a village of huts, and at a short distance, two giants' tombs and a dolmen.

be99aebc35660776.text: Single-tower built on the summit of a cliff, almost completely collapsed, walls about two metres thick, previously used as a shelter for animals.

be9a5273ef7db97e.text: The menhir, located within a flat field, is about 1.67 m high, with cup-shaped decorations.

bead79495695649c.text:
It is a large proto-nuraghe with a single tower, equipped with some auxiliary structures, built with enormous basalt blocks.  

Due to collapses, access to the interior is possible only partially.

bebc3a915037d093.text: The structure's upper portion is visible because it is buried. It consists of a larger tower joined by walls to a smaller tower. The features best visible and documented are in the north, where 2–3 courses of the towers and the wall connecting them emerge. The stone used is limestone.

bebe5d083b3343c2.text: From a period subsequent to the adjacent Monti Pintau II, about seven courses of ashlars strongly densified remain.

bed31693db829149.text: Nuraghe characterized by a calcareous lintel, white on dark walls. The tholos has collapsed inward.

bedbd488d5086143.text: The nuraghe is easily identifiable as it is located near the reservoirs of the hydro-voro system of the Central Sardinia Irrigation Consortium. On the eastern slope of this hill, large slabs of shale emerge from the ground; however, a more detailed assessment of the site is not possible due to its very poor state of preservation.

beed40f4013e5018.text: This is the nuraghe Monti di Deu, still partly buried, in a good state of preservation; it stands on the summit of Monte di Deu on the Limbara massif, on the Calangianus side.

bf14ec8b16a4a59d.text:
On site and in the surrounding area there are several alignments composed of large basaltic blocks and at least two large tumuli resulting from the destruction of structures due to past agricultural works carried out in the area.

Oxidized obsidian fragments appear along a path, and in the exposed section corresponding to the left side of the path, north of the Temannu nuraghe.

bf4fbccfb84f205f.text: Nuraghe with a system of outer walls surrounding it, visible from the adjacent path.

bf62c9098b2ea8ad.text: There are some subsquared granite blocks, on two courses, attributable to a nuragic structure.

bf6cc3755e85b910.text: Nuraxi – Pauli Onigus shows few and uncertain traces of a settlement in its immediate vicinity, while remains of a village can be seen at Pauli Onigus, a locality about 200 m to the south but separated by the course of the Riu Cardaxu. The extent of the villages, based on the materials visible on the surface, almost always varies between 7,000 and 10,000 sq m, apart from the village of Is Arruinalis, with remains mostly of the BFII-FI phase, which covers an area of about 4 hectares.

bf7ef95e7f5fcc3c.text: The Mura Craba Nuraghe is located near a quarry, about 2 km east of Bauladu. It is a single-tower nuraghe built with basalt blocks in good state of preservation.

bf8e5111a6734ab8.text: The area is heavily anthropogenically modified from ancient times. The site's significance is evident from the numerous surface exposures and the distinctiveness of these features, which are not found elsewhere on the island. Currently, a project focused on the architecture of the Giants' Tombs is under study, with researchers preparing a specific book on the subject.

bf92e484a11b4390.text:
The nuraghe is heavily eroded.

In the vicinity lies a pre-Nuragic settlement dating to the Neolithic period.

bfb710779d21c1e3.text: The Nuragic complex of Tamùli is an important archaeological site dating to the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC). The site was already well known in the first half of the nineteenth century, thanks largely to the description given by the scholar General Alberto Della Marmora in his Voyage en Sardaigne, published in 1840. In the accompanying atlas he illustrated the nuraghe, two of the three giants' tombs present, the baetyls and several ashlars on the spot with numerous drawings.

bfb96f65a207cb25.text: Natural cave characterized by a large chamber used as a sacred area where various votive offerings (small lamps and miniature cauldrons) were found on a natural stone altar shaped like a countertop. Occupation spans from the Neolithic to the Iron Age and includes the San Ciriaco, Bonannaro, and Nuragic cultures.

bfbec558c02d98b7.text:
Complex nuraghe, at the main tower a bastion was added, composed of at least three towers, though a fourth tower may have existed, currently invisible due to the dense vegetation covering the entire nuraghe.

It retains the tholos intact.

bfca1b6f9b97023c.text: The nuraghe of Tuppedili, located along the road to Mandas, is of particular archaeological significance. Still awaiting a complete study, so far excavations have yielded a large number of artifacts datable to the Nuragic and Roman periods.

bfdba63136e3370d.text: Single-cell domus de janas partially collapsed

bfdd7ba25394ac2c.text: Two tombs partially collapsed and eroded beneath a striking natural dolmen

bfe4e1f5f7f2057f.text: damaged nuraghe near a complex of domus de janas

c042b2c11794450b.text:
Of the nuraghe only a few base courses remain, with a maximum height of about 2 m, composed of large polygonal basaltic blocks arranged in a circular pattern.

The internal chamber is completely blocked by debris from collapse and covered by a thick layer of vegetation, including brambles and shrubs. The entrance, now invisible, was oriented to the south.

c0733884b213b71d.text:
It is located in the municipality of Bolotana.

Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber.

The nuraghe is cut by a recent wall.

The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

c07a742c970361d0.text: It is located in the municipality of Orani and consists of 8 domus de janas.

c086d5e01785f29d.text:
The building, situated in a dominant position at the eastern end of the named hill, appears as a three-lobed complex nuraghe with a village surrounding it.

Here too there must have been a king who dominated the entire plain.

From the remains it seems that Romans also arrived later.

c0957a3840de8697.text: Complex cave with three entrances (two of which are artificial), heavily altered and plundered of its beauty as it was previously used partially as an onyx quarry and as a wartime shelter. It was frequently used during the Early Bronze Age. A small park has been set up at the entrance, managed by an association that periodically organizes guided visits.

c09b3c1b05c0cb03.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, a ground-floor chamber flanked by two subsidiary rooms, and a further room above the corridor. It probably had an added structure (a courtyard?) and an outer wall enclosing various related structures of the adjoining settlement. The nuraghe is easily reached from the road called Valle dei Nuraghi, following an unsurfaced track that lies on private property, so access is not guaranteed.

c0e9f9d5ca9035e2.text: The area around the Nuraghe Su Angiu is further enriched and distinctive due to the nearby Punic and Roman villages, the remains of which are still visible today.

c101770e312e6522.text: It is located within the municipal territory of Pula (CA) inside the archaeological area of Nora.

c12b9a140cba8c6c.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a nearby Nuragic spring, in good conservation, features a rectangular entrance with an architrave (approximately 0.95 m by 0.90 m). From this entrance, access is gained—via a staircase of four steps, each 24 cm high—into a dromos (length 1.00 m; width 1.06 m; height 1.82 m).

c14ea2c53f9027de.text: It is also known as Matzone (Maxia records Massone). Su crastu covaccadu probably comes from the presence, not far away, of a giants' tomb that had a trilithon and a cist covered with a flat lintel, hence su crastu covaccadu. It is a single-tower nuraghe and its features cannot be made out because it is completely covered by plants and bushes. However, the Nuragic spring that supplied drinking water (so the owners told me) until a few years ago is noted.mu

c18993cbc9a3c3b5.text: Known as Coarittos nuraghe, but there is no trace of that type of monument.

c19c6c1da4f53754.text:
It is practically destroyed. The few remains that allow it to be identified consist of two courses of stones, just emerging from the ground, that define the tomb corridor. In the area of the exedra (itself more guessed at than actually present) lies the so-called dentilled ashlar, not in its original position; its presence indicates that the burial was built with squared ashlars laid in courses, like the nearby Sa Presone II.

The monument lies in the municipality of Bultei (SS).

c1a9f1fb0a5a5226.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a giants' tomb nearby

c1d0e04376ca37f0.text: On the summit of the nuraghe ruins, during the post-war period a watchroom was built for the sentinels of the powder magazine. Single-tower, rock-cut, collapsed and buried.

c1f3da4885e4c01a.text: It is in a state of considerable degradation. Covered by moss and shrubbery, it is inaccessible. Constructed of trachyte. From the outside, a small window can be seen, high up, facing east. The walls still standing are about four metres high.

c1fbf6b751123a8d.text:
It is a village of considerable size; dozens of circular structures can be made out on the ground, mainly to the south-west of the nuraghe of the same name.

Given the presence of four other nuraghi within a radius of just a few kilometres and an exceptional view over the Gulf of Asinara (on clear days ships off Porto Torres are clearly visible), the village probably played a strategic role.

c23a530dbdefcb8a.text: With the presence of two nuraghi, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, it forms a significant complex for reconstructing the historical events of the territory. The single-tower Nuraghe Corru 'e Oe stands on a small plateau visually linked with the four-lobed Aidu and with three others that appear to have belonged to a single defensive and territorial surveillance system. Near the nuraghe the remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;

c24fd14c0f4d26e8.text: Giants' tomb with a cyclopean corridor in good condition, while the exterior appears buried and partially eroded.

c26ce1d43afa2cb5.text: It is located a short distance from Lake Cuga; as can be seen in the photos, only 2 or 3 courses of stones from the foundation remain, which give a clear idea of the internal layout of this single-tower nuraghe.

c2789e572285a7a7.text: The monument is named after the ancient name of the area where it is located (Nixias) and the unusual hole positioned on the right side of the large stele, which was believed (perhaps incorrectly) to have been used in historical times to tie horses. The monument is of great interest as it represents a rare example of a giants' tomb with a centinated stele in central and southern Sardinia.

c29e463b3791083e.text:
The nuraghe is inaccessible due to the presence of a high metal mesh.

Nearby is a menhir, always within the fenced area.

c29e717c57f74c69.text:
A semi-circular exedra oriented to the south-east, bounded by large orthostatic slabs; an elongated body (length 6.15 m – width 3 m at the junction with the exedra – and 2 m in the terminal section) with a burial chamber 4.43 m long and 0.55 m wide.

In the centre of the exedra the lower part of the bilithic arched stele is visible, truly majestic (width 1.10 – thickness 0.22) with a trapezoidal doorway (width 0.24 – height 0.20).

Another arched fragment of the stele lies overturned on the tomb.

c2b13a1ba1170022.text: It is a nuraghe that is particularly dear to me, not only because it was the site of a discovery of an object that I donated to the Sanna Museum in Sassari, an object that has unfortunately disappeared. I have monitored the nuraghe over the years and reported its imminent collapse. I have visited it inside and believe I am one of the few to have ever known the full extent of its internal equipment.

c2b96c451968dadd.text: Tomb I features a elongated, apsidal tombstone, including a burial chamber and a large semicircular exedra facing it. For tomb II, situated to the south-east and overgrown by collapse and earth, only the profile of the apsidal tombstone and the exedra can be identified. Tomb III, possibly a dolmenic burial, is in very poor condition of preservation.

c2bf05a03a0e7582.text: Pre-Nuragic menhir about 5 metres high, still standing upright. This menhir has been named after a giantess, a figure frequently appearing in Sardinian folk legends. The presence of many other menhirs in the area attests to the widespread nature of megalithic religious practices.

c2e335b02b7b45d2.text: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed and looted. Only some stones of the outer wall face and the circular base alignment remain; no other elements are detectable.

c2e5532a26f68d3d.text: It consists of a central tower and three auxiliary towers connected together by stairs and corridors, some of which are no longer accessible today. Access to the ground floor and the upper level—currently without a roof—is provided via a staircase on the right. The ground floor chamber, of considerable size, is characterized by the presence of three large niches reaching up to 4 metres in height.

c2ed22b31cc3f192.text: The probable Nuragic village consists of several structures that were almost certainly reused up to the last century. The huts, whose remains can be glimpsed, were probably originally circular and rectangular in shape. Parts of the walls survive, built of semi-worked stones of varying sizes. The very dense vegetation, which in places has grown inside the structures, has contributed to their collapse. About 200 m to the east lies the Noccus pond.

c3189371f2675a01.text: It consists of four underground chambers. Probable location.

c3217b8ab15431f8.text: Complex nuraghe partially dismantled, with only the low courses remaining

c3687b62d49f4f3b.text: The complex corridor nuraghe Sa Conca ‛e sa Cresia originated as a corridor nuraghe in the Middle Bronze Age and was remodelled into a tholos nuraghe in the Recent Bronze Age. The surrounding areas were landscaped in the 1990s. From the tholos one enters corridors dug by tomb robbers that lead inside the tholoi. Outside, to the west and south, two elliptical vaulted structures, now ruined and of uncertain purpose, are reported.

c37b50af9963126b.text: “Su Posidu”, meaning treasure. A very unusual well set between two enormous granite boulders, about 60–80 centimetres apart and 5–6 metres high. A series of schist steps, set between the two rock spurs, deliberately worked and cut, form a double staircase that allowed easy access to the central part of the well, where the precious liquid was found: water, what treasure was as precious to the people of that time as water?

c38e1f17ac2b81b4.text: Complex quadrilobate nuraghe of considerable size. Never excavated and located within a private property, thus inaccessible. It is distinguished by some particular artefacts placed inside, including a menhir.

c3d7d29689185372.text: Single-tower nuraghe of tuff, with a megalithic wall attached that encircles the promontory. Located within a private farm.

c3f49bddc3abf3e4.text:
It is located in the territory of Muravera, at a short distance from the Cuili Piras menhirs and near the border with the territory of Castiadas.

More specifically, it is a proto-nuraghe.

Of particular interest is an entrance, for which the lintel is well preserved.

c4081ec797e22d07.text: Almost nothing of the tower remains.

c40f2c48f6283743.text: Possible corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, entrance to the south-east, helical staircase on the left leading to the second level now collapsed. Studied by Lamarmora in 1830.

c420ff0b01683318.text: Complex nuraghe of mixed and trenched type, with a central tower and two additional towers. The central chamber, slightly elliptical in shape, features two niches and a roof of slabs rather than a tholos, which brings it closer to a proto-nuraghe. Built of granite. The exact location of the nuraghe is not confirmed and is not marked on the IGM map.

c422caa459b7ecdd.text:
The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of huts. The nuraghe comprises a central tower refaced by a bastion with a straight-convex-curvilinear profile that incorporates two minor towers to the ENE and SSE.

The village, dating to the early Iron Age, extends to the NW of the nuraghe. The dwellings, sub-circular and sub-rectangular in shape, are arranged in "blocks" with several rooms that generally connect onto a central courtyard.

c46aea889e9e24d5.text: Almost imperceptible remains of a nuraghe

c47174acb8a32eb0.text: Illegal diggers have exposed some courses of the wall of a small elliptical structure.

c4792e1605fa1159.text: It was a tomb of the "architectural façade" type. The façade is completely ruined and hidden by vegetation. Currently it lies beneath the viaduct of the new Uri-Scala Cavalli road. Source: Wikimapia

c49e5ddcf0d4d103.text: The domus has an ESE-facing entrance and a cruciform ground plan like the previous one, but with a different structure. It has a dromos raised above ground level that leads to a rectangular vestibule giving access to the main chamber. The chamber is rectangular, and on its three sides, oriented SSW, NNW and NNE, there are three parietal niches raised above the floor that originally had a central pilaster.

c49ef908759eb5f1.text: Nuraghe of which only a few courses remain

c4a4e73012ec3d0b.text:
It is a Neolithic burial cut into a schist ridge near a watercourse.

The burial consists of a single cell with a sub-circular plan. Traces of the entrance hatchway can be seen.

To the right on entering there is a small niche/cupboard. There is no chronological evidence, either because no finds were recovered or because the structure was used several times, even in recent times, and has been completely disturbed; indeed it lacks a floor.

c4a818853d20ca5e.text: It is one of three nuraghe that surround the artificial pond along the perimeter of the former Madau estate. The basal circle is formed by cyclopean stones that give it a imposing presence, almost acting as a guardian of the surrounding valley, which itself is heavily anthropized and rich in other notable features. Hill of the deer.

c4f3a327a835d6a3.text: Likely a three-lobed nuraghe, if not even four-lobed; the planimetry is almost impossible to read due to the poor state of preservation.

c501599a31316fd9.text: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.

c51bfdcb7a8cab48.text: Currently, in the site we can observe an old stone enclosure, below which several stones belonging to the nuraghe are visible.

c5297c1f4611e70a.text: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower closed by a three-lobed bastion. It still rises, despite its current residual height of only five metres, above the plain of Birori, offering a breathtaking view. It was the subject of an excavation campaign in 1995.

c5332c07e7b49db9.text: This nuraghe is laid out longitudinally and has several cavities (presumably towers..) of small size.. four can be seen from the aerial photo, but there are at least five if not more... it is really interesting and it would be worth clearing the parts still standing, today cluttered with the collapse of the upper parts, to understand better how it was laid out; the towers are small and it is not clear whether they were access ramps for an upper structure or something else.

c53cc9327c752dc0.text: The nuraghe structures, of the simple tholos type, show considerable erosion and are covered by dense vegetation. Partially emerging at the summit of the small ridge formed by the structures and the soil covering them are some courses composed of local basalt blocks.

c54e24aac28814eb.text: The Nuragic structures that closed the two entrances to the Domusnovas cave were already described in 1840 by Angius. He says that at the first entrance, on the left, there are the remains of a cyclopean wall that closed it off. A small doorway by the cave wall is as high as the ordinary stature of a man; to the left of the doorway a staircase 1.30 m wide led up onto the rampart where there were merlons and loopholes. At the exit there is another wall 3.20 m thick.

c55a1c858969da16.text: This is a single-tower nuraghe in a clearly degraded state. Nevertheless, its bulk and the harmony of its construction make it an interesting nuraghe both for its building techniques and its architectural features. It stands on a brown trachyte outcrop, and in places the base boulders merge with the natural rock, giving the structure solidity.

c5624e8719bd9c76.text:
The village of "Cuccuru Ambudu" extended over a broad hilly area (61 m a.s.l.) on the north-eastern outskirts of Serramanna, between the roads leading west to Serrenti and east to Villagreca.

The characteristics of the village, reconstructed through careful analysis of the finds, suggest it was already occupied in the pre-Nuragic period, in a phase datable between the Late Neolithic (Ozieri Culture) and the Chalcolithic (Monte Claro Culture).

c56bd894eeafb915.text: It is a completely collapsed nuraghe that retains a maximum height of 1.90 m.

c57fb86cdd738948.text: Remains of a nuragic hut near Mount Margherita or the Manu mountains.

c5b86672649447ad.text: Only the base of the tomb is visible, and what remains is almost entirely covered by vegetation.

c5bdb6bfeff2b695.text:
Situated on the southern bank of the Rio Berchida a short distance from the sea, it appears as a shapeless heap of collapse from which the upper part of the central tower can be glimpsed, and it can be inferred that additional structures were present.

On one side of the structure several courses of blocks roughly hewn from the local granite are visible, and damage caused by clandestine excavation is clearly evident.

c5f1bc81617587a0.text: Nuraghe dominating the landing points and the area below the coast. Walls in good condition. Open tholos, probably collapsed.

c600889faaa1001e.text: A burial of the Nuragic period, of dolmenic type, built with lithic orthostats inserted vertically and covered with horizontal slabs. The tomb's corridor is visible, while the elements of the exedra are likely incorporated into the dry-stone wall built along the front. On the front, lying upside down and, unfortunately, fragmented, is the beautiful arched stele.

c60ca45b26c1de04.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

Almost no description is needed as it is clearly visible in the satellite image.

c8b6c88638e3d210.text: It has a feature never described before: it is built "in the round": the water collects in an apsidal rear body.
