cebf6ba456488099.text: It is located within the territory of the comune of Uras; given the construction technique used, it is likely that the structure dates to the Nuragic period.

ceccc4cde1b4b80d.text: Today, in the territory of Serrenti, there are at least 12 sites with evidence of the Late Bronze II - Iron I periods (S'Urbale and Genna Maria facies)... Except for one, all the others are settlements that were already active during the Recent Bronze period. Only at Is Arruinalis, Monti Angurdu, and Monti Crastu do we find evidence extending into the Orientalizing and Archaic phases (7th–6th centuries BC).

cee02f6cb60aa0c7.text: Completely collapsed and overgrown with bushes. Like the nearby Zianeddu (B), it is classified as a "tancato" nuraghe: on the front face of the main tower there is a wall structure enclosing a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.

cf1bb874398b607a.text: Nuragic dolmen burial, with the funerary corridor remaining, composed of finely finished basalt slabs, without steles.

cf1c2743e056d511.text: The tomb follows the usual architectural layout: elongated and apsidal body (length 14.50 m – width 4/4.30 m), a wide curved exedra (current arc 11.70 m – arrow 3.25 m) and a rectangular corridor (length 11.55 m – average width 0.10 m and 0.55 m at the entrance). In summer 1982, excavation and partial restoration of the monument were carried out.

cf4a9722a92fb246.text: Complex nuraghe with a village, located very close to the better known Nuraghe Majore. At the central tower, which still retains an intact tholos chamber, a transverse-frontal bastion with two towers and an intermediate courtyard has been built. Moreover, a third tower, set back from the two front ones, is clearly identifiable, featuring a corridor of access and an intact tholos.

cf63e4ed23b70b5a.text: The structure composed of basalt blocks is rubble and collapsed. The remains are scattered over a wide area covered with vegetation.

cfa5309d2c50a322.text:
It consists of a temple, a nuraghe almost completely collapsed, a large circular hut, and a series of tombs "a tafone".

The temple at Malchittu undoubtedly represents the most interesting building in the complex, both for its excellent state of preservation and for the uniqueness of its construction, comparable to only a few other examples in Sardinia.

cfc98a6e7ec2849f.text: Sacred well that shows features of both a well and a Nuragic sacred well. Notable is the presence of a stone with a hollow inside.

cfd265edc13786ff.text: Single-tower nuraghe hardly accessible due to vegetation.

d00c0b43df45ca62.text: Site of Cuili Piras behind M. Su Crobu. The surrounding area is ploughed and access to the site is quite difficult. Unfortunately, the land was recently devastated by a widespread fire. The site is located within a private property and it is advisable to inform the landowners of one's presence.

d00de3c44f5f0aef.text:
The overall plan of the structure must have been quite irregular and adapted to the natural contours of the rock, which was incorporated over large stretches in the construction.

The remaining structure extends along a north:south axis of 7.35 m and an east:west axis of 0.78 m, and preserves a high point reaching up to 1.90 m above the camp level.

d014e7e036177489.text: In the middle of the forest, dug into trachyte and decorated on the portal with probable bull's-head protomes.

d038a9623b75689e.text: It takes its name from an old church. It stands on a small promontory on the right bank of the Riu Mannu. The lintel is broken and the whole monument is in a state of complete decay and abandonment. There were two entrances (one has collapsed) and several sacrificial stones. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is that the tholos, perfectly intact, was built with dark boulders formed from agglomerations of fossil shells. A rarity, since no trace of this type of material is found in the area.

d06d0d919d769554.text: Source very likely of Nuragic origin.

d07db71fc442d1a9.text: In total, the ruin still reveals only a few stones that form the basal circle, composed of white, friable limestone. mu

d0a51466f8a130d8.text: Nuraghe completely destroyed by quarrying activities

d0a9e6ec62a24b25.text:
The site exhibits a planimetric and architectural layout among the most remarkable produced by the Nuragic culture. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

The complex shows various construction phases characterized by the use of local stone: basalt from the Giara, which predominates, and calcareous marl.

d0b37496ca6c666c.text: Complex nuraghe with village. Damaged and difficult to read due to being covered by collapsed walls. Occupies an area used for agriculture and pastoralism. Built from granite blocks; only the central tower and the two lateral towers are visible.

d0b4f39f1bfd9135.text: Nuraghe with frontal bilobate addition. Today completely submerged by the waters of the Cuga basin. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes surrounding the Chessedu Cuga valley.

d0cbdc15b4bafeb7.text: The S'Ulumu well (Dorgali) features a circular cell with a short external vestibule, built in horizontal courses and covered by a tholos. Precisely because of its simple architectural and structural form, it served essentially as a functional water supply for the nearby village.

d0d0f0dab2a01bcc.text: Single-tower nuraghe reduced to ruins. Only a single circular wall section remains, about 4 metres high and featuring seven courses. The monument is almost completely destroyed, and the materials have been reused for the construction of animal enclosures and sheepfolds in recent times.

d0d2028b5a9f170e.text: Cut into a basalt wall, the tomb has its entrance facing west, 0.80 m below ground level; it is rectangular and well carved, set within a deep recess. The threshold has a drainage channel, and along the wall thickness, beside the jamb, there are two opposite recesses, perhaps to allow the closing slab to slide more easily. The chamber, irregularly semi-circular in plan, has a flat floor and a domed roof with curved walls.

d0d95ce95940ba14.text:
The complex consists of a nuraghe, an outer wall and a village.

The nuraghe comprises a central tower to which at least two lateral towers were added, now not fully detectable.

A large outer wall, incorporating at least four towers, with an irregular curvilinear course, surrounds the complex.

In the area in front, the remains of numerous huts and rectangular apsidal dwellings leaning against the inner profile of the outer wall.

d126d80bff729439.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall, partly overgrown with vegetation around almost the entire perimeter; nevertheless, through the doorway facing south-east one can enter the tholos, which is open at the top. Inside there are two large niches and another doorway to the north-west, half buried in soil.

d15d95abbe573b2c.text:
Nuraghe with attached village of huts.

The tholos is still intact.

d167da265c54e0bf.text: Feature covered by vegetation of indistinct nature

d16eba07d6122e10.text: Sacred area of probable Nuragic origin, reused in Punic and Roman periods, where abundant building materials and ceramics are found.

d18a0ba3c1bac185.text: They are carved from a rock composed almost entirely of white quartz pebbles. The origin of these pebbles can be traced to a fluvial-deltaic environment dating back to about 166 million years ago.

d1ac4961f56dc8bc.text: The name of the nuraghe derives almost certainly from the toponym of the location. It is a particularly unusual nuraghe in terms of its construction. Unfortunately, it has suffered a conspicuous collapse to the west, limiting its survey. Nuraghe of the elongated height of Pantaleo or "Pantaleo Serra", proper name. It is the first of three nuraghi situated along the edge of an elongated height. See Sèrra Pantalèo. mu

d1bb4933fbe44235.text: In a private plot. There are decorations in the form of probable bull's-head protomes.

d1bbab6f1d0b8fb7.text: Giants' tomb of Deruta. Located just 50 m from another Giants' tomb in better condition, on which the municipality has carried out minor interventions for cleaning and improved accessibility.

d223f1efbb9e6369.text: It is located in the territory of the comune of Urzulei at an elevation of 1,030 metres. It was a complex nuraghe, of which only a few ruins remain. Nearby are also important giants' tombs.

d231605b45cbe6aa.text: The construction is unique, as it incorporates elements typical of the subterranean context. It is a domus de janas repurposed in the Nuragic period, where a stele and a corridor were built. It represents a distinctive tomb with an architectural façade.

d2405514fd95f4f2.text: Domus de janas located near the provincial road. Excavated on limestone, featuring particular bull's-head protomes in relief.

d24912a112b0009c.text: To the north-east of the nuraghe there is a well whose masonry consists of polyhedral stones of various shapes and sizes. The north wall's masonry is hidden by vegetation and appears to have collapsed at first glance. Around the well, several stones are present, likely part of the original structure.

d25a2ac77eab8454.text: Of this nuraghe only a small portion remains: the first two courses of the foundation on the northern side, and the upper part of the basaltic ashlar courses arranged in curved lines at the other cardinal points. Clearly, the nuraghe bears no blame. What can be documented is documented.

d2699deaf78d5358.text:
The monument, four-lobed and sub-rectangular in plan, features a central tower made of trachyte in circular plan, with a diameter of about 10 m, and lateral towers connected by a curtain wall constructed using polygonal masonry with roughly shaped stones.

Remains of some structures with circular rooms are visible at the south-east and north-west corners.

d26ef3e28caad021.text: Tomb circle built of polyhedral boulders of various sizes. The structure is circular, formed by superimposing one or two rows of polyhedral boulders. The upper part consists of 13 boulders arranged in a circle (diameter about 150 cm), of which: the tallest, placed to the east in the circle, is triangular and stands out from the others; to the south and north of it are two boulders set on edge with their dressed faces visible; seven boulders of various shapes and sizes follow, completing the circle.

d27dfb8bfb7e9436.text: Giants' tomb completely embedded in the undergrowth, never apparently excavated and totally collapsed. Only a few isodomic ashlar stones remain from the inner wall of the corridor...

d290ef47c5cd52f9.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four lateral towers enclosed within a large outer wall provided with ten towers, for a total of at least 15 towers. Seven of the outer wall's towers are visible, while the others lie buried under the mantle of earth. In the excavations of recent years the structures belonging to the complex nuraghe have been brought to light, of which two of the lateral towers are discernible.

d294397cc1203caf.text: Apart from the two monumental giants' tombs, unique and clearly visible and of exceptional craftsmanship, three other tombs have been identified. For those familiar with nuragic buildings and urbanism, this means the existence of a community of several hundred people who had the need to multiply their cemeteries.

d2cc1e15be850e82.text: Ruined nuraghe submerged by the floral scrub

d2e0703e30c2504e.text: In total ruin, the few remaining fragments are incorporated into a section of the perimeter curtain wall. Its existence is remembered only through the historical accounts of the adjacent landowners. A few stones of medium and large size are barely visible.

d30188f3d4be921b.text: Traces of the Nuragic village are also present.

d31d575fe6b32b93.text: The nuraghe has an elongated elliptical plan corresponding to the type of corridor nuraghe, and its structure is built upon the natural rock, adapting partially to it. At several points along the external perimeter, the elevation is preserved up to six courses in height, so that one can observe how the base blocks gradually decrease in size from bottom to top.

d31e5459f60d464f.text: Dolmen located near the homonymous nuraghe

d33cb2224d40573e.text:
Hidden by dense vegetation, we find the nuraghe Arigau. Completely covered in earth and vegetation, with only a few courses of the base visible.

The nuraghe lies at Santa Maria Acquas, on a hill behind the amphitheatre. Apparently a single-tower nuraghe. Never studied and completely covered in earth and vegetation.

d356e70470838dd8.text: Unidentified nuraghe, located on the summit of a hill between two valleys, now reduced to a heap of large ashlar stones.

d3588920de425e06.text: It consists of two large outcrops of rock near the SS 131 state road. The smaller of the boulders that make up Perda Longa is thought to have been used as a "sacred stone" in the Ozieri culture period, as shown by the cupmarks carved in it and the remains of obsidian tools and pottery found around it. From: Biddas e nuraxis de su sattu de Serrenti de su Brunzu de mesu a su Ferru I, by Daniele Carta

d35b8a3090d6e9bc.text: Village, giants' tomb, menhir and remains of a nuraghe in the middle of the agricultural farm

d3624615b25efd94.text: The ashlars making up the tomb, largely buried, are of various types: limestone, basalt and even granite can be seen. A hole lets us see several metres of the side walls and a couple of limestone roofing slabs placed to the west. The right-hand side of the exedra is visible, though not clearly because it is buried; I have tried to document it as fully as possible. To the east, beyond a few trees, stands one of the stelae that were placed at the entrance of giants' tombs, at the centre of the exedra.

d37b30cf350ee58e.text: Ruined, in poor condition, covered by vegetation and partly buried, it remains interesting for its position right against the coastal cliff. Some internal chambers are visible but cannot be entered. It is certainly a single-tower nuraghe.

d37e5d122c892cd2.text: The giants' tomb is located in the south-west direction relative to the homonymous nuraghe, of which only the tomb corridor remains.

d39c9d90e3759d9f.text: Stone worked with hammers on the outer surface. Probably a prehistoric altar.

d3c4686ddf58c743.text: The nuraghe stands about 400 metres north-west of Nuraghe Biriola, while 350 metres to the east there is a Roman cemetery, attested by about ten cinerary urns of different shapes cut into the outcropping rock. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase and a central chamber flanked by two niches. The tower, circular in plan, has its top missing at a maximum height of 5.80 m with 11 courses, while a large collapse has affected the perimeter wall facing north-north-west.

d3fc9c67803464ab.text: The necropolis of Santu Pedru is a pre-Nuragic archaeological site. The necropolis is located on the eastern slope of the trachytic hill of Santu Pedru, in a position of wide visibility over the valley below, in the Nurra, a region in northwestern Sardinia. The complex includes a dozen tombs with a corridor entrance ("dromos") and a planimetric layout composed of multiple cells.

d447ef1ba10da881.text: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, comprises a sacred well set inside an irregular courtyard, a 'megaron' temple surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut with an entrance room and an inner chamber. This was a 'communal' building, the so-called 'meeting hut' typical of Nuragic villages. Pilgrims would usually stop here, perhaps for an audience with the priests.

d44c89995fb47082.text: Remains of the nuraghe and the Nuragic and Neolithic village.

d44e64ae9ac52f53.text: Three-lobed nuraghe serving as a foundation for the church of San Saturnino.

d45014c26dd87254.text: The nuraghe is a single-tower type, with a curtain wall about 80 cm thick; it rises from the surrounding vegetation to a height of 4 metres. Its position is strategic, lying halfway between the Fenu nuraghe and the nearby spa area where three other nuraghi stand, one of them part of the same spa complex. It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the municipal territory of Sardara. The size of the lintel is striking

d468bac559ef6946.text: Inside a lentisco trunk, probably ready for transport to the client, the sarcophagus (2.00 x 0.90 x 0.90 m) is made from a single monolithic brown trachyte of considerable size.

d47023be9471a3dc.text:
The cemetery includes 11 domus de janas, generally multicellular, some of which are characterized by architectural reliefs.

The most interesting burial consists of 11 rooms arranged in an irregular pattern.

d4b873756cab557f.text:
Nuraghe of corridor type, composed of two towers connected by an internal courtyard, accessed through the entrance.

The oldest part of the nuraghe is the tower on the right when entering, while the left tower and the connecting walls were added later.

d4bb156f199e508c.text:
A small cemetery with chambers interconnected and with traces still visible of red ochre.

Located on SP 15, towards Sorradile, clearly visible at the junction leading to the lake.

The entrance is very finely carved; the collapses of the antechamber are evident, and there were certainly other chambers, as clear traces remain in the ground immediately in front.

d4bc681752dda768.text: Currently it has been largely buried prior to carrying out interventions for its preservation.

d4f08b93c9f1622b.text: Simple single-tower nuraghe, in very poor condition, with traces of a possible settlement.

d508e128e5dd10ba.text:
Hidden among the vegetation, only a small part of the tomb remains.

The filar type and the walls of the burial chamber employ isodomic masonry technique; the monument, oriented to south-east, has a total length of 7.60 m, measured to the edge of the exedra, and a maximum width of 3.15 m. Partially visible are a portion of the tomb and the exedra.

d5208b22e176bc01.text: Single-tower nuraghe made of granite blocks, with in situ evidence of trachyte ashlar finely worked for decorative purposes.

d52295a01151f694.text: In poor state of conservation, the corridor and several squared stones that originally were meant to form the entrance are still visible.

d52332ff1575d804.text: Neolithic rock-cut burial, typologically perhaps attributable to the Filigosa culture (about 2500 BC). The monument is hard to read because it is covered by dense vegetation. The burial consists of an entrance corridor (dromos), an antechamber and a chamber. The narrow corridor leads into the roughly circular antechamber. The chamber proper, smaller and roughly rectangular in plan, is reached through a roughly rectangular/trapezoidal doorway.

d53a37729e4f7baa.text: Complex nuraghe, known to many elders by the name "Sa Reggia", was probably a three-lobed structure with a village. Today it is a heap of ruins and undergrowth more than 10 metres high.

d5531c58175dbcb0.text:
A single-tower nuraghe on the basalt plateau of Su Gollei, in the area of S'Iscampiatorju. It is a perfect tholos. The south-facing entrance, with the stair on the left and the guard cell on the right, leads to the central chamber.

To the east there are traces of a first outer wall in a crescent shape, leaning against the nuraghe itself; further east a second outer wall surrounded the Nuragic village.

d58a0616cb9f88a2.text: The Sant' Uanni site is located on a hill just a short distance from the village of Dolianova; besides the remains of a multi-lobed nuraghe and the basal part of a church that bears its name, some remains attributable to the Nuragic and Roman periods have been found, suggesting the presence of both a Nuragic and a Roman settlement.

d592317b9435e30c.text:
Uncertain location, to be defined. Single petroglyph

Overlapping the upper part of the residential centre of Baunei, it echoes the name of the domus de janas. It is a depiction composed of a total of 18 shallow channels branching out from a main depression a few centimetres deep, which then connect to various terminal cups arranged without apparent pattern.

d59d7914654c7392.text: Very eroded, so its structure is difficult to identify. To the north of the chamber a flat-laid corridor is visible. To the south an ovoid chamber. Around the remains of the village huts are discernible.

d5c3a0ed94065a6b.text: Single-tower, of limited architectural value but of significant strategic importance, as it allows control over the entire Gulf of Palmas.

d5c9cb360cfe4dba.text:
The village is located a few metres south of the homonymous nuraghe, on top of "Su Monte 'e Subra". Once you reach the summit, you are faced with an enormous expanse of stones and ashlar blocks, covering at least two hectares.

As you approach the various mounds, circular, rectangular, and complex structures, long walls and curtain walls begin to emerge. The site has never undergone any excavations.

d5d288d7881bf1f6.text: Dolmen composed of a large horizontal slab placed on a dry-stone wall of cyclopean masonry.

d5e50e728332bbe3.text:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a refacing and an outer wall that recalls the Nuraghe Aidu Olostru of Bortigali in some respects. To the WNW the remains of a massive outer wall (thickness 2.30 m; height 3.00 m) are visible for about thirty metres; it probably enclosed the nuragic tower but now survives only partially, with three or four courses, at a distance of 12–20 metres from the nuraghe.

An extensive village, of which the remains are visible, extended around the inside of the outer wall.

d6166759f0da947f.text: It is hard to say whether this was a village. Because the site lies on a steep slope, sediment has covered the structures. The area has never been excavated. Massive walls, tens of metres long and very thick, run downhill towards the river, while others run parallel to it. One particularly striking feature is an extensive wall made of two parallel lines of walling separated by a ditch about two metres wide.

d619bd5fce811f10.text: It may be a proto-nuraghe, and it is almost square in plan.

d625226735a69329.text: The Adoni nuraghe is a complex nuraghe dating to the Bronze Age, located in the municipality of Villanovatulo in the province of Cagliari. The site stands on a rise about 800 m high in the centre of the historic Sarcidano region. The first excavations date back to the mid-nineteenth century. The whole complex consists of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion, surrounded by a village. Various finds have been recovered at the site, including pottery and a fragment of a bronze handle.

d626d094e8674722.text: It includes two complete domus and a third that is just beginning.

d6987b955baef277.text: It consists of two single-cell tombs, side by side, each with a rectangular entrance.

d6ddfc4ec35fd6f1.text: complex nuraghe with a village nearby

d71ce5fe8baf1ac8.text: Single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition, with its tholos intact. Surrounding traces of other towers and huts are visible.

d72a420fe60bc365.text:
The nuraghe is located on the outskirts of Sassari, on SS 127 towards Osilo, behind a sheepfold, and sits on the edge of a cliff in a dominant position overlooking the valley below. In addition to being on the edge of the cliff, it is built upon a natural bastion, as it stands atop a block of limestone detached from the cliff face itself.

Various structures of uncertain chronology are attached to the main tower.

d7545aaf315a461c.text: On site the carved stones belonging to the nuragic fountain still remain, presumably the nuragic fountain was destroyed during the works for the construction of the water trough complex.

d77c8dcb03ea5beb.text:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The external profile, the funerary corridor and the exedra can be observed.

The construction technique is regular coursed masonry using sub-squared polygonal blocks.

The tomb has the peculiarity of being unusually oriented towards the south-west, and is also very close to its reference nuraghe (about 25 m).

The monument lies in the municipal territory of Villagrande Strisaili (OG).

d7805428ab79f9e0.text: Unique construction situated exactly on the summit of the rocky Pedras Serradas, barely discernible. It appears to be a semicircular nuraghe. Some consider it a circular nuraghe, while others see it as remains of a nuraghe after the collapse of the underlying ground. Unparalleled views over Giorrè.

d782ee9fa6712fe6.text: The tomb is of the coursed type, built with slabs of slate, about one metre long, of which six courses of the external wall of the chamber and eight courses of the exedra remain in situ. The central portal of the exedra is constructed in a dolmenic style, with two slabs placed edge-to-edge and one slab above; the drainage opening is missing. The exedra is joined to the external wall of the chamber by a concave line.

d78ac873d55fd7e2.text: It is an unidentifiable structure without an appropriate archaeological excavation. Limestone slabs set vertically, adjacent, tall but not very thick, are visible; a semicircular structure emerging from the ground, built of limestone blocks and with two openings. A long circular row, perhaps delimiting the structure, at the top of which cavities covered by a few slabs can be seen. Further west, a structure with two adjacent vertical limestone slabs positioned to the north, with another slab to the right while to the left there is a wall of ashlars. Traces of tomb-robbers' digging are evident.

d79b034875175522.text: The Nuragic fortification consists of a tholos tower enclosed in a courtyard which in turn is protected by an outer wall provided with five further towers. The entrance lies to the south and leads into a small courtyard where several rooms are found that were used for metal smelting, as shown by the bronze-smelting waste discovered all around. The central tower has an elliptical plan; inside, on the right, a stairway branches off leading to the upper floor.

d7c2e3441e758489.text: The nuraghe is currently in poor state of conservation, with several collapses that prevent a precise assessment. Only two towers are clearly distinguishable, between which a small courtyard—typical of complex nuraghe—may have once existed. In the main tower (mastio), niches and a staircase are present, which led to the upper levels, now collapsed.

d7cf85c4ddda8b12.text: The site dates to the Bronze Age and is built entirely of finely worked basalt rock. The structure consists of a perimeter wall that is almost totally destroyed: only the base of the well is visible, as it lacks the tholos roof (which is difficult to reconstruct), even though the chamber has remained intact. Nine steps can be counted descending downwards until they reach the water about two metres underground.

d7edb05f272f2e4a.text: The nuraghe has about eight surviving wall courses. The entrance lacks the outer lintel. The stair is visible on the left side and the entrance niche on the opposite side. The tholos chamber has its top missing and is almost completely filled with vegetation, collapse debris and sediments up to a height, against the walls, that exceeds the lintels of the niches, except for the one on the left, whose far end can be glimpsed.

d802edc794fea2cd.text: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower.

d82d87f0f51fc4e0.text: Some wall courses remain, probably belonging to the outer wall.

d84c6274704430cf.text: Nuragic village composed of about 30 huts, and at a short distance there was a sacred well.

d84ead257d019b1e.text: Archaeological trace corresponding to the area of the trigonometric point.

d8518d7d2bacb1e3.text: The nuragic sacred well is a special structure attached to the spring vein; the sacred spring structure is usually composed of a chamber enclosed by stone slabs.

d85a45b7894d7016.text: It is located on the hill overlooking the commune of Silanus. It is a complex nuraghe, mainly built of granite. The central tower, originally about 12 metres high, remains almost intact and was originally flanked by two or three additional bodies. The nuraghe features two superimposed tholos connected by a main staircase and a secondary, hidden staircase with a mezzanine. At the base of the nuraghe, remnants of other nuragic constructions are visible, still insufficiently studied.

d8954c1a093209b4.text:
Built of limestone and sandstone blocks, it consists of a central body with two towers, an outer wall, and a village of huts.

The oldest structures, dated to the 15th–10th centuries BC, are the main tower and some huts. The tower, with its entrance to the ENE, survives to a height of 8 m. The inner chamber preserves its tholos vault intact.

In the back wall opens the ogival stairwell that led to the upper floor and the terrace.

d89f5422b023a655.text: The site includes 17 domus de janas, two of which are incomplete and one almost entirely buried. The numbered positions of the domus are taken from the book Itinerario Archeologico nel territorio Orgolese.

d8b65d59813a409d.text:
The complex, one of the most important and best preserved in Nuragic Sardinia, comprises a village-sanctuary with about a hundred huts, two small temples with adjoining enclosures, and two megalithic burials.

The village consists of isolated huts and clusters of huts arranged around central spaces. Six groupings can be counted, some equipped with well-cisterns and small wells connected to water channels. The huts, circular, are built of drystone masonry with irregular courses.

d8d80c2358c7c3f9.text: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.

d8db480b3332ff8b.text: Single-tower nuraghe surrounded by dense vegetation.

d8e81a3276dd23d4.text: On the site there are as many as two giants' tombs of modest size, largely stripped of the stones that originally composed them. The exedra and the burial chamber are still discernible.

d90fbf683aa8aba1.text: It is a domus de janas, a burial of the "double oven" type, attributable to a period spanning from the third to the second millennium BCE.

d916b729ef5179f9.text:
Single-tower nuraghe built of sandstone boulders. The main chamber has three asymmetrical niches.

From the corridor, a staircase with 15 steps starts on the right. Maximum height of the tower 9.15 m.

Nearby are the remains of the settlement and two domus de janas.

d922e4568de61dcc.text: Nuraghe probably of a single-tower tholos type. Almost completely hidden by dense vegetation, it appears as a heap of polygonal basaltic blocks arranged in a disordered manner. Some courses can be read inside a lentisco thicket, on the west side.

d92bf8619c6bfb39.text:
The tomb was part of a funerary complex originally composed of four megalithic burials set a short distance from one another and very close to the Ilòi and Logula nuraghi.

The present road alignment has split the small necropolis of giants' tombs built to serve the villages along a network of transhumance routes. It is a dolmenic tomb, originally furnished with a bilithic arched stele with a doorway at its base, placed at the centre of the exedra.

d93ebc141a96f717.text: It is probably the domus reported by engineer Melis in the census of archaeological sites in Mamoiada; the site should be Locu Lenardu, although today the entire area is known as Su Dovaru. It is a single-cell domus carved into a granite outcrop.

d95d6658faedb9ef.text: Total ruin. The older inhabitants of the area recall its existence, though only a few basal circles remain. When the fast-moving road between Sassari and Tempio was constructed, excavation work affected more than one site, in total disregarding their immense historical value. mu

d96324eb985de668.text: Complex-type nuraghe, presumably of the frontal addition type. The nuraghe shows numerous structural modifications carried out after its initial construction. However, it is possible to discern a main tower to which two secondary towers have been added.

d964bdac40dc837d.text: It is submerged beneath the waters of Lake Omodeo.

d97db196f8676b8d.text: Single-tower nuraghe and remains of huts and giants' tomb.

d98c7ecffcf58a28.text: It is a single-tower nuraghe built of large, well-worked basalt blocks. The entrance, oriented SSW, is topped by a rectangular relieving window and leads into a corridor with an ogival roof; on the left of the corridor is a niche. The chamber, completely filled with collapse, survives to almost 5 metres (9 courses). On the right side of the chamber a niche cut into the wall thickness is visible.

d98d4d19d5673d8f.text: A tholos nuraghe whose north tower is clearly visible. The south tower has collapsed on the seaward side. An artificial entrance dug by curiosity-seekers is present.

d98f4c17cd534c03.text: It lies within the municipal territory of Seneghe (OR). Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The vault has collapsed and the chamber is filled with the collapse debris. The surviving height of the building is about 3.50 m. The trapezoidal entrance is clearly visible, fitted with a monolithic lintel and faces east (1.70 m high x 0.80 m wide at the base).

d99720c73d5f1507.text: The monument stands on the basalt plateau that extends at the southern foot of the Marghine chain, south of the Rio Tossilo. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a central chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a height of 2.90 m on the north-west side, with 6 courses, and 2.20 m on the north-east side with 5 courses. The masonry consists of medium and large blocks, carefully worked and laid in regular horizontal courses.

d9a147c17cec9dc6.text: The structure still preserves 12 benches. Complex nuraghe with an outer wall and a surrounding village built of basalt blocks. Notable for the presence of benches still in situ. Entrance to the west (rare). Unfortunately, it is covered by dense vegetation.

d9aad4bbc405b0d9.text: The tomb has a rectangular apsidal chamber, with the exedra and entrance facing south. The chamber was built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, bonded dry with packing wedges. The tomb has certainly been violated by looters; the burial chamber is covered by vegetation and filled with collapse stones and earth. On the east side of the tomb there are collapse boulders that certainly belong to the monument. The west wall is hidden by vegetation.

d9bc7e021a327f74.text: The domus de janas of Scala Coperta lies a few hundred metres from the Roccia dell'Elefante, in the locality of Pedra Sciolta. Cut into an erratic trachyte boulder, it consists of an antechamber and four small cells arranged in a cross. On the outside, on top of the boulder, there are three holes for housing small baetyls; a fourth hole is set slightly further back than the others and is now barely visible because of the vegetation.

d9c1ee4f2ba77fa9.text: Of the monument, only some base courses remain, while the entrance has been incorporated into a modern hut.

d9d2fd4c6836ac7d.text: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of stones about two metres high. Inaccessible due to the dense vegetation present. Complex structure with a settlement from the Bronze Age and remains of Punic-Roman houses.

da02726c5b8008cd.text:
A folk tale tells that these rocks are a married couple turned to stone by the deity for mocking the sound of the bells coming from the nearby church of Masullas during the feast of Sa Gloriosa.

It seems that in the past these statue-like rocky blocks, which geologically are nothing other than submarine lava outcrops, were worshipped by the proto-Sardinians as fertilising deities.

da084491c550f9ad.text: The condition of the tomb is unknown.

da0d659e4baea129.text: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe, of whose external wall only four courses remain.

da0ff2ff4ed1b7ef.text: At present it is completely buried and covered by shrub vegetation. Because of this its ground plan cannot be read, except for a single course of blocks emerging from the hillock; judging by the extent of the remains it is likely to be a complex type. In the surrounding ground outcrops of roughly dressed limestone ashlars can be seen, suggesting the existence of a village, traces of which are also detectable through photogrammetric analysis.

da68b2309111cf6e.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which half the perimeter wall survives for seven courses.

da7c28d68453325a.text: Near the nuraghe Arrubiu are located two giants' tombs, one of which yielded a sword.

da7e584051a50fa5.text: Inscribed stones, petroglyphs with concentric circles and cups

da9020df24fd26ee.text: This nuraghe, located at the border between the municipalities of Olmedo (SS) and Sassari, is listed in Filippo Nissardi's Nuragographic Map of the Nurra (published by G. Pinza in 1901) as "Nuraghe Grascioleddu" and assigned to Olmedo.

daa6651934fe5dcb.text: They are two distinct collective burials that share the same exedra. They are located at a short distance from the homonymous nuraghe situated at the top of the plateau.

dac708dae322b6ad.text: Hut with enclosure. The structure is built of small and medium-sized polyhedral stones, dry-laid and arranged in fairly regular courses. It is very likely that the hut was modified and reused right up to the last century.

db085f0b3e27579c.text: The find is located in the municipality of Orani and consists of five hypogea.

db136495596bedbc.text:
It has a vaguely trapezoidal plan (10.50 x 10.20 x 11.10 x 4.50 m) with rounded corners and a raised entrance (0.75 m above ground level), with a rectangular opening (width 1.47 m – height 1.98 m), lintelled and facing north-east.

The interior of the monument is not visible because of the collapse.

The masonry consists of roughly dressed polygonal blocks of medium and large size laid in irregular horizontal courses.

db1e336ca2a44170.text:
The nuraghe is situated practically at ground level.

The poor quality of the rock has likely contributed to the poor condition in which the monument now exists.

db1f5d07fc46e977.text: South-east of Siurgus-Donigala, near the boundary with the territory of Goni. Built on a rise at 494 m above sea level, well-worked limestone blocks were used that survive today to a height of about 5 m. The inner chamber has its top missing, is filled with collapse debris, and shows an ogival entrance. Around the nuraghe the basal courses of the huts of a village can be seen, and slabs driven into the ground that may indicate burials.

db4c53f1b667d61e.text: It is the collapsed nuraghe, reference point for the beautiful and nearby giants' tomb.

db574508c5d9245e.text: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part. Collapse material lies on the west and north sides of the nuraghe. The structure is accessible only along the entrance corridor, which is 5 m long; to its left a chamber opens, partly blocked, which must have given access to the stair leading to the upper chamber.

db5dd55d5673977a.text: Nuraghe now almost completely destroyed. Only a heap of stones remains.

db5ee561b724138f.text: The site comprises a main tower, a sub-elliptical structure that must have served as the entrance, and remains of an outer wall all round the perimeter. The various rock outcrops complete the masonry and dictate the ground plan. The sub-elliptical structure, on the south side, probably formed the entrance to the complex and linked the interior rooms by a corridor, now blocked by collapse. A terrace can be made out in the north-western area.

db64c31a6f3cd83d.text: It is a complex structure built of squared limestone blocks, in which an inner chamber is clearly visible; its archaeological deposit has been disturbed by looters. Inside, three niches with ogival vaulted roofs are clearly visible, as is the entrance, positioned to the south-east; to the right of it a short blind corridor can be seen, in front of which a small niche opens.

db6caf56e0542862.text: Name inspired by which the director Mauro Aragoni drew for his short film "Nuraghes S'Arena"

db88c85d98473f83.text: The nuraghe is located in an area where, for a long time, an Ozieri culture settlement (4th millennium BC) and a lithic cist tomb of Campaniform-Bonnanaro type (late III–early II millennium BC) have been known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

dbb80234a812c936.text:
Nuragic village near Monte Maiori, located in the territory of the comune of Guspini.

A fascinating site because it is set within the natural landscape. It is undoubtedly adapted by the local shepherds, yet it retains a living history.

It is not the only one in this comune.

dbb8ec5ed3f6f40a.text: The nuragic settlement comprises a hundred circular huts distributed without any apparent order, at regular distances from one another. It is built with regular courses of limestone blocks; the rare trachyte blocks probably come from the nearby Monte Imberi. The huts, circular (diameter about 6/7 m), are mostly currently covered by debris and invaded by dense Mediterranean scrub.

dbbbe49a2dd66bce.text: Location of the remains of the Antoi Letze nuraghe

dbf77ab3177176c5.text: The hypogeum is cut into an isolated basalt boulder. The doorway opens at some height above ground level and is surmounted by two deep grooves cut horizontally and parallel in the rock. The doorway still shows a clear rebate for the closing slab. A narrow groove cut into the thickness of the doorway outlines all four sides. The oval chamber is of the oven type. The tomb was explored in 1927 by A. Taramelli, who found it already violated and emptied long before.

dc0270bb0b757053.text: The proto-nuraghes of Serrenti are mostly of small size and, as observable, have an elliptical or irregular plan. The ones at Monti Mannu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Crastu, and Sa Corona appear larger; the last two may have been enlarged or restored between BR and BFI. Around this proto-nuraghe there are traces of a small settlement.

dc0433b88340c4da.text: Nuraghe of which only a small portion remains at the centre of the settlement of Is Collus. Following a report to the supervisor, archaeological investigations were carried out, but the results are unknown.

dc3a231cad055670.text: An inhabited space is present within the site, on the inner face of the wall, and a so-called dentilled stele from a giants' tomb. The stele, finely carved, was reused in Roman times and attests to the existence of a Nuragic funerary structure of the coursed type, in isodomic masonry, whose original position has not yet been located.

dc42b840cbfcf454.text: Well-preserved nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower still has its roof and a lower level below which entry has not yet been achieved.

dc470f3442aaf81f.text: Single-tower nuraghe, enveloped in dense vegetation.

dc7b7d7cc2fd97b3.text: Settlement in considerable decay. Situated at 256 m above sea level. On the summit a crown of limestone rocks surrounded by shrubby scrub is visible, including s'arrùda (Ruta d'Aleppo). The remains of the Nuragic construction have an internal diameter of 4.05 m. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe but the dense expanse of scrub could hide other structures. The position is strategically elevated, with a very wide visual basin.

dc91183cd164218f.text: Characterized by a large Nuragic settlement to which several archaeological excavations have been carried out.

dca4fdd58a554597.text: Almost certainly present up to the 1960s, when major land improvement and land reorganization works were carried out. The toponym of the area, "su crastu covaccadu", suggests the presence of a trilite or a set of flat slabs forming a possible cover for a burial tomb. mu

dcb13d530d68941f.text:
The nuraghe was built directly on the bedrock, and its plan appears to have been adapted to the irregularities of the rock, since walling can be seen on several levels along the slopes of the outcrop.

On the summit the monument, now almost completely destroyed, seems to have an elongated plan, but its very poor state of preservation and an illicit excavation make the whole difficult to interpret.

dcc337bc3417bd67.text: Situated about a hundred metres east of the well-known giants' tomb of Imbertighe, with which it had an obvious cultural connection, the nuraghe now lies inside a farm. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a slightly elliptical plan (14.10 x 15.25 m), an entrance to the south-east, and a surviving height of 2.75 m to the north-west and 1.70 m to the south-west, with five and four courses respectively.

dcd82a569dcb1b26.text: The Orizanne nuraghe is located alongside the road from Nuoro to Bitti. Like other nuraghes, it has a large oak tree inside the collapsed tholos.

dcdae954496f446f.text: Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain, as the stones were removed to build a road.

dd055adc225b2edd.text: Very little of the village remains, only the ruins of huts are visible, and I believe this was the regular settlement; at a short distance lies the Sanctuary and Temple of the same name, with adjacent the Hut Settlement of nuraghe huts, partly still standing. I think these latter were (Cumbissias), inhabited only during periodic festival days or pagan rituals.

dd12b30336fc1306.text: The abundant collapse of the structure and the vegetation covering the monument make the site difficult to read, it could be a corridor nuraghe.

dd217a5bdb18cf63.text: Complex three-lobed nuraghe. The central tower has a chamber with three niches set around it. Built of granite.

dd2b5c911d46148e.text: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with only faint traces remaining

dd45d124c1afec08.text: Domus de janas fractured and covered with debris

dd9b202c3eb2d06f.text: location of the remains of the nuraghe Antoni Letzesa sea

ddb55da86d576a43.text: Remains of nuraghe or nuragic huts

ddc9573343eef51c.text:
The underground tomb opens into a shallow outcrop, about 150 metres east of the municipal boundary Borore – Silanus.

The underground chamber, oriented south-west, consists of two sub-circular chambers arranged along the longitudinal axis; the walls are carefully smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.

ddd3b8510de1e7d8.text: Practically the nuraghe no longer exists; only some piles of large stones remain, which still allow one to perceive its original location.

ddd883a269efc07b.text: Complex nuraghe with an adjacent giants' tomb and a spring, called "Roia Zrighidanu", which flows into the Riu Pizziu further downstream. It is a settlement used up to the Imperial Roman period, and the rectangular structures in the area of the nuraghe probably date from that period. Five hundred metres from the nuraghe, the researchers Dyson and Rowland report a Roman necropolis with at least 32 cist tombs.

de0007ef133122f5.text: The hut had already been described by Taramelli: "The remains of a circular structure were evident, and after excavation it appeared as a circular enclosure of a nuragic construction with a diameter of about 8 m… The narrowness of the wall in comparison with the vastness of the internal space does not allow us to claim it was a true nuraghe."

de03f1dd97c13b24.text: Covered with stones gathered from a collapse.

de04aae0be2da344.text:
The tomb, of dolmenic type and oriented to south-east, features a semicircular exedra (arc m. 9 – arrow m. 3) delimited by orthostatic slabs, a rectangular apsidal body (length m. 6 – width m. 4), and a modest funerary corridor (length m.  3.70 x width 0.75).

Currently, the northern side and the right arm of the exedra are incorporated into a dry stone wall.

de06e23a5e1f31e6.text: Part of the monument retains the funerary corridor; six courses of stones remain on the right side and only two on the left, with a maximum length of 7.70 m and a width of 1 m.

de09fba8a7d2ba42.text: The nuraghe has a base diameter of 12.60 m and, although demolished in its upper parts, survives to a height of 8.60 m. Through the south-facing entrance one enters the corridor, on the right of which opens a rectangular niche and, on the left, the stair, still passable, which led to the upper chamber, now destroyed. The corridor leads to the fine circular chamber, 4.15 m in diameter, off which three niches open in a cross formation.

de151e1eda156f53.text: Located in a position somewhat detached from the funerary complex of Madau, despite the few visible structures and modest dimensions, it appears to retain the characteristics (and thus possibly also the construction period) of the "larger sisters". Of the tomb, currently partially buried by sediment, only the exedra and part of the corridor are visible.

de9142f586ac3ea5.text:
Single-tower nuraghe. Four courses survive intact. In poor condition. Built of roughly dressed medium-sized blocks. Signs of human spoliation. Already shown on Filippo Nissardi's nuraghe map (in Pinza G. 1901).

The hillock occupied by the nuraghe includes a stretch of Roman cobblestone paving identified to the north-west of the monument. The dense vegetation covering the site makes it impossible to detect any remains or traces of a possible village.

dea380756fdc2f0d.text: The sacred well or well temple represents without doubt the most striking example of a sacred building among those so far discovered and studied in the Mediterranean basin. This type of building, belonging to the rich Sardinian civilization, dates back to the long and diverse Nuragic period. It was conceived as a place for carrying out various rites related to the cult of water.

deabdb0e35b01cf9.text: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only a single row of calcareous blocks remains, arranged in a curved line, about 4 metres long. In the north-northeast direction, a section of wall is visible, composed of blocks laid in a line for a length of about 3.20 metres.

dee57d0d9140e84b.text: Single-tower with a circular plan and a chamber completely missing its top; three niches arranged in a cross can be seen. The external wall face remains with five courses. The entrance, located in the south-east, has collapsed.

df03712455c7a1e6.text: It is characterized by having been built with both calcareous and trachytic stones, as in the nearby nuraghe Corvos; however, while the latter shows a clear distinction between the calcareous and trachytic sections, in the nuraghe Sa Menta stones of different types are intermixed in the wall face without any discernible pattern.

df1b5e0d1f5c9251.text: The area consists of a enclosure enclosing a megaron temple.

df1c504ad4f324e4.text: The menhir placed beside the ramp leading to the upper part of the altar was raised prior to the construction of the altar itself. It was the centre of a Neolithic village.

df38461a4d5704ff.text: Up to five courses emerge, composed of cyclopean blocks of varying shapes, massive, reaching a height of up to 2.5 metres, in basalt. The central tower is incomplete, forming an angle of 270 degrees. From it extend a wall to the east and another to the north. The structure enclosed by these walls is entirely unclear due to brush and various restorations.

df40806c99b02f41.text: Nuraghe on an acrocoro from which the Coros is seen. Single-tower, built with local limestone ashlar, its tholos has collapsed inward.

df44991f001dccce.text: Nuraghe partially enclosed by the walls of the small church dedicated to San Lorenzo, on the north-east side of the structure (the side facing the village), some remains of the S. Lorenzo nuraghe are still visible.

df5274cfa9d5faff.text: It is the most imposing monument preserved on the territory. It is almost certain to have been a complex structure, given the prominence of its walls compared to other monuments. Inside the chamber, a niche positioned towards the north-west is still visible, and slightly to the west, a small access chamber appears, which seems to correspond to a staircase.

df77bda119c82aab.text: Almost hidden by the dense undergrowth of shrubs.

df8510710e05e5eb.text: At the site, especially on the steeper side facing the Aldo Moro road, remains of numerous huts are visible, along with worked stone and ceramic material of various types. Ceramic material is also present in large quantities on the opposite, flat side, to the south of the nuraghe. In appearance, some fragments with smoothed surfaces and fewer intrusive elements suggest later occupations following the Nuragic period.

dfb985af6fde3dcd.text: Located on a hilltop. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with evidence of huts in the surrounding areas.

dfc5cd399d2e67cf.text: It stands on a rocky spur along the Pardu River. This is a nuraghe of at least four towers surrounded by a defensive curtain wall. Of the four towers, three are still in good condition, while only the base of the fourth can be made out. The site today appears split in two. The east side, which does not face the river and stands on the rock, is still intact. The west side, which faces the river, has almost completely collapsed, with an enormous quantity of boulders scattered down the slope.

e03b2ea54d5ad52e.text:
The single-tower nuraghe stands right next to the SS131, beside a sheepfold. It is used as a shelter for sheep. The tholos is almost intact except for the top courses.

Little or nothing remains of the huts that presumably stood beside the tower.

e042a9427bcc18be.text: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"

e057e717d58b1719.text: This nuraghe, already noted in the 1922 EEM, is included in the Archaeological Map of Taramelli at a short distance to the west of the Nuraghe Pischedda. Of the monument, which already in the 1930s appeared almost completely destroyed – “Only the foundation remains, one metre high” – no trace remains today. It was also known by the name of S. Giuseppe.

e05cbe265415027d.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The interpretation is based on the circular plan of the monument, although its poor state of preservation and the vegetation cover make it impossible to observe other characteristic details. The entrance cannot be identified. Much of the material from the collapse of the nuraghe has been reused to build contemporary enclosures leaning against the ancient structures.

e07a92a4be4604a1.text: The village was enclosed by a megalithic wall.

e0879b0f376f9ea4.text: Cemeteries with nine hypogeic tombs, located in an area with rocks protruding from the surrounding ground. The tombs were accidentally discovered during recent excavation work. It is believed that the site was first used from the recent Neolithic (about 3500 BC).

e08affdc853ff2c3.text: A site that is difficult to interpret. The nuraghe is certain, but the presence of a giants' tomb also seems certain; it disappeared after land-reclamation works. The term cantòne refers to squared stone blocks, often of limestone or trachyte tuff (pèdra contonina). This surname, no longer in use, probably originated from the quarryman's trade that the unknown brothers from whom the place-name derives must have practised.

e0a6415338094b96.text:
The site underwent two main building phases: the first in the Middle Bronze Age and the second in the transition period between the Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age.

The complex consists of a megaron temple, about 17 metres long, surrounded by an enclosure known as a temenos and by other cult and residential buildings, including actual workshops for metal smelting; a complex nuraghe with a trilobate plan lies nearby.

e0c091b90000b3f9.text:
The temple of Sant'Anastasia stands near the church of the same name, in the upper part of Sardara, at the foot of the ridge that rises towards the hill of Pran'e Cuaddus, in the central Campidano.

The sanctuary, one of the most important in Nuragic Sardinia, centres on the sacred well temple.

The temple, dated to the Late Bronze Age (13th–12th century BC), is set within an articulated settlement of both civil and religious character that is still being excavated.

e0fcb310520fa884.text: Nuraghe and village, of which only faint traces remain

e109717799470542.text:
Complex nuraghe.

Of the nuraghe, located on a modest hill (563 m. a.s.l.), only a few courses of the central tower remain.

e1365fade1488bb2.text: Through a gap between the large ashlars of the upper part of the outer wall face, one enters the corridor that housed the helical staircase giving access to the upper part of the tower. In fact, the corridor ends against two large lintels that are completely buried. The nuraghe is in very poor condition. It is partly enveloped by mastic shrubs and prickly pears, the cause of the collapses and the burial, up to about two metres from the floor level.

e142f17b4af19adc.text: It is a bilobate structure of which only a portion remains, although several collapses have affected most of the structure. The trilithic and flat-laid junction is clearly visible and very interesting. mu

e174567bbc85569f.text: The archaeological area consists of the ruins of a Punic fortress and a complex nuraghe.

e1771376682ec7ca.text: The site, besides the nuraghe Iscalas, includes Roman-era and prehistoric menhir structures. The nuraghe, of which only some portions of the walling remain today, had a circular tower constructed with medium and large polygonal stones laid without the use of binding mortar.

e1b1fc5c102e5875.text: It lies a short distance from the beautiful eponymous nuraghe of s'Enalonga, now covered in brush and thorny bushes. A small spring of water still emerges here, which in ancient times must have fed the fountain. No particular masonry is visible.

e1d7682c044398be.text: Single-tower, difficult to access, partially collapsed, with the tholos destroyed.

e1f13b373b8418eb.text: The nuraghe Sa Murallia takes its name from a massive wall leaning against the original structures on the downhill side; it is largely hidden by deposits, layers and structures that have been built up against or over it over the centuries. In the same period and in later phases, the first settlements sprang up beside these nuraghi, sometimes enclosed by imposing oval or circular walls that are still partly visible today (Tradori, Araganzola, Maganzosa). (from the Narbolia municipal website)

e1f28192a4e4e5d6.text: To the north-northwest, adjacent to the rocky outcrop on which the northern tower of the nuraghe is built, there are two natural semicircular cavities, about 200 cm deep, closed by a roughly elliptical enclosure constructed of polyhedral stones of various sizes.

e1ff589e67868e7b.text: Remains of a nuraghe tower built from basalt blocks.

e20574353074e43c.text: Complex structure, almost entirely buried. The nuraghe is surrounded by dense vegetation, and furthermore, a fence has been erected on top of it, preventing view of the eastern part.

e208b5c922170cf4.text: The complex contains a sacred well with a paved area, a temple on a rectangular plan, a corridor building, and some stretches of cyclopean walls. The nuraghe Cherchizza stands at the western end, along the edge of the plateau. The site would have served as a landmark for the population of a wide surrounding area. Excavations have yielded bronze artefacts, including a figurine of the mother goddess, as well as amber objects.

e21c41a3d2e1118d.text: A few white limestone stones forming the basal perimeter. Only the entrance and a little else are visible, all set within a dense thicket of fetid anagiride (sa giolva). The name should derive from the local topographic term. Pastoralists believe that the leaves of this plant impart a bitter taste to the goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas.

e227d7e1463c6f85.text: A short distance from the settlement of Sassari, the domus of Oredda reveals its decorative splendour only to those who seek the mystery that defines the domus de janas. We went in search of this jana in a field, where one would expect to find nothing at all—except a ditch—and then entered it, holding one's breath at the concentrated art found within.

e230179f994f30a1.text: The central tower survives on the outside to a height of 6.40 m; on the left of the corridor the stairwell opens, with a trapezoidal opening, completely filled with collapse; the entrance to the chamber also has a trapezoidal opening; the inner chamber, essentially circular in plan, has a maximum diameter of 4.76 m and a maximum height of 5.60 m; the tholos survives almost entirely, except for the last two courses.

e23af137c2272a7a.text: Unfortunately not much remains, but those few surviving ashlars are enough to let us understand this temple. It has circular ritual huts, where benches run all round the inside circumference. Countless parallelepiped ashlars of basalt and trachyte tuff, shaped like a T, cover the whole site; they are perfectly worked and finished. In a sudden flashback this brings me back to other Sardinian sanctuaries.

e240a3ead73c556b.text: Genetically attributable to the Ozieri culture, 3500–2700 BC, it is a simple tomb structure of rectangular shape with the entrance facing east. It has a trapezoidal chamber 2.65 m long and 2.20 m wide. The side walls consist of a stone slab topped by packing material, while the back wall is formed by a single flat quadrangular orthostat that projects beyond the side walls by almost half a metre.

e2a03facd95e7241.text: The Fund'e Monti necropolis (also known as Tracucu) consists of 15 hypogean tombs, locally known as Domus de Janas (fairy houses). The tombs, both single-chambered and multi-chambered, have entrances marked by an access corridor (dromos) up to 5 m long, or by an antechamber. The doorways are the most carefully finished elements, finely carved with frames (to hold the stone doors) and rebates (for draining liquids).

e2aa4ebfa6972353.text: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a very small amount remains

e2aa4ffb0ab4d355.text: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building is hard to read because vegetation — shrubs and climbers — covers the structural parts. The main tower, presumably the older one, can be made out; it survives to a height of almost 6 m. This joins a secondary tower positioned to the south of the first. The secondary tower survives to a height of about 4 m.

e2bebb54c8568b9a.text: In the countryside of Osilo there is a very large domus de janas, greatly modified, located beneath the foundations of a church now reduced to ruins.

e2d4aa1528d3645a.text:

e2d4c5c2dd6ab872.text: It is a quadrilobate rectangular structure very similar to Santa Barbara in Macomer. It has a ground area of about 400 m².

From the structure a large part of the Irgoli plain is clearly visible; to the north-east Monte Oddie can be seen.

In the surrounding area there are several collapses, and many ashlars from the structure have been used to build the dry-stone walls.

This is a tholos nuraghe partly leaning against the natural rock to the west; it has an inner and an outer wall face, and between them the spiral staircase can be made out; a guard chamber to the east is plausible, and a possible access ramp starting from the west.

e2ed7f0ad70b79d3.text: The Crabia nuraghe is a single-tower type, built on two superimposed storeys that are still intact, each with a circular central chamber roofed with a tholos. Its distinctive feature is the presence of two staircases: one to the left of the entrance corridor, leading to the first floor and perfectly preserved, while the other, running in the opposite direction to the first, is concealed in a niche inside the tower on the right and leads to a hidden niche on the first floor.

e2fa0ab2edc57889.text: When the Rio Murrone meets the Rio Oloitti, further down by several hundred metres, it drops by about twenty metres, forming a roaring, foaming waterfall in a wild and captivating setting of untouched, primordial nature. The river has a winter torrential character and completely ceases during the driest summer months.

e337a3b56430e204.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are covered by a large fig tree and bramble bushes. Despite this, the building is in fair condition, partly because it has been used as a livestock shelter, an activity that has led to some internal alterations. The lintelled entrance faces south-east. On the left side of the entrance passage opens the stairwell, now blocked by collapse debris.

e33d4c78d9a981f9.text:
1. Of the monument, unusually close to the reference nuraghe, only a fragment of the burial corridor emerges from the soil.

2. The monument, currently destroyed, reveals only some worked ashlar stones, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.

e347afa507594403.text: Within 50 metres of the right bank of the "Riu Vacchetta", 250 metres from the railway line, and about 800 metres south of the Proto-nuraghe Gazza, there are two artificial caves, located just a few metres apart.

e358fb6c8e9408e8.text: A hill covered with vegetation hiding a nuraghe among the largest in the area. It extends over at least two hectares of land to the lacaras.

e35e5d9dee989695.text: It has architectural features similar to those of cisterns with a pointed vault. The internal basin is wide and still collects sacred liquid. Its conservation state, as of July 2022, is very poor and the site is not widely known.

e381335d3c45d8c2.text:
The peculiarity of this nuraghe lies in the fact that the chamber wall opposite the entrance has a short passage leading to a large lintelled window, topped by a relieving window.

The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe and shows no trace of any kind of staircase. The entrance, set to the north-west, has a lintel surmounted by a carefully worked relieving window.

e3a5375d82b134ea.text:
Complex consisting of five towers connected by thick curtain walls resting on natural rock.

The site is internationally known because, for the first time in Sardinia, Minoan ceramics have been discovered.

e3a8f826b418c408.text: Of the monument, largely destroyed, the funerary corridor is visible, composed of polygonal blocks finely finished on the exposed sides.

e3af73782b279ef1.text: Some courses of large stones can be seen, together with part of the summit, which includes a blocked access. At 40 metres to the east, the remains of a "sacred" well.

e3b3700c000e9145.text: Located about 300 metres from the nuraghi Sas Casas and Columbos, respectively to the west and south-east, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche and a corridor staircase, and a central chamber bordered by three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a maximum height of 4.70 m with seven courses to the south-east, while the minimum height is recorded to the south-west at 0.40 m with only a single course: the wall thickness ranges from 4.25 m to 4.75 m.

e3c97795f1539f29.text: The underground chamber is cut into a limestone cliff. "The whole appears carefully organised and balanced in proportion, producing a powerful compositional harmony" (Giuseppa Tanda).

e3cb93959eb908eb.text:
Domus 1 has a multi-chambered layout, with a semicircular antechamber giving access to a first trapezoidal cell that features a central pillar. An opening cut into the top of the pillar leads to an upper level with two small chambers superimposed on the one below.

Domus 2 has a multi-chambered layout, with a corridor, an elliptical cell, a roughly rectangular central chamber with a niche, and a third quadrangular cell.

e3eba253bee46d79.text: The domus is very deeply buried and entry into it is practically impossible.

e3f05863d4c104f7.text: Nuragic village located to the south-south-east of the homonymous nuraghe. In the area, cyclopean wall courses and remains of at least one possible hut are detectable. The abundant vegetation growing there, mainly composed of lentisk, makes it impossible to determine the layout of other possible wall structures. Nearby, on the ground, ceramic fragments are visible.

e401af9db0d1199c.text: It is 7.50 m high, composed of 21 courses, with an 11-metre diameter; it features a very high tholos with thick walls. Adjacent to it is a Nuragic-Roman-medieval village, later abandoned due to epidemics; to the north-west there is an outer wall possibly extending for about one hundred metres, following a natural cliff face.

e42f1cf47ed47211.text: This dolmenic tomb, of the Early Bronze Age, is in an excellent state of preservation; indeed it retains the funerary corridor almost intact, with a flat-lintel roof formed by stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele consists of a centinated monolith in which the small doorway giving access to the burial chamber is cut. The exedra still preserves several stones set in the ground exactly as they were originally.

e438527d273aa4bc.text: Complex nuraghe, the architecture cannot be determined due to the poor state of the structure.

e43cf063bcf5bbad.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt and survives for 2–3 courses laid in a circle to a maximum standing height of about 2 m. The entrance, fitted with a well-worked monolithic lintel, like the blocks of the jambs, faces east. The passage between the inner chamber and the entrance can still be traced, although the whole upper covering is missing.

e447280a42c15953.text: Proto-nuraghe of circular or sub-circular form

e452a11a260029a4.text: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and two additional towers with a courtyard, built of limestone. Traces of a settlement.

e471eb46f34ce9d3.text: The nuraghe takes its name from “pibiri”/pepper. The monument and the surrounding area were investigated scientifically in the early 2000s. The main body, built of limestone, consists of a central tower and at least two additional towers linked by straight curtain walls. The spiral staircase is visible. The main body is enclosed within an outer wall made up of several towers connected by both straight and curved walls.

e4a2b6960c7e460a.text:
In a dominant position, a few metres from the northern bank of the Rio Merchis – which marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Borore and Norbello – less than 400 metres SE of the Nuraghe s'Istrampu and about 250 metres SW of the domus de janas of Ortigosu.

The monument appears as a hill strewn with rubble and covered by dense shrub vegetation. The collapse and the vegetation make a correct planimetric definition of the monument very difficult.

e4d25fa8c60b622d.text: The pre-Nuragic necropolis of S'Elighe Entosu consists of eight very distinctive domus de janas: for example, one preserves in its cell a circular stone hearth carved into the floor, a ceiling carved with a double pitch replicating the timbering of a wooden roof, and on the sides a reproduction of the walls of prehistoric huts. Another, called "delle Sette Stanze", has medieval graffiti along the entrance corridor and seven small cells arranged around the main chamber.

e4e0b3eb895b3578.text: It was built right at the base of the rocky outcrop on which the nuraghe Is Berritta stands. The only visible portion is perhaps the apsidal section, while the exedra has not been identified.

e4f402929f4da866.text: Built of granite as a collective burial and, at the same time, a place of worship, it is a classic example of the megalithic culture that characterised Europe, and the island in particular, during the Copper Age (3rd millennium BC). The dolmen is constructed using the trilithic system (from Greek tri, three, and lithos, stone) – the oldest known architectural scheme – characterised by vertical load-bearing elements that support others laid horizontally.

e51fc852c17a0b9a.text: Little or almost nothing remains standing; a portion of the outer facing of the south side can be distinguished, and all around a very large number of scattered blocks from the collapse. It is classified as a single-tower nuraghe with a circular base and an external diameter of about 11 metres.

e52010df6f9870d1.text: The Flumenlongu nuraghe is a single-tower structure with at least two superimposed levels, and beyond these, in addition to an open courtyard, there is a secondary tower and several accessory chambers. Along its margins extends a village of circular huts, the extent of which has not been defined; from one of them comes an important storage site that has yielded panels, axes, a few scapulae and some bracelets.

e56558db38bb742a.text:
The entrance, about 110 cm x 60 cm, is at floor level. There is a single oval chamber about 150 cm high, 250 cm deep and 130 cm wide, apparently undecorated. At the back of the chamber a pit occupies about two-thirds of the short side and is about 3 m deep; it has not been explored and contains a large niche within the same cavity.

Around the domus de janas cut into the limestone there are rectangular basins that look like quarrying for building material, almost as if the site had been used as a quarry.

e59185c4296f2fe7.text: On a small relief located on the eastern bank of the Rio Monte Ozzatru, which joins the Rio Caddare just a few dozen metres away, there are numerous stone accumulations likely the result of a collapse; in the immediate vicinity, fragments of Nuragic pottery and a fragmented granite mill emerge from the ground.

e5948832db76536c.text: Jewel among the jewels of the archaeological treasure chest of our commune of Chiaramonti. It is a domus whose womb is still intact, preserved by Mother Earth. Visible only is the rich antechamber, adorned with petroglyphs of rare beauty. mu

The nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill, a short distance from the domus de janas of the same name and from Nuraghe s'Aspru.

Of the monument, perhaps an enclosure rather than a nuraghe, two or three courses survive on the west and north sides, to an average height of 2 metres, together with other stones scattered on the ground. The masonry incorporates the natural rock into its circuit and must have enclosed a diameter of about 11 metres. The stones are large and only roughly dressed.

A few kilometres from the village of Uri, a tall stone stele stands in the middle of a field, giving the site its name: Sa Pedra Longa (The Long Stone). In the past it formed the front of a Nuragic giants' tomb, dating to the Middle Bronze Age (about 1700–1350 BC).

Of the original monument only the monolithic arched stele (cut from a single block of rock) survives; its type and relatively modest dimensions suggest an early date.

e5f8feeef7dbdb7f.text: Caves frequently used and modified during the Neolithic. Nearby are the remains of a Nuragic village. Sacred well dismantled using mechanical tools. Some arenaria blocks and T-shaped ashlar stones remain. Where the well or the temple once stood, there is now a crater.

It is a complex nuraghe with a central tower and two partially preserved secondary towers. The main chamber is circular and has three niches arranged in a cross; the tholos survives intact. At present it appears to the visitor 'protected' by dense vegetation that almost completely covers it.

The Accas nuraghe is in a fair state of preservation. The monument has not been excavated, and both the entrance and the interior are partly buried, probably to a depth of about 2 m relative to the nuraghe's original floor level.

The rock face of this hypogeum has the peculiarity of bearing, above the doorway, a bull sign consisting of a line (1.14 m) incised with its ends turned upwards (height 0.18 m).

It is a representation of the bull deity drawn in an extremely elementary and rough manner, which is nevertheless of considerable interest because it is the only known example in the area. Chamber measurements: depth 1.24 m; width 1/1.18 m; height 0.70/0.94 m.

e8cb7a68c732eb3a.text: Among the nuraghes in the Mores area, this one is the best preserved and most intricately structured, thanks to its three towers connected by a bastion. Surrounding it, traces of the ancient village are visible.

e8ce87d5f260d38b.text: This spring lies a few steps from the Nuraghe Sa dom'e S'Orcu, in an area rich in springs and wells of different periods. Architecturally, the sacred area seems to recall, at least in its general lines, structural models of an earlier period. As early as 1990 G. Lilliu noted that "the plan of a round well-shaft preceded by a long rectangular atrium, widening in the middle, resembles the well-known scheme of the proto-Sardinian well temple".

e8df68cacce8d818.text: Uncertain location. Illegal excavation. The excavation extends for about 5 m. An apse is visible at field level.

e8f43ad02c73e666.text: It is not certain what it exactly is, perhaps a unique site that encompasses the giants' tomb, the trilithic dolmen, and the Nuragic fortress. Undoubtedly, it was a very important place for the defense of the territory and the clan. It is a sacred place in every sense, and it is no exaggeration to think of the rock where the rite of the Accabadora was performed. mu.

e92c38380d646af1.text:
A ruined, buried nuraghe of unidentifiable structure.

The nuraghe is located near the settlement of Birori and is composed of a modest hill that has formed over time on top of the ruins of the monument.

It must have been a pass used in antiquity as well: near the rocky spur that overlooks the saddle to the east lie the scant remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone.

Dated to 900 BC by the archaeologist Anati in 1985[2], the site was constructed using cyclopean technique, the same method used for the nuraghes, but unlike the nuraghes, it employed carefully shaped stones, not roughly hewn. In antiquity, the temple was covered.

A short distance before Muravera, at km 51, next to the SS 125, the monument is well signposted and easy to reach. The building consists of a central tower to which a three-lobed bastion with a concave-convex outline was added later, enclosing a small courtyard. The whole complex measures 24 m on the N-S axis and 16 m on the E-W axis.

The central tower, circular in plan (9 m external diameter), survives to a maximum height of about 10 m.

enclosed by a dry-stone wall.

ec40451667a905bd.text: The Pranu Muttedu park is one of the most evocative archaeological sites in inland Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, for a total extension of about 200,000 sq m. Excavations have brought to light numerous artefacts attributable to settled communities of the "Ozieri" culture dating to the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex has the highest concentration of menhirs known in Sardinia.
