Thanks to an architectural restoration project of great scenic impact designed by the architect Pietro Reali, both the baronial palace and the underlying nuraghe, duly brought to light, have become the seat of a museum complex, inaugurated on 29 July 2006.

ecb39d6e2f53b4bd.text: The arched stele of this giants' tomb, lacking an entrance lintel, must have rested directly on the posts that mark the entrance. Alternatively, it could have rested on a lintel, which would have added greater grandeur to the monument.

ecd19520f8f9d6a2.text:
The Nuragic people decided to wall up the tafoni and erect a single, distinctive tower that probably had an additional room above the surface of the rocky outcrop.

Inside these walls fitted into the granites there are very steep stairways.

Not much remains of the large central communal building, perhaps also because of the choices made by La Marmora and Spano who, in their search for the "floor level", had part of the original superstructure moved and pushed down below.

ecd4a550946a6f95.text: Ugas mentions this site as a probable village and workshop of the pre-Nuragic period. Along the regular furrows of ploughing, still today, fragments of pottery, obsidian, and remains of lithic hammers are found.

ecd7b8c4f882b053.text: The tower, circular in plan (13.20 x 13.50 m at the top) and with an entrance facing south-east, survives to a maximum height of 9.30 m, while the average height remains at 8.50 m. The tomb belongs to the category of tombs with an architectural façade, also known as "Nuragic domus", that is, hypogeal burials cut into the rock, often by reusing pre-existing Neolithic domus de janas.

Above it the relieving window survives. A corridor 4 m long and 1.00–2.00 m wide, corbel-vaulted in the first part and flat-lintelled in the second, leads into the chamber.

ee6de48669b12b81.text: We are confronted with only a few basal circular elements of the construction, consisting of stones arranged in courses, some of which have been broken and affected by collapses. It consists of numerous huts, with circular and oval plans, among which one is of particular interest for its ritual religious function.

Trilobate nuraghe (?) on the summit of the Ghilotta hill, built with polygonal blocks of the local volcanic rock.

At the south-east edge of the complex the Case Lenzu, an agro-pastoral farm of the medau type, have been extensively altered in recent times.

f2c3c9b2a59d69a8.text: The concentration of menhirs in this area is considerable; they are in close continuity with those at Ovau, S'Aspiddarju, and Teularju. The menhir FIRULI in the vicinity and along a stretch of 6 metres and 60 cm.

f2c4c0916b4388fb.text: Subtrapezoidal in plan, it stands on a granite outcrop. It is built of large granite blocks laid in polygonal masonry. The only well-worked block is the lintel, with a sub-triangular section shaped to divert the thrust of the overlying structures onto the jambs. On the more accessible sides, to the west and east, the nuraghe is enclosed by a curtain wall, of which the west stretch survives for about 17 m.

f2c82eb40ec06195.text: It is described as a nuragic enclosure by A. Moravetti.

f2c99517e7dc5fa3.text: Corridor nuraghe in good state of conservation

The cyclopean stones involved are disordered and registered in a haphazard manner as a result of land improvement works.

f302a1b77171a55e.text: A single-tower nuraghe of which very little remains

Unfortunately the latest restoration work has not had the desired effect, since the workforce and the site directors have not always been up to the task. The area that was meant to be equipped for groups leaves much to be desired. The interior spaces, on the other hand, are interesting (when they are not full of water), as are the engravings/drawings on the walls.

f376d0b367dce40e.text: It is impossible to enter due to the conspicuous collapse affecting the entrance area.

A violent fire marked the end of Nuragic occupation, although the site was occasionally used during the Punic and Roman periods.

f3a3d3a892ffa9ed.text: The nuraghe is a single-tower structure on two levels, elliptical in shape, which makes use of natural rock masses in which it is embedded. Due to poor conservation, its form is not clearly legible.

f3a46a07ce3a0a73.text: From the upper level of the nuraghe in the north-east, a view of the village is visible, with huts still discernible amid thick vegetation and among the various collapses.

f3b2acdc7a0d8204.text: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, nestled within the dense forest of Scala Argiolas, an ancient entrance to the high plateau of Giara.

f3b3c1af43ef1439.text: One of the numerous nuraghes in this region, located near three giants' tombs.

f3d10a55b2c66ede.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, hidden beneath the thickets of Mediterranean scrub that cover it, only the corridor, the exedra, and inside this the dentilled ashlar stele that once adorned the front remain identifiable.

f423dcd210ef0792.text: Single-cell domus de janas dug into trachyte

f45da258f064349b.text: Proto-nuraghe with multiple towers, almost completely destroyed. With its height it dominates the entire area of "Su Padru". The name derives from the fact that the nuraghe is situated on a very sharp hilltop, from which Punzu Rudu is seen.

f47cb66549d8acd4.text: A small isolated domus de janas, particularly notable for the presence of a rock-cut terraced basin (ancient vats for pressing grapes to extract wine) carved into the rock.

f47d19cfceeefad7.text: in poor condition, the external megalithic circle was destroyed to make way for sheep grazing; in this nuraghe a bronze boat was found and stolen, the largest ever discovered in Sardinia, measuring about 38 cm in length, known as the boat of the sun king, now preserved at the archaeological museum of Sanna in Sassari.

f49006a28db8618c.text: The nuraghe stands near the coast of Trinità d'Agultu, south of Isola Rossa. It has an almost elliptical plan and is accessible from the hamlet of Paduledda by taking the road to “La Scalitta”.

f4919576d2c121cc.text: A kind of ceremonial altar of uncertain period. Located in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe and the homonymous Nuragic village.

f4b821f62d391cd8.text: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses of the wall face remain

f4bb53af72c53186.text: It is located on the summit of the same hill. At first glance it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe partially buried, but it may actually be four-lobed. The lintel above the entrance is particularly distinctive, being slightly curved. The main entrance is pointed. It is also partially buried, as the lintel of the entrance is only a few centimetres above the ground.

f550c4ac582b7b54.text: This nuraghe represents a unique case in the Padadese area, as it was built with stones considerably smaller than the average, except for beams and lintels. Its structure suggests it belongs to a proto-nuraghe (1800–1600 BC).

f55cdea5f0cd56c4.text: The entire oval perimeter outline is preserved. The external wall face reaches its maximum height on the western side, where eight courses of polycyclic stones are counted. Unfortunately, the internal space is covered by vegetation and collapse, preventing any view of its contents.

f55d0efab5cb5dfa.text:
The structure consists of a large horizontal basalt slab resting on seven smaller stones that form a polygonal chamber. Around it is a circle of stones that was intended to contain the earth forming the mound cover.

The construction of this funerary monument dates back to the third millennium BCE.

f55daf4229a67ee3.text: Complex nuraghe consisting of 3 towers connected together. The structure shows heavy damage caused by tomb robbers.

f582ac75132cb3a5.text: It includes at least seven hypogea, most of which are damaged by collapses and significant reuse.

f587316a48eb3340.text: The monument, built with polygonal masonry using granite stones, is of the corridor type and has a subcircular plan; the entrance leads through a small flat-laid corridor to a central circular chamber without a roof, which once connected to two other rooms, now inaccessible due to collapses.

f58748b4e7edfb53.text: During excavation works for the road connecting Santu Miali to the church of Santa Maria de Aidos, further down, a burial was destroyed, which may have been a giants' tomb or possibly a medieval tomb. Still visible in its original position is a lintel in dark trachyte.

f58789204a38c8f3.text: A small alignment of menhirs appears on the slope leading to Mamucada inside the plot of sa Figu on the border with the land of Padedda. On closer inspection they seem little worked and of a shape vaguely comparable to a pyramid prism with a polygonal base that is never the same. According to the old people most of them come from the steep part of Badde Saltara, which looks over the plain of S.M de Orria Pitzinna. mu

f58e05194543ceb9.text:
Comprises one hundred reoccupied nuragic huts in Roman period.

Near the village there is also a nuragic well and it appears that there are some menhirs.

f58f1902cab54c35.text:
Other towers are attached to the central tower, possibly five in number. The entire structure is hardly discernible due to the presence of dense vegetation and thorny bushes that block access (good thing!). Internally, almost the whole structure can be visited and one appreciates the harmonious development of the powerful and majestic construction.

f5b2d63e141f7165.text: There are three isolated tombs in the municipality of Mamoiada.

f5b50a933890f662.text: Within the broad and intricate framework of Sardinian subterranean architecture, the magnificent necropolises of Mesu 'e Montes, S'Adde 'e Asile, S'Isterridolzu, Noeddale, Su Littu, and the Tomba di Littos Longos have provided extremely significant data regarding the phenomenon of subterranean burial. The entrance is marked by a long corridor cut into limestone. Inside, bull's-head protomes and other carved decorations are present.

f5f5545418180708.text: The well consists of a rectangular, paved atrium that leads to the stairwell through a strongly tapering trapezoidal passage; the stairwell, about 6 metres long, leads down to the underground chamber, which is sub-circular and covered by a tholos, where the water table is intercepted. The structure is built of local marl blocks, regularly squared, bush-hammered and laid in staggered courses with earth inserted between the bedding planes.

f60dcaa3fa7bab60.text:
In a dominant and strategically privileged position.

It is a single-tower with an added body, featuring a circular chamber with three niches arranged in a cross pattern.

Due to the collapse, the entrance to the south-east and the passage, as well as any associated auxiliary spaces (niches and/or stairs), are currently not visible; however, their presence is likely certain given the evolved typology of the chamber.

f613b83ada713f78.text:
It consists of two single-chambered hypogea dug into a trachytic bed at an elevation of 190 metres.

Surrounded by dense and impenetrable vegetation, it is very difficult to locate.

f6327688ca2f5c4f.text: The tomb is dug into a granite outcrop; it consists of a dromos and a chamber in which a small niche has been carved. The underground chamber opens above a gentle slope just a few centimetres above the field level.

f639262e3349aa36.text: Dolmen composed of a large covering slab supported by three vertical orthostats

f63b1f8e424adb01.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is built in isodomic masonry with basalt elements finely squared and finished, found both in their original orientation and incorporated into the dry-stone walls of the surrounding enclosure. The burial chamber is visible through its corridor, with the terminal slab at the end, the exedra with the central slab through which the entrance portal is cut, and the dentilled lintel.

f63d89bd50809220.text:
The monument has a fairly complex plan characterised by successive additions to the main body; the latter has an elliptical plan with a maximum diameter of 13.5 m and is provided with two entrances, to the north and south-west, which give access to two corridors that join at right angles at the centre of the central tower.

Two structures abut the central tower: one is on the north side, the other must have encircled at least two-thirds of the whole.

f644622b6b8c9b0d.text: Single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed, situated on a trachyte rise near the Cuga valley.

f674d3f5d3b021e8.text: Single-tower composed of large, roughly hewn limestone blocks with an entrance oriented to south-east. The tower remains up to a maximum height of 2.50 m. To the left of the entrance is a staircase. The visibility of the nuraghe is greatly impaired by the vegetation that covers it.

f67971527f6c581f.text: Simple-type nuraghe, completely ruined, reduced to a heap of rough blocks, about two metres high.

f67b4bed0b90390d.text: Datable to the 13th century BC. Belonging to the Albucciu nuraghe. In this tomb the rectangular body, of flat slabs, is surrounded by a mound of rubble. The exedra is reduced to a series of blocks and small slabs that deprive the monument of the sense of grandeur that characterises the other megalithic burials. The wall thickness of the tomb is remarkable, at about 6 metres. The structure has undergone alterations in different periods and has been reused several times.

f6abda7cd426bf59.text: Complex nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

f6c3a122942a31e6.text: The exceptional nature of the Pranu Siara site lies in particular in the fact that the tomb is not isolated but forms part of an extensive necropolis perfectly aligned for several hundred metres and overlooked, at the change in level, by a kind of fortified enclosure that appears to protect the plateau, following settlement models of a similar type documented in the north-western area of the island, in the Olmedo and Castelsardo zones.

f6d1af4d6ca11320.text:
It is a single-tower with a niche, a ramp, and a chamber bordered by two niches.

The tower, circular in plan (diameter 11.60 m), survives to a maximum height of 6.00 m with 14 courses on the north-west side, while at the entrance the height is 5.20 m on 11 courses; the south-east wall, however, is largely collapsed.

f6d76858a0c60287.text: Single-tower nuraghe, half-destroyed, at Su Billianu in Uri

f6eedb7cbdfc8ddf.text: Likely complex nuraghe today partially collapsed and difficult to read.

f7085f2892398844.text: Two huts with sacred functions are present. Structure A has a semicircular shape and is considerably larger than structure B.

f73daf49bfff75c8.text: Nuraghe of undetermined type; only a few remains are left on the site among the vegetation. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

f73f6be823ce93d0.text:
Remains of a megalithic tomb that, as can be seen, appears to be clearly a dolmen.

Of the monument, only one orthostat remains “in situ” (width 1.52 m – thickness 0.40 m – visible height 1.10 m), while numerous other slabs have been overturned in the area directly in front of the exedra. The covering slab lies broken into several fragments; the presence of a peristalith is evident.

f74c016b9d786654.text: Single-tower nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

f74f1f085cefbd57.text: The dolmenic tomb stands on a modest rocky rise, about 200 metres north-west of the giants' tomb of the same name and less than 500 metres south-east of the Nuraghe Cherbos. The burial chamber, of a vaguely quadrangular shape, is bounded by five stones set on edge that appear to rest directly on the outcropping rock. The cover consists of a polygonal slab, now slightly tilted by the fall of an orthostat and with widespread chipping, thinner than the supports.

f767fbc5d1c7449c.text: Complex nuraghe visible seasonally depending on the water levels in the Cuga basin. A considerable village once surrounded the nuraghe.

f771b3b38e61fc3a.text: Situated a short distance from the Durane stream, the tomb has a burial chamber about 9 metres long and a broad exedra on the front, 14 metres long. It is built entirely of granite with ashlars laid in regular courses. The central part has the entrance doorway surmounted by the so-called “dentilled ashlar”. The large exedra, provided with bench-seats for pilgrims to rest on, contains a small baetyl to the east, which must have been an object of worship.

f782502dedad9526.text: (da Mitz'arramini, site where it is located), it is a complex nuraghe with multiple towers, near which a village also exists. The building is situated in an area with a toponym indicating a copper-related reference, where the central tower and a secondary tower can clearly be identified, although both are currently sealed by eolian and agricultural deposits due to the lack of thorough investigations.

f79e1f9d0c05b770.text: Su Stampu de su Turrunu o de su Turnu is a unique sinkhole spring, originating from the Rio e Spinedda, whose waters emerge in a cascade from a hole in the rock, falling into the centre of an attractive lagoon.

f7a1960119590c79.text: Only small portions of the wall of the nuraghe remain. The collapse makes it impossible to read the plan.

f7d0ffbe10e3373e.text: Proto-nuraghe of corridor type, with an ellipsoidal–sub-quadrangular plan, built with polygonal basalt blocks. Only a few courses of the base remain, less than 2 m in height. The nuraghe is built upon a solid rocky foundation that emerges and forms an integral part of the structure.

f7e2745200540474.text: The Tolinu nuraghe, located in a fine position on a plateau overlooking the Tirso valley, is an imposing complex nuraghe consisting of a large central mastio with a truncated conical shape, surrounded by a bastion that encloses several smaller towers.

f7ed994da8c83104.text: "On the site, some large slabs are found partially embedded in the ground, partially fragmented and not in situ, which might be related to a dolmenic structure. Although no archaeological material is found on the ground, the shape and dimensions of the blocks suggest the site should be included among areas at risk." The name recalls other toponyms of dolmen.

f7f4c8b7dd4dfc5f.text: Externally, two windows are visible, located 1.60 m above the floor level, each measuring about 35 cm in width. The access opening, measuring 1.60 m in height and 1.30 m in width, features a 35 cm descending step to enter the chamber. The room is 4 m wide, 3 m deep, and about 2.5 m high; at its centre there is a circular ditch, 60 cm deep and 10 cm wide, slightly offset to the right of the entrance.

f804e5469d184ec2.text: Adjacent to a probable Nuragic enclosure, there is a trachyte block of red stone that appears at first glance to be a door or an entrance slab. This block, irregular in shape and resembling a parallelepiped, has a plane on two offset levels visible in the exposed section. At the upper level, and at the ends, there are two holes: one circular and the other rectangular.

f82e6fa968831119.text: It appears as a heap of stones and a few large blocks of red sandstone, located on a piece of land excluded from cultivation and grazing, near the necropolis of Anghelu Ruiu. State of conservation: poor.

f83b987b336768aa.text: Single-tower nuraghe in limestone, almost half-covered by vegetation, stands at the edge of a cultivated area within a bend of the Riu Filibertu. State of conservation: good. It is suspected that a village once surrounded it.

f845fe40cb8ec562.text:
Angius with the name “Macariu 1849. Taramelli. and 1883 land register. Also Girillis.

It is a single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte, its structure hard to read because of the dense vegetation. Inside, the outline of the tower is partly distinguishable. Next to the nuraghe are structures probably belonging to the village. The area also contains several pottery fragments.

f84be14d210d8c80.text: Like many others, in total ruin. Enough evidence of the ancient construction can still be distinguished, with some boulders of the basal circle visible. Unfortunately, in the 1960s several sites in the area disappeared because of land-reclamation works, but above all because of the construction of the reservoir dam, which never fully served its intended purpose. Nuraghe of the hill of the deer. See Montìju de chèlvos I.mu

f86b3c41e6b8c2de.text: Archaic corridor nuraghe. The building stands on a valley floor just 4 m from the watercourse called Riu e'Sa Tanca, on its eastern bank. It is completely covered by vegetation, in particular dense bramble thickets growing abundantly along the stream banks make observation difficult. Some large polygonal basalt blocks laid one on another can be seen on the north and east sides.

f86f82064355b713.text: Feature whose plan is not easily interpretable

f87196502bd98591.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The structures are almost completely enveloped by vegetation. The stacked blocks on the southern side can be seen, with a residual height of about 2.50 m. The rest of the building is not visible due to poor visibility. Accumulations of fallen blocks can be observed on the small slope to the south of the nuraghe.

f89844ce83439de1.text: Single-tower nuraghe, in poor state of conservation, traces of inter-wall stairs and lateral niches are visible. In the best-preserved section, the nuraghe rises by about 3 m, with six courses of roughly hewn stones.

f89dd727c4f245f5.text: In this area there are 11 menhirs and one carved stele, most of them made of granite. None of them has retained their original position; almost all are broken, probably they were buried by mechanical equipment during land improvement works.

f8a7a7f7a4a5066e.text: The entire area between the domus de janas necropolis and the church of Santo Stefano is rich in weathered stones adapted to niches and recesses, where it is often difficult to distinguish between natural and human intervention. In particular, around the church five sites with carved stones can be identified:

f8b84bc99e1b017b.text: Single-tower nuraghe, built with calcareous stones, of which only one to two courses of stones of the external wall face remain.

f8c85955ead52a60.text: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos still intact

f8e9b0f387b41e54.text: About 200 m from the rise in terrain indicating the presence of the nuraghe, in a north-north-east direction, an settlement is visible covering an area of 6–700 m² and revealing a series of quadrilateral rooms delimited by large trachyte stones.

f909c7ac01cea8dd.text: The cemetery is carved into a granitic outcrop of the Buddusò plateau. It consists of 6 hypogea and dates to 3200–2800 BC. Some domus have single-roomed spaces, while others have a multi-room layout. One of the domus shows traces of red painted murals in parallel bands applied to raised strips.

f948b1e845f77d37.text:
The nuraghe, situated on the summit of the hill, is very damaged.

It consists of a circular tower and an elliptical, eccentric curtain wall elongated towards the south-east, where the entrance is presumably located.

f96370418bbe8e11.text:
Nuraghe. Located on top of a hill, with views over the area of Sa Gruttixedda (Pozzo/Village Nuragic)

Covered with large stones and vegetation.

f98302bd9075f52f.text: Under current conditions, there is no evidence of lithic or ceramic material scattered on the ground; however, the presence of possible village structures cannot be ruled out, whose remains might have been obscured on the surface by land transformations and land use.

f9a5e072dac89868.text: Tholos nuraghe. There were two towers; one has been completely dismantled to build the drystone wall that runs along the mountain. On the south-east side the tower stands over 4 m high, while the interior is blocked by a layer of earth and debris that makes it inaccessible. Beside it is a cave recently explored by the Uras caving group.

f9afde37a6e644d4.text: It overlooks the Monte Ozzastru valley, a short distance from the Porchiles nuraghe, and only the base of the monument is visible.

f9bfb89fb91ce480.text: Nuraghe Carcina stands in the countryside of Orroli, about 1.5 km south-east of the village. It is abandoned but in fair condition. It appears as a complex nuraghe with two towers clearly visible. The main tower has a surviving height of over 3 metres and is entered through a doorway topped by a fine sloping lintel. This doorway is largely buried and gives access to a chamber with a tholos that is missing its top courses.

f9c315ab016e26fe.text: Of the nuraghe, in very poor condition of conservation, only a few large trachytic stones remain, which once formed the first course of the base and which today barely suggest the circular plan of the structure.

f9e26b52a065f70a.text: The tomb, located beside a narrow path and built with courses of large stones, features an exedra facing south and a gallery partially damaged. Nearby, scattered stones and large rubble heaps are visible.

fa03111ac3187ba2.text: Ruins of the base drum of a classic single-tower nuraghe in polygonal masonry, with a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, an internal chamber roofed with a tholos and provided with a small subsidiary niche, and an entrance stair – unfortunately completely destroyed – defended by an opposing guard chamber. The building, already dismantled in Roman times, was reused, incorporating five fragments of figured statue-menhirs that already existed in the area.

fa1ff845685f491c.text: The domus de janas cemetery is excavated in a basalt outcrop that dominates the Riu Mannu valley, along the provincial road Suni-Pozzomaggiore, in the Planargia region, in north-western Sardinia. The underground complex includes 12 single and multi-cellular burials, all accessed almost always through a vestibule.

fa243a4645808007.text: Sacred area, probably pre-Nuragic in date. It consists of a stone bench with niches, hollows, and artificial recesses. The summit of the hill is covered by stones fallen from a nuraghe.

fa2a800d2061a5b5.text: the rock that is visible at the site) and a landslide of medium to small stones

fa7947fcf31658e4.text: It is an almost inaccessible site with a clear view of much of the nuraghi of the Ogliastra plain. I think it is a multi-lobed nuraghe, but between the vegetation and the collapse it is illegible. The photo I sent is the only part facing south from which anything can be understood; the rest is embedded among natural rocks and, I repeat, with the collapse nothing can be made out. The area is scattered with small terracotta ashlars. (Report by Daniele Murgia, Triei)

fa7e5213f7cfa712.text:
Nuragic temple with sacred well and circular chamber, originally covered with a tholos vault, now lost, preceded by a staircase of which seven steps remain.

The underground structure is built with andesite blocks arranged in concentric courses, eight of which remain.

Water from the groundwater table still accumulates at the bottom of the chamber. The monument is currently located within a small enclosed area.

faa2c4fa0c577fe4.text: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with only a few ashlar stones remaining and its location difficult to determine.

faa3a4b8c0f08c01.text: Site located in the Su Pranu area, on top of a hill with a truncated pyramidal shape. Here the remains of a nuraghe or more likely a temple are found, attested by votive material discovered at the base of the site and along the ridges of the small hill; on its southern-facing slope there are subterranean tombs that are extremely difficult to access.

faa792395ac7ad13.text: The Sa Linnarta complex, a three-lobed nuraghe with numerous associated huts and a beautiful sacred well, is, according to experts, one of the most important Nuragic sites in the Baronia.

faad4995253ac71c.text: Towards the road that leads from Samatzai onto the SS 128. On the right you reach the locality of Bidda Mendula. On a low sandstone promontory (altitude 150 m) the ruins of a nuraghe built of large sandstone marl blocks can be seen, belonging to a Nuragic settlement. On the surface a circular building is visible, probably a single-tower nuraghe, 14 m in diameter, which on the west side shows the remains of a facing wall 2.30 m thick, visible for several metres.

faf45d335e2c3b6e.text: Complex nuraghe composed of a central tower and possibly two other towers. Unfortunately, the original structure is hidden by a conspicuous collapse and the presence of dense vegetation. Adjacent to the central tower, in front-facing position, two possible towers can be glimpsed. To the north-east a rectangular room built in cyclopean masonry is visible, featuring a flat-laid roof.

fb0d2457164c04ea.text: The site includes the nuraghe and the remains of an extensive village. It also features two burials: a giants' tomb and a burial known as "the lilies" because there appear to be many of them.

fb182f0caf95328d.text: Su Scusorgiu: "The Treasure". In this storage room, 40 complete pre-Nuragic swords were found. They are now on display at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.

fb18a5b9d3b2f7a7.text: It is the "father of all the nuraghes", the proto-nuraghe Madugui (local name) or Maduli (archaeological designation), which projects prominently on the south-eastern edge of the upland. Today its walls are four metres and a half high, though they were once taller. It is one of the most significant examples of proto-nuraghe architecture (or pseudo-nuraghe) – a prototype of the "corridor nuraghes", later evolving into towers or clusters of towers closed in a false dome (tholos).

fb301922607a2eac.text: In the centre of the village, research has shown “the existence of important portions of the nuragic structure still preserved around the water basin constructed on the site in the 1920s. Despite the ancient building having been used as a foundation for the modern structure, excavations have revealed extensive remains of a tower featuring a powerful masonry of polygonal basalt blocks”.

fb6644344bea5b86.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. Almost completely destroyed, it appears as a heap of basaltic stones. The first two courses of the base are visible on the south side.

fb8985aded7908ce.text: Located in the valley of the Rio Siniscola, near the mouth of the river, it has a rectangular plan with an internal chamber of elliptical shape, preserved to a height of about 2 metres, and is built with white limestone incorporating slabs of shale.

fb9499c609bafb9e.text: Baetyls placed near the Corbos nuraghe, used as posts for a metal gate.

fb9e63b8625cf8c7.text: The tomb extends along a north-east/south-west major axis 5.50 m long and has its entrance opening to the south-west at the centre of a semicircular exedra that has almost entirely disappeared. The rear apse was probably straight-sided, but the closing masonry has not survived. It should be noted that the tomb is still largely buried, giving the impression that what is currently visible is actually the uppermost courses, lacking their covering.

fbb2eed84bd46dac.text: The spring has no steps and is in an almost perfect state of preservation[1]. The wall structure, entirely of granite, is completely preserved and the entrance to the inner chamber consists of a large vaulted opening. The spring is covered with two granite slabs. It encloses a spring vein, still active, and has a large threshold stone at the front with a channel cut into it for the water to drain away.

fbb3e610f2dae881.text: The Nuraghe Nuracale is a four-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, or central tower, surrounded by four smaller towers held together by massive straight walls. The main entrance, located in the east bastion, gives access to the internal courtyard, shaped like a half-moon, onto which open the entrance of the central tower and of the south-east and north-east lateral towers, while the other two towers were linked to the courtyard by two long corridors cut into the bastions.

fbb5a74985bbfa45.text: The two menhirs are located about fifty metres apart.

fbba8f913b13c586.text: It is an acrocoro surrounded by a wall, probably of Nuragic period, partially buried and never investigated, near which stands the baetyl (warrior's head of Bulzi). From it, all the numerous nuraghes that existed in the surrounding area are monitored.

fbbc493b97e8f1d7.text:
The monument stands on the edge of a rise looking towards Montagna di Sant'Antonio; the Nuragic tower is bounded on the west-south-west by the steep profile of the rock, while a quadrangular enclosure opens on the front.

The building is circular, but the western profile tends to be straight for a length of about 5 metres: the sector facing west-south-west cannot be surveyed because of the collapse and the dense shrub vegetation.

fbc25345bf108503.text: DIRROCCATO NURAGHE WITH ABOUT SIX COURSES EXTERIOR TO GROUND LEVEL

fbca86f75858ba19.text: It belongs to the group of nuraghi with a basement level, I say this with the benefit of inventory because survey is prevented by sturdy thorny plants that have colonised the structure. The basal circle is composed of vaguely squared boulders that interlock well, creating a regular wall face together with some natural rock outcrops. It has a raised entrance above ground level that highlights the sacred character of the construction.

fbef0f274d3b10c7.text: Nuraghe site located just a few metres from the cliff formed by the Rio Carrabusu. The state of conservation is precarious and the structure is partially buried.

fbfd681976746b46.text: The nuraghe was almost completely destroyed in the 1960s to extract stone for use in house construction. Nearby, a well of the same period and likely belonging to the structure is present.

fc094f50a6b7c095.text: USAI (2014, p. 42) includes it within the typology "the 'small nuraghes' probably unfinished".

fc154a54a2ac1867.text: Buried nuraghe, whose layout is difficult to determine. It was certainly a complex and multi-lobed structure. The name suggests its probable function as a watchpost at an embarkation point during the Nuragic period.

fc20f83eb4b7e08f.text: The toponym dates back certainly to the medieval period and is due to the fact that the nuraghe rises above the most extreme promontory, directly jutting over the valley below. There are still several circles of stones, variously fallen. The interior can be visited, and the entrance, strictly oriented towards south-south-east, is clearly visible.

fc5030e9a5d685c4.text: Four-lobed nuraghe. A nuraghe with the addition of two lateral towers connected to the original tower by a semi-circular corridor.

fc6b39cc50a65fdf.text: The Sos Muros complex occupies an area of over twenty hectares, showing clear signs of circular huts and this sacred well.

fc6ecf5a0dbdcea3.text: Two small domus de janas visible from the road

fc707613e2068e85.text: A very unusual and unique structure in form. Known as the rectangular nuraghe. Situated atop a stratified mass of limestone shaped like a reproductive member, around which the river makes a bend. It could be a temple with buildings serving communal gatherings.

fc86be8b0caff09b.text: The remaining buried structure extends at least two metres below the current campagna level, due to the outward escape of the “sacco” from within the wall face, making it impossible to access the internal rooms of the corridor nuraghe.

fcab5573bd524538.text: The condition of the domus de janas is unknown.

fcb5ab8be88326d0.text:
Only a few of the basal stones remain. They are hard white tuff, still friable. They are located directly above the curved alignment along the mountain ridge, where several domus de janas are visible, extending along the crest of the named mountain and down its slope. www.archeologosardos.it

Nuraghe of the forated mountain. See Mònte pertùsu.

fccc75b5fbc13e1d.text: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is completely covered by a layer of mastic but the terminal section of the corridor is still visible.

fcd57e39e9c6e1a8.text: Domus de janas of which no description is available

fd0964e804d0836b.text:
The Nuraghe Tunis is in a precarious state of preservation, particularly the central tower and the southern parts of the four-lobed bastion; of the latter the two northern towers can be seen, with stretches of the three adjacent curtain walls, and the eastern boundary wall of the courtyard with the large window connected to the staircase leading to the wall-walks.

Around the ruins of the bastion, stretches of straight walls and parts of circular buildings emerge.

fd155c02bd32a2da.text: Near the Massidda or Ghisu medau two small dry-stone buildings with circular plans can still be seen, occupying two eminences overlooking the valley that slopes down to Porto Paglia: they are probably a single-tower nuraghe or a tower-hut and a smaller hut.

fd2177e6984fa4c7.text: It is undoubtedly the most imposing and best-preserved nuraghe in the Solarussa area. The layout is that of a tancato nuraghe, with a main tower and a secondary tower separated by a courtyard. The main tower is in good condition, with its tholos vault substantially intact. The secondary tower has partially collapsed, while the internal courtyard is blocked by the collapse debris.

fd23d4c303ffeef3.text: The megalithic structure is currently located within a sheepfold.

fd3383f2b505e42c.text: It lies in the area of the great Nurra land-reclamation scheme and is one of the nuraghi in the zone that has a mezzanine floor. A complex nuraghe of roughly dressed sandstone blocks, well preserved, it stands inside a private farm used for fruit and vegetable growing. It was reused during the Second World War by the construction of bunkers. In 1940–43 Nuraghe Cubalciada was incorporated into the defensive system of the 204th Coastal Division.

fd3f82b84c03b85c.text: Probable proto-nuraghe, of semicircular plan attached to a rocky mass. Presence of two menhirs

fd58b5336eaf9fdc.text: The Arbu Dolmen II is instead composed of a rectangular corridor (1.84 m x 0.78/0.72 m), bounded on the longer sides by naturally occurring rock carefully smoothed and by an orthostat on the head end; above it, a covering slab (1.70 m x 1.22 m x 0.45 m thick).

fd83a28f99273c82.text: The tomb currently features only a corridor aligned along the SE-NO axis, bordered by orthostats and open on the shorter sides, now destroyed. Although no secure elements remain to determine the entrance's location—only a trench excavation could clarify whether it opened on one or the other side—it is plausible to assume that the entrance, in line with typical features of such tombs, faced south-east.

fd85671eecc1347f.text: The Nuraghe Agnu is built of granite, with a horseshoe plan because it is partly set against the rock face. It has a monumental entrance, oriented to the east and fitted with a lintel, leading into a corridor that was once fitted with a wooden sliding door descending from above. On the sides two corridors open; one leads to a domed cell, the other passes through the wall and out through the natural rock.

fd94a6f1c8ce55fb.text: Very ruined: vertical orthostats (with transverse cuts) and the tumulus closure and part of the exedra can still be identified.

fd987d6a233dc248.text:
The tower, truncated-conical in shape, shows a marked structural subsidence on the south side running from the entrance up to the top where the masonry is missing, also affecting part of the tholos.

From the entrance, oriented south/south-east and lacking its lintel, you enter a corridor that splays inwards with a partially surviving ogival roof. On the left side of the corridor the stairwell opens, roofed with flat slabs, of which three blocks remain.

fdc43627ba1d11b0.text: Reduced to a state of ruin, like most of the other sites in the commune of Chiaramonti. It nevertheless shows a few basal circles of cyclopean stones, with the main opening particularly well highlighted by a massive lintel oriented towards south-south-east.

fe0340317c28f0c7.text: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing; the position of the nuraghe is uncertain, and it does not appear marked on the IGM map.

fe0bc79b77e531ad.text: The monument is a single-tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber surrounded by three niches in the classic cross-shaped arrangement. The masonry work is composed of large stones in the first courses and progressively smaller stones towards the top. Around the nuraghe remain traces of the village, to the east, and a section of outer wall to the north.

fe1df8b11052f037.text: The giants' tomb is located in the municipality of Romana; the remains of the burial are visible today embedded in a dry stone wall.

fe21abc9cd50b160.text: Small atypical single-tower nuraghe, belonging to the Appiu village context. Located at the end of a path that extends from the village to the Giants' Tomb, two small dolmen, and finally this small nuraghe.

fe3973eb52d17df1.text: The cemetery, dated to the second half of the fourth millennium BC and attributable to the Arzachena culture, consists of five lithic cists, four of which are surrounded by circles of stones driven into the ground that, originally, marked the burial mound composed of earth and rubble erected over the burial.

fe3bfdbec79fdad3.text: Within an olive grove, following land clearing, numerous ceramic materials from different periods have come to light; among the prehistoric fragments, there are no doubt typical Nuragic vessels such as storage jars and ovens. No clear structures remain, as the site has undergone constant agricultural transformations.

fe452ca654dee2e2.text: Unfortunately, almost entirely destroyed by erosion. Only a few blocks remain in their original position.

fe63d02db97953c6.text: The nuraghe is a complex structure consisting of a main tower to which two further towers, linked by a straight curtain wall, were added at later stages. The main tower, built of well-worked basalt blocks (especially in the upper parts) laid in regular courses, has its entrance to the north-east, topped by a lintel with a relieving window and raised above ground level.

fe76130759960867.text: Due to the collapse, which affects the entrance, access to the chamber is impossible. The polygonal masonry work is composed of well-shaped granite blocks, frequently using wedges of the same lithological material. The foundation, in contrast, shows a very compact structure relative to the upper plane of the monument, with large blocks roughly worked.

fe7821f6883fa64a.text: The nuraghe consists of a main tower, two additional structures joined to it, remains of the outer wall along much of the perimeter, and the remains of several huts. It is not well preserved except for the main lintelled entrance with its relieving window and the remains of a staircase. A few dozen metres to the north-west there is a cave used as a necropolis. The skeletal remains have been studied and date to the Nuragic period.

feafbb6e16c99040.text: Temple dedicated to Astarte, the Phoenician goddess of love, fertility, and war. What made their places of worship notable was the fact that they were associated with a particular practice: sacred prostitution.

fec2af2adc342f0b.text: 'Perdas de Fogu' on the slope of a small hill contain the remains of a giants' tomb built with large calcareous stones. The burial chamber is polygonal with an entrance to the south where part of an exedra with a 12.10-metre circumference is visible. The chamber is preserved for a length of 6 metres, a width of 1.20 metres, and a height of 0.50 metres.

fedb614b06203502.text: It is a large village, showing a spread of ruins, with nuraghe walls covering an area of about eight thousand square metres.

ff0129571dd7d385.text: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which very few remains can be seen

ff0a204cd398bbbd.text: Single-cell domus de janas built within a "trovante"

ff161b8db71ec684.text: Comprised of a Nuragic village, a circular temple, and a megaron temple, and upstream a series of springs, wells, and channels for the collection, gathering, and channeling of water towards the sacred area located downstream.

ff280b1622433f81.text: The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

ff3b22b43a6cd206.text: Domus de janas submerged by the Omodeo flood. It preserves a unique bull's-head protome in high relief.

ff42f029c5a65adc.text: Nuraghe eroded and surrounded by vegetation, of which three or four courses remain.

ff572b34e36bfaa0.text:
The name is linked to a legend: after a human skull was found inside the cave, it was thought to belong to one of the unmarried mothers who, it is said, were shut inside as punishment until they died of suffocation.

More recently, human remains accompanied by coarseware pottery fragments have been found there. It is clear that Su Secretu is a small natural cave that must have served for funerary depositions.

ff70b1020d9ee8aa.text: A single-tower nuraghe overlooking the Rio Santu Milanu valley in an area reused in the medieval period.

ff848ec6f1270da6.text: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. In very poor condition, a few boulders of the entrance jamb and part of a basal course are visible. The entrance faces west. The nuraghe has suffered repeated robbing, as shown by several heaps of basalt boulders a short distance away. Even so, it cannot be ruled out that the nuraghe was never finished, as is documented elsewhere in the area.

ff951fdcb70d3e6c.text: Only a few courses of porphyritic material are visible.

ffbbac4cae4ffe49.text:
There are no features sufficient to classify it as a nuraghe. It appears to be a simple megalithic wall composed of roughly squared stones, possibly serving as a rudimentary fortification for a watchpost (?)?

Nuraghe of the ruins. The ruins referred to here are those of the nuraghe that gives its name to the locality. See Carràlzu. Ardu Pinzone = cardinal axis. mu
